# EchoAI Development Changelog

> **Purpose**: Single source of truth for every code change with the *reason* it
> was made. Read this **before** changing any subsystem to avoid undoing past
> fixes or re-doing work that was deferred for a known reason.

## 2026-09-03 (perf) — doubling the cores made it 40% SLOWER; the ISA is the lever

**Rapid Compute doubled VM-1 and the system got worse.** Same four questions, same
corpus, single user, sequential, semantic cache disabled in both runs.

| | Before (32c) | After (64c) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prefill | 111.7 tok/s | 101.8 tok/s | −9% |
| Decode | 13.2 tok/s | **7.2 tok/s** | **−46%** |
| Output rate | 33.7 chars/s | 20.2 chars/s | **−40%** |
| Mean response | 114.2 s / 3,909 chars | 134.9 s / 2,785 chars | shorter answers, longer wait |

Map-reduce question moved the same way: 202.9 s → 323.6 s.

**⭐⭐⭐ Why: they did not add cores, they moved the VM to a different CPU.**
Intel Ice Lake → **AMD EPYC-Rome (Zen 2, 2019 — an OLDER generation)**, losing
AVX-512/VNNI/BF16. Verified in `/proc/<pid>/maps`: llama.cpp dropped from
`libggml-cpu-icelake.so` to **`libggml-cpu-haswell.so`**. Decode is largely
memory-bandwidth-bound so extra cores add little; prefill is compute-bound and
held up (−9%). All 64 cores ran at 99.7% — the capacity is used, it just does
less per instruction.

▶ **Ask for AVX-512, not cores**: Ice Lake+ or AMD Genoa (Zen 4)+; Sapphire
Rapids adds AMX. A 32-core AVX-512 box beat this 64-core one.

**⚠️⚠️ The semantic cache silently invalidates any repeat-question benchmark.**
The first re-run returned 44 ms / 49 ms / 8.3 s, `cache_hit`, byte-identical
answers — no inference at all. Tier-0 cache (`query_router.rs:1204`, cosine ≥
0.92) is ON by default in release (`query_cache_enabled()` `:2843`). Set
`ECHO_QUERY_CACHE=0` for hardware work. ⭐ As a *product* number it is excellent:
a repeat question in **44 ms vs 114 s**.

**⚠️⚠️ The reboot killed llama.cpp** — it runs under tmux, which does not survive
a restart. Port 8080 was dead and Noviq had no backend, with no alarm anywhere.
`-t 32` was also hardcoded in `start-server.sh`, so a plain restart would have
used half the new cores (now `-t 64`; original at `start-server.sh.bak`).
▶ Make it a systemd unit.

**Latency stage split re-confirmed on the new hardware:** retrieval + preparation
**100 ms**, LLM **134.8 s**, post-processing **1 ms** — model inference is
**99.93%** of a response. Nothing outside the model is worth optimising.

**Corpus:** the 16-PDF Solid Waste set is indexed (2,933 chunks). Only PDFs; the
`.pptx`/`.docx`/scripts in that folder were excluded.

## 2026-09-03 (deploy) — the image is BUILT and RUNNING; building it found 3 defects

**Result first.** The single-image CPU stack is live on Rapid Compute VM-2 and
answers grounded, cited questions through VM-1. Full turn on an in-corpus
question: **12.5 s**, two correct citations with verbatim text. An out-of-corpus
question is refused in 1.8 s. Indexing works: 5 chunks parsed, **embedded in
97 ms**. First boot (initdb + pgvector + every migration + admin seed) to
`/api/health` 200 in **~20 s**.

**Topology, and the reason it is this shape.** VM-1 `srv1` 192.168.10.167 (Ice
Lake, AVX-512, llama.cpp + Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M on :8080) and VM-2 `srv2`
192.168.10.254 (EPYC-Rome, **AVX2 only**, our container on :8080). ⚠️ VM-2 cannot
reach VM-1's PUBLIC address at all — Rapid Compute's source-IP allowlist, the
2026-08-28 blocker, filters the path between their own two VMs. The private link
answers in 4.6 ms. `NOVIQ_REMOTE_URL` must be the private address; that the
backend sits on VM-2 is what gets it inside the allowlist.

**The `--no-default-features --features server` hypothesis HOLDS.** The no-`llm`
compile succeeded first try: 28 warnings, zero errors, 37 MB binary, no CMake, no
ggml, no CUDA. Plan B was never needed.

### Three defects the build found — two of them from one root cause

`.dockerignore` excludes `.cargo/`, and `[env]` in `.cargo/config.toml` is where
this repo keeps its **compile-time pins**. The build context silently discards
them.

**1. PostgreSQL drifted to 18.6 — and the fix did not work the first time.**
`postgresql_embedded` ("bundled") resolves the archive at COMPILE time from
`POSTGRESQL_VERSION`. Unpinned it takes the latest. `ENV POSTGRESQL_VERSION` in
the Dockerfile was **not enough**: the crate's build script emits no
`cargo:rerun-if-env-changed`, so against a warm `target/` cache mount cargo
called it fresh and the "rebuilt" binary came out BYTE-IDENTICAL — same size,
same mtime. The container then died in a restart loop:

    incompatible library "/data/pg/install/17.10.0/lib/vector.so": version mismatch

with an install dir NAMED `17.10.0` (that is what `engine.rs:25` asks for) whose
`postgres --version` said **18.6** and `PG_VERSION` said `18`. Fix: `rm -rf
target/release/{build,.fingerprint}/postgresql_*` before the build, plus a
build-time assertion that `PostgreSQL 18` is absent from the binary. Now:
install `17.10.0`, `PG_VERSION` 17, pgvector loads, 768-d halfvec HNSW created.

**2. No onnxruntime in the image at all.** `ort` is `load-dynamic`
(`Cargo.toml:160`) — it dlopen()s `libonnxruntime.so` at runtime and the build
emits none; the dev machine's `ORT_DYLIB_PATH` points at `.ort-runtime/`, which
is **not tracked in git**. The Dockerfile's `find -name libonnxruntime*` matched
nothing and `|| true` swallowed it, so `/opt/noviq/lib` shipped EMPTY and
fastembed would have died on the first embed — taking indexing AND retrieval with
it. Now fetches the official CPU build (1.20.1, tracking ort-sys' 1.20.0) and
asserts it landed.

⭐ **The lesson in both:** a `|| true` and an unchecked `find` turned a missing
artefact into a green build. Both are gone; the build now fails loudly.

**3. Transient rustup timeout.** `rust-toolchain.toml` pins channel `stable`, so
rustup re-syncs channel metadata at the START of the long cargo RUN — one
`static.rust-lang.org` timeout (os error 110) threw away the whole compile while
the host reached that URL in 0.47 s a minute later. Moved into its own cached
layer before `COPY . .`.

**`env.example` was wrong in three ways** (`62c9e653`), all now measured: port is
**8080** not 8000; the server **enforces `--api-key`** (a missing key is what the
admin UI reports as the misleading *"API service unavailable"*); the URL must be
private; model id is case-sensitive `Qwen3-8B`.

**On context, since it surprised the architect.** VM-1 reports `n_ctx` 16384
because `-c 32768 -np 2` splits the server's KV budget across 2 slots. Production
serves 10240 (`NOVIQ_VLLM_MAX_MODEL_LEN` 8192 + 2048 headroom) because KV for 16
concurrent sequences must fit beside AWQ weights in a **12 GB** A40-12Q; on a
62 GB CPU box that constraint does not exist. The server window is NOT the prompt
budget — Noviq builds prompts up to `NOVIQ_REMOTE_MAX_MODEL_LEN`
(`assistant/mod.rs:421`), kept at 8192 so CPU numbers stay comparable. The smoke
turns confirm `n_ctx: 8192` in the audit block.

**Files.** `deploy/docker/Dockerfile`, `deploy/docker/env.example`,
`deploy/docker/RAPID-COMPUTE-VMS.md` (new — full measured spec sheet for both
boxes).

**Corpus loaded, and the CPU indexing rate measured.** The 16-PDF Solid Waste set
(5.1 MB) indexed in **3 min 52 s** — 2,933 structural chunks parsed, 4,692
embedding vectors, all 16 classified `act`/`rules`, none needing OCR.

⚠️⚠️ **On CPU, indexing is EMBED-bound — the opposite of the GPU box.** Embedding
was **213 s of the 232 s wall clock (92%)**, at **22 chunks/s**. The previously
recorded "indexing is PARSE-bound, not embed-bound" is a GPU-box fact and does
NOT transfer: on CPU, estimate from the chunk count, not the page count. The full
304,617-chunk Sindh corpus would be ~3.8 h of pure embedding on one 32-vCPU box.

⚠️ Parsed chunks (2,933) vs embedding vectors (4,692) do not match, ratio varying
1.4x-2.3x per document. Flagged, not explained.

**⚠️ Follow-ups.**
- Only ONE account exists (`admin`, seeded from `.env`). IBA users do not exist
  here — they live in that cluster's DB, never copied, exactly like the corpus.
  Create testers via `POST /api/admin/users`, which returns a 6-char temp
  password; roles are `user` or `admin`.
- `psql` inside the container fails on a missing `libreadline.so.8` (slim runtime
  image). Use the API.
- The volume now holds a 17.10 cluster — do not restore an older snapshot over it.
- `NOVIQ_ADMIN_PASS` is set in `~/noviq/deploy/docker/.env` on VM-2 (value not
  recorded here), and travels over plain HTTP. Rotate it before anyone else
  uses the box.
- Production at IBA could drop the `llm` feature too (`vllm` is also `is_http()`),
  cutting CUDA/CMake fragility out of `deploy.sh`. Now proven, not theoretical.

## 2026-09-01 (deploy) — Docker: one image = backend + bundled PG + web client

**Why.** Rapid Compute spun up a SECOND VM on their own network so our backend can
sit beside the llama.cpp box and skip the source-IP allowlist that blocked us on
2026-08-28. Goal: deploy fast, then measure CPU inference. The IBA VM is
unreachable (VPN down), so this is a standalone stack on their network.

**Shape is forced by the code — ONE image, not a compose stack.** `db/pg/engine.rs`
embeds PostgreSQL *in our binary*: we unpack PG 17, copy in vendored pgvector, and
start a cluster on `listen_addresses=127.0.0.1`. There is no `DATABASE_URL` anywhere
in the tree — I grepped. App and DB are one process tree by construction, so a
`pgvector/pgvector:pg17` sidecar is not an option and no wiring is needed.

**The build shortcut (the reason this is a 20-minute job, not an hour).**
`query_router.rs:4194` gates generation on `engine_from_env().is_http()` and returns
from the HTTP path **before** touching `ModelSlot`. `EngineKind::Remote.is_http()` is
true; the in-process fallback needs `NOVIQ_VLLM_FALLBACK`, off by default. So with
`NOVIQ_INFER_ENGINE=remote` the `llm` feature is dead weight at runtime:

    cargo build --release --no-default-features --features server --bin noviq-server

That drops CMake, ggml, nvcc, and the `-C target-cpu=native` build-host==run-host
constraint that `deploy/deploy.sh:88` carries. `build.rs` already guards
`tauri_build::build()` behind `CARGO_FEATURE_DESKTOP`; reqwest is `rustls-tls`, so no
OpenSSL either. Verified statically only — **the first compile happens on their VM**.

**Cost, and the architect's ruling.** The `llm`-gated paths stub out: F006 LLM PDF
importer (`doc_ir`), one-ask, drafting. Architect 2026-09-01: *"these features are no
more required"* — permanently dropped, not just for this test. Code left compiled-out
and untouched; removal is a future cleanup.

**The one llm-gated helper that is NOT a named feature, checked.**
`assistant/n_ctx.rs::for_model` (reads the trained window off the GGUF) is
`#[cfg(feature = "llm")]`, and its stub returns `FALLBACK_TRAINED = 4096`. That would
have silently halved the prompt budget. It never fires: `assistant/mod.rs:420`
returns early for `is_http()` engines and reads `NOVIQ_REMOTE_MAX_MODEL_LEN` instead.
No quality regression. ⚠️ If the engine is ever switched back to llamacpp in a no-llm
build, the window silently becomes 4096.

**Files.** `deploy/docker/{Dockerfile,entrypoint.sh,env.example,README.md}`,
`.dockerignore`, `.gitattributes`.

**Gotchas encoded in the image so they cannot recur:**
- ⚠️⚠️ **PostgreSQL refuses to run as root.** Entrypoint chowns `/data` and drops to
  uid 10001 via `gosu`. Most likely first-run failure; pre-solved.
- ⚠️ **`NOVIQ_BIND` must be `0.0.0.0:8080`** in a container — the code default
  `127.0.0.1:8080` is unreachable from outside. Baked into the image ENV.
- ⚠️ **`embedder.rs::cache_dir()` has NO env override** — it walks up from the exe for
  an existing `.fastembed_cache`. Entrypoint symlinks `/opt/noviq/.fastembed_cache`
  onto the volume, or the 1.1 GB nomic-embed download repeats on every run.
- ⚠️ **The volume is not disposable.** The cluster password is stamped at initdb into
  `/data/pg/.pgpass` and re-read on every boot (`engine.rs:144`).
- ⚠️ **A stale volume overrides env** — engine/model/URL can be persisted in
  `db_config` by the admin dashboard and win over `NOVIQ_INFER_ENGINE`.

**Connecting to the LLM.** `NOVIQ_REMOTE_URL` is the **host root**; the client appends
`{api_prefix}{route}` = `/v1` + `/chat/completions` (`remote.rs:59,:110`). So
`http://<vm1-private-ip>:8000`, never with `/v1` on the end. Pre-flight from VM-2:
`curl http://<vm1-ip>:8000/v1/models`. ⚠️ llama.cpp binds localhost unless started
with `--host 0.0.0.0` — the same class of bug as `NOVIQ_BIND`.

**Follow-up (not done).** Production at IBA runs `NOVIQ_INFER_ENGINE=vllm`, which is
also `is_http()` — so the production build could drop the `llm` feature too, cutting
deploy time and removing the CUDA/CMake fragility from `deploy.sh`. Worth doing once
the Docker path is proven.

**Not done / next session:** the image has never been built. `docker build
--target builder` first to isolate the one unproven step. Plan B on failure:
`--features "llm,server"` plus `cmake` + `libclang-dev` in the builder stage — never
add `cuda`, it is a CPU box. Corpus starts EMPTY (IBA unreachable); seed a small set.

## 2026-08-30 (citations, 4) — "Open document" had the SAME gap, in a second place

Architect: *"unable to open the document"*. My previous entry fixed
`openOriginal` in `AnswerBody` and missed that **`ChunkViewer` has its own
"Open document ↗" button in the drawer header** calling the same
`/sources/{id}/file` route with no project. Same 404, one component over.

Fixed there too (query string, `project_id`, snake). Swept every caller:
`/sources/{id}/file` has exactly two non-admin call sites, both now scoped;
everything else under `/admin/sources/...` uses admin scope, not project scope.

**`ChunkViewer` mount points, all four checked:** `AnswerBody` ✓ and
`ChatPage` ✓ pass `projectId`; `IndexedFolders` is `audience: "admin"`;
`SearchPage` is `audience: "user"` but sits on the GLOBAL `/search` route, where
`visible_source_ids` already excludes project documents — so a project document
cannot surface there to be opened. Left alone deliberately.

⚠️ **Lesson: one fix per call site is not a fix.** The first pass patched the
path I had just read. The route had a second caller in a component I had already
edited that day, and only the architect trying it found it. When a scope
parameter is missing, grep every caller of the ROUTE before claiming it is done.

## 2026-08-30 (citations, 3) — opening a citation NEVER worked inside a project

Found while verifying the clickable-Sources fix on the live build: the new button
opened the drawer and the drawer said **"Could not load chunks: document not
found"**. Clicking an inline `[n]` marker on another answer failed **identically**
— so this was not the new code. Citation click-through has been broken for
**every project document** since F027.

**Cause.** `source_chunks` resolves visibility through
`scope_for(&st, &user.id, req.project_id, false)` and project scope is
**EXCLUSIVE**. `ChunkViewer` never sent `projectId`, so the scope fell back to the
global corpus — which a project document is deliberately not part of —
`visible_source_ids` did not contain the id, and the route returned its
indistinguishable-from-absent 404. The server has accepted `projectId` (aliasing
`project_id`) since F027; **the client simply never sent it.**

⭐ The server-side comment on `SourceChunksReq.project_id` warns at length that a
key mismatch "fails SILENTLY in the worst possible direction". The failure that
actually happened was the mirror image: sending **nothing** fails silently in the
*safe* direction — closed, 404, feature dead, and no error anywhere that
names the cause.

**Fix.** `projectId` threaded end to end: `ChatPage` → `AnswerBody` →
`ChunkViewer` (POST body, camelCase per `rename_all`), and `ChatPage` → its
own Sources `ChunkViewer`. `openOriginal` ("Open document ↗") had the same
gap and is fixed too — `source_file` is a GET, so the project goes in the
**query string as `project_id`** (snake, per `ProjectQuery`), not camelCase.

⚠️ Both spellings appear in one feature and neither is wrong: `projectId` in JSON
bodies, `project_id` in query strings. Check the struct before adding a third
call site.

▶ **Not verified for the corpus (non-project) path** — that always sent no
project and was always correct, so it should be unaffected, but it is worth one
click to confirm.

## 2026-08-30 (citations, 2) — the Sources list is clickable; it never was

Architect, on a live answer: *"there is no clickable citation in the answer, as it
return 3 to 4 citations in the end but there is no citation so how we can go to
the document then?"*

**He was right, and the cause was not what it looked like.** The only
click-through in the main chat was the inline `[n]` marker: `AnswerBody`
rewrites it to `<sup class="nq-cite nq-cite-open">` and opens `ChunkViewer` on
click. The **"Sources" block under the answer was plain `<li>`/`<span>` text** —
no button, no handler, confirmed in the DOM (elements come back as `listitem`).

So the chain was: model emits no `[n]` → nothing in the prose is clickable →
**and the Sources list was never clickable either** → the answer had no route to
the document at all. Exactly the `Model cited: NO` case from the entry above.
`SharedChatPage.tsx` had made its citations `<button onClick={openCitation}>`
long ago; the main chat never did.

**Fix (`src/pages/ChatPage.tsx`).** Each Sources row is a `<button>` that opens
`ChunkViewer` at the cited chunk, via a page-level `openSource` signal (the
viewer inside `AnswerBody` is scoped to that component, and Sources renders
after an unrelated block, so lifting the list into `AnswerBody` would have
reordered the answer). Gated on `chunk_id && source_id` — the same condition
`AnswerBody` uses, so an unopenable row stays plain text instead of offering a
button that goes nowhere. `audience: "user"`, never `"admin"`.

⚠️ **This decouples verification from whether the model remembered to write
`[3]`.** That matters more than it sounds: an answer can be entirely correct and
still leave the reader stranded.

**Also observed, not fixed.** On the fines question the answer asserted SEPA Act
2014 S. 22(1) with figures, and **SEPA 2014 was not in the Sources at all** (all
three rows were SWM Act 2021). The claim checks out against the PDF, but the
citation set does not cover every instrument the answer names. Worth a look at
how the fallback picks its top-3.

## 2026-08-30 (citations) — an uncited answer no longer wears "CONFIDENCE: HIGH"

Architect, on a live answer: *"and there are no citation inside the answer why?"*

**What the trace actually said** (`8962bc98`): STEP 19 `Citations found: 0`,
`Uncited factual sentences: 6`, `Score 0.00/1.00`, `Fallback triggered: true`;
STEP 21 `Model cited: NO — top-3 by rank, supports no specific claim`,
`Citations shipped: 3`. The model emitted **no `[N]` markers at all**. The three
chips under the answer were the top-3 retrieved chunks BY RANK, attached so the
passages are not lost. The UI badged that `CITED 3 TIMES · CONFIDENCE: HIGH`.

⚠️ **The server knew and could not tell us.** `query_router` builds a quality
notice — "This answer could not be verified against a specific source" — but
`services/assistant::TurnResponse` has **no `quality_notice` field**, so it is
dropped between the router and the client. Same shape as `945fccce`: a response
type that never grew the field someone added upstream.

**The fix, frontend-only for now (`src/pages/ChatPage.tsx`).** New `modelCited()`
re-derives the fact the way the server does — indexed `[N]` markers in the prose.
When citations exist but the answer cites none: the chip reads "N related
passages" instead of "Cited N times", Confidence reads **Unverified** in amber,
and an amber notice says the documents are the closest matches retrieved, not
references the answer stands on.

**Why not plumb the notice through properly?** No local Rust toolchain and the
VPN is down, so a `TurnResponse` change could not be compile-verified before the
31 Aug MD meeting. `modelCited` can only UNDER-report verification (the server
also accepts a matched legacy ref) — it errs towards "check this", never towards
unearned confidence.

**▶ Follow-up (do this properly).** Add `quality_notice` (or at minimum
`citations_verified: bool`) to `services/assistant::TurnResponse`, populate it
from `query_router`'s `effective_notice`, and render the server's own words.
Then `modelCited` becomes a fallback, not the source of truth. Also consider
`ECHO_CITATION_STRICT=1`, which makes "no citations" honest at the source.

⚠️ **Demo consequence:** with this live, an answer with no inline markers shows
an amber "not cited" banner. Verify which demo answers carry markers before
deploying ahead of a presentation.

## 2026-08-30 (F020) — confidential masking is now OPT-IN, and off by default

Architect, watching a live demo query: *"this masking is by default on, i want it
by default off. so if anyone wants this feature so he can on it."*

**Why it had to change.** Masking shipped on-for-everyone, and `detectNames` runs
deliberately high-recall — the 2026-07-12 entry settled that "a missed name is
worse than an over-mask". That trade is right *once masking is on*; on by default
it charged every user for it. On ordinary legal text it misfires badly: typing
*"Under the Sindh Solid Waste Management Act 2021…"* flagged **Solid Waste
Management** as a NAME, and *"Town Municipal Corporations"* as another — the
composer read "2 will be masked", and sending it would have redacted the statute
out of the question. An officer who did not notice the tray would get an answer to
a question they never asked.

**The change (`src/components/ConfidentialComposer.tsx`).**
- `maskingOn` signal, default **false**, persisted at `localStorage["noviq.masking.on"]`
  (read + write both in try/catch — a blocked store must not break the composer).
- **One gate**: `activeSpans` returns `[]` when off. The overlay highlights, the
  tray chips and what `onRanges` hands the parent to mask on submit are all
  derived from it, so nothing can leak past. `chips` is gated too, for the count.
- The tray label **is** the switch (`aria-pressed`), reading "Masking off" /
  "Masking on". The tray still always renders — that was the 2026-07-04 fix and it
  still holds: masking must be reachable from the first keystroke.
- `markSelection` turns masking **on** rather than being silently swallowed by the
  gate — marking text by hand IS the request to mask.

**Cross-cutting.** Server-side masking is unaffected; the label→value map still
never leaves the browser (2026-07-03). Existing users start OFF — the preference
key is new, so an absent key reads false. `ChatPage`'s `maskRanges` simply
receives an empty array, so no call site changed.

**Follow-up.** `detectNames` flagging two-to-three-word Title Case institution
names ("Solid Waste Management", "Municipal Corporations") is still wrong when
masking IS on. A legal-entity blocklist, or requiring a person-name shape, would
cut the false positives that made the default untenable.

## 2026-08-29 (F027 UI) — a document you added was there; the rail just never asked again

Architect, on the live build: *"during indexing and adding documents, it never
shows document we need to refresh the screen, and after that again it is showing
indexing only after that it needs to again reload the page."*

**Two separate misses, both the same shape — nobody re-read the server.**

**1. The upload path never refreshed the store.** `AddProjectDocuments` has two
tabs. "My documents" calls `addDocuments()`, which calls `openProject()` for you,
so that path always worked. **"Upload new" does not go through it** — the server
attaches the file itself during upload — so nothing put the new rows into
`documents()` and the rail stayed empty. ⭐ The document was in the project the
whole time; only the client's copy was stale. `onUpload` now awaits
`openProject()` before closing.

⚠️ This is the THIRD bug on this exact path (`945fccce` dropped `attached` in
the transport; before that the ids were re-derived by name from a folder listing
a project document is designed not to appear in). **Two tabs doing the same job
through different code is what keeps producing them** — worth collapsing.

**2. Nothing ever moved a document off "indexing…".** Indexing runs in the
background and the server pushes nothing. `openProject` was called once, when the
document was added, so the pill sat at "indexing…" for ever; reloading the page
was the only way to see a document become searchable. New `createEffect` in
`ChatPage` polls `openProject` while any document is `pending`.

⭐⭐ **The trap in writing that poll**: the effect must not read
`projectDocuments()` in its own body. Refreshing sets that signal, which would
re-run the effect, which would tear down and rebuild the interval — a poll that
churns a timer instead of waiting. The interval is created ONCE per project, and
the pending check happens inside the timer callback, which is not a tracked
scope. Backs off from 4s to 20s after a minute so a document stuck pending (a
parse that failed without reporting) does not query fifteen times a minute for
the rest of the session.

**Verified**: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vite build` clean (`index-BLCDj8Yy.js`).

## 2026-08-29 (F027 UI) — a project is a chat, and the overview page is gone

**Architect's call**, after reviewing an interface proposal: naming a project
should land you in its chat, not on a page in between.

### What was wrong

Creating a project navigated to `/projects/:id`, an overview page holding four
things — the document list, the chat list, Share, and per-document Remove. On a
brand-new project the first three are **empty**, so the screen existed only to be
clicked through. Two of them were already duplicated: the chat rail lists the
project's chats, and the right rail lists its documents.

⭐ **A screen whose every section is empty on first use is not a destination.**

### The flow now

`ProjectsPage` → chat, both on create and on clicking a row, via a new
`enterProject()` in the store: open the project, return its most recent chat, or
start the first one. ⚠️ Creating a chat there is a side effect of **entering**,
which the officer asked for — it must never become a side effect of deleting one,
the bug fixed in `0e130b3` where a deleted chat appeared to come back.

`ProjectPage.tsx` and the `/projects/:id` route are **deleted**. Everything it
owned moved into the chat screen:

- **Documents** → the right rail (`ProjectDocuments`), which gains a name filter,
  an "Add documents" button pinned to its footer, and a per-row remove revealed
  on hover.
- **Rename / Share / Delete** → a kebab menu beside the project name in the left
  rail, with the FR-024 sharing disclosure carried over **verbatim** — it is a
  requirement, not UI polish.
- **The add-documents dialog** → hosted by `ChatPage`, opened from the rail footer
  or the empty-state call to action. `AddProjectDocuments` itself is unchanged.

### Three things that had to be got right

1. ⚠️ **The remove button is not inside the `<label>`.** A row was one big label
   wrapping checkbox and name; a button added inside it is still part of the
   label, so clicking remove would ALSO toggle the tick on the way out —
   deleting a document and silently changing the next question's scope at once.
   The row is now a div, with the label wrapping only the checkbox and name.
2. **A removed id must leave the selection.** `ProjectDocuments` decides "all are
   selected" by comparing `selected.length` to the ready count. A stale id left
   behind makes that comparison never match again, so "Select all" sits there
   with nothing left to select. `onRemoveProjectDocument` prunes it, through a
   new named `applyProjectSelection()` that both call sites share.
3. **The rail header had no number.** `RepositoryStats` is fed by `DocumentTree`,
   which project mode does not render — so the header read "Documents" and
   nothing else. New `ProjectDocStats` reports "12 documents", adding
   "· 2 indexing" only while something actually is (FR-008); `RailStats` picks
   between the two so they cannot drift.

Deleting the last chat in a project now falls back to `/projects` rather than the
retired overview page. A project with no documents gets a call to action where
the three example questions used to be — all three would have come back empty.

**Server: nothing.** No endpoint, no migration. Retrieval scope still comes from
`conversation_id` via `project_chat` (FR-038, ADR-0028).

**Verified**: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vite build` clean (`index-Bh5_4Psg.js`).
⚠️ Not yet exercised in a browser — behaviour unconfirmed.

## 2026-08-29 — project upload reported a false failure: the transport dropped `attached`

**Symptom.** Creating a project, then adding a document to it, ended with
"Uploaded, but no document was indexed." — although the upload had fully
succeeded and the document was in the project.

**Why.** `AddProjectDocuments.tsx:79` shows that message when the server reports
no rejections AND `outcome.attached` is empty. The server was doing its part:
`src-tauri/src/api/uploads.rs:572-637` waits for the source rows to register (up
to 10 s), writes `project_source`, sets `sources.project_id`, and returns the ids
in `UploadOutcome.attached` (`uploads.rs:160`). The field was destroyed in
transit. `uploadDocuments` (`src/api/transport.ts`) parsed the body into
`Partial<UploadOutcome>` and then rebuilt a **new** object naming only two
fields:

    return { folder: body.folder ?? null, rejected: body.rejected ?? [] };

so `attached` was always `undefined` at the call site.

**⚠️ Two other features were dead from the same line** and nobody had connected
them to it: `IndexedFolders.tsx:565,569` reads `multi_instrument` and
`similar_existing` off the same response. The split-instrument prompt and the
near-duplicate warning have therefore never fired through this path.

**Fix.** `src/api/transport.ts` — copy the whole outcome through (`attached`,
`multi_instrument`, `similar_existing` with `[]` defaults) instead of
whitelisting two fields. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

**⭐⭐ The lesson.** Two earlier fixes in this exact area were both correct and
both missed it: 2026-08-15 fixed the SERVER's timing (it now waits for the rows),
and an earlier client fix stopped re-deriving ids from folder listings. The fault
sat one layer below either — a hand-written DTO mapper that whitelists fields
**silently drops every field added after it was written**, and TypeScript cannot
catch it because the dropped members are all optional. ▶ Other transports in
`src/api/transport.ts` rebuild responses the same way and may hide the same bug.

**Not yet verified in behaviour** — the VM was unreachable this session (VPN
gateway down), so this has only been typechecked. Re-run a real project upload
after the next frontend deploy.

## 2026-08-26 — scoping tick finished; the latency register found stale; Sindh pilot planned

**UI (shipped).** `DocumentTree.tsx` — the architect's outstanding request from
2026-08-25 ("smaller tick, tighter to the arrow") is applied. My previous attempt
failed its assertion and shipped nothing, so this closes it.
- `Box` sizes down a step: group 14px -> **12px**, document 12px -> **10px**; the
  check mark and the indeterminate dash scale with them. ⚠️ **The ratio between
  the two levels is deliberately preserved** — shrinking only the leaf would
  collapse the size cue that tells a document from a department, which is the
  whole reason the two sizes exist (see the `Box` doc comment).
- The group tick button gains `-ml-1`, pulling it back against the row's
  `gap-1.5` so tick and arrow sit ~2px apart and read as ONE cluster at the right
  edge. At the full gap the tick floated free and looked like it belonged to the
  next row down.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. No component tests exist for this file.

**⚠️⚠️ The limitations register's "latency 90–120 s" is STALE and was about to
drive a plan.** The figure traces to the 2026-08-07 notes — **before** the
2026-08-12 AWQ->Marlin fix. Measured after it: production-shaped query (4.4k
prompt, 479 out) **36.2 s -> 7.7 s**, decode 13.75 -> 81.3 tok/s (169–181 with
n-gram speculation), and F016 **SC-002 (p95 <= 10 s) PASSES** single-stream.
- The architect caught this mid-task. Two downstream errors had already been
  made from it: a session plan cut from 30 queries to 22, and a hardware sizing
  of five GPUs where one suffices.
- ⚠️ Also mis-cited from the same session: **"8 concurrent streams held 13.0
  tok/s each"** is the BROKEN-kernel measurement, quoted on 2026-08-12 to
  *disprove* GPU saturation. Post-fix the 8-user aggregate is **596.8 tok/s** and
  the slowest of eight concurrent requests finishes in **4.02 s**.
- MEMORY.md's open-bugs line has been annotated rather than deleted, so the
  stale figure cannot be re-quoted innocently.

**⭐⭐ The serving ceiling is VRAM, not compute — corrects the July analysis.**
Eight concurrent requests with the slowest at 4 s means the card is nowhere near
compute-bound. What limits concurrency is the **KV cache**: weights ~6 GB, the
rest becomes cache, and cache / prompt-window = requests in flight. The A40-12Q
holds **13,968 cache tokens against an 8,192 window = 1.7 concurrent**.
- Scaling from that measured anchor: a 24 GB card ~5.3 in flight (~2,475
  answers/hr), a 48 GB card ~12 (~5,600/hr).
- **One 24 GB card covers all fifteen departments at peak (1,126 answers/hr).**
  The current A40 slice does NOT (795/hr) — and the reason is cache room, not
  speed. Buy VRAM, not FLOPs.
- Break-even vs cloud: owning pays back in 13 months against a 24/7 rented card
  and **never** against a business-hours schedule. So on-prem is a sovereignty
  decision, not a cost one; the whole 15-department inference bill is $154/mo
  scheduled or ~$250/mo owned.

**⚠️ The vGPU "expiry" is a ROLLING LEASE, not a deadline.** The 2026-08-13
inventory recorded `2026-09-10` and it was written up as a blocking gate. Re-read
live on 2026-08-26 it says **`2026-09-24`** — +14 days in 13. The guest driver
auto-renews a ~28-day client lease from the NVIDIA License System; there is
nothing for us to renew and no September cliff. The entitlement behind it lives
on the HOST licence server (the provider's) and is invisible from inside the
guest, so **the signal to watch is whether the date is still moving**, never the
date. Check:
`ssh appadmin@10.150.0.100 "nvidia-smi -q | sed -n '/vGPU Software Licensed Product/,/^$/p'"`

**Planning artefacts (no code).** Two published documents for the 15-department
Government of Sindh pilot, split after the architect noted one document was doing
two jobs: **Volume 1 Field Manual** (process) and **Volume 2 Pilot Readiness**
(engineering). Grounded in web research rather than recall — Sindh Government
Rules of Business 1986, OECD *Generative AI Experimentation in Government* 2026,
the UK *People Factor* study, and the Australian DTA Copilot trial. Key finding
for engineering: two metrics we cannot currently produce — **explainability rate**
(share of answers carrying a traceable citation) and **automation-bias rate**
(marked correct with no citation opened) — are the two a reviewing committee will
ask about first. Both are B3/B5 work in Volume 2.

**▶ Unchanged and still open: G2, the 342 unretrievable chunks.** It remains the
only genuine blocker on the pilot and is a P1 by any UAT reading.

## 2026-08-25 (later) — oversize-chunk repair, responsive fit, trial switched on

**Trial is LIVE.** `NOVIQ_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` set on the VM and the consent screen
is **In production**, so anyone with a Google account can start a trial.
`/api/auth/google` went 503 → 401-on-a-fake-token, which is the correct
behaviour. Demo corpus seeded: 9 statutes, 3,199 chunks.

**⚠️ A frontend-only deploy does NOT restart the backend.** `deploy.sh` reports
`frontend=1 backend=0` and skips the restart, so a new `.env` value sits unread.
Verify with `tr '␀' '
' < /proc/$(systemctl show noviq-server -p MainPID
--value)/environ` — checking the FILE proves nothing.

**⚠️ Privacy/Terms needed REAL URLs.** They were view state, so `/privacy`
served the landing page — invisible to Google, which fetches those URLs to
publish a consent screen. Then, once fixed for signed-out visitors, `/privacy`
rendered BLANK for signed-in ones (a session routes to the app router, which had
no such route). Now mounted in both places.

**The oversize-chunk bug, measured properly**: 366 chunks over the 512-token cap
across **349 documents** (337 pdf + 12 xlsx). ⚠️ **341 of those documents have
exactly ONE bad chunk** — the signature of the whole body becoming a single row,
not of occasional bad chunks among good ones. 23 chunks exceed 4,000 tokens and
are effectively unretrievable; the worst was 125,405 (the entire Sindh Water
Management Ordinance), now repaired.

**`POST /api/admin/resplit_oversize`** repairs them in place instead of
re-indexing: 342 of 367 repairable, writing ~1,700 rows rather than rewriting
32,775. ⚠️ Dry run by default. 20 chunks are SKIPPED because another chunk is
their child (`parent_chunk_id` is NO ACTION) and 5 gain nothing from splitting.
- ⚠️ **The real run must be DETACHED.** The first attempt repaired one chunk then
  stopped: the handler ran inline, so navigating the browser tab aborted the
  fetch and axum cancelled it, leaving a document holding its old oversize chunk
  plus 166 unembedded replacements. Reverted cleanly — because embedding happens
  BEFORE the delete, a failure never leaves a hole. `query.rs` already carried
  this lesson for chat turns.

**Responsive**: the empty chat had a scrollbar before any question — at 1024px
the pane is 464px and the hero needed 594px. ⚠️ Fit is a question about window
HEIGHT, so a `sm:`/`lg:` ladder cannot answer it; a short 1440px window
overflowed exactly like a 768px one. The hero now sizes in `clamp(min,vh,max)`.
Verified across 16 viewports (360x640 → 1920x1080): no vertical scroll on an
empty chat, no horizontal overflow, all cards and the composer visible.

**⚠️ I restarted the live server as a "permissions test"**, which killed the
in-flight re-index sweep at 332 documents remaining. Nothing was stranded, but
`sudo -n systemctl restart` is not a test. Make every restart-requiring change
first, and start long jobs LAST.

▶ Open: run the repair (342 chunks); the 20 child-blocked and 12 xlsx chunks
need another path; the re-index sweep is stopped at 332 docs and is largely
unnecessary if the repair succeeds.

## 2026-08-25 — public landing page, quote pipeline, and the free trial

Three features in one day, all live on noviq.pk. The landing page and quote
inbox are described in the entry below this one; this covers the **free trial**
(migrations 028 + 029) and the decisions inside it that are easy to get wrong.

**Symptom/why**: the site had no way for an organisation to reach us and no way
for anyone to see the product without an account being issued by hand.

**Fix**:
- **Migration 028 `quote_request`** — the first table in this system written by
  an UNAUTHENTICATED caller. Honeypot field, per-IP and global hourly limits,
  length bounds at API *and* schema, and its payload is never interpolated
  anywhere that executes. Admin inbox at `Admin → Inbox`; notification email
  over ZeptoMail's HTTPS API (no new crate), env-gated and fire-and-forget.
- **Migration 029 — the free trial.** A trial user is an ordinary `users` row
  with `role='trial'`, so sessions, `AuthUser`, the audit trail and every
  ownership check work unchanged. Google Identity Services in the browser;
  `POST /api/auth/google` verifies the ID token at Google's `tokeninfo`.

**Cross-cutting impact / follow-ups**:
- ⚠️⚠️ **`role != 'admin'` no longer means "a real customer".** Every existing
  role test that meant "not an admin, therefore a paying user" is now wrong for
  trial sessions. The surface gate is ONE allow-list in `require_auth`, so a
  newly added route is refused for trial users until someone opts it in — the
  safe direction to fail. Hiding a tab in the UI is presentation, never a gate.
- ⚠️⚠️ **`RequestScope.trial` FAILS CLOSED and must stay that way.** It is
  checked FIRST in `visible_source_ids` and returns totally. An empty
  `demo_source` means "reaches nothing", never "unrestricted" — everywhere else
  in retrieval an absent scope means *everything*. `is_unrestricted()` now tests
  `!trial`; without that a trial request fell into the everything-indexed branch
  and would have published all 3,931 Government of Sindh documents to anyone
  with a Google account. It is set from the SESSION role, never the request
  body: a client-settable value could only ever be set to `false`.
- ⚠️ **`tokeninfo` proves signature and expiry, NOT audience.** Every Google ID
  token in the world comes back "valid" from it. The `aud == our client id`
  check is what makes `/api/auth/google` authentication rather than a way for
  anyone holding any Google token to become a Noviq user. Identity is `sub`,
  never the email (an email can be reassigned inside a Workspace domain).
- ⚠️ The daily quota is a SINGLE conditional `UPDATE` (`trial::consume`), so two
  turns racing for the last question cannot both win, and it is spent on
  **asking** — before the audit row, the spawn and the generation permit. A
  refused turn must not occupy the single-permit gate, and aborting the stream
  must not recover a question. Days elapsed are counted on the UTC **calendar**;
  `3 * 86_400_000` would cost someone signing up at 23:50 a day ten minutes on.
- ⚠️ Sessions are minted in exactly ONE place — `auth::issue_session`, extracted
  from `login` and shared with Google sign-in. A second copy would be a second
  place to get token lifetime, hashing or storage wrong.
- ⚠️ **Privacy/terms pages are load-bearing**: Google will not publish an OAuth
  consent screen out of Testing without both URLs. They also now disclose that
  trial contact details are used to follow up about the product — that was added
  when the architect asked to collect sign-ups for sales, because the original
  wording promised a narrower use and would otherwise have become untrue.
- ▶ **Two things are needed before sign-in works**: `NOVIQ_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` in
  the VM `.env` (the endpoint refuses cleanly with `google_disabled` until then),
  and either test users added in Google Cloud or the consent screen published.
- ▶ **`demo_source` is EMPTY.** Until documents are put in it, a trial user
  retrieves nothing and every answer is a refusal. Choosing those documents is
  outstanding.
- ▶ `NOVIQ_MAIL_*` unset, so quote notifications are stored but not emailed.

**Cross-cutting impact / follow-ups**:

## 2026-08-23 — Zoho Mail live on noviq.pk: MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC published and verified (F028 T019–T026)

**Symptom/why**: F028's whole US2 (official mail on `noviq.pk`) had been stalled since
2026-08-20. The 2026-08-21 session confirmed 4 of 4 mail records missing at the
*authoritative* nameserver and correctly diagnosed it as "never entered, not propagation" —
but the entry itself was blocked: Zoho needed an account, and account creation with a
password sign-in is not something the agent may do. The architect signed into Zoho, which
unblocked the rest.

**Fix**: Completed T019–T025 in-browser and verified T026.
- **Zoho org** `Noviq` on the **Forever Free** plan. ⚠ The console hard-gates on a plan
  chooser that only offers paid tiers ("Buy now" / card-backed trial); the free plan is
  reachable *only* via `https://mailadmin.zoho.com/hosting?plan=free`. Free = 1 domain,
  5 users, 5 GB/user, and **no IMAP/POP/ActiveSync** (webmail only — no Outlook/Thunderbird).
- Data centre resolved to **zoho.com (US)** → `mx.zoho.com` 10 / `mx2` 20 / `mx3` 50.
- Records added in Cloudflare (`specs/028-noviq-pk-cutover/quickstart.md` Steps 4–5), all
  **DNS only**: verification TXT `zoho-verification=zb38175890.zmverify.zoho.com`;
  the 3 MX; SPF `v=spf1 include:zohomail.com -all`; DKIM at `zoho._domainkey` (2048-bit);
  DMARC `_dmarc` = `v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@noviq.pk`.
- `admin@noviq.pk` is Super Administrator; `dmarc@noviq.pk` added as an **alias** on it so
  the `rua=` address exists without consuming one of the 5 free seats.
- `scripts/verify-mail-dns.sh` line 16: default DKIM selector **`zmail` → `zoho`**.

**Cross-cutting impact / follow-ups**:
- ⚠️⚠️ **The checker was wrong, not the DNS.** The first `verify-mail-dns.sh` run reported
  `FAIL DKIM` — it hardcoded Zoho's older `zmail` selector while the console had generated
  `zoho`. A stale assertion in a verification script reads exactly like a real failure;
  the record was correct the whole time. Default corrected, still overridable as arg 2.
- ⚠️ **SPF: spec overrides vendor.** Zoho's console recommends `~all` (softfail); T023
  specifies `-all` (hardfail) and that is what was published — Zoho accepted it. This is
  only safe while **Zoho is the sole sender** for `@noviq.pk`. If the VM, ZeptoMail, or any
  SaaS is ever made to send as the domain, `-all` will hard-reject it. Confirmed **exactly
  one** SPF record at the apex (a second silently invalidates both).
- ⚠️ **Zoho's DMARC tab is a generator, not a control.** It builds a suggested string; the
  live policy is the Cloudflare TXT record, which is what receivers actually read. Editing
  the Zoho page changes nothing on the internet.
- ⚠️ Cloudflare's "Add record" dialog is **type-first and coordinate-hostile**: changing the
  type re-lays out the form, so a click captured from a screenshot one step earlier can land
  on the wrong option (HTTPS instead of MX) or fall through and dismiss the dialog. Two
  records were silently not saved this way. Set the type via the combobox + `Enter`, then
  re-screenshot before touching any other field, and confirm the record count went up.
- ⚠️ The DKIM public key trips the content filter (`[BLOCKED: Cookie/query string data]`),
  so it cannot be read into context. Route it **page copy button → clipboard → paste**, and
  verify by *shape* (length, prefix, terminator, whitespace count) rather than by value.
- ▶ **T027/T028 remain**: send from `@noviq.pk` to external Gmail *and* Outlook and confirm
  inbox placement with passing auth, plus one inbound delivery. These need a human at a
  mailbox — and note the free plan is webmail-only, so test at `mail.zoho.com`.
- ▶ **T029**: leave DMARC at `p=none` for ~2 weeks, read the aggregate reports arriving at
  `dmarc@noviq.pk`, and only then consider `p=quarantine`.
- F028 now **33 done / 40**.

## 2026-08-21 — `release` is auto-deployed; VM checkout reconciled

**⚠️ Read this before deploying anything.** `noviq-deploy.timer` on the VM is **active and
fires every ~2 minutes**, and `/opt/noviq/deploy.sh` runs **`git reset --hard
origin/release`**. That *discards* uncommitted work rather than refusing to proceed.

Consequence discovered this session: the landing page had been living on
`/opt/noviq/echoAI` as **uncommitted working-tree edits** (put there by the scp +
build-on-VM recipe). Any unrelated push to `release` would have silently destroyed it —
the hazard was never a merge conflict, it was a silent `reset --hard`.

**Reconcile performed** (VM now at `7a53f5e`, tracked tree clean):
1. md5'd all 20 files on both ends — identical, so nothing on the VM was unique.
2. Confirmed `release` was an **ancestor** of the branch (fast-forward; nothing lost) and
   that the branch touched **no `src-tauri/`** (so it could only be a frontend deploy).
3. `git push origin 028-noviq-pk-cutover:release`; the timer deployed it,
   `frontend=1 backend=0`; verified the live bundle hash matched the local build.

**Deploy loop from now on**: commit → `git push origin <branch>:release` → wait ~2 min →
verify the live bundle hash. The scp-and-build-on-VM recipe still works but is no longer
necessary, and it is what created the dirty tree in the first place.

## 2026-08-21 — noviq.pk cut over to a named tunnel (F028)

The public entry point moved from a Cloudflare **quick tunnel** (random four-word
hostname, regenerated on every restart) to a **named tunnel** on the organisation's
own domain. `https://noviq.pk` and `https://www.noviq.pk` are now permanent addresses.

### What changed on the VM

- `/etc/systemd/system/cloudflared.service` — `ExecStart` went from
  `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8080` to
  `cloudflared tunnel --no-autoupdate run --token ${TUNNEL_TOKEN}`, with
  `EnvironmentFile=/etc/noviq/cloudflared.env`. The previous unit is preserved at
  `/etc/systemd/system/cloudflared-quick.service.bak` for rollback (procedure in
  `~/ROLLBACK-cloudflared.md` on the VM, deliberately not only in the repo — an
  operator on a box with the app down cannot read a repo file).
- `/etc/noviq/cloudflared.env` — `root:root 0600`. The token is **never** inlined into
  `ExecStart`, where `systemctl cat` and `ps` would expose it.
- `noviq-url-watch.service` — **stopped and disabled**. Its grep only ever matched
  `trycloudflare.com`, so after cutover it could never match and would have pinned a
  dead address indefinitely *without erroring*.
- `/opt/noviq/current-url.txt` — now `https://noviq.pk`.

### The delegation was never the blocker anyone thought it was

Six days had been spent "waiting on propagation" for a PKNIC nameserver change that
**had never been entered**. ⭐⭐⭐ **Verify a change was actually made before waiting
on it.** Once entered, the delegation published in ~3 hours.

A second unlisted prerequisite surfaced during the cutover: Zero Trust → Tunnels is
unreachable until **Zero Trust is activated on the account**, and activating even the
$0 "Free" tier routes through a billing checkout that demands a card or PayPal. The
spec's quickstart assumed Tunnels was directly reachable. Recorded as T008a.

### ⚠️⚠️ Three silent corruptions while moving the token through PowerShell

The connector token was piped `Get-Clipboard` → `ssh` stdin so it never entered a
transcript. Every one of the following produced a plausible-looking file that would
have failed at connect time with a misleading error:

1. **PowerShell 5.1 prepends a UTF-8 BOM** when piping to a native command. Fix: set
   **both** `$OutputEncoding` and `[Console]::OutputEncoding` to
   `New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding $false`.
2. **PowerShell eats backslashes** in native-command arguments. `printf "...
"`
   emitted a literal `n` onto the **end of the token**, and a `tr -d "
"` filter
   stripped the *letters* `r` and `n` instead of CR/LF — which also broke sudo by
   leaving a 9-character password. Fix: `echo` for the newline, `tr -dc '[:print:]'`
   for the filter.
3. `cut -d" "` and `awk '{...}'` lose their quoting across the same boundary. Stage a
   script on the VM and run it there instead.

⭐⭐⭐ **Verify a secret by hash on both ends.** A byte count alone would have passed
case 1. `sha256` matched at `b816e4ea…` only after all three were fixed.

### Verified by behaviour, not by logs

Three `systemctl restart cloudflared` cycles **and a full host reboot**
(boot id `b98c931e…` → `e1880eac…`). Afterwards `https://noviq.pk`,
`https://www.noviq.pk` and `/api/health` all returned **200** with no DNS or config
change — which is the entire point of a named tunnel over a quick one. Certificate is
`CN=noviq.pk` (Google Trust Services, valid to 2026-11-18).

⭐⭐ **Postgres survives reboot because `noviq-server` owns it.** The embedded
postmaster sits inside `noviq-server.service`'s cgroup (`postgresql_embedded`). There
is **no postgres systemd unit and no crontab entry**, and its parent shows as `init`,
which makes it look unmanaged — this was checked *before* rebooting, not after.
⚠️ Its port drifted **37855 → 33493** across the reboot; never hardcode it.

⚠️ `cloudflared` settled at **3 of 4 edge connections**. `connIndex=2` flapped with
`control stream encountered a failure` against edge ip `198.41.192.167` for ~2 minutes
after boot, then went quiet. Serving is unaffected; redundancy is reduced. Re-check on
the next restart.

⚠️ **The old `trycloudflare.com` address is dead** and its watcher is disabled. Anything
still circulating that URL — including the NIC application draft — needs updating.

### Still open

T015 (a signed-in corpus query returning a cited answer) and T018 (measure whether web
token streaming improved on the named-tunnel path) both require an authenticated
session and are not yet done. **T018's result is not recorded here yet** — this entry
must be amended once it is measured. The polling fallback stays in place regardless.

A group row and a document row rendered the **same 4×4 `Box`**, so the only cue
that a document sat *inside* a category was a 20 px indent; at ~50 department
groups and ~4,000 documents the two levels were indistinguishable. Changes:

  shrank the leaf tick and the architect still reported "looking same", because

first surfaced as citations [10]/[11] on a Sindh policy question. Both had
