## 2026-08-15 — GPU hold for bulk indexing, and PP-OCR on CUDA measured and REJECTED

### `deploy/gpu-hold.sh` + `deploy/gpu-release.sh` (new, installed on the VM)

The corpus driver needs GPU embeddings for hours at a stretch, and the one-minute
poller (`gpu-index-auto.sh`) decides afresh every tick — so it can toggle
mid-run. Entering GPU mode costs a server restart, and `add_indexed_folder` walks
its directory **lazily**, so that restart kills the walk; files not yet reached
have no `sources` row and `resume_interrupted_indexing` cannot re-queue what does
not exist (HEALTH stopped at 46/132 this way). `gpu-hold.sh` **stops
`noviq-gpu-index.timer`** and switches once; `gpu-release.sh` restores CPU
embeddings, chat and the timer.

⭐ The pause sentinel `GPU_MODE_DISABLED` is deliberately **left in place** during
a hold. If the timer ever returns on its own (reboot), the poller sees pause +
`GPU_MODE_ACTIVE` and *releases* — so the accident restores chat instead of
extending the outage. The env/drop-in split is copied verbatim from the poller
and must stay identical: `ORT_DYLIB_PATH`/`ECHO_EMBED_GPU` in `.env` (the app
force-loads it and clobbers drop-in values), `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` in the systemd
drop-in (read at exec, before `.env`).

### ⚠️ PP-OCR on CUDA is **3.4× SLOWER** here — measured, then not shipped

`ECHO_EMBED_GPU=1` switches only the Rust embedder. OCR runs in a **separate
Python process** (`ocr_sidecar.rs` spawns `<venv-python> ingestion_sidecar.py`)
whose venv holds the CPU `onnxruntime` wheel, so OCR was CPU-bound by
construction. Built a venv with `onnxruntime-gpu==1.19.2` (last cp38 build) and
confirmed det/cls/rec all on `CUDAExecutionProvider`. Same 4 pages, idle box:

| runtime | steady state |
|---|---|
| CPU | **2.9 s/page** |
| CUDA | **10.0 s/page** |

Char counts matched (8,115 / 8,118) — same work, genuinely slower. PP-OCR is many
small **dynamic-shaped** inferences (one detection pass, then dozens of text-line
crops), so cuDNN re-selects algorithms per shape and the card never reaches a
batch size worth the setup, while the CPU path spreads each page over 12 cores.

⭐⭐ **The first benchmark said GPU won 1.8× — and it was wrong.** It ran while the
corpus load had the CPU saturated: the GPU path sits at ~9–10 s/page regardless
of load, while CPU went 16.3 → 2.9 s/page once the box quietened. *Contention on
the baseline manufactured the win.* Benchmark against an idle box or not at all.

`_ocr_rapidocr` keeps an **opt-in** `ECHO_OCR_GPU=1` path (default off) that reads
the providers back off the live sessions and logs which models actually landed on
CUDA — absence of that line is the silent-CPU-fallback trap from 2026-08-04.

### ⭐ Where scan time actually goes

On a 162-page 20 MB scan: `pdftoppm` rasterisation **28 min** vs OCR **10 min**.
Rasterisation is single-threaded per invocation and CPU-only — no GPU path
exists. Splitting one document across several `pdftoppm` page ranges (`-f`/`-l`)
is the untaken lever. Also confirmed: the folder-scan path registers and
processes files **one at a time**, so `ECHO_INDEX_CONCURRENCY=4` buys nothing
there (it applies to the upload path, which spawns a task per file) — measured
20–45 s/file on real departments.

## 2026-08-13 — audit trail: read access was never recorded, and nothing could read the log ✅ BUILT + TESTED, NOT DEPLOYED

Triggered by an audit of the nine customer-facing feature claims. The claim
*"full audit logging of queries and access"* was checked against the code and
found to be two-thirds true — with a third problem nobody had noticed.

### What was actually true before this change

- **Queries** ✅ — `query_log` (migration 007) stores one row per chat turn.
- **Mutations** ✅ — `audit::insert_user_event` fires on index/upload/delete and
  every admin action (`api/documents.rs`, `api/admin.rs`).
- **Document READS** ❌ — `source_file`, `source_chunks` and `global_search`
  check permission through `visible_source_ids` and then serve silently. "Who
  opened this file?" had no answer.
- ⚠️⚠️ **Nothing could READ the audit log.** `audit_log` had been written since
  F014 and the only reader was `commands/audit.rs` — a **Tauri** command, and
  Tauri is vestigial in the client-server deployment (`router.rs` had no audit
  route at all). The trail existed solely in the database, reachable only by
  opening psql on the VM. ⭐ **A log nobody can produce on request is not an
  audit trail** — this was the bigger half of the gap, and it was invisible
  because the *write* side looked complete.

### Fix

- **`db/repositories/audit.rs`** — added `AuditRecord` (full row + actor username
  + document title via LEFT JOIN, so a deleted user never loses the event),
  `AuditFilter`, and `query`/`count`/`export`/`distinct_actions`. First use of
  `sqlx::QueryBuilder` in the codebase; the WHERE clause is built once in
  `push_filters` and shared by all three, so **a filter cannot mean one thing on
  screen and another in the downloaded file**.
- **`api/audit.rs`** (new) — `GET /admin/audit` (paged) + `GET
  /admin/audit/export` (CSV/JSON download), both `AdminUser`-gated. Dates are
  calendar days; `to` resolves to **midnight of the following day, compared with
  `<`** — an inclusive `23:59:59.999` bound silently drops events in the final
  millisecond, which is how a "complete" export quietly isn't. A malformed or
  inverted range is a 400, **not** a silent full-log dump behind a filled-in date
  box. **No delete route, deliberately.**
- **`api/documents.rs`** — new `audit_access` helper; calls sit immediately after
  the `visible_source_ids` decision (the one place access is settled), so a new
  read route cannot skip the trail without also skipping the permission check.
  Actions: `document_open`, `document_read`, `document_denied`, `global_search`.
  ⭐ **Refused reads are recorded** while the response still says "not found" —
  the caller cannot tell it was logged, and "did anyone try?" is usually the
  question being asked.
- **Migration 025** — index-only, additive: `(user_id, created_at DESC)`,
  `(action, created_at DESC)`, `(target, created_at DESC)`. Read rows arrive far
  more often than mutations and only `created_at`/`event_type` were indexed.
- **`pages/Admin.tsx`** — new **Audit Log** tab: day range + user + action + free
  text, quick spans, paging, row detail, and three downloads (filtered CSV, JSON,
  whole log). Loads lazily on first open. CSV fields are formula-guarded (`=+-@`
  prefixed with `'`) because details carry user-supplied search terms and an
  export is exactly the file someone opens in Excel.

### Volume decision, made explicitly

`source_chunks` logs **every** window, not just the first. Scrolling a long
document therefore produces several rows — `offset` in the details distinguishes
the opening read from paging. Rejected the "log only offset 0" optimisation: a
caller supplying its own offsets could then read a whole document off the record.
▶ **Retention is now a real decision** (12 months was suggested); it is NOT
implemented — nothing prunes `audit_log` today.

### Verification status — READ THIS BEFORE DEPLOYING

- ✅ Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run build` clean, 26/26 vitest pass.
- ✅ Backend: `cargo check` **and** `cargo test --lib … api::audit` on the VM via
  the detached-worktree recipe — 0 errors, **7/7 new tests pass**, no new
  warnings in the touched files. Prod verified untouched throughout (HEAD
  `728d373`, binary mtime `2026-08-12 21:46`, both services active); worktree,
  temp branch and the 4.6 GB target dir removed afterwards.
- ⚠️ **Pre-existing breakage found, NOT caused by this change and NOT fixed:**
  `tests/ingestion_hardening_acceptance.rs:155` calls
  `structured_importer::persist` with 4 arguments; it takes 6 (E0061). This
  breaks **any** plain `cargo test` (the whole run aborts at compile), which is
  why `--lib` was used. ▶ Worth fixing separately — it silently costs the suite.
- ❌ **Not deployed and not behaviour-verified.** Per
  `feedback_verify-deploys-by-behaviour-not-by-logs`, after deploying: open a
  document, attempt a forbidden one, run a search, then confirm all three appear
  in the Audit tab **and** in a date-ranged CSV. Migration 025 runs at boot.

### ⚠️ Process note — a truncated bundle nearly produced a false green

The VM check was run twice. `git add <files>` → `write-tree` → `commit-tree` →
**`git reset`** was used to build a temp commit without moving the working
branch; on the second pass the `git reset` from the FIRST pass had already
emptied the index, so the second bundle contained **one file** instead of eight.
The worktree checkout silently reverted `api/mod.rs` and `router.rs` — and the
test run reported `EXIT=0`, `0 tests, 997 filtered out`. ⭐⭐ **"Zero tests ran"
read as a pass in the exit code**; only grepping for the test names showed the
module was not compiled at all. Always assert the expected test COUNT, and
`git diff --stat <base> <commit>` the bundle before trusting a remote check.

## 2026-08-12 (b) — "conflict between X and Y" returned nothing: three stacked causes ⚠️ PARTIALLY FIXED

Reported: a live question — *"is there any conflict between @Constitution.pdf and
@Sindh Local Government Act 2013.pdf"* — answered *"The retrieved documents do not
contain enough information."* Trace `a8ab8eac`.

### Cause 1 — intent routing was correct, then discarded ✅ FIXED

`classify_capability` DID return `Capability::Conflict` (the `conflict_re()`
high-precision override at `intent.rs:163` matched). Three lines later
`assistant/mod.rs:583` rewrote it to `Guidance`, because `Conflict.is_map_reduce()`
and production had **`NOVIQ_MAPREDUCE=off`**. ⭐ **The classifier was never the bug —
a latency kill-switch silently demoted the capability.** That kill-switch exists
because map-reduce cost ~80 s/turn at the OLD decode speed; the 10× speedup earlier
today removed its justification.

### Cause 2 — no per-source floor in the Guidance path ✅ FIXED

Both documents WERE in scope (STEP 3: `Sources in scope: 2`) and the Constitution
WAS retrieved (4 of 72 vector hits, ~17 of 72 keyword hits). But the merge ranked
globally with **`ECHO_SOURCE_CAP=off`**, so top-K=36 went **36–0 to the SLGA**
(helped by `ECHO_INSTRUMENT_BOOST=2.0`, which the @-mention feeds by putting the
instrument's own name in the query text). The model was handed one side of a
two-sided question and correctly refused. ⚠️ **A comparison question has no topical
signal to rank on — ranking is the wrong instrument, and nothing guaranteed the
second document a single slot.**

### Applied to prod (`.env`, backup `.env.bak.retrieval`), server restarted

`NOVIQ_MAPREDUCE=on` · `ECHO_SOURCE_CAP=auto` (= `ctx_k/3` clamped [6,12] = 12;
round-robin waves per source via `apply_source_diversity`, NOT a hard cap).

Retest through the real `/api/query`: capability `guidance` → **`conflict`**;
citations 0 → **62, drawn from BOTH documents**; 4.4 s.

### Cause 3 — STILL OPEN: map-reduce no longer provides coverage

The answer is **still the 82-char refusal**. Reason: `gather_provisions_retrieved`
swept **62 provisions ≈ 3% of the two documents' 2,083 chunks**. Since 2026-07-06
map-reduce means "the doubled-K hybrid slice, batched" — NOT the full sweep the
comment "full coverage by construction" still claims. For conflict detection that
is the whole ballgame: a conflict can sit anywhere, and a relevance slice cannot
find what relevance cannot rank.

⭐ **The refusal is arguably CORRECT behaviour** — on 3% of the text, "not enough
information" is honest. The guardrail works; the capability is under-resourced.

`gather_provisions` (true full sweep over `scope_ids`) still exists at
`capabilities/mod.rs:39`, marked `#[allow(dead_code)]` — *"kept for the deferred
whole-document audit path"*. Wiring it back is a **code change, not a flag**.
Cost at the NEW speed: 2,083 chunks ÷ ~31/batch ≈ 67 batches × ~1.6 s ≈ **~2 min**
(estimate) — a deliberate "deep audit" action, versus 10+ min before, which is why
it was cut. ▶ Architect's call.

### Interim decision (architect, 2026-08-12): say "not yet" instead of failing

Rather than ship a capability that answers "not enough information" after an
officer names two documents and waits, `Conflict` and `Compare` now return an
explicit not-yet-available notice on the normal path — no retrieval, no model.
**The point is that the product must not LOOK broken while the real
implementation is pending.**

- `TurnResponse::cross_document_unavailable` (`assistant/mod.rs`) + a guarded
  dispatch arm; `ECHO_CROSSDOC_CAPABILITY=mapreduce` restores the old path for
  development on the VM. Default = notice.
- ⚠️ **The copy deliberately does NOT tell the officer to switch Deep search on.**
  Deep search does not implement these capabilities today — it is wired into
  `guidance` only (`guidance.rs:530`) and is admin-gated (`deep_enabled_for_role`)
  — so "use Deep search" would be a dead end that reads as *more* broken. It names
  Deep search as where the feature is going, not as a workaround available now.
- Tests: notice names the capability, offers a next step, and asserts the absence
  of dead-end phrasing.

▶ **Planned implementation — Conflict/Compare onto Deep search, NOT the full sweep.**
Deep's first stage (`expand`) decomposes into sub-questions, which converts an
unrankable relational question into several rankable topical ones — attacking the
root cause instead of brute-forcing past it. Bounded at **≤3 LLM calls / 2
retrieval rounds** (ADR-0021) ≈ 15–30 s, versus ~67 batches ≈ 2 min for a true
sweep. `run_agentic_deep` already takes `system_prompt` + `scope_source_ids`, so
the wiring is a dispatch change at the capability site.
Three things to get right when it is built:
1. ⚠️ **The SC-011 dual-citation gate must survive into the deep synthesis path**
   (`conflict.rs`: suppress any conflict statement the source cannot support
   verbatim). Trading "returns nothing" for "confidently asserts a conflict that
   is not there" is strictly worse for a legal product.
2. **Auto-escalate; do not require the Deep toggle.** Deep is admin-only, so
   gating on it would silently remove the capability for every non-admin. The
   classifier already detects Conflict deterministically — let the capability pick
   its engine.
3. **Bounded ≠ exhaustive.** Answers must read "based on the provisions
   retrieved", never "there are no conflicts" — which is what `conflict.rs`
   already promises (candidates for review, not assertions).

### ⚠️ Graph findings (checked directly, correcting an earlier claim in-session)

The legal overlay is **NOT empty**: `graph_nodes` 10,879, `graph_edges` 12,289
(`graph_summary` 0 — the known unbuilt-summaries gap). Constitution.pdf has 975
nodes, SLGA 2013 has 820. But:

- ⚠️⚠️ **ALL 12,289 edges are intra-document — ZERO cross-document, of any type**
  (`contains` 10,853 · `cross_reference` 1,346 · `non_obstante` 90). The graph is a
  per-document structural tree, not a corpus knowledge graph, so it **cannot** express
  a relationship between two instruments. That is why STEP 11 reached 1 node and added 0.
- ⚠️ `instrument_id` is **NULL on all 10,879 nodes**; the link survives only via
  `chunk_id → chunks → sources` (resolves 10,879/10,879).
- ⚠️ Coverage is **26 of 118 sources** — built before the Sindh harvest.
- The 90 `non_obstante` edges are legitimately self-referential ("Notwithstanding
  anything contained in the Constitution", inside Constitution.pdf) — the extractor
  is right; it just never resolves a reference to a DIFFERENT instrument.
- ▶ Highest-value slice: **amendment chains**. SLGA 2013 (1,108 chunks), SLGA
  Amendment 2013 (134) and SLGA Amendment 2021 (91) are three unlinked documents, so
  "what does section 74 say?" serves the 2013 text as current. That is a wrong-answer
  bug, not a missing feature. (`amendment_events` has 82 rows but annotated 0 of 36.)

## 2026-08-12 — inference was 5.9x slow because vLLM was forced onto the legacy AWQ kernel ✅ DEPLOYED 19:09

Asked: "why our gpu inference of llm is so slow?" Answer: one flag.

### Symptom

Generation ran at **13.4 tok/s**, and decode was **98.5% of a 36.2 s answer**
(vLLM `/metrics`, 50 real production requests: TPOT 74.45 ms, TTFT 661 ms; the
arithmetic closes to 36.3 s vs 36.2 s measured). Users called it "so slow"; five
rows of the customer-facing limitations register blamed it on a "time-sliced ¼
GPU" and recommended procurement.

### Root cause

`deploy/vllm/run-vllm.sh:30` defaulted `QUANT` to `awq`, so the sidecar launched
with `--quantization awq`. Passing that flag **explicitly** suppresses vLLM's
automatic upgrade to the Marlin INT4 kernel. vLLM said so in every startup log
since 2026-06-28 and it was read past every time:

    INFO [awq_marlin.py:117] Detected that the model can run with awq_marlin,
    however you specified quantization=awq explicitly, so forcing awq.
    Use quantization=awq_marlin for faster inference

### Why it was NOT the GPU (each eliminated by measurement, not argument)

| Path | Measured | vs hardware |
|---|---|---|
| Prefill compute | 4,804 tok/s @ 8.7k | 77.6 TFLOPS = **52% of full A40 FP16 peak** |
| Raw memory bandwidth | d2d copy in guest | **564 GB/s = 81% of A40 spec (696)** |
| Decode (before) | 13.7 tok/s × 6.10 GB | 84 GB/s = **15% of the 564 available** |

Two of three paths healthy ⇒ the kernel between them was the fault. Also killed:
long prompts (14-token prompt decoded at 13.76, a 4,423-token one at 13.43 —
flat across 300× context); saturation (8 concurrent streams held 13.0 tok/s
each, 104 aggregate); the CUDA compat shim (prefill crosses the same R470 shim
and is fine); eager mode (`enforce_eager=False`, graphs captured).

⚠️ **The "time-sliced ¼ GPU" premise is FALSE and must be retracted from the
limitations docs.** A40-12Q partitions *frame buffer* (12 of 48 GB), **not
compute** — 52–61% of the full card's FP16 peak is impossible under a 25% cap.

### Fix

`NOVIQ_VLLM_QUANT=awq_marlin` in `/opt/noviq/echoAI/.env` (backup at
`.env.bak.marlin`), and the `run-vllm.sh:30` default changed to match so the
next deploy cannot regress it. Restart only — no code path touched.

### Measured before → after

| Metric | Before | After | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decode, 300 tok | 13.75 tok/s | **81.32 tok/s** | **5.9×** |
| Production-shaped (4.4k prompt, 479 out) | 36.2 s | **7.7 s** | **4.7×** |
| Decode bandwidth utilisation | 15% | **88%** of achievable | near-optimal |
| VRAM free | 1,400 MiB | 1,998 MiB | improved |

**F016 SC-002 (p95 ≤ 10 s), written off as unreachable on this hardware, now
passes on a single-stream production-shaped request.**

### Follow-up same session: n-gram speculative decoding (FLAGGED, default OFF in repo, ON in prod)

New opt-in knob `NOVIQ_VLLM_SPEC=ngram` (plus `_SPEC_TOKENS` / `_SPEC_LOOKUP_MIN`
/ `_SPEC_LOOKUP_MAX`), wired as `--speculative-config '{"method":"ngram",...}'`.
Draft-model-FREE: guesses by copying a matching run out of the prompt, then the
real model verifies in one pass. **Output is bit-identical** — rejection sampling
discards wrong guesses — so this is a pure latency change, and it costs no extra
weights (matters: only ~1.2 GB free).

⚠️ **It forces the V0 engine** (`ngram is experimental on VLLM_USE_V1=1. Falling
back to V0 Engine`). **Chunked prefill SURVIVES the fallback** (`chunked_prefill_enabled=True`
verified in the V0 config line) so the F016 §7 two-wave pathology does NOT return —
that was the specific risk and it was checked, not assumed.

Measured A/B (identical tasks, `/tmp/spec_bench.py` + `/tmp/conc.py`):

| | spec OFF | spec ON |
|---|---|---|
| 1 user, quote-heavy | 83.8 tok/s | **133.8** (1.6×) |
| 1 user, RAG shape | 84.8 tok/s | **168.9–181.0** (2.0–2.1×) |
| 1 user, free prose | 83.0 tok/s | **113.3** (1.4×) |
| 8 users, aggregate | **596.8 tok/s** | 461.4 (**−23%**) |
| 8 users, slowest request | **4.02 s** | 5.20 s |
| VRAM free | 1,784 MiB | 1,234 MiB |
| KV cache | 15,456 tok (1.68×) | 13,968→2.72× reported on V0 |

⭐ **Speculation buys single-user latency with spare compute — under a full batch
there IS no spare compute, so it costs throughput.** Enabled anyway because
production is ~15 requests/day and has never shown `num_requests_running > 1`;
the bad case (8 concurrent) still returns in 5.2 s, inside the SC-002 10 s gate.
**Reset switch: `NOVIQ_VLLM_SPEC=` (empty) + restart `noviq-vllm`**, or
`sudo bash /tmp/spec-toggle.sh off`. Flip it OFF before any multi-tester demo.

**Cumulative: a production-shaped request went 36.2 s → 7.7 s (marlin) → 3.6 s
(＋spec) = ~10× end to end.**

### ⚠️ CORRECTION — `run-vllm.sh` is OUT OF TREE, like `deploy.sh`

The earlier claim in this entry that fixing `deploy/vllm/run-vllm.sh:30` prevents
regression was **wrong**. `noviq-vllm.service` runs
**`/opt/noviq/vllm-scripts/run-vllm.sh`**, not the repo copy — the repo file is
documentation unless it is copied across. The marlin fix held only because `.env`
sets the key explicitly, overriding the live script's stale `awq` default.
Both copies are now reconciled (2026-08-12) and carry the marlin default + the
spec block; the live one had also drifted by a `--load-format bitsandbytes` line
that the repo lacked, now merged back. Backup: `run-vllm.sh.bak.<date>`.
Same disease as [[reference_vm-deploy-script-is-out-of-tree]].

### Trade-off and follow-ups

- **Prefill got ~27% slower** (4,804 → 3,516 tok/s). Accepted: prefill is <2% of
  request latency, so the net is a 4.7× win. Do not "fix" this by reverting.
- KV cache 14,800 → 13,968 tokens; max concurrency 1.61× → 1.52×. Minor, and a
  separate constraint from decode speed.
- ▶ Next lever: **n-gram speculative decoding** — our answers quote retrieved
  passages verbatim, which is the ideal case. Expect a further 1.5–2.5×.
- ▶ Retract the ¼-GPU claim from `noviq_limitations.docx` (both variants),
  ADR-0020's "~14 tok/s vGPU" aside, and `docs/kimi-k3-cpu-feasibility-2026-08.html`.

⭐ **Lesson: a warning in a log you already have beats any amount of reasoning
about hardware.** Two plausible hypotheses (long prompts; vGPU time-slicing)
both felt right and were both killed by a single measurement each.

## 2026-08-11 (e) — images never reached OCR at all ✅ DEPLOYED 22:21

Reported: "unable to upload image/scanned pdf in attachment and upload documents
… use paddleocr there also", and the same for project uploads.

### Scanned PDFs were already fine

`pdf.rs` tier 3 OCRs them, and `attach_document` routes through the same
`index_sources` pipeline, so attachments and project uploads inherit it. No
change needed. ⚠️ If a scanned PDF still fails, it is the (d) §3 timeout
question, not a missing OCR path.

### Images were not — `indexer.rs` never called OCR for them

`FileFormat::Image => parsers::image::describe(&path_buf, &tier_clone, None)`.
That third argument is the **vision model path, hard-coded `None`**, so
`describe` returned `CapabilityNotAvailable` — *"Vision model not loaded. Please
download Qwen2-VL 2B"* — on **every** image, always. Images never touched the OCR
ladder at all.

⭐ A photographed notice is the most common thing an officer uploads, and what
they need from it is the TEXT. Captioning was the wrong treatment.

**Fix:** new `ocr::ocr_image()` — same ladder as scanned pages (PP-OCR via the
sidecar, tesseract on failure), minus rasterisation since the file already IS a
page image. `OcrConfig::for_image()` carries the `ECHO_OCR_*` overrides.

### ⚠️ On "use PaddleOCR"

**Literal PaddlePaddle cannot run on the deploy VM** — the vCPU is masked to
Core2 with no AVX, and `import paddle` raises **SIGILL, killing the process
outright** (uncatchable; the `noavx` wheel imports but still SIGILLs on first
matmul). This is why the live path is **RapidOCR running the same PP-OCR det/rec
models on ONNX Runtime**. So the PP-OCR models ARE what runs — the new image path
joins that, and adding real Paddle would crash the indexer.

✅ **Deployed 2026-08-11 22:21** (`release` = `7af05eff`, a clean fast-forward from
`863ade71`). Compile-checked first in an isolated VM worktree
(`--no-default-features --features server`, 0 errors) — valid because the delta
touches only `indexer.rs`/`ocr.rs`, outside every `llm`/`cuda`/`desktop` gate.
Prod stayed isolated during the check (HEAD, binary mtime and `noviq-server` all
unchanged), and the worktree + target dir were removed afterwards.

Deploy verified the way `deploy.sh`'s fail-soft demands — **not** by the commit:
binary mtime `16:28:25` → **`22:21:45`**, `Finished release profile in 5m 40s`,
`deploy done at 7af05eff (frontend=0 backend=1)`, service restarted 22:21:46 and
`active`, `/api/health` 200. `frontend=0` is correct: no frontend files changed.

⚠️ The good path depends on `paddle_ocr_enabled()`, which is **true by default**
(`ECHO_PADDLE_OCR != "0"`) **and** requires `ocr_sidecar::available()`. Confirmed
live: all four of `ECHO_PADDLE_OCR`, `ECHO_OCR_PYTHON`, `ECHO_INGESTION_SIDECAR`,
`ECHO_TABLE_SIDECAR` are set in `/opt/noviq/echoAI/.env` (the service's
`WorkingDirectory`, so dotenv picks it up — there is **no** systemd
`EnvironmentFile`), and the OCR venv exists. Without those, images would silently
fall through to tesseract — the quality trap from the 2026-07-10 entry.

⏳ **Not retro-applied**: images ingested before this deploy still hold the
`CapabilityNotAvailable` failure, not text. They must be re-uploaded.

### Sindh harvest — COMPLETE: 3,900 files / 3.1 GB at `D:\Sindh-Corpus`

⚠️⚠️ **A "failed" verdict is not proof of a failed download.** The SRB run
reported `ok: 0, failed: 864` — while writing **665 MB of perfectly good PDFs** to
disk. srb.gos.pk (WordPress/PHP) emits a **UTF-8 BOM before the file body**, so
every response starts `EF BB BF %PDF-1.5`; the sniff test is
`body[:5] == b"%PDF-"`, which fails, so `download_all` saved them as `.bin` and
recorded `ok=False`. The bytes were always fine — only the verdict was wrong.
`repair_bom.py` strips the BOM, restores `.pdf` and rewrites the manifest rows
(the BOM is not cosmetic: leading bytes before `%PDF` break strict parsers, and
pdftotext/lopdf are exactly that). ⭐ Sniffing a magic number at offset 0 is wrong
whenever a server may prepend a BOM.

⚠️ **Two sites silently ignore their own filters** — rtw's page URL (known) and
sindhlaws' `DepartmentCode.aspx` DepID (new). Assume a government-site filter is
decorative until a narrow query returns a *small* result.

⭐ **srb.gos.pk was a total loss and became a net gain.** All 651 catalogued srb
URLs were dead (0/118 attempts) because SRB rebuilt on WordPress; the old
`/contents/...` tree is gone. Re-enumerating the new index pages yielded **868**
documents — more than the original catalogue. Two traps there:
- **TLS**: SRB serves only its leaf certificate, no intermediate, so OpenSSL
  fails where Windows curl succeeds (curl fetches the issuer via AIA). Fixed by
  building a bundle with the Sectigo intermediate — **not** by `verify=False`.
- **Titles**: all three sections are tables whose download cell is an `<img>`
  inside `<a>`, i.e. **no anchor text**, so anchor-based extraction produced
  `04 09 2024` / `CamScanner-04-09-2024-15`. Titles must come from the sibling
  cells. 868/868 usable, 804 dated.

⚠️⚠️ **Department categorisation is NOT solved for sindhlaws — do not trust
`dept_map.json`.** It reported **1768/1768 coverage**, and that number was the
*symptom*: two buckets (GENERAL DEPARTMENTS 1150, AGRICULTURE 306) absorbed 82%
of the corpus because their DepID pages dump nearly everything. Spot-checks put
`AL-KAWTHAR UNIVERSITY ACT` and `SALES TAX ON SERVICES` under Agriculture. The
main grid (`# | TITLE | English | Urdu | Sindhi | DATE`) has no department column,
so that broken axis is sindhlaws' only source. rtw (1,325) and srb (868) are
reliably categorised; sindhlaws (1,768) is not.

Final: **3,900 files, 3.1 GB** — sindhlaws 1,758 · rtw 1,278 · srb 864. 62 sha256
duplicates. 280 failures: 125 superseded srb links (not a loss), 90 permanent
404s, 54 transient worth a retry, 11 other — itemised in `DEAD_LINKS.md`.
⚠️ Failures are written to the manifest and **resume skips anything recorded
there**, so retrying the 54 requires filtering those rows out first.

### Sindh harvest — how it was run

The download runs **on the VM**, not the laptop: the ~3,899 files land where they
will eventually be indexed (no second 1.5 GB hop over the VPN), and a ~2 hour
foreground SSH from Windows is killed by the Sangfor VPN (exit 255) — hence tmux.

Staged at **`/opt/noviq/harvest`**, deliberately *outside* the prod tree so
`deploy.sh`'s `git reset --hard` can never touch it. `harvest.py` derives its
output dir from `Path(__file__).parents[2]`, so the copied layout
(`/opt/noviq/harvest/scripts/corpus_scrape/`) puts the corpus at
`/opt/noviq/harvest/corpus-harvest/` with no code change. Runner:
`run_download.sh`; log: `download.log`.

⚠️ VM python is **3.8.10** — the scripts only survive it because of
`from __future__ import annotations` (they use `list[dict]` / `int | None`).
`py_compile`-checked there before launching; any new 3.9+ *runtime* syntax will
break this.

Smoke-tested 25/25 → real PDFs, 0 failures, 3.9 MB (~160 KB/file, so the haul is
nearer **~625 MB** than the 1.5 GB first estimated). The manifest is keyed by
`source_url`, so the smoke test resumes into the full run rather than refetching.
⚠️ The catalogue spans **more hosts than the two harvested** (`srb.gos.pk`,
`pas.gov.pk`, `sindhhealth`, …); per-host failures are recorded in the manifest
rather than aborting the run, so read the final stats, not the exit code.

## 2026-08-11 (d) — every project upload reported failure, and the picker
## promised formats we cannot index

Two defects from the architect testing project uploads, plus one open report.

### 1. ⭐⭐ "Uploaded, but could not match the files to indexed documents."

Shown on **every** project upload — deterministic, not intermittent. The upload
had actually SUCCEEDED: `api/uploads.rs` indexes, calls `projects::add_sources`
and stamps `sources.project_id` before it responds.

The lie was in the confirmation step. `AddProjectDocuments.tsx` re-derived the
new source ids by calling `listSourcesInFolder(folderId)` and matching file
names — but the (b) fix earlier the same day added `AND project_id IS NULL` to
`api/documents.rs::list_sources_in_folder`, precisely so a project document
stays out of the global tree. **So the confirmation looked for the document in
the one listing the document is designed to be absent from**, found nothing, and
reported failure on success. `props.onAdded`/`onClose` never ran, so the dialog
stayed open and the list never refreshed.

⭐⭐ **The lesson is the shape, not the line**: a hardening change that hides
rows will break any caller that was using that listing as an existence check.
Grep for readers of a listing before narrowing it.

**Fix — the server reports what it attached.** `UploadOutcome` gains
`attached: Vec<String>` (the ids bound to the project); the client trusts it and
drops both the folder lookup and the now-redundant `addDocuments` call. The
server is the only party that can answer this honestly, since it did the work.

### 2. The upload picker offered audio, video and code

Hint text read "PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, text, images, audio, video, code".
Audio/video/code parse (`FileFormat` knows them) but nothing transcribes or
indexes them into retrievable text, so accepting them created sources that could
never answer anything.

New `src/lib/uploadFormats.ts` holds one list (`UPLOAD_ACCEPT`, `UPLOAD_HINT`),
applied to all three upload surfaces — `AddProjectDocuments`, `IndexedFolders`,
`ChatPage` attach — and `api/uploads.rs` now rejects the same set at the
boundary so the promise and the enforcement match. ⚠️ Narrowed at the upload
boundary, NOT in `FileFormat`: folder indexing and the parser tests still use
the full set.

### 3. ⏳ OPEN — a 20 MB CrPC PDF will not upload into a project

Ruled out by reading the code: there is **no per-file size cap** on this route.
20 MB sits under the 256 MB route body limit (`router.rs` — the per-route
`DefaultBodyLimit` is applied inner, so it correctly overrides the 8 MB global)
and under the 500 MB user quota. The 8 MB cap in `attach_limits` is the CHAT
attachment route, a different path.

⚠️ What the code does show: **upload indexes SYNCHRONOUSLY inside the HTTP
request** — `index_folder(…).await` runs before the response — so a ~900-page
CrPC holds one connection open for the entire parse + chunk + embed. Any proxy
or tunnel in front will time out first. Needs the exact error text and the
server log before naming a cause; do not guess.

## 2026-08-11 (c) — one turn PER CONVERSATION, and the rail must not erase it

Two symptoms from the architect testing (a): the generating chat vanished from
the rail once he clicked another chat, and **"New chat" could not be used at
all** while an answer was in flight. Both are defects the (a) fix introduced or
exposed. Frontend only.

### 1. `syncConversations` erased the chat being waited on

It did `setConversations(rows.map(…))` — a **wholesale replace** with the
server's history. ⚠️ **The server lists a conversation only once a turn has
LANDED in `query_log`**, so a chat whose question is still generating is not in
`rows`. Remounting (coming back from another tab) therefore deleted the rail
entry for the very chat the officer was waiting on, leaving nothing to click.

The answer was never lost — it sits in the store's queue keyed by conversation —
but nothing could reach it, which is indistinguishable from lost. Now MERGES:
the server stays authoritative for what it knows, local-only entries are kept
and re-sorted by recency.

⭐ Latent before (a): a fresh chat only existed within one mount, and the sync
ran at mount *before* any question was asked. Making the page remount into a
live turn is what surfaced it.

### 2. A global `busy` disabled the composer everywhere

The (a) store held ONE active turn, so `busy()` was global and
`disabled={busy()}` froze the composer in every conversation — including a
brand-new one. That is the reported "unable to start a new chat". Worse:
`runTurn` early-returned while busy, so a second send would have appended the
question and produced **no answer and no error**.

**Fix: the store is keyed by conversation** — `active`, `streaming` and `phase`
are all `Record<conversationId, …>`, `stopped` is a `Set`, and the exported API
is `busyIn(id)` / `streamingIn(id)` / `phaseIn(id)` / `stopTurn(id)`. There is
deliberately **no global "is anything running"**: that shape is what caused the
bug, so it is not available to be misused again. `runTurn` refuses only a second
turn in the SAME conversation (two answers racing into one transcript); a turn
in another chat is allowed and queues server-side on `gen_gate`, which already
exists because the deployment targets concurrent users.

`resumeConversationId()` (newest running turn) replaces
`activeTurnConversationId()` for the mount-time reopen.

⚠️ Still open: an answer that completes while its conversation is CLOSED stays
in the in-memory queue and does not reach that chat's localStorage cache until
it is reopened. A reload before then loses the client's copy (the server still
has it). Same root as the reload gap noted in (a).

## 2026-08-11 (b) — a project's documents belong to the project (migration 024)

Follow-up to the leak below, reported after it deployed: *"still it is showing
my projects documents in chat window"*. **Different cause, correctly so.** The
morning's fix changed who ELSE could see a project upload; it never touched the
owner's own view, and the owner sees their own documents by `owner_id`
(`documents.rs:134`). Both halves were real.

⚠️ It also exposed a wrinkle in that fix: `list_sources_in_folder` matches
`file_path LIKE '<folder>%'`, a **prefix** — and the new `__project__<id>`
directory sits INSIDE the uploads folder, so project files still matched the
parent folder's listing. The per-project directory alone was never going to
clear the rail.

### Mechanism — `sources.project_id`, not a path convention

⭐ `sources.conversation_id` has marked conversation attachments since F021 and
is the same shape of fact: *this document belongs to one place and must not
surface in general listings*. Migration 024 adds `project_id` beside it rather
than inventing a `__project__` path rule — a path is a heuristic, a column is a
fact.

⚠️ **`project_id` and `project_source` are different things and both are
needed**, which is the distinction the whole fix rests on:

| | meaning | cardinality | set by | global tree |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_source` | membership | many-to-many | add + upload | **stays visible** |
| `sources.project_id` | origin | at most one | upload only | hidden |

So a document UPLOADED into a project is hidden from the general tree and from
general retrieval; a corpus document ADDED to a project keeps appearing
everywhere, because adding is a reference, not a move — the same principle as
ADR-0028's "sharing is a copy". Architect's call, asked explicitly.

Applied in three places, deliberately not four:
- `list_indexed_folders` — hides the `__project__` folder itself (its sources are
  already filtered; an empty unexplained folder is worse than none).
- `list_sources_in_folder` — `AND project_id IS NULL`.
- `visible_source_ids` — **`AND project_id IS NULL` on every general branch.**
  This is the one that matters: without it the officer's own project files were
  answering their ordinary chat questions. That changes the ANSWER, not just a
  rail.
- **NOT** `list_folder_sources` (Settings). A project upload must stay visible
  where documents are managed and deleted, or it becomes unreachable content
  that still bills against the storage allowance.

### Data fix

One legacy row existed (`Noviq_Issues_and_Fixes_2026-08-06.pdf` in project
`test1`) and it was the leak in its purest form: `visibility = 'shared'` with
**`owner_id` NULL** — ownerless and world-visible. ⚠️ Flipping visibility alone
would have made it invisible to EVERYONE including its owner; `owner_id` had to
be set in the same statement.

## 2026-08-11 — leaving chat mid-answer lost the turn, + four defects

Five findings from the architect using the live product. ⚠️ The Rust half of
this entry is **NOT compile-checked** (no toolchain on Windows — see
`reference_vm-safe-compile-check-recipe`); the TypeScript half typechecks and
builds.

### 1. Navigating away mid-answer threw the answer away (the reported bug)

Every tab is a sibling route under `AppShell` (`App.tsx:296`), so leaving `/`
**unmounts `ChatPage`**. The whole running turn lived in component signals, so:

- `sendMessage` resolved into a **disposed reactive scope** — `setTurns` at the
  old `runInference:1149` wrote nowhere and the answer was dropped;
- the `on(turns)` effect that caches the transcript was disposed too, so the
  answer never reached localStorage either;
- returning to `/` minted a **blank New chat** (`onMount:766`), and reopening the
  real conversation showed the question with **no answer, permanently** — server
  hydration only fires for an EMPTY cache (`selectConversation:1331`).

⭐ The server had finished and persisted the turn the whole time (that is what
`recoverTurn` exists for). Only the client had no path back to it.

**Fix — new `src/stores/chat.ts`.** Module state outlives every unmount, so the
turn now owns itself: `runTurn`, the SSE, `stopActiveTurn` and the tunnel-recovery
poll all moved there. The answer lands in a queue keyed by conversation; whichever
`ChatPage` mounts next drains it (`createEffect` on `completedSignal` +
`conversationId`). `onMount` reopens the conversation that is still generating
instead of a blank chat. The turn is **never cancelled on navigation** —
architect's call: someone who waited 90 s wants the answer, not the freed GPU.

Consequences worth knowing:
- `busy()` is now global (a turn anywhere disables Send). That was already the
  behaviour within a page; what is new is `generatingHere()`, which gates the
  live-answer block, the deep-search notice and the **Stop button** so another
  chat's turn is neither painted here nor stoppable from here.
- Masking is re-filled **in the page and nowhere else** — the label→value map is
  browser-session state the store deliberately never sees.
- `recoverTurn` no longer abandons when the officer switches chats; the answer is
  queued against its own conversation, so leaving is not a reason to discard it.
- Not covered: a full page RELOAD mid-turn still loses the client's view of it
  (the row is in `query_log`; nothing pulls it back). Cheap follow-up: hydrate
  when the cache ends on an unanswered user turn.

### 2. ⚠️ A project document was visible to EVERY user

Reported as "I shared a document in my project but it is visible to all users".
A source inherits visibility from the FOLDER it is indexed into
(`scope_for_notebook` → `indexed_folders.visibility`), and that folder is created
once per path and reused forever. `upload_documents` sends every upload to the
officer's one uploads folder — and for an **admin** that folder is created
ownerless, i.e. `visibility = 'shared'`. So an admin dropping a file into their
own private project **published it to the whole deployment** and into the indexed
documents list.

Retrieval scoping was never wrong (`visible_source_ids` exclusive mode is intact);
this was ownership stamped at index time.

**Fix**: a project upload gets its own folder (`__project__<pid>`) owned by the
uploader whatever their role, so `folders::insert` makes it private by
construction. ⭐ The server has always read a `projectId` upload field — **the
client simply never sent it**, so the project path was dead code and every
project upload took the corpus route; `uploadDocuments` now sends it.

⚠️ **Retroactive**: documents already uploaded this way are still `shared`.
Flip them in My documents, or by `id` in `sources`.

### 3. Web search stayed ON for every later question

`webSearch` was documented as per-turn ("a deliberate act each time") but nothing
ever cleared it — only `corpusThisTurn` was. One click left it on for the rest of
the session. **Not cosmetic**: with nothing attached a web turn is EXCLUSIVE (the
legal corpus is not consulted at all), so a forgotten toggle silently converted
grounded legal answers into unverified web answers. `submit` now clears it, and
`runInference` takes `web` as a PARAMETER — reading the signal inside would have
returned the value after the clear.

### 4. ⚠️⚠️ Every answer offered "Rule 10" — the same mistake, twice

`bureaucrat.toml` `[capability.guidance].offer` carried one illustrative
question, *"What is the appeal period under Rule 10?"*, to demonstrate the FORM.
The model recited it verbatim on every answer, on every subject. This is the
**second** time: the pre-2026-07-29 wording handed it a fixed menu and it recited
that too (trace a2dff44d) — which is why the example was added.

⭐⭐ **An example in this fragment is not read as a demonstration of form; it is
read as the answer.** Replaced with a schema (question openings, and "build it
only from provisions this answer cited"). A comment in the file now says so,
because the fix for round one CAUSED round two.

### 5. No limit on question length

A pasted chapter became the question. The prompt is carved out of a fixed window,
so an enormous question **evicts the retrieved law** and the answer returns
"I don't have enough information" after minutes of GPU time. Cap: **2,000 chars**
(≈500 tokens), `NOVIQ_MAX_QUERY_CHARS` overrides. Sized against the DEPLOYED
window rather than a guess: `NOVIQ_VLLM_MAX_MODEL_LEN=8192` less the 1,024
`gen_reserve_qa` leaves ~7,168 tokens for persona + history + law + question, so
the cap costs the law ~7%. Longer text is a document — attaching it is supported
and strictly better, since an attachment is retrieved FROM rather than crammed
into the prompt. Enforced in
`api/query.rs` **before** the audit row, the spawn and the generation permit —
the composer's `maxlength` + counter is the courtesy half, not the gate.
`chars()` not `len()`: a byte cap would refuse a legitimate Urdu question at a
third of the stated limit. ⚠️ The desktop `send_message` command is uncapped;
the web server is the deployment.

## 2026-08-07 (F027 UI, cont.) — chat switching, delete, responsive

Four follow-ups from the architect testing the live feature, in order.

**1. `New chat` created a chat and never opened it (`f3c0b48`).** Navigating
between two conversations on the SAME route **reuses the component** — `onMount`
does not run again. Reading the conversation id only in `onMount` meant the URL
changed while the transcript stayed put, so chats were created server-side and
never shown; clicking any other chat in the rail did nothing either. Fixed with a
deferred `createEffect` on `routeParams.conversationId` calling the existing
`selectConversation()`. ⭐ **A route-param change is not a mount.**

**2. No delete on project chats (`69805fd`).** Adding the button alone would have
been wrong: `project_chat.conversation_id` is a bare TEXT primary key with **no
conversation table to reference**, so it cascades from `project` only, and
`delete_conversation` has never touched it. A "deleted" chat would have stayed in
the listing forever. New `POST /delete_project_chat` owns exactly the membership
row; ownership is checked on the **chat** (which already carries `owner_id`), not
a client-supplied project id (ADR-0029). The client then does what the global rail
does — cache, attachments, migration-020 soft hide — so the two cannot drift.

**3. Deleting the open chat spawned a replacement (`0e130b3`).** The cleanup
called `newChat()`, which in project mode calls `startProjectChat` — **creating a
chat server-side**. A fresh "New chat" appeared in the deleted one's slot and read
as the chat coming back. Now moves to the most recent survivor, or the project
page when none remain. ⭐ **Creating is something the user asks for, never a side
effect of deleting.**

**4. Responsive pass (`b34d445`).** The project *chat* was already responsive —
project mode renders inside the existing `<aside>` elements, which carry the
compact drawer treatment. The project *pages* had **zero breakpoints in all four
files**.
- **Real defect**: the Add-documents panel had no max height and no internal
  scrolling, so a viewport shorter than the panel (phone in landscape) clipped
  the footer and put the Add button off-screen, unreachable. Now `max-h-[90vh]`
  flex column, scrolling on the **body only**, header/tabs/footer pinned, and a
  bottom sheet below `sm`.
- Rows stack below `sm` instead of squeezing a truncated name between two text
  buttons; share form stacks; headers wrap; `break-words` on a phone and
  `sm:truncate` above. Tap targets padded — they were text-sized.

⚠️ **Verifying a UI deploy**: grep the hashed bundle named in `dist/index.html`,
and check the **CSS** for escaped selectors (`.sm\:flex-row`) — a plain
`grep "sm:flex-row"` over ssh returns 0 because the shell eats the backslash and
Tailwind escapes the colon. Compare local and served hashes instead; they match
when the deploy is honest.

## 2026-08-07 (F027) — you could not put documents IN a project

**Deployed `9a2133d8`.** Found by the architect on first real use.

`ProjectPage` said *"No documents yet. Until you add some, questions in this
project have nothing to search"* — and offered **no way to add any**. Only a
remove handler existed. The single route in was a shared copy from another user,
so a project you created yourself was a **dead end**.

⭐ The backend half had been there the whole time: `add_project_documents`
attaches already-indexed sources by id. Only the UI was missing — the same shape
as the blank chat screen: F027's server was finished and its client was not.

New `AddProjectDocuments` panel, two tabs:
- **Upload new** — the existing `uploadDocuments` pipeline, then the files are
  resolved to source ids **by name** via `listSourcesInFolder` and attached.
  ⚠️ By name deliberately: the uploads folder also holds the officer's earlier
  uploads, so attaching the whole folder would sweep unrelated documents in.
- **My documents** — pick anything already indexed and not already present, so a
  document is never stored twice.

Wired at both entry points: a header button, and a call-to-action **inside the
empty state that previously only described the problem**.

## 2026-08-07 (F027 UI) — a project is now a workspace, not a filter

**Deployed `528f4dac`.** ⭐ First **fast-forward** push since merging `release`
into `027-my-projects` — no cherry-pick.

### The structural defect

`ProjectPage` sent you to `/chat/:id`, which renders the **global** `ChatPage`:
left rail = every conversation you own, right rail = the **whole corpus**
document tree. So a brand-new project chat looked like it already had history and
documents. ⚠️ **Answers were never leaking** — the server derives the project from
`conversation_id` via `project_chat` (FR-038, ADR-0028). A presentation defect
that destroyed the mental model.

Earlier the same day: `/chat/:id` **did not exist at all**, so "New chat" from a
project rendered a blank screen (fixed in `1562b8f6`).

### Fix — `ChatPage` in project mode

New route `/projects/:projectId/chat/:conversationId`. Gated on
`inProjectRoute()`, **additively**: left rail lists only this project's chats;
"New chat" calls `startProjectChat` so the chat *belongs* to the project instead
of minting a bare uuid that belongs to nothing; right rail renders the new
`ProjectDocuments` panel; a header names the project and links back; the global
conversation cache is not loaded.

⭐⭐ **Two near-duplications caught by reading before writing:**
1. `inProject()` **already existed** — a signal the SERVER answers, deciding
   whether the per-turn corpus tick shows. Mine is route-derived and decides
   which project's rails to render. **Different questions; kept both**, named
   `inProjectRoute()`.
2. I had built a corpus toggle into the new panel. `CorpusToggle` already owns
   that flag and clears it on every send (FR-017). **Removed it** — two controls
   for a deliberately non-persisted setting is two sources of truth.

`DocumentTree` was left alone: it always loads the full corpus and has no scoping
prop, so a small dedicated panel beat bending a much larger component.

### Styling

Both project pages shipped with **default Tailwind** and no Noviq tokens. Theming
only the centred container left the surround dark — ⭐ **`AppShell` sets no
background; every page owns its own.** Now a full-bleed `bg-noviq-paper` shell
with the container nested inside. Creating the first project is a centred rounded
card; it collapses to a compact row once projects exist, and the old "no projects
yet" fallback is gone rather than sitting under a card already asking for one.

### Also this session

`Features` tab in the admin console (`5f907af1`) — the My Projects gate moved out
of "Model & Inference", which is not what it is. And the gate needed a browser
reload because **`App.tsx` and Admin each held their own copy of the flag**, read
once at mount; now one shared signal in `stores/projects`.

⚠️ Verify UI deploys by grepping the **hashed bundle named in `dist/index.html`**,
not the commit — `deploy.sh` fails soft on the frontend build.

## 2026-08-07 (tier 5e) — the chunking-audit remainder is MOSTLY ALREADY DONE

Checked the three outstanding items against the **live corpus** instead of
trusting the 27-day-old audit note. Two are obsolete; the third is one provision.

| item | status (verified live) |
|---|---|
| SPPA-2009 `manual`→`act` | ✅ **already fixed** — `Sindh Public Procurement Act 2009 → act`, by the title-first classification (ADR-0019 follow-up) |
| `act.rs` + Item for the Constitution | ✅ **obsolete** — **280 distinct articles, ZERO missing in 1..280**. Classified `manual`, but `resolve_citation_unit` re-mints its labels as "Article", so the profile does not matter |
| `manual.rs` port for RoB | ⚠️ **one gap, not ~16** — RoB has 58 numbered provisions spanning 2–60, missing only **13** |

### RoB Rule 13 — root-caused, NOT fixed

Rule 13 is **absorbed into Rule 12**. The stored chunk reads:

> `Rule 12  12. The Chief Minister may require the law Department to obtain orders of`
> `Power to  the Governor on the summoning prorogation and dissolution of the give`
> `direction  Assembly.  regarding  Assembly  13.  13. The Chief Minister may approve…`

⭐ **Cause: the marginal catchline column is interleaved into the body text**
("Power to give direction regarding Assembly" is a margin note, not prose), so
`13.` never lands at line-start and the `^\d+\.` heading regex cannot see it.
This is the RC-A family again, but the fix is **marginal-note separation** (the
sidecar's `provision_titles` path), not another opener pattern.

⚠️ **Deliberately not attempted at the end of a long session.** A mid-line
heading heuristic ("match `N.` after a run of 2+ spaces") is exactly the shape
that mints FALSE provisions — the failure this corpus has already had twice
(front-matter rosters as `Article 1..46`, schedule lists as `Article 4`).
**Never add a matcher without listing what it newly accepts.**

### ▶ Re-index verdict

**Safe to run now.** Nothing outstanding would change its results except RoB
Rule 13, which is already absent today — re-indexing neither fixes nor worsens
it. The re-index banks Pass 3a's measured win (319 title-box chunks).
