**The three that remain are all understood:** a date-range filter the plan
language does not express (it now filters to July alone rather than ignoring the
range); the FEC share reading **27.22%** because it divides by the sheet's
printed 845 rather than the corrected 850 — arithmetically right, and above the
25% threshold either way, so the forum conclusion is unaffected; and a grader
artifact where a correct `51,500` is marked against `51,500.0`.

## 2026-08-03 — Spreadsheet arithmetic: the model plans, Rust computes

> *"our app is not good in finance… if someone attaches a spreadsheet and asks
> finance questions it is not able to answer those."* Measured before changing
> anything: **19 of 53 correct** across 7 workbooks.

**The measurement is the point.** The failures were not retrieval failures:
`Financial_Test_1` extracts to ONE 393-character chunk, so the model received
every row and still answered `1,263,651` for a revenue total of `1,273,872` —
in bold, with a citation mark. Asked `107506 + 107559` with no document and no
retrieval at all, it answered `415065`. It also failed `arg_max` over ten rows
(said Sep 64,256 when Oct is 94,064) and `arg_min` (said Jan when Apr is lower).
`Complex_A_Scale` (240 rows) returned **HTTP 400 from vLLM in ~15 ms on every
turn** — the rows overflowed `max_model_len`, and the user-facing text blamed
the inference engine rather than the document size. 0/8.

A control fixture settles it: `Complex_C_CachedFormulas` is the same shape with
the formula results already cached in the file, and it scored 4/4. **When the
sheet has computed the numbers, the app is fine. When it must compute, it isn't.**

**So this is not a prompt problem, a chunking problem or a retrieval problem,
and no amount of tuning any of those fixes it.**

**The split** (`services/tabular/`), the same one ADR-0019 drew for counting —
*the model decides what to compute; the code computes it*:
- `sheet.rs` — workbook → **typed** table. `extract_xlsx` calls `.to_string()`
  on every cell and discards the types calamine already knows; that is fine for
  retrieval and fatal for arithmetic. Also recovers numbers written as text
  (`Rs. 1,250.00`, `12.5%`, `1,234`) and **accounting negatives — `(45.20)` is
  −45.20**, and reading it as positive flips the sign of every overspend.
- `plan.rs` — a closed set of ops (sum/avg/min/max/count/count_distinct/arg_max/
  arg_min/lookup/ratio/list/group_sum) with filters and a row selector. The
  model emits one small JSON object; **the executor is pure, total and
  unit-tested against the exact figures prod got wrong.**
- `cross_foot` — the sheet's printed `Total` rows checked against the sum of its
  own rows. No model, no question. On `Complex_B` the printed grand total is 845
  where the items sum to 850, and prod reported 845 as "the correct total
  capital cost" because it had no reason to disbelieve the sheet.

**Total rows are excluded from every sum** — including one is the fastest way to
get an answer exactly twice too large.

**The model never sees the data.** `describe()` sends column names and three
sample rows. That fixes the 240-row overflow (the prompt no longer grows with
the sheet) and is the stronger privacy position, since the active engine may be
a hosted API: the figures stay on the box and only the headers cross.

**A plan that does not fit the sheet is refused, with the column names**, never
worked around — falling back to the model there would reintroduce exactly the
invented numbers this lane exists to remove.

⚠️ **`wants_computation` matches whole words, not substrings.** The first cut
listed `"sum"`, which also fires on *summarise*, *summary* and *consumption* —
so "summarise this document" routed into the arithmetic lane. The unit test
caught it; the guard now tokenises.

**Verified:** 19 new unit tests pass, `cargo check --lib` and `--bin
noviq-server` clean. The other 70 lib-test failures are the pre-existing
`libssl.so.3` test-Postgres problem (`NOVIQ_TEST_PG_INSTALL_DIR`), unrelated.

**Result, same 53 questions, same harness: 19/53 → 49/53.** All three original
`Financial_Test` workbooks went 2,3,4 /10 → **10/10 each**; the 240-row sheet
went 0/8 → 7/8 (the overflow is gone); the messy-types sheet 3/5 → 5/5. Of the
four remaining, one is a **grader artifact** (my normaliser strips the decimal
point, so a correct `51,500` is marked against `51,500.0` — the true figure is
50/53), one is a date-range filter the plan language does not express, one is a
ratio over a totals row, and one is the corpus join below.

⚠️ **Three defects found only by running the eval, all of the same shape — a
wrong number presented as computed**, which is worse than the model guessing
because the wording invites trust:
- **Two-row header detection was too eager.** A flat header followed by a
  mostly-text data row read that row as a sub-header: the first transaction was
  swallowed (239 of 240 counted) and columns came out named `Amount · 1241226`.
  A merged span leaves trailing cells Empty, so a real two-row header has a GAP
  in its first row; a flat one does not. That is now the test.
- **Trailing rows were counted.** A footnote and a `Utilisation … 94.2%` line
  below a blank separator added 94.2 to a total of 2,390.45. Reading now stops
  at the first blank row once data has begun.
- **An unsupported period qualifier was silently dropped.** "Total for Jul-Sep
  2024" returned the total for the whole sheet, labelled as computed. The
  planner now declines rather than ignoring a range it cannot express.

⚠️ **The first deploy moved the score only 19 → 23.** The lane fired on just 12
of 53 turns: `plan_prompt` had no no-think prefix, so Qwen3 opened a `<think>`
block and spent the entire token budget without emitting JSON. That is why
`planner.rs` exists — "what is the total revenue" names an operation and a
column, and the column names are in the sheet, so **no language model is
required at all**. The model is now only a fallback for unmatched phrasings, and
45 of 53 turns are answered with no model in the loop.

**Known gap:** "which forum approves this project?" still fails. The rule is
indexed and citable (Manual for Development Projects 2019 ¶2.8 — DDWP up to
Rs 2,000M *provided FEC < 25%*), but an attachment-scoped turn never searches
the corpus, so the compute lane and the legal lane do not yet meet. That join is
the next piece of work, not this one.

## 2026-08-03 — The chat sidebar ignored the categories (021 follow-up)

> Reported straight after 021 shipped: *"i grouped the documents it is showing in
> admin panel but not reflected to chat tab where on right side it is showing all
> documents under admin folder only."* Correct, and it was a gap in the original
> delivery, not a defect in it — I wired categories into the **admin** document
> list and never into the officer-facing picker.

**Why it looked like that.** `DocumentTree` is a *folder* tree, and folders are
where the files were written, not how the corpus is organised: `uploads/admin`
(the whole shared corpus) plus one private folder per user. So every instrument
sat under a single node called "admin" and the admin's categories were nowhere.

**Now grouped by category** — categories in the admin's display order, then
Uncategorised, then the viewer's own uploads last.

⚠️ **Folders were carrying something categories do not: F021 ownership.** Dropping
the folder row would have silently thrown away the `Private` / `Shared · user`
badges and mixed a user's private uploads into Uncategorised alongside the shared
corpus. So ownership **moves to a per-document badge**, and private uploads get
their own **"My documents"** group rather than being folded in. Categories are
corpus organisation and only ever apply to shared documents; personal uploads
have no category and must not look as though they do.

**Officers could not read the category names.** `/admin/categories` is
`AdminUser`-gated, so an officer would have got a 403 and an unlabelled sidebar.
Added `GET /api/categories` (any signed-in user) returning names and order via
`corpus_category::list_names`. It deliberately **omits `document_count`**: that
count is computed over every row in `sources`, including documents the viewer
cannot retrieve, so publishing it would disclose the size of a corpus they have
no access to. The sidebar renders counts from the documents it was actually given.

`stores/categories.ts` picks the endpoint by role, so there is still exactly ONE
category list in the app — the property that keeps the manager and the pickers
from disagreeing after a rename.

**Collapse state inverted to `collapsed`** (default empty = all open) so a group
that appears after mount — a category created while the sidebar is open — is not
silently collapsed. With no categories defined the sidebar renders as the flat
list it was before 021.

**Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vite build` clean, `cargo check
--no-default-features --features server --bin noviq-server` clean on the VM.

## 2026-08-02 — Corpus organisation: categories and withdrawal (migration 021)

> The corpus is one flat, unlabelled list of nineteen instruments. An officer
> browsing it has nothing to group them by, and nothing tells them which are
> actually in service. The admin had no way to supply either.

**Both are metadata. Nothing here moves a file, re-chunks, re-embeds or
re-indexes.** A category is a column on `sources`; a withdrawal is a timestamp on
`sources`. That is the whole reason re-filing an entire corpus is instant and a
withdrawal is reversible in one click.

**Migration 021** (additive): `corpus_category(id, name UNIQUE, sort_order,
created_at)`, `sources.category_id` (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), `sources.disabled_at`,
plus an index on each new column.

- **One category per document**, like a folder, so "which category is this in"
  always has a single answer. `NULL` = Uncategorised, where every existing
  document and every new upload starts.
- **Deleting a category never deletes documents** — `ON DELETE SET NULL` drops
  them back to Uncategorised. The delete route returns how many were released so
  the UI can say so rather than leave the admin guessing.
- **`disabled_at` is a timestamp, not a boolean**, because it records *when* a
  document was withdrawn — which the admin list shows and a boolean could not.

**Enforcement is in exactly one place.** `visible_source_ids` (`repositories/
sources.rs`) now excludes `disabled_at IS NOT NULL` on both its branches, desktop
included. That one function is what chat retrieval, global search and citation
opening all scope through, so a withdrawal takes effect across all three at once,
on the next turn, with no re-index — the same property that makes F021 visibility
work. The corpus **listing** reads deliberately still return withdrawn documents:
listing and retrieval are different questions and collapsing them into one query
would make a withdrawn document look deleted.

**Routes** (`api/admin.rs`, all `AdminUser`-gated): `GET/POST /admin/categories`,
`POST /admin/categories/:id`, `POST /admin/categories/:id/delete`,
`POST /admin/sources/categorize`, `POST /admin/sources/:id/disabled`. A duplicate
category name is a **400, not a 500** — "Finance already exists" is an answer the
admin can act on.

**The DTO had to carry the columns.** `SourceDto` and `repositories::sources::
Source` gained `category_id` + `disabled_at`; without them the admin document list
could not group or grey anything. All six `query_as::<_, Source>` sites use
`SELECT *`, so no query needed changing.

**UI.** New `components/CorpusCategories.tsx` (create / rename / reorder / delete,
mounted in Admin → Indexing & Data) and `stores/categories.ts`. Filing happens in
the **document list**, not the manager — that is where the documents and the
selection already are. Every mutation re-reads the server list rather than
patching the local array: `document_count` is computed server-side and a delete
releases documents, neither of which the client can derive without
re-implementing the query.

`IndexedFolders` now groups by category with **Uncategorised first** — deliberate,
not cosmetic: a new upload is always Uncategorised, and this list's design rule
since the folder tree was removed is that the file you just added is the easiest
one to find. With no categories defined it renders exactly as before.

⚠️ **The officer-facing scope picker had to change too, and this is the part that
would have been a real defect.** `DocumentTree` is how an officer scopes a
question to specific documents. Left alone, it would have offered withdrawn
documents as selectable — the officer picks one, `visible_source_ids` excludes it
server-side, retrieval returns nothing and the answer refuses, with the picker
having shown the document as available. **The scope the picker offers and the
scope retrieval honours must be the same set.** Withdrawn documents are now
excluded from the default selection, from folder select-all, and from the
`@`-mention catalog, and are rendered struck through and marked *Unavailable* —
still listed, because an officer who used one yesterday needs to see where it
went, but plainly inert. Same "two places measuring one thing" trap as before.

**Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vite build` clean, and `cargo check
--no-default-features --features server --bin noviq-server` clean on the VM
(warnings only, none in the changed files), run in a throwaway detached worktree
at `/opt/noviq/check-021` with its own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` — `release` and
`origin/release` were never touched, so the 2-minute deploy poller stayed inert.

⚠️ **The first check failed, and the reason is worth recording.** Adding the two
columns to `Source` broke `repositories::sources::create`, which mirrors the row
it just inserted back as a struct literal (`Ok(Source { … })`). The audit that
preceded the change grepped for `source_repo::Source {` and `sources::Source {`
and found nothing — **it missed the bare `Source {` inside the type's own
module**, which is the one place the qualified name is never used. Both fields
are `None` there, correctly: the INSERT sets neither column, so a new document is
Uncategorised and in service. When adding a field to a struct, grep the bare name
as well as the qualified one.

⚠️ Production builds with `--features llm,server,cuda`; this check used `server`
alone, which skips a llama.cpp/CUDA rebuild. Every changed line is outside those
gates — the only `SourceDto` construction sites are the three in
`services/indexing.rs` and the only `Source` literal is the one above — so the
narrower feature set still covers the whole delta.

⚠️ **021 cannot be cherry-picked onto `release` alone.** The `admin.rs` handlers
are appended directly after `split_source`, which is part of the still-unshipped
compendium-split work, so the patch has no context to land on in the deployed
tree. Shipping this means either taking the held commits with it or rebasing the
handlers onto a `release` base first.

⚠️ **Same rollback caveat as 020.** Additive at the schema level is not a
reversible deploy: `init_schema` runs the migrator with `ignore_missing = false`,
so once 021 has applied a pre-021 binary fails at startup with `VersionMissing`.
Rolling back requires deleting the 021 row from `_sqlx_migrations`; the columns
are inert to older code and can stay.

## 2026-08-02 — Reading an old chat pushed it to the top of the rail

The rail is ordered by activity, and **reading is not activity**. Opening a
conversation hydrates `turns`, which the persistence effect could not tell apart
from answering in it, so merely looking at an old chat re-sorted it to the top and
displaced whatever the officer was actually working on.

`ChatPage` now keeps a `railSeen` map of how many turns each conversation had when
it was opened, set at all three points where turns arrive without being authored:
`selectConversation` (local cache), the server-hydration path (migration 020), and
the effect itself. Only a genuinely new turn re-sorts. A conversation the rail has
never heard of is still inserted regardless — otherwise a brand-new chat's first
turn would go unlisted.

Frontend-only; follow-on from the account-bound history work below, which is what
made server-hydrated transcripts a second silent source of "activity".

## 2026-08-01 — Chat history was bound to the device, not the account

> Reported from prod: *"chat history is bound to device only, as we sign in to
> other device it vanishes."* Correct — and it also vanished on clearing browser
> data, or on the same device in a different browser.

**The bug.** `ChatPage` wrote the entire history to `localStorage` and nowhere
else: `noviq:conversations` for the rail and `noviq:turns:<id>` per transcript.
Browser storage is per-origin *per profile*, so a second device started empty.

**The turns were never actually lost.** The server has recorded every turn since
F014 in `query_log` — `user_id`, `conversation_id`, `question`, `answer`,
`citations_json`, `created_at`, one row per turn, and `poll_turn` already reads
it back for tunnel-timeout recovery. The history existed server-side the whole
time; there was simply no route by which the officer who wrote it could read it.
So this is three read endpoints and two columns, not a new subsystem.

**Migration 020** (additive, rollback-safe):
- `query_log.response_json` — the full serialized `TurnResponse`. `citations_json`
  alone cannot rebuild a chat: web results, capability, `scoped_to_attachment`
  (the "Search all documents" button) and `trace_id` all live on the response.
  NULL on pre-existing rows, which replay from answer + citations.
- `query_log.hidden_at` — soft delete, see below.
- `idx_query_log_user_conv` — both new reads are (user, conversation, time).

**Routes** (`api/history.rs`, all scoped to the session's `user.id`, never a body
field): `/api/list_conversations`, `/api/conversation_turns`,
`/api/hide_conversation`.

**Delete is a soft delete, deliberately.** `query_log` is also the *only* record
of what was asked — the admin usage panel, activity list and per-user export all
read it. A hard `DELETE` would let any user silently punch holes in that audit
trail. `hidden_at` is set instead; the officer-facing reads filter on it and the
admin reads deliberately do not.

**Masking: placeholders on the second device, by design.** Confidential values
are masked in the browser and the label→value map never leaves it (F020) — the
server only ever received `[NAME_1]`. A chat opened elsewhere therefore *cannot*
show the real values, and now says so on the turn rather than looking corrupt.
Consequence: the **local cache is preferred** whenever it exists, because it is
strictly richer than the server copy. Merge rule — *the server decides which
conversations exist, the local cache supplies the contents of the ones it has*.
That also means one officer's cached chats can never appear in another's rail.

**`clearChatCache()` on logout** (`lib/chatCache.ts`, called from `stores/auth.ts`).
The cache holds questions with the confidential values **unmasked**; on a shared
browser, leaving it behind would hand them to whoever signs in next. Nothing is
lost — the turns are on the server. This also puts the three storage-key strings
in one module instead of two files.

Desktop (Tauri) is unchanged: no session to scope by, so it keeps local history.

**Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vite build` clean, and `cargo check
--no-default-features --features server` clean on the VM (warnings only, all
pre-existing) — first against the `release-deploy` base, then again on the
`release` base this actually shipped from.

⚠️ **Rollback caveat.** Additive at the *schema* level is not the same as a
reversible deploy. `init_schema` runs the sqlx migrator with `ignore_missing =
false`, so once 020 has applied, a PRE-020 binary fails at startup with
`VersionMissing`. Rolling the code back requires deleting the 020 row from
`_sqlx_migrations` (the columns can stay — older code never selects them).
Ordering is fine in the other direction: sqlx 0.8 has no monotonicity check, so
020 landing on prod ahead of the still-unshipped 018/019 is safe, and all three
touch disjoint tables.

**Shipped alone**, cherry-picked onto `release` — NOT by pushing
`release-deploy`, which would have dragged the twelve commits being held for
beta testing into prod with it.

## 2026-07-31 — A search hit was a dead end: open the passage like a citation

> Follow-on from the route fix below, reported the moment search started working:
> *"it is not leting user go to that document, like in citation."*

**Two silent failures stacked.**
1. `SearchPage` passed an `onClick` that only `console.log`-ed the file path — a
   T055 placeholder (*"Future: open source in notebook view or file explorer"*)
   that shipped and stayed.
2. `SearchResultCard.handleOpen` then called `openInDefaultApp`, which imports
   `@tauri-apps/plugin-shell` to hand the path to the OS. **That module does not
   exist in the browser**, so it threw into a `console.warn` nobody sees.

Net effect: the click did nothing, and said nothing about why — the same silent
`catch{}` shape as the clipboard-to-Word bug. A browser also has no business
opening OS file paths, so the desktop call is now gated behind `isTauri()`.

**Fix.** The card opens **`ChunkViewer`** — the same drawer a clicked citation
opens — with `focusChunkId` set to the matching chunk, so a search hit and a
citation land the reader at the same passage in the same UI.
`audience="user"` is passed **explicitly and is required**: the prop defaults to
`"admin"` (the corpus-wide console view) which would 403 an officer. That path
reads `/source_chunks`, scoped through `visible_source_ids` — the same invariant
the new `/api/global_search` uses, so **anything a user can find they can also
open, and nothing beyond it**.

Frontend-only (`FE=1, BE=0`) — no CUDA rebuild, no restart.

## 2026-07-31 — Global Search had no server route (405 read as "API error")

> ✅ **DEPLOYED** — `release` @ `4372f02`, backend rebuild + restart 19:57 PKT.
> Route verified live (401, was 405). **Not yet exercised with a real query** —
> no credentials on this machine; the architect was asked to try it.

**Reported from prod:** Global Search showed "API error" on web *and* mobile.
Not a responsive regression — `SearchPage.tsx` had only had padding changed.

**The bug.** `global_search` was only ever registered as a **Tauri command**
(`lib.rs:124`). When the product became client-server the HTTP route was never
added, so `/api/global_search` did not exist and the server answered **405**,
which the frontend surfaced as "API error". The Search tab has therefore never
worked on the web build.

**How it was found — worth reusing.** Probe an endpoint unauthenticated: every
live route answers **401**, an absent one answers **405** (the fallback handler).
`/api/global_search` → 405 while `/api/query`, `/api/me`, `/api/source_chunks`
→ 401. `grep -c '\.route(' api/router.rs` = 76, none matching "search".

**The fix is NOT a verbatim port, and that matters.** `commands::search::
global_search` selects across *every* indexed chunk. Correct for a single-user
desktop app; on a multi-user server it would let any officer read excerpts from
every document in the database — **including other users' private uploads**.
This repo already recorded that lesson for `browse_chunks` (see 2026-07-28: the
officer-facing `/api/source_chunks` is scoped precisely so a citation link cannot
become a way to read documents the caller may not see).

So `api/documents.rs::global_search` is scoped through `visible_source_ids` —
shared corpus + the caller's own documents. Conversation attachments are
deliberately **out** of scope: this is a corpus search, not a chat turn, so there
is no conversation to attribute them to. The desktop `indexed_folders` predicate
is dropped (server-side corpus documents need not sit under a registered desktop
folder; visibility is the rule that matters). Embedding runs on `spawn_blocking`
— `embed_one` is CPU-bound ONNX and would otherwise stall the async runtime for
every concurrent searcher. Empty query and empty visibility short-circuit before
touching pgvector. Response shape matches `SearchResult` field-for-field
(`relevance_score = 1.0 - distance`), so one frontend type serves both transports
and **no client change was needed**.

**Verification.** `cargo check --no-default-features --features server` clean, run
in a **throwaway worktree on the VM with a separate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`** — never
the prod tree — then removed (disk unchanged, 42G free). There is no Rust
toolchain on the Windows dev machine, so without this the deploy would have been
blind. Post-deploy: `/api/global_search` → 401.

> ⚠️ **The divergence trap caught this twice in one session.** The first
> `cargo check` failed with `admin::inspect_source` / `admin::split_source` not
> found — because `release-deploy`'s `router.rs` was copied onto a `release`-based
> worktree, and those compendium-split routes do not exist on `release`. **Errors
> from a cross-branch file copy are not errors in your change.** Re-checked with
> the right file before pushing.

## 2026-07-31 — Responsive layout for mobile / tablet / laptop (all 4 parts)

> ✅ **CODE COMPLETE across every reachable surface.** `tsc --noEmit` exit 0,
> `vite build` clean. **NOT deployed, and never opened in a real browser** — see
> "Verification actually performed" below for exactly what was and wasn't checked.

**Reported by the architect:** "we still don't have responsive layout for mobile
and tablet and for laptop." Confirmed by audit — the frontend carried **6
responsive utilities across 10,269 lines** (`Admin.tsx` ×4,
`CitationFeedback.tsx` ×2, both from the 2026-07-03 feedback-panel polish).
Everything else is fixed-width. The viewport meta tag was already present
(`index.html:5`), so that was never the cause.

**The three structural blockers found (scope agreed: all surfaces incl. Admin,
down to 390px):**
1. `ChatPage.tsx:1074`/`:1876` — hard three-column shell, left rail `w-64`
   (256px) + right rail `w-72` (288px), both `flex-shrink-0`, never collapse.
   At 1366×768 that leaves ~820px for the conversation; at 768px the rails alone
   eat 544px.
2. `App.tsx:69` — nav bar is one non-wrapping row (logo + 4 text links + badge +
   gear + bell + avatar), every child `flex-shrink-0` → overflow below ~700px.
3. `App.tsx:191` — root shell is `h-screen overflow-hidden`, so overflow was
   **clipped and unreachable**, not scrollable. This is why it read as "broken"
   rather than merely cramped.

**Part 1 — primitives + app shell.**
- **`src/lib/breakpoints.ts` (new)** — `useMediaQuery` / `useBelow` / `useFrom` /
  `useIsMobile` (below `md`) / `useIsCompact` (below `lg`), hand-rolled on
  `matchMedia` with `onCleanup`. **No new dependency** (`@solid-primitives/media`
  deliberately not added for ~15 lines). Exports `SCREENS` matching Tailwind 3
  defaults — a component branching on `isBelowLg()` in TS and styling with `lg:`
  in markup **must** agree on the boundary or a drawer and a static rail can both
  render at once. Non-browser safe: no `matchMedia` → always `false` → the old
  desktop layout, so nothing regresses.
- **`App.tsx` nav bar** — the four page links move into a hamburger dropdown
  below `md`; inline row at `md`+. Links extracted to a `PAGES` array so both
  renderings stay in sync. Added `pagesOpen` to the existing one-menu-at-a-time
  discipline (all three toggles + the click-away backdrop now go through
  `closeAllMenus`). Padding/gaps step down at `sm`.
- **`index.css`** — `.app-viewport` (`100vh` then `100dvh`, fallback-first) now
  used by the shell instead of `h-screen`: on iOS/Android `100vh` counts the
  space behind the collapsing URL bar, which put the chat composer below the fold
  and unreachable. Also `.tap-target` (44px min hit area under
  `@media (pointer: coarse)`, WCAG 2.5.5) — **defined but not yet applied**.
- **`App.tsx` storage-low banner** — `min-w-0` + non-shrinking dismiss button so
  a long message wraps instead of squeezing the `×` off the row.

**Part 2 — ChatPage rails (`ChatPage.tsx`).** Both rails become `fixed inset-y-0`
slide-over drawers below `lg` and revert to static columns at `lg`+. The
positioning needs **no JS branch** — `lg:static lg:w-64 lg:translate-x-0` is
emitted after the base `fixed … -translate-x-full`, same specificity, so it wins
(verified in the built CSS, see below). JS drives only the open/closed transform.
Opening one rail closes the other (two stacked overlays at 390px leave no way back
to the conversation); `newChat`/`selectConversation` close the rails, since acting
on an overlay must hand the screen back; a `createEffect` clears drawer state when
the viewport widens, so a later narrowing doesn't re-open a stale drawer. Backdrop
sits at `z-30` under the rails' `z-40` and only mounts when compact, so it can
never intercept clicks in the desktop three-column layout. A compact-only toolbar
in `<main>` carries the two toggles. Transcript/composer/bubble padding steps down
below `sm`. **Rail semantics from 2026-07-02 are unchanged** — left is still chat
sessions, right is still the DocumentTree; only presentation is conditional.

**Part 3 — remaining user surfaces.** `SearchPage`, `SettingsPage`, `LoginScreen`,
`ComingSoon` (which is the whole of Workflow + Meeting Assistant — both pages just
delegate to it), and `DeepSearchNetwork` (decorative canvas 300px → 180px below
`sm`; it measures its own rect so it re-fits). `ConfidentialComposer`,
`DocumentTree`, `IndexedFolders`, `SearchResultCard`, `AnswerBody` and
`ChunkViewer` were **already fluid** and needed nothing.

**Part 4 — Admin console (`Admin.tsx`).** Tab bar scrolls sideways
(`overflow-x-auto` + `whitespace-nowrap`) instead of wrapping and pushing content
down a line. The three tables were treated differently on purpose:
- **user list (10 columns)** → new **`.stack-table`** (in `index.css`): below `md`
  each row becomes a card and each cell a "LABEL: value" line, the label coming
  from `data-label` on the `<td>`. Done in **CSS, not a second JSX branch**, so the
  row markup stays one source of truth — a duplicated card branch is exactly how
  two renderings of the same data drift apart. `data-label=""` opts a cell out
  (used for the actions cell and the `colspan=10` activity panel).
- **query traces (6 short columns)** and **split-plan editor (4)** → `min-w` inside
  an `overflow-x-auto` box: horizontal scroll is genuinely fine at that column
  count, and stacking them would be worse.
- **storage-per-user (3 columns)** → unchanged, it already fits at 390px.
Two `min-w-[Nrem]` selects became `w-full sm:w-auto sm:min-w-[Nrem]`.

**Verification actually performed — and what was not.**
- `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; `vite build` clean.
- **Cascade order confirmed in the built CSS**, since the whole rail approach rests
  on it: `.-translate-x-full` at byte ~27.9k, `.lg\:translate-x-0` at ~68.5k —
  later wins. (An earlier check appeared to show the `lg:` utilities missing
  entirely; that was a **grep quoting artifact** — CSS escapes the colon as `\:`.
  They are all present.)
- `.stack-table` rules confirmed present in the `(max-width: 767.98px)` block, and
  the 9 `data-label`s confirmed to match the 9 corresponding `<th>` texts in order.
- ❌ **Never rendered in a browser at any width.** `/api` is same-origin with no
  vite dev proxy, so `npm run dev` alone hits the auth gate and cannot reach
  ChatPage; a real check needs the VPN + a prod login. **This is the main open
  risk** — every layout claim above is static analysis, not observation.

**Deliberately skipped (not oversights).**
- `KnowledgeGraphPage.tsx`, `components/knowledge-graph/*`, `components/meeting/MeetingPanel.tsx`
  — **imported nowhere**; Workflow replaced the Knowledge Graph tab. Making dead
  code responsive would be pure cost.
- `overlay/OverlayWindow.tsx` (`w-[480px]`) — a Tauri popup whose window is sized
  by Tauri itself, and Tauri is vestigial in the client-server product.

**Unrelated finding, NOT fixed (one-character fix, architect's call).**
`ConfidentialComposer.tsx` line 32 embeds a **raw NUL byte** as a key delimiter:
`` `${type}<NUL>${text}` `` instead of the `\0` escape. It compiles and behaves
correctly, but `file` reports the source as `data`, so **grep/ripgrep treat all 565
lines as binary and skip them silently in every repo-wide search** — this sweep
included; that component had to be inspected by hand. Writing `\0` instead of the
literal byte is behaviour-identical and makes the file searchable again.

**Follow-ups / risks.**
- Browser verification at 390 / 768 / 1366 is outstanding and should happen before
  this rides a deploy.
- `.tap-target` (44px coarse-pointer hit area) is applied to the new drawer/rail
  controls only — the older icon buttons across Admin and Settings still have
  sub-44px targets on touch.

## 2026-07-31 — Web search: the toggle now decides the turn, and the lane remembers

> ✅ **DEPLOYED — the only two commits shipped today.** Prod `release` @
> `0cbe5aa` (`e55022c6` + `ac4936aa` here, patched on as `be86f41` + `0cbe5aa`).
> ⚠️ **Neither has been exercised in a real turn** — compile + unit tested only.

**Reported from prod.** "what are new amendments IN sindh public procurement
rules in 2024" answered *"No amendments are recorded for `<the entire question>`
in the indexed documents"*, while the same question phrased "amendments OCCURED
in …" was answered from the web. **One intervening word** decided whether the
toggle the officer had switched on applied at all.

**Three defects behind it.**
1. **Web search lived in `guidance` alone.** Every other capability silently
   ignored the switch. `amendments in` matches a Timeline cue
   (`intent_router/classifier.rs:80`) → `AmendmentChain`, a SQL/graph lookup that
   reads NEITHER the corpus NOR the web. Web on now routes the turn to the web
   lane whatever the classifier decided — the toggle is an explicit instruction
   and outranks classification.
2. **Whole-question-as-provision.** Dispatch did
   `extract_provision_ref(text).unwrap_or_else(|| text.to_string())`, feeding the
   entire sentence in as the provision to find. No provision reference now means
   the capability does not apply and the question goes to normal retrieval. That
   refusal also claimed the indexed documents had been checked by a lane that
   never reads them.
3. **Presentation.** `[W1]` markers were dead text (web answers carry no
   `citations`, so ChatPage dropped them to plain Markdown); the answer was a
   wall of prose where the corpus equivalent is headed and itemised; and all
   twelve results were listed as equals, burying the three the answer rested on.
   Markers are now clickable and AMBER — never citation blue, so an unverified
   web page is never mistaken for an indexed instrument — the prompt asks for a
   lead sentence, a bold heading and a BULLETED LIST when the answer is a set of
   items, and the block splits CITED from the rest behind a disclosure.

**⚠️ Fix 1 made something else worse, and that is the lesson.** Widening the lane
exposed that **the web lane never carried conversation history**: it built its
prompt from scratch (rules + results + current sentence), so it forgot every
earlier turn while the corpus lane has always carried them. A gap that affected
*some* web queries now affected *all* of them. **Widening a lane without first
checking what that lane drops** is the mistake not to repeat.

Fixed in two halves, the SEARCH mattering more than the prompt because no context
rescues results never fetched:
- **Search:** "…SPPR in 2024?" then "and in 2023?" searched the public web for the
  bare word `2023`. On a follow-up (`is_followup_query`, now `pub(crate)`) the
  previous question is prepended before filler-stripping. Deliberately NOT
  `extract_carryover_keywords` — its stop-list drops "sindh", "rules",
  "procurement" because for CORPUS retrieval those match everything; on the open
  web they are the disambiguating words.
- **Prompt:** injects the SAME `prior_turns_block` the corpus lane uses, so both
  lanes remember identically — already ChatML, already capped 600 chars/message
  over the persona window, already EMPTY for a self-contained question (zero cost
  on the common turn, which matters because the web block is large).

**Deploy recipe proven** (`release` is cherry-pick maintained, so bundles do not
apply): `git format-patch -1` → scp → `git clone --shared -b release` on the VM →
**`git remote set-url origin <github>`** (the clone's origin is the prod repo and
refuses the push) → `git config user.email` → `git am --3way` → verify tests AND
`npm run build` on that tree → `git push origin HEAD:release`. ⚠️ `deploy.sh` runs
`git reset --hard`, destroying any tracked modification in the prod worktree.

**Still open here.** `AmendmentChain` answers "none recorded" to every question
because `amendment_events` is empty corpus-wide — the capability is effectively
dead but answers confidently. The Timeline cue remains loose (`amendments in
<anything>`), harmless while web is on, still wrong when it is off.

## 2026-07-30 — One file is not one law: splitting a compendium

> ✅ **Built and verified end-to-end. NOT DEPLOYED — deliberately held until
> after beta testing.** Prod runs `release` @ `1083142` and has none of this.
> ⚠️ Applying it needs a deploy, which auto-ships every commit of 2026-07-30 at
> once (extraction fixes, migrations 018+019, upload detection, the split).

**Why.** `Compendium Rules under SLGA 2013` is **twelve** separate rule-sets in
one PDF, each numbering its provisions from 1. Indexed as a single source it
makes "Rule 4" ambiguous across instruments, yields one meaningless document
summary, cites answers to a book rather than a law, and is the sole reason
`query_router.rs:6537` carries a hand-written demotion for that document. The
pipeline assumes file == instrument; **the unit of indexing should be the
INSTRUMENT.** A corpus audit settled the scope: exactly **1 of 19** documents is
a container — not a corpus-wide problem, and over-splitting is the real danger
(Constitution, RoB, Secretariat Manual and Delegation all restart numbering for
Schedules and must stay whole).

**Detection** (`services/instrument_detector.rs`, mirrored in
`scripts/detect_instruments.py`). Deterministic, no model, `pdftotext` only,
~1s per 30 pages — fast enough to run at upload, which is the point. Unions two
signals because **neither is complete**: the short-title clause ("These rules may
be called the X Rules, 2015") is an excellent LOCATOR and a poor LABEL (from
`-layout` text it absorbs the marginal catchline); the contents list has clean
titles but WRAPS rows across lines and prints BOOK pages. Measured: the clause
pass finds `Sindh Councils (Budget) Rules, 2017` at p.150 which the book's own
index omits entirely, while the index carries four instruments the clause pass
misses. The page offset is DERIVED by matching the two by title (+1 here).

**Execution** (`services/instrument_split.rs`, `POST /admin/sources/:id/split`).
Cuts with poppler `pdfseparate` + `pdfunite`. **NOT lopdf** — already a
dependency, and it cannot even open this document ("Invalid cross-reference
table"); government PDFs here are routinely malformed in ways poppler tolerates.
**NOT ghostscript** — installed, a one-liner, and it re-encodes the file, putting
the embedded text layer (the entire reason extraction works) at risk. The
container's ROW is deleted so its chunks stop competing in retrieval; the FILE
moves to `_split_originals/` because it is the only record of what was cut and
leaving it in the indexed folder would let the next scan re-create it.
**Migration 019** records `split_page_offset` (page 5 of a piece is page 9 of the
printed volume — without it a citation cannot be checked against the book) and
`split_from_file`.

**Review** (`Admin → Indexing & Data`). Every proposed range is editable, with
live validation mirroring the server's, an "add an instrument the detector
missed" row, and the third outcome the flow was missing: *"This is one document
— leave it"*. Each row shows which signals vouched for it and the FIRST LINE of
its opening page — one line of real text is the cheapest check a human can make.
Pages covered by nothing are shown but never block: dropping front matter is
normal, doing it unknowingly is not.

**⚠️ FOUR defects were found only by running the real thing**, every one of which
passed unit tests, the compiler and review:
1. `lopdf` cannot open the Compendium at all (found by cutting the real file).
2. The detector proposed a plan **its own executor refused** — `pdftotext`
   terminates every page with a form feed, so the trailing empty element counted
   as a page and pushed the last range one past the end (41 vs 40). Fixing that
   by dropping ALL trailing empties then lost `Sindh Local Government Act 2013`'s
   genuinely blank last page (149 vs 150). Drop exactly ONE; guarded by
   `page_count_agrees_with_pdfinfo` across the whole corpus.
3. `index_sources` returns `id: String::new()` for a new file, so the split's
   `UPDATE … WHERE id = ''` silently named nothing. Resolve by `file_path`.
4. `indexer::index_file` overwrote the citation string with a name rebuilt from
   the filename ("Sindh Local Councils Election Rules 2015" for
   "Sindh Local Councils (Election) Rules, 2015"). It now only fills a
   `display_name` that is NULL — a deliberate title beats a derived one.

**End-to-end proof** (shadow server, isolated `NOVIQ_DATA_DIR` + its own
PostgreSQL, loopback only; prod's database never touched). Upload → detection
warns → inspect → split → verified from the DB and disk: container row deleted,
its chunks cascaded (018), 226 and 200 chunks under the two pieces, offsets 0 and
20, provenance recorded, original retired — and the two instruments carrying
**distinct citable labels** (`Rule 1, Rule 10 …` against `Section 1, Section 10
…`), which is the whole point.

**The real Compendium is CUT AND VERIFIED but NOT APPLIED** —
`/opt/noviq/compendium-split/out/` on the VM, 12 pieces, page counts exact, text
layers intact, each naming itself. 203 pages assigned; 36 deliberately dropped
(pp.1-5 front matter, pp.209-239 the *Functions to be Performed* schedule).
⚠️ p.92 is SHARED — the Conduct of Business Rules begin there, but the top of the
page carries unrelated Education Department notices from the same gazette issue.
Page-level cutting cannot separate instruments sharing a physical page.

**Open.** Detection WARNS at upload rather than blocking (blocking needs a
"held, awaiting review" lifecycle the pipeline has no notion of). Ranges are
editable; a preview of the PDF page is not built.

## 2026-07-30 — Extraction lost 13 provisions while scoring itself perfect

> ✅ **Three defects fixed, verified against the real PDFs.** Found while building
> a baseline for a Marker/Docling bake-off — the baseline was the finding.
> ⚠️ **Takes effect only on RE-INDEX.** The corpus keeps the missing provisions
> until the documents are re-ingested.

**Symptom.** `05_Compendium_Rules_under_SLGA_2013` extracted via pdfplumber lost
13 line-initial provisions that `pdftotext -layout` finds — including Rules 1
(*Short title and commencement*) and 2 (*Definitions*), the most-cited rules in
any instrument. `extraction_method: pdfplumber, quality_score: 1` — the pipeline
graded its own truncated output **perfect**.

**1. `text_normalizer::provision_dot_space` missed `N.(1)`.** The Compendium's
Election Rules print `19.(1) The Returning Officer…` — glued onto an opening
PAREN because the provision leads with its sub-clause instead of a catchline. The
repair required `["']?[A-Z]` after the dot, so it never fired, and the heading
patterns deliberately refuse a bare `\s*` there (the guard against `1996.The Act`
minting "Section 1996"). Lost 19, 24, 25, 26, 31, 44, 50, 53. Third variant of
this defect — capital (Art 142), then quoted term (Rule 131), now sub-clause.
Fix: allow `|\(`. The 1–3 digit ordinal still blocks years.

**2. `ingestion_sidecar._crop_preserves_anchors` summed instead of comparing.**
The catchline crop's safety check totalled anchors across the sample: nine body
pages each "gained" 2–3 (an artefact — removing a column re-flows `layout=True`
so mid-line numbers become line-initial), which paid for the table of contents
losing all 13 (52 → 57, approved). Lost 1, 2, 11, 12, 13.

**⚠️ The obvious fix was wrong twice, and the bake-off caught it.** Rejecting the
crop document-wide recovered the provisions but destroyed all **53 catchline
provision titles** (the geometry was discarded wholesale). Decoupling pairing
from cropping then produced GARBAGE titles on hanging-indent documents (`'1. 2.
3'` on Delegation), because there the "margin" is the number column itself.

The discriminator is the anchor-loss RATE, measured: **Constitution 0% of sampled
pages, Compendium 7%, Delegation 70%.** A genuine catchline margin fails on
almost no page; a hanging indent fails on most. `_column_consensus` now returns
`(geometry, verify_pages)`: above `MAX_ANCHOR_LOSS_FRAC` (0.25) the document is
treated as single-column; below it the margin is real and each page is verified
before cropping — but only when the sample saw any loss, so a clean document
(Constitution) pays nothing. Result: 5 provisions recovered, 53 titles kept, body
still cropped on 28/30 pages.

**3. `text_quality::score` structurally cannot see truncation.** It grades one
tier ALONE on shape — chars/page, tiny-line ratio, non-ASCII punct, dict hits.
Truncated-but-fluent English passes all four, so pdfplumber won Tier 0 at 1.0 and
`pdftotext` never ran. Added `pdf::tier0_is_complete`: before accepting Tier 0,
compare its provision-anchor count against `pdftotext` on the same file and
refuse a material shortfall (2%, floor 2). Counts the ordinal's PRESENCE, not its
detectability, so a merely-glued number is not accused of loss. **Fails open** —
a missing pdftotext accepts Tier 0 as before; this catches silent loss, it must
never block indexing. Costs one extra `pdftotext` run per document Tier 0 wins.

**Verification.** Rust built on the VM against a throwaway copy (prod worktree
untouched), with a matched control run: **zero regressions** (baseline 777/70,
with changes 783/69; the single delta is `pass2_coverage_tests::legacy_absolute_
count_overrides_pct`, a pre-existing env-var race between parallel tests). Five
new tests. Sidecar verified directly on the real PDFs — Compendium, Constitution
(252 pp, 313 titles, unchanged, 0 pages kept whole), Delegation, Secretariat.

**Bake-off, same six pages:** pdftotext / ours-fixed / docling / marker all find
13 ordinals, Rules 1&2, 5 instruments, 0 glued — **a tie on completeness.** On
the full 30-page file docling `std::bad_alloc`d and marker's worker died; times
were ~1s / 103s / 332s. Marker's reading order and sub-clause nesting are
genuinely better, but it mis-attributes catchlines, which our `provision_titles`
pairing gets right. **Not adopting either.**

**Follow-ups.** The Compendium is 13 instruments in one file (its own TOC lists
them with start pages) — segmentation is still open and no parser solves it.
`_ANCHOR_RE` cannot see a cropped prose page with no ordinals; the document-level
rate is what protects those.

## 2026-07-30 — Golden extraction set (the fast loop)

> ✅ **Working. 13 fixtures, 847 lib tests green.** Regenerate with
> `scripts/build_golden_fixtures.py` on the VM (it needs the source PDFs).

- **It corrected my model of the pipeline on its first run** — four of five
  initial "failures" were WRONG EXPECTATIONS, not defects, and that is the set
  paying for itself immediately:
  * `scan_with_profile` emits the profile's DEFAULT unit word. A `manual`
    document yields `Section 90` here and `Rule 90` in prod, because
    `resolve_citation_unit` re-mints it later in `structured_importer`.
  * `drop_footnote_tail_outliers` is DOCUMENT-GLOBAL (needs ≥20 distinct numbers),
    so `Article 343` is suppressed on the real document and cannot be on one page.
  * `strip_table_regions` removes tables BEFORE heading detection, so a raw page
    fixture still contains contents-table rows that never reach the scan in prod.
  Those three are recorded as **fixture-scope limits**, not defects — the
  distinction matters because "known broken" and "not exercised at this layer"
  call for different work.
- ⚠️ **A marker matched the TABLE OF CONTENTS.** `75. Commercial Schemes` appears
  in both the SLGA's contents and its body; the first generation silently captured
  p.6 instead of p.52 and would have asserted a provision on a page where the
  dotted-leader filter is *supposed* to suppress it. Now matched on provision TEXT
  (`Government may set up a Board, Authority`), and the TOC page became a case in
  its own right — it must yield NO provisions.
- **Why.** Every extraction defect through July was found by indexing the whole
  corpus on prod, running `scripts/corpus_gap_check.sql`, noticing a missing
  number and working backwards. That loop needs a re-index per attempt and is why
  the false-table guard took FOUR rounds — each dry run was a manual comparison
  against live extraction.
- **What** (`services/heading_detector/golden.rs`, test-only): twelve cases, each
  ONE real page saved verbatim from `pdftotext -layout`, paired with the labels
  the scan MUST and MUST NOT produce. Covers raw page text → `normalize` →
  `scan_with_profile`, which is the seam every defect lived in. No DB, no PDF, no
  re-index, no VM.
- **It normalises before scanning, deliberately.** Several fixes were repairs
  inside `normalize` (the space before a glued provision number, curly→ASCII
  quotes); asserting on raw page text tests the wrong layer. Same trap as the
  two-layer year guard.
- **The `forbid` half matters more than `expect`.** A missing provision is a gap;
  an invented one is a citation to law that does not exist. Cases cover footnote
  343, `153` with no dot, APT table serials and the Dev Manual contents rows.
- **Two cases are `xfail` WITH REASONS** — APT's fused table labels and RoB's
  doubled number. A known defect written down is a decision; one quietly absent
  from the suite is a surprise waiting for a customer. An `xfail` that starts
  PASSING is reported loudly so the marker is removed rather than masking a later
  regression.
- **A second test asserts the fixtures exist**, because a lost directory would
  otherwise let the whole set pass on zero cases.
- **Fixtures are located by MARKER TEXT, not page number**
  (`scripts/build_golden_fixtures.py`). Page numbers move — the SLGA was swapped
  from an 8-page scan to the 150-page principal Act mid-project — and a fixture
  silently pointing at the wrong page is worse than a missing one. A marker that
  stops matching is itself a finding.
- ⚠️ **Regenerate the fixtures whenever the extractor changes.** That is the
  point: for the layout-extraction work, rebuild against the new extractor and
  these expectations say whether it is BETTER or merely DIFFERENT.

## 2026-07-29 — Three more provision shapes: quote, `[XXX]`, catchline dash

> ✅ **VERIFIED ON PROD 2026-07-29 13:0x after re-index of 5 documents.**
> Gap report **9 documents / 16 gaps → 4 documents / 5 gaps**, and every
> survivor is diagnosed. Tests 821/0. Commits `668d5894`, `14618b52`
> (`9ced1c90`, `d8f9917b` on release).

- **Quoted defined term** (`90. "Secret" and "Top secret" documents…`).
  Secretariat Instructions Rules 90 and 131 were the only two of 187 the
  patterns could not see. TWO layers were blind, each for its own reason:
  Rule 131 is GLUED like its neighbours 129/130/132 but
  `restore_provision_dot_space` only inserts a space before a CAPITAL; Rule 90
  is already spaced but the heading pattern requires a capital after the dot.
  Fix: allow an optional `"`/`'` before the capital in the normalizer and in
  all three profiles. `normalize` folds curly quotes to ASCII first, so only
  the ASCII forms need matching. **Result: 184 → 186 of 187.**
- **Omitted-rule marker** (`56. [XXX]`). SPPRA Rules 2010 blanks five repealed
  rules (56, 59, 60, 69, 86) this way. `act.rs` has always allowed a bracketed
  title, `rules.rs` had not — so each marker was absorbed into the PRECEDING
  rule's chunk (a Rule 55 query retrieved text containing `56. [XXX]`, and a
  Rule 56 query found nothing and could be answered from its neighbour).
  **Result: 86 → 91/91, and 0 neighbours still carry a stray `[XXX]`.**
- **Catchline dash tight against the dot** (`10.- (1)`, `14.- Vacancies`).
  Sindh drafting writes it this way. E&D 1973 Rule 10 prints as
  `3[10.-  (1) A civil servant aggrieved…`; APT Rules 1974 uses it 20 times.
  Applied to the general AND sub-clause-opener patterns of all three profiles.
  **Result: E&D 13 → 14/14; APT's real rules recovered (see below).**
- **`corpus_gap_check.sql` now classifies** each gap TABLE/TOC vs UNEXPLAINED
  by checking whether the missing numbers sit in a table region. The Manual for
  Development Projects "gaps" 24–29 are a contents listing on pp.80-81 and had
  been re-reported as loss in every audit so far.
- Year guard survives all of it — a test asserts no year is minted as a rule in
  the plain, dashed, sub-clause and bracketed forms.

**Deliberately NOT fixed, with reasons:**

- **Secretariat Rule 153** prints as `153 This category shall include…` — *no
  dot at all*, a typo in the source PDF. Accepting `N ` + capital would mint a
  label from any sentence opening with a number. Asserted as a NEGATIVE test so
  a future "be more tolerant" change argues with a failing test.
- **RoB 1986 Rule 13** prints its number twice: `13.    13. The Chief Minister…`.
  Matching that needs "number, any other number, text", which would let a table
  row (`1.  2. Something`) shadow a real heading. regex_lite has no
  backreferences, so the second number cannot be required to be the SAME. One
  rule is not worth loosening the pattern corpus-wide.

**Two larger defects surfaced while diagnosing — both still open:**

- ⚠️ **APT Rules 1974 is substantially mis-indexed.** Its `Rule 9/10/11` chunks
  were SCHEDULE TABLE ROWS (`10. Civil Judges, Senior Civil Judges…` — an
  appointing-authority table), not rules. The audit's "1 missing" was an
  illusion: schedule serials filled the numbering run, the same false-label
  mechanism that hid the SLGA problem. The dash fix recovered the real rules,
  so labels now carry BOTH the genuine rule and its schedule twin —
  `suppress_schedule_table_serials` is not firing on this Schedule.
- ⚠️ **SPPRA Review Guidelines: text damaged inside our pipeline.** Rules 1 and
  4 are absent from the corpus entirely and the preamble reads
  `INSTRUCTIONSFORTHEAPPELLANTSREGARDING`, `Rs. 10o`, with item `e)` replaced
  by a stray `s`. **`pdftotext -layout` output has none of that** — it reads
  `Rs. 100` and item `e)` intact. So good input is being corrupted by our
  extraction path (pdfplumber), not by the PDF. Not a label bug.

## 2026-07-29 — Footnote numbers minted as provisions: the TRAILING-OUTLIER rule

> Closes the false-label debt the amendment-bracket entry below explicitly left
> owing ("the false-label work still owes `Article 343`"). Lib suite
> **815 passed / 0 failed** (VM, `NOVIQ_TEST_PG_INSTALL_DIR` set).
> ⚠️ **Requires a re-index** of Constitution, Civil Servants Act 1973 and
> Manual for Development Projects before it changes anything on prod.

- **Symptom**: three labels that do not exist in their statutes —
  `Article 343` (Constitution), `Section 1752` (Sindh Civil Servants Act 1973),
  `Section 156` (Manual for Development Projects). They inflate every gap
  report (the Constitution reads as "62 missing" purely because of 343) and,
  worse, they invent citations: `Article 343` had ~14 chunks of genuine
  **Article 232** text filed under it.
- **Why the existing guards all miss them** — each for a different reason, and
  none is fixable by widening a threshold:
  * `looks_like_year` rejects 1800–2099, so **1752 is below the floor**.
    Widening the range is wrong: 1752 is a footnote ordinal, not a year.
  * `drop_out_of_sequence_articles` is a **streaming** rule carrying a running
    max. Its far-forward test needs `max_num >= 20 && n > 2*max && n-max > 300`:
    - `Article 343` sits at p.168 where the run is already ~230 → 343 is
      neither 2× nor +300. Kept.
    - `Section 1752` sits at p.8 where the run has only reached ~9 → the
      `max_num >= 20` precondition is not met. Kept.
    - `Section 156` is +133 → under the 300 cut. Kept.
- **Fix** (`regex_pass::drop_footnote_tail_outliers`): a second, **global**
  sequence pass. Real provisions form one dense run; a footnote number is an
  isolated island *above its top*, which is only visible with the whole
  document in hand. Peels from the top while the gap to the next-lower number
  beats BOTH an absolute floor (25) and a fifth of the span below it — so a
  280-Article statute is not judged by a 27-section act's yardstick.
- **Runs LAST**, deliberately (after the dotted-leader and roster filters): it
  reasons about the shape of the whole run, so it must see the final set. A
  stray contents line surviving `strip_front_matter` would otherwise distort
  the very statistics it judges by.
- **Fail-safes**, per the poison-guard lesson below (a rule that silently
  deletes law must fail safe): off under 20 distinct numbers; only ever
  inspects the TOP of the run, one number at a time; caps removals at 10%.
- **Validated against real data, not intuition.** The distinct provision-number
  set of all 19 prod documents was pulled from the DB first; the rule fires on
  exactly the three false labels and on nothing else. Every legitimate document
  in the corpus has a top-of-run gap of exactly **1**. Those real number sets
  are the test fixtures — incl. SPPRA Rules' genuine internal holes (56, 59-60,
  69, 86) which must be ignored, and the Manual's `Section 30` (gap 7) which is
  run jitter and must survive.
- Tests: 8 added — one per false label, the legitimate-corpus sweep, internal
  gaps, both fail-safes, structural-heading pass-through, plus an end-to-end
  `scan_with_profile` case at the Constitution's exact shape (run to 280 +
  footnote 343) where the far-forward rule provably cannot help.
- ⚠️ **Known residual**: dropping the label merges the footnote text into the
  preceding provision's chunk, so superseded text quoted in a footnote stays
  retrievable under a neighbouring Article. That is the status quo for every
  other footnote in the corpus and strictly better than minting a citation to a
  provision that does not exist — but it is not the same as *understanding*
  footnotes. A footnote-aware container is the real fix, if it ever matters.

## 2026-07-29 — Amendment brackets/asterisks hid the last two Articles

> ✅ **VERIFIED ON PROD 2026-07-29 01:54 — the Constitution is COMPLETE.**
> Articles 90 and 272 recovered; a `generate_series(1,280)` check reports
> **"missing in 1..280: NONE"**. Distinct numeric Article labels = 281 = the
> full 280 + the one known FALSE label `Article 343` (pp.168-169), which the
> false-label work still owes. Session total: **265 -> 280 Articles** across
> four distinct ingestion defects.


- **Article 90** prints as `[[90. (1) Subject to the Constitution…` — the
  provision was substituted TWICE, so it carries NESTED amendment brackets.
  Article 91 beside it (`[91. (1) …`) has one bracket and was detected. Every
  provision pattern allowed a single optional `[`.
- **Article 272** prints as `272. *Notwithstanding anything…` — a footnote
  marker sits between the space and the text. Knock-on from the superscript
  filter, which strips the marker's raised digit (`3*`) and leaves the `*`.
- **Fix** (`doc_profiles/{manual,act,rules}.rs`): allow REPEATED leading
  brackets (`\[*`, and `(?:\d*\[)*` in rules) and CONSUME an optional
  footnote asterisk after the dot. Markers are consumed, never captured, so
  labels stay clean. Applied to all three profiles — amendment-heavy statutes
  (E&D 1973) carry the same shapes.
- **Year guard verified, and clarified.** It is TWO layers, and a test that
  checks the wrong one is worthless: the PATTERN refuses only a GLUED year
  (`1996.The Act` — this is why the dot requires `\s+` or a bracket, never
  `\s*`), while `regex_pass::looks_like_year` (1800–2099) is what drops the
  spaced form `1996. The Act`. The spaced form has ALWAYS matched the pattern;
  the new asterisk form is protected by exactly the same second layer. Test
  now asserts each layer where it lives, incl. `[[1996. (1)`.
  ⚠️ Note for the FALSE-LABEL work: `Section 1752` slips through because 1752
  is BELOW the 1800 floor — the fix there is a sequence-sanity check, not a
  wider year range.
- ⚠️ Requires a re-index of the Constitution.

## 2026-07-29 — Six Articles lost to a MISSING SPACE after the provision number

- **Symptom**: Constitution Articles 90, 113, 142, 152, 197, 217, 219, 272 had
  no chunk of their own (280 articles; 272 present + 1 false label = 273 rows).
- **Not** content loss, despite an earlier (wrong) reading of mine: the text is
  in the corpus, absorbed into the PREVIOUS article. My DB probe searched for
  `142. Subject` with a space and found nothing — the stored text has no space.
- **Cause**: pdfplumber sometimes emits `142.Subject to the Constitution—`
  where `pdftotext` gives `142. Subject …`. Page 95 is the proof: Articles 141
  and 143 kept their space and were detected; 142 did not and was absorbed.
  Same glueing on 113 (p.83), 152 (p.98), 197 (p.130), 217 and 219 (p.155).
- **Why the patterns can't just be relaxed** (comment in `manual.rs`): the
  provision regexes require `\.(?:\s+\[?|\[)` deliberately, because a bare
  `\s*` would let `1996.The Act` mint "Section 1996" — the same false-label
  family as `Section 1752`.
- **Fix** (`text_normalizer::restore_provision_dot_space`, run inside
  `normalize` after `repair_spaced_words`): re-insert the space at line start
  for a **1–3 digit** ordinal followed immediately by a capital. A 4-digit
  year can never match, so the year guard is untouched. Benefits every profile
  and every document, not just the Constitution.
- Tests: repair cases (incl. `[113.The`, `19A.Right`), plus a guard test that
  `1996.The Act` and `2009.Procurement` are NOT split, and that mid-line text
  and decimals (`1.5 million`) are left verbatim.

  they show no glued occurrence and still need diagnosis.

## 2026-07-29 — False-table guard, round 2: the prose was in the HEADER

> ✅ **VERIFIED ON PROD 2026-07-29 after re-index.** Guard fired on pp.55/89/
> 175/187. Constitution Articles **60, 61, 127, 128, 240, 241, 242 recovered**
> with correct catchline titles and pages; **table chunks 8 → 0**; distinct
> Articles **266 → 273**. Delegation (75 tables) and the Manual (63) were not
> re-indexed and did not need to be — the dry run showed 0 → 0 change for both.


First guard (below) recovered Constitution Articles 60/61 but NOT 127/128/
240/241. Asking the sidecar what it actually sees explained why: on pp.89/175/
187 pdfplumber puts the **entire page of prose in the table's HEADER cell**
(1,581–1,721 chars) and leaves ONE data row holding only the footnote rule
(`––––– 1See …`, 133–371 chars). `looks_like_prose_not_table` measured data
rows alone → "371 chars, too small" → region kept → provisions still lost.

- **Fix**: the header is measured as one more unit, and a header with **2+
  populated cells is proof of a real table** (an early accept).
- **Validated against live extraction BEFORE deploying** (dry-run script over
  the sidecar's own `extract_tables` output, rather than a third speculative
  re-index): Constitution **1/4 → 4/4** regions rejected; Delegation of
  Financial Powers **75/75** tables still kept; Development Projects Manual
  **63/63** still kept. Zero genuine tables affected.
- Method note worth keeping: the first guard's thresholds were derived from
  chunk text in the DB, which showed only what SURVIVED. Reading the sidecar's
  raw structure showed where the content actually was.

## 2026-07-28 — Provisions were being DELETED by false table detection

- **Symptom**: provisions missing from the corpus. Constitution Articles 60,
  61, 127, 128, 240, 241 had no `Article N` chunk at all; the sequence ran
  57, 58, 59 → 62, 63, 64.
- **How it was found**: two "failing" tests (stale 1024-chunk expectations)
  led to a corpus audit. Provisions are numbered, so the corpus can be audited
  against itself — new **`scripts/corpus_gap_check.sql`** reports numbering
  gaps per document AND searches for where the missing text ended up.
- **Root cause**: the missing text was stored under labels like `Table (p.89)`
  (`| 127. Subject to the Constitution, …`). `table::reflow_with_sidecar`
  **replaces a page's text** with `above + linearised rows + below`, so when
  pdfplumber's ruling-line detector false-positives on a page of prose, those
  provisions never reach heading detection — no label, uncitable, and the
  original prose is gone from the body.
- **Fix** (`table.rs::looks_like_prose_not_table`, called from
  `reflow_with_sidecar` before a region is marker-wrapped): reject a region
  when every row collapses to ONE populated column **and** the rows are
  paragraph-sized (≥400 chars total, ≥200 mean). Thresholds measured, not
  guessed: the false regions were one row of 1,720–2,600 chars in a single
  column; genuine tables carry 2+ populated columns with rows averaging
  113–576. Rejection is the SAFE direction — the page keeps its own text, so
  content is chunked as prose rather than lost. Golden delegation-table tests
  still pass (genuine tables unaffected).
- **Scale**: ~138 provision-shaped rows trapped in table chunks — Development
  Projects Manual 90, Delegation of Financial Powers 42, Constitution 6.
- ⚠️ **Requires a re-index** to take effect on already-indexed documents.
- **Still open** (different causes, see `project_missing-provisions-table-swallow`):

## 2026-07-28 — Split chunks stamp their own page; "Open document" from a citation

Both from tester feedback.

- **Symptom**: a citation showed `p.27` for content printed on p.18 (path
  `Part-I/(b)/p5`).
- **Root cause**: `build_tree_from_headings` records `offset_by_path` for
  HEADING nodes only; `finalize_tree` then creates `/pN` paragraph children and
  `/mN` merged scraps, which therefore had no entry — and
  `structure_parser::collect_chunks` resolves a page as
  `page_by_path.get(unit_path).or(parent_page)`, so every piece of a section
  spanning a page break claimed the section's FIRST page.
- **Fix** (`structured_importer.rs::stamp_split_child_offsets`, called from
  `import()` right after the tree is built): walk the tree in document order
  with a forward-only cursor and locate each unmapped node by a 48-char prefix
  of its own text (only the head is verbatim — `split_long_text` trims pieces
  and the coalescer joins them). Linear in body length. A node that cannot be
  located keeps the old inherit-from-ancestor behaviour, so this can only add
  precision. Regression test: `split_children_stamp_their_own_page_not_the_parents`.
- **Open document from a citation** (`api/documents.rs::source_file`, route
  `GET /api/sources/:id/file`): serves the ORIGINAL file, scoped through
  `visible_source_ids` exactly like `source_chunks` (a citation link must not
  become a way to read an invisible document; 404 — never 403 — so existence
  isn't leaked). PDFs/text are served **inline** so the browser opens them in a
  tab; the FE appends `#page=N` to land on the cited page
  (`transport.ts::openAuthedInNewTab` — bearer auth means a plain
  `target="_blank"` cannot work, so it fetches and hands over a blob URL,
  revoked after 60 s). Buttons in the citation popover (`AnswerBody.tsx`) and
  the source viewer (`ChunkViewer.tsx`); pop-up-blocked and fetch failures are
  both surfaced, never swallowed.
