## 2026-07-27 — Citations pointed at the wrong provision: four extraction/parse defects, one release

> ✅ **Compiled and tested on the VM** (throwaway worktree, `--no-default-features --features server`).
> **714 passing / 69 failing**, against a **baseline of 696 / 69** measured by reverting the same
> files in the same worktree. The 69 are pre-existing DB tests that cannot run there (`initdb` fails
> on `libssl.so.3`); the failure set after the change is **identical** to baseline. Frontend
> `tsc --noEmit` clean. Sidecar binary rebuilt and smoke-tested on the real Constitution.

**Symptom.** Trace `a72f1539` showed a chunk labelled **Article 154(e)** whose text is really
**Article 63(1)(e)**. Retrieval returned the right *content* under the wrong *citation* — the worse
failure for a legal product, because a wrong citation looks checkable and passes casual review.

**Two earlier diagnoses in this thread were wrong and are retracted.** (1) "pdftotext `-layout` is
the extractor" — it is not; `pdfplumber` is Tier 0 and primary, so every measurement taken against a
`pdftotext` dump was measuring a code path production does not run. (2) "the TOC leak is the whole
cause" — it is *a* cause, not the main one. Everything below was measured against real pdfplumber
output, per document, across all 18 corpus PDFs.

**Measured — Articles 50–80 anchored at line start in the Constitution body:**

| stage | found |
|---|---|
| pdfplumber today | 19 / 31 |
| + D1 superscript fix | 21 / 31 |
| + D2 column crop | 28 / 31 |
| + D4 heading patterns | **31 / 31** |

**D1 — superscript amendment markers fuse into the provision number.**
`extract_text(layout=True)` places a footnote marker flush against the number, so `54.` emits as
`154.`; Articles 54–63 then inherited that label. Fixed in `ingestion_sidecar.py`
(`_superscript_keys` / `_page_without_superscripts`): a digit both smaller than AND raised above its
own line's modal size/baseline. Restricted to **digits** — without that the rule also ate the
marginal catchlines. Verified the size-8 footnote block survives (0 of 709 chars dropped).

**D2 — the marginal catchline column is flattened into the body line.** The dominant defect. A
statute prints each provision's short title in the outer margin; layout extraction merges the two
columns onto one line. On recto pages the catchline lands right (harmless); on verso pages it lands
LEFT and displaces the number off the line start, where no heading regex can anchor it:
`Qualifications [62. (1) A person shall not be qualified…`. That one mechanism hid 10 of 31 Articles.
Fixed by detecting the whitespace gutter and cropping to the body column (`_column_consensus` /
`_body_box`), decided **per document** from a 40-page sample, never per page — page 61 of the
Constitution has no detectable gutter at all.

> ⚠️ **Geometry alone is not sufficient, and the corpus proved it.** The first version regressed
> `01_Sindh_Rules_of_Business_1986` (60 anchors → 33) and
> `09_Sindh_Delegation_of_Financial_Powers_2019` (37 → 30): both use a **hanging indent**, where the
> provision number itself sits left of the body text with a gutter between, so cropping decapitated
> every provision. A catchline margin and a hanging indent are geometrically identical. The fix is
> `_crop_preserves_anchors`, which **measures the crop's actual effect** on a sample and refuses to
> crop unless the line-initial provision count holds. Final sweep: Constitution +15, SPPRA Rules +5,
> E&D Rules +1, **15 documents unchanged, zero regressions.** Validated on the Constitution alone,
> this would have shipped broken.

**D3 — a dot-leader-less table of contents mints fake Articles.** The new Constitution typesets its
contents WITHOUT dot leaders, so `is_dotted_line` saw nothing; each `146. Power of Federation…` line
matched the bare-number heading pattern, pushed the running maximum past 280 before the body began,
and `drop_out_of_sequence_articles` then deleted every genuine Article below ~140 as an
out-of-sequence restart. New detector in `front_matter.rs` (`numbered_toc_runs`).

> ⚠️ **Shape and density are NOT enough** — an earlier version lifted 40 real provisions out of the
> body and broke the existing `mid_body_dotted_line_is_not_front_matter` test. TOC titles (median 32
> chars, max 56) and body lines (median 54) **overlap**, so no length threshold can separate them.
> The discriminator that works is semantic: **a contents entry points at a provision that appears
> again below it** (`entries_recur_below`). Measured: real contents runs recur at **94–100%**, a run
> of genuine body provisions at **0%**. Threshold 60%.

**D4 — amendment brackets after the dot.** `56. [(1)]`, `71. [Mediation Committee]`, `73. [(1)`,
`58.(1)` — the patterns allowed a bracket BEFORE the number but not after, and required whitespace
before a sub-clause opener. Relaxed in `manual.rs` (the Constitution's profile — confirmed by score:
manual 160 vs act 117), `act.rs`, `rules.rs`. The bracket alternative is deliberate rather than a
bare `\s*`, which would match `1996.The Act`.

**A3 — catchlines become provision titles.** `DocNode::title` is documented as "an Article's marginal
note" and had never been populated, because the note lived in a print column the extractor flattened.
The sidecar now pairs catchline to provision by y-position — done there because it is the only stage
holding both columns' geometry — and emits a `{number: title}` map flowing through
`ParsedDocument::provision_titles` into `apply_provision_titles`. 313 titles on the Constitution, so
a citation can read *Article 54 — Summoning and prorogation of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament)*.

**Also shipped — document indexing console + clickable citations.**
- `GET /api/admin/chunks` (paginated browse, capped 200) and `POST /api/admin/sources/delete_bulk`
  (preview mode, capped 100, reuses `hard_delete_source`).
- `ChunkViewer.tsx` — one drawer serving both the admin console and citation click-through. Surfaces
  `label_status`, the parse-health flag the importer has always written and nothing ever displayed.
- Admin Indexing tab: document table, checkbox multi-select, and a confirm dialog naming each
  document with **counts the server computed** — never re-derived in the browser, because the
  folder-delete bug was a silent no-op that read as success.
- Citations now carry `chunk_id` / `source_id` and open the source at that passage on click. Hover
  already worked; click did nothing because there was no handle to navigate to.

> ⚠️ **`browse_chunks` is admin-gated but officers click citations.** A separate officer-facing
> `POST /api/source_chunks` is scoped through `visible_source_ids`, so a citation link cannot become
> a way to read documents the caller may not otherwise see. It returns the same 404 for "not visible"
> as for "absent" — whether a document exists is itself information.

**Cross-cutting / follow-ups.**
- **A re-index is required** before any of the parser work appears in the corpus.
- `04_Sindh_Local_Government_Act_2013.pdf` (8pp) and `SPPRA_Policy_Letter_16Oct2023.pdf` (3pp) yield
  **zero extractable characters** — pure image scans, wholly dependent on the OCR tier. Unverified
  whether they are actually indexed or silently empty.
- The TOC detector also lifts the numbered officer roster in Delegation of Financial Powers (recurs
  at 100%). Consistent with this module's stated purpose — a roster is not a provision — and the text
  stays retrievable as a front-matter block rather than being discarded.
- `services::indexer::pass2_coverage_tests::legacy_absolute_count_overrides_pct` is **flaky, not a
  regression**: it passes alone and fails beside siblings because these tests mutate process-global
  env vars with no serialization.
- `11_Sindh_Civil_Servants_APT_Rules_1974` shows 1 anchor in 11 pages — **not a defect**; the
  document is almost entirely tabular.
- The sidecar build pins **pdfplumber 0.11.5** while development measured on 0.11.10; the frozen
  binary was re-verified end-to-end on the real Constitution and produces identical output.

## 2026-07-26 — Folder delete silently kept every chunk: membership union, delete counts, confirm dialog

> ⚠️ **NOT compiled.** No Rust toolchain on this box (same constraint as 2026-07-24). `folders.rs`,
> `documents.rs`, `router.rs` are **unverified by the compiler**. Hand-checked: `crate::db::Driver`
> does NOT exist (only `pub type Db = sqlx::PgPool`) so the generic bound is `sqlx::Postgres`;
> `serde` + `log` are available in `folders.rs`; the desktop caller
> (`commands/folders.rs:93`) discards the new return value via `?;` which is legal for a
> non-`must_use` type. Frontend `tsc --noEmit` clean.

**Symptom.** Architect deleted the admin corpus folder in the UI, re-uploaded 18 documents, and the
document count came back **30**. 30 = the original 12 + the new 18: the folder delete had removed
nothing but the folder row.

**Why.** `folders::delete()` cascaded from a single predicate —
`sources.file_path LIKE '<folder_path>%'` — inside `if let Some(f) = folder`, while
`DELETE FROM indexed_folders` sat **outside** that block and ran unconditionally. For an **uploaded**
corpus the sources are linked to the folder through the `__folder__<id>` stub notebook, **not** by
living under the folder's path (see migration 009's backfill, which joins exactly that way), so the
LIKE matched zero rows. Result: folder vanishes from the UI, every source/chunk/embedding survives,
and the caller reports success. Re-uploading then produced two live copies of every document —
including two different answers to "what is the SPPRA Rule 17(1) threshold?" (the stale copy says
Rs 100,000–1M, the current one Rs 300,000–2M).

**Fix.**
- `folders.rs`: new `folder_source_ids()` selects by **both** membership signals —
  `file_path LIKE` **UNION** `notebook_sources.notebook_id = '__folder__<id>'` — and every delete is
  now keyed on that id set (`= ANY($1)`), not a path prefix. Covers watched folders *and* uploads.
- `delete()` returns `FolderDeleteCounts {sources, chunks, embeddings, folder_found}` and logs
  `warn!` when a folder row is removed having matched **0** sources — the exact silent case above.
- New `delete_preview()` (read-only) + `POST /api/folder_delete_preview`.
- `revoke_indexed_folder` returns the counts and writes them into the audit event; a 0-source revoke
  is no longer indistinguishable from a clean one in the audit trail.
- `IndexedFolders.tsx`: `handleRevoke` now previews, shows a `confirm()` quoting **real numbers**
  ("removes 18 documents, 12,431 chunks and 12,431 embeddings"), states that files on disk are kept
  but the index is not, and surfaces a warning if the server reports 0 sources removed.

**SQLite-era → Postgres.** The stale comments claimed `chunk_embeddings` is "a vec0 virtual table"
where "FK CASCADE does not apply", and cited `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_FOREIGNKEY (787)`. Verified against
the actual PG schema: `chunk_embeddings.chunk_id → chunks(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` (runtime DDL in
`schema.rs::ensure_vector_table`) and `chunks.source_id → sources(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`
(`001_baseline.sql:92`). So both *would* cascade unaided. The explicit deletes are **kept
deliberately** — the counts we show the user are a promise, and an explicit delete keeps that promise
true if a later migration relaxes a constraint — but the comments now say why, not SQLite folklore.
The `graph_nodes`/`graph_edges` pre-deletes remain genuinely required (FK NO ACTION, nothing
cascades to them). Also dropped the "SQLite writer lock" rationale from the transaction comment.

**GPU runtime rebuilt + script repointed + preflight guard (VM, 2026-07-26 — DONE, VERIFIED).**
- Rebuilt `/opt/noviq/ort-gpu/` (2.7 GB): GPU onnxruntime 1.20.1 + CUDA EP from the surviving uv
  cache entry, and **only** the CUDA 12 components the provider actually links —
  `cublas, cuda_runtime, cudnn, cufft, curand, cuda_nvrtc, nvjitlink` — determined by
  `objdump -p libonnxruntime_providers_cuda.so`, not guesswork (`cusolver`, `cusparse`, `nccl`,
  `cupti`, `nvtx` are **not** needed). CUDA libs copied from vLLM's venv, ORT from
  `~/.cache/uv/archive-v0/KI7KYdRg9QPdzV9k/`.
- `ldd` under the constructed `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`: **ALL RESOLVED**, no `not found`.
- `gpu-reindex.sh`: `NV`/`ORT_GPU`/`CAPI` repointed at the new tree (backup at
  `gpu-reindex.sh.bak.pre-ortgpu-2026-07-26`). `LDP` construction unchanged.
- **New preflight guard**, inserted right after `exec >>"$LOG"` — checks the ORT lib, the CUDA EP
  `.so`, all seven component dirs, and runs `ldd | grep "not found"`. On failure it exits **90
  BEFORE stopping vLLM or touching `.env`**, so a missing runtime now costs nothing instead of
  producing CPU embeddings labelled as a GPU re-embed.
- **Guard verified in all three states** (isolated harness, `LOG` redirected to /tmp, no side
  effects): healthy → exit 0 + "preflight: GPU runtime OK"; CUDA EP hidden → exit 90 + "CUDA
  execution provider missing"; `cudnn/` hidden → exit 90 + "CUDA component missing". Files restored.
- `DO-NOT-DELETE.txt` written into the directory explaining what it is, why the predecessor was
  deleted, what the silent failure looked like, what is safe to reclaim instead, and a copy-paste
  read-only health check.
- ⚠️ **`gpu-reindex.sh` is out of tree** (same as `deploy.sh`). Added `deploy/gpu-reindex.sh` as a
  clearly-marked **reference copy** so the logic is version-controlled — editing it changes nothing
  on the VM until copied across by hand.
- ⚠️ **Not run.** The actual GPU re-embed stops vLLM (chat down ~7–10 min) and was not triggered.
- Near-miss worth recording: a test invocation used `sudo -n bash /opt/noviq/gpu-reindex.sh`, which
  would have run the real orchestration. Passwordless sudo is not configured so it failed and `set -e`
  aborted — production was verified untouched (vLLM active, health ok, no `DEPLOYING` sentinel,
  gpu-reindex.log still ending 2026-07-12). **Test safety guards via an extracted harness, never by
  invoking the orchestration script itself.**

**GPU indexing — no code change; it is an infrastructure regression.** Asked for "indexing from the
admin UI should use GPU". That button **already exists** (`Admin.tsx:596 gpuReindex` → `POST
/admin/gpu_reindex` → trigger file → systemd path unit → `/opt/noviq/gpu-reindex.sh`), with its own
confirm dialog. It is broken because the 2026-07-25 disk cleanup deleted `/opt/noviq/ort-gpu-spike/`,
which held the GPU-capable onnxruntime **and** the CUDA 12 libs the script puts on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
Current live state: `ECHO_EMBED_GPU=1` is set, but `ORT_DYLIB_PATH` points at
`/opt/noviq/.ort-runtime/libonnxruntime.so.1.20.1` — **16.5 MB with 0 CUDA dynamic symbols, a CPU-only
build** — and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` is unset. `embedder.rs` appends `CPUExecutionProvider` as a
deliberate fallback, so this degrades **silently**: the flag is on and does nothing. Last successful
GPU re-embed was 2026-07-12, before the cleanup.
⚠️ In-process GPU indexing at upload time is **not** achievable on this host: the A40-12Q slice has
~1.4 GB free because vLLM holds 9.6 GB, which is exactly why the script stops vLLM first and restarts
the server with a different ORT. Two-phase (CPU ingest → GPU re-embed) is the correct model here.
**Follow-up:** rebuild a stable `/opt/noviq/ort-gpu/` from the surviving copies in
`~/.cache/uv/archive-v0/*` (full GPU ORT + `libcublasLt.so.12` + `libcudnn.so.9` are all still there,
no download needed) and repoint `gpu-reindex.sh` at it rather than the prunable uv cache.

**Cross-cutting / follow-ups.**
- ⚠️ **Production is currently in the broken state**: 30 sources, 10 documents duplicated, the stale
  2012 Constitution and 2013 SPPRA rules still indexed. Clean up via **per-document** delete
  (`documents.rs`, keyed on `source_id` — cannot miss), not folder delete, until this fix is deployed.
- ⚠️ Two superseded PDFs remain on disk at `/opt/noviq/data/uploads/admin/`
  (`constitution.pdf`, `02_SPPRA_Rules_2010_Revised_2013.pdf`). Backed up to
  `/opt/noviq/data/corpus-backup-2026-07-26/`. They were *not* re-read during the 2026-07-26 index
  (atime 00:01 vs 20:05 for the new files), but they are a landmine for the next folder-level index.
- Tightened `/opt/noviq/data/pg/.pgpass` from `rw-rw-r--` to `0600` — psql refuses a group/world
  readable pgpass, and a DB password readable by any account on the box is worth fixing regardless.

  nothing here can be run locally).

## 2026-07-26 — API-integration tab: server-served provider catalogue, tier tags, per-model key probe

> ⚠️ **NOT deployed, NOT compiled.** Same constraint as the 2026-07-24 entry — no Rust toolchain on the
> Windows box (`cargo` absent from PATH and from disk; only the repo-local `.cargo` registry + a stale
> `target/` exist). So `services/inference/catalog.rs` and the two new handlers in `api/admin.rs` are
> **unverified by the compiler**; the 7 unit tests in `catalog.rs` have **never been run**. Verified
> locally: `catalog.json` parses (12 providers / 41 models, 17 free + 24 paid, no duplicate ids, every
> tier ∈ {free,paid}); frontend `tsc --noEmit` clean; `vite build` clean. `vitest` still cannot run
> (`jsdom` dev-dep missing — pre-existing, unrelated).

**Context.** Research deliverable first (`docs/llm-provider-api-analysis-2026-07.pdf`, 10 pp): free/paid
LLM API tiers, current state, and a 1–2 year outlook. Its §8 is the design input for this change.

**Symptom / why.** The "Model & Inference" tab already had provider→model→API-key plumbing
(`EngineKind::Remote`, runtime-swappable `RemoteConfig`, `db_config` persistence, write-only key). Three
gaps made it misleading rather than merely incomplete:

1. **Model ids were a bare `string[]` hardcoded in `Admin.tsx`.** Fourteen widely-used ids retire between
   Jul and Dec 2026 (GPT-4o, GPT-4 Turbo, o1, Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash on 16/23 Oct). A list in the frontend
   bundle is partly dead within a year and needs a full rebuild to correct.
2. **Free/paid was not represented at all**, and a binary split would still have hidden three
   *disqualifying* conditions: trains-on-your-data (Mistral free, Google free outside EU/UK/EEA, xAI
   credits), non-commercial-only (Cohere free), and context-below-our-prompt (Cerebras free 8K,
   Cloudflare 2K–8K — these silently truncate retrieved passages, i.e. manufacture ungrounded answers).
3. **No validation.** Entitlement is per *model*, not per key: one valid Google key returns 200 on Flash
   and 404 on Pro. "The key is valid" was never an answer to "will this selection work".

**Fix.**
- **New** `src-tauri/src/services/inference/catalog.json` — 12 providers / 41 models with tier, context,
  prices, RPM/TPM/RPD, `shutdown_date`, and provider-level `trains_on_data` / `non_commercial_only`.
- **New** `src-tauri/src/services/inference/catalog.rs` — `catalog()` resolves
  `{NOVIQ_DATA_DIR}/provider_catalog.json` first, else the `include_str!`-bundled default. A malformed
  override is logged and **ignored**, never propagated: losing the provider list would take the whole
  tab down, which is worse than a stale catalogue. Also `effective_rpm()` + `CONTEXT_WARN_TOKENS`.
- **New** `GET /api/admin/providers` and `POST /api/admin/inference/validate` (`api/admin.rs`,
  `api/router.rs`). The probe is a 1-token non-streaming chat call that saves nothing; it maps status
  onto actionable text and deliberately reports **429 as success for the key** (auth + entitlement both
  passed, only the rate limit hit).
- `src/pages/Admin.tsx` — `PROVIDERS`/`ProviderId` constants deleted in favour of the fetched catalogue;
  model dropdown replaced by a tagged, filterable (All/Free/Paid) list; "Test key & model" button;
  provider-terms panel; `manualConn()` keeps URL/prefix/model hand-editable when the catalogue is absent
  (older server) so the form never dead-ends.

**The non-obvious bit — headline rate limits are wrong for RAG.** Free tiers advertise requests/day, but
our traffic is token-heavy per request, so the **TPM cap binds long before the daily one**. Groq's
14,400 req/day reads as ~10/min of headroom; at 6,000 TPM and an 8K-token prompt the true sustained rate
is **0.75/min** — a ~13× overstatement. The UI therefore shows a *derived* effective rate
(`effective_rpm`, unit-tested) with the headline demoted to a tooltip. This is the project's recurring
"two places measuring one thing" trap: a number shown to a user must come from the thing itself.

**Cross-cutting / follow-ups.**
- `load_from_db` / `save_to_db` / `RemoteConfig` untouched — saved configs round-trip unchanged, and
  `catalog.rs` has tests pinning the Groq/Google/OpenRouter base URLs + Gemini's empty prefix so a
  stored config still maps back onto the right provider.
- ⚠️ **Model ids in `catalog.json` are from July-2026 aggregator sources, not probed.** Some may 404.
  That is what the probe is for; the "Other…" free-text path is the escape hatch. Re-verify on the VM.
- Prompt caching (up to 90% off input, and our system+grounding prefix is identical every query) is
  **not** wired into the adapter yet — highest-value follow-up, larger than any model choice.
- Deferred: per-model cost telemetry, and using `shutdown_date` to warn on the *saved* model at boot
  rather than only in the picker.

## 2026-07-24 — Auto-rebuild with no push + a badge that lied: deploy trigger, circuit breaker, sentinel ageing, honest banner

> ⚠️ **NOT deployed, NOT compiled.** No Rust toolchain on the Windows box (`cargo`/`cmake` absent), so
> `api/health.rs` is **unverified by the compiler**. Shell side IS verified: `deploy/test_deploy_rollback.sh`
> **13 passed / 0 failed** (6 new assertions). Frontend `tsc --noEmit` clean; `vitest` could not run
> (`jsdom` dev-dep missing locally — pre-existing).
> ⚠️ **VM diagnosis never happened** — SSH to `10.150.0.100` timed out (VPN down) and the tunnel URL in
> the ops file is **NXDOMAIN** (quick-tunnel hostnames rotate). So the *specific* live cause is still
> unconfirmed; these are fixes to mechanisms proven from the code, not from a captured trace.

**Symptom.** Architect saw the frontend banner "Noviq is updating to a new version" and asked why the app
rebuilds when nothing was pushed. **Two independent defects, routinely mistaken for one.**

**Why 1 — the badge did not mean "updating".** `ServerStatusBanner.tsx` rendered on
`serverStatus() !== "ok"`, so `unreachable` (health fetch threw: VPN drop, server down, **rotated tunnel
URL**) displayed the *deploy* copy. Worse, `serverStatus.ts` mapped **any non-2xx → `deploying`**, and a
dead-but-resolving quick tunnel returns 502 — a permanent false "updating" badge with zero builds.
**Fix:** `<Switch>` on the state with distinct copy (amber "updating" for `deploying`, rose "can't reach
the server — check VPN" for `unreachable`), and non-2xx now reports `unreachable`. Auto-reload is
unaffected: a real deploy sets `sawDeploying` from the sentinel *before* `deploy.sh` clears it and
restarts (`deploy.sh:82`). **This mislabel is what caused the misdiagnosis** — never claim a deploy we
cannot see.

**Why 2 — builds really can start with no push.** `check-release.sh:14` compared the working-tree
`HEAD` to `origin/release`. Any persistent drift makes them unequal **forever**, so the 2-minute
`noviq-deploy.timer` fires every tick. The drift was usually self-inflicted: on a failed health probe
`deploy.sh:109` does `git reset --hard $PREV_COMMIT`, pinning `HEAD` *behind* release → next tick
rebuilds **the same broken commit** (full CUDA build) → fails → rolls back → forever. No breaker, no
backoff. Manual VM git state (checked-out branch / stash / worktree — both outstanding there) does the
same. **Fix:** trigger now compares `origin/release` to a recorded `LAST_DEPLOYED_SHA` (written *before*
the build, so a rollback can't re-arm it), and skips entirely when `origin/release` equals a parked
`DEPLOY_FAILED_SHA`. `deploy.sh` writes that breaker file before rolling back and `rm`s it on a healthy
deploy. Breaker clears on a new push, or by hand to force a retry.

**Why 3 — a killed deploy pinned the banner forever.** `health.rs:44` reported `deploying` on mere
*existence* of `$NOVIQ_DATA_DIR/DEPLOYING`; the `trap cleanup EXIT` that removes it does **not** run on
SIGKILL (OOM, `systemctl kill`, VM reset). An orphaned sentinel also makes the FR-017 probe roll back a
**good** binary. **Fix:** `sentinel_fresh(path, max_age)` ages it out by mtime,
`NOVIQ_DEPLOY_SENTINEL_MAX_AGE_MIN` default **120 min** — deliberately generous, since too low clears
the banner mid-build and shows users a broken page. Split as a pure fn so tests need no env mutation;
3 unit tests (absent / fresh / stale).

**Files.** `deploy/check-release.sh` (rewritten trigger), `deploy/deploy.sh` (`TARGET_SHA`,
`LAST_SHA_FILE`, `FAILED_SHA_FILE`, breaker on rollback + clear on success),
`src-tauri/src/api/health.rs` (`sentinel_fresh`/`sentinel_max_age`/`deploy_in_progress` + tests),
`src/components/ServerStatusBanner.tsx`, `src/stores/serverStatus.ts`,
`deploy/test_deploy_rollback.sh` (cases 3-6: breaker holds, drift alone does NOT trigger, **a real push
still DOES**, success clears breaker), `specs/014-server-thin-client/deployment-and-updates.md`
(inlined the old looping logic — corrected with a do-not-revert note).

**Cross-cutting / follow-ups.**
- ⚠️ **The live VM runs OUT-OF-TREE copies** (`deploy/deploy.sh:9-11` → `/opt/noviq/deploy.sh`).
  Committing here changes **nothing** on the box until they are copied across; `diff` both, and confirm
  whether `check-release.sh` is also out-of-tree.
- Phase 1 diagnosis still owed: `HEAD` vs `origin/release`, `deploy.log` stanza frequency, sentinel
  mtime, `pgrep cargo`. Containment if a loop is live: `sudo systemctl stop noviq-deploy.timer`.
- Root cause behind dead URLs and stale tabs is the **Cloudflare quick tunnel** rotating its hostname on
  restart; a *named* tunnel with a stable hostname is the real fix (`noviq-url-watch` only tracks churn).
- Sentinel max-age default (120 min) was picked without a measured worst-case CUDA build — confirm from
  `/var/log/noviq/deploy.log` and tune per box.

## 2026-07-24 — Retrieval pool: ECHO_VEC_K 20→25, ECHO_FTS_K 20→10 (VM `.env`, live)

> ⚙️ Config-only change on the VM (`/opt/noviq/echoAI/.env`), not code. Restarted
> `noviq-server`; verified live (query trace STEP 12 "Total unique chunks = 35").
> `release` NOT pushed — env config, and the amendment-graph WIP `cf4310d6` is held back.

**Why.** Architect wanted a 35-chunk LLM-context pool split ~70/30 vec/fts. Prior values
were 20/20 (→40 unique). Note the pool cap `ECHO_VEC_K`/`ECHO_FTS_K` is the per-list cap
INSIDE `union_merge` (`query_router.rs:1224`), NOT the fetch depth — the fetch of 70+70 is
budget-derived (`fetch_k = ctx_top_k*2`, `query_router.rs:905`) and is unchanged. So 25+10
caps the merge to ≤35 unique; the token budget (`build_context`) remains a second downstream
limiter (may yield <35 on heavy queries). For a hard 35 regardless, use `ECHO_CONTEXT_K=35`.

**Cross-cutting.** `union_merge` dedups by chunk_id, so overlapping vec/fts hits reduce the
total below 35. Values live only on the VM (untracked `.env`) — fold into `.env.example`
on the next code push to `release` so a rebuilt box keeps them. See PHR 099.

## 2026-07-18 — Notice Assist: match provisions as the GAZETTE prints them (the actual `Rule 4A(1)` bug)

> ✅ VM worktree `/tmp/rrwt3` at `b8ebb3d8`: **full suite 762 passed / 0 failed** (1 new test).
> Not flag-gated — the old matcher could not match real corpus text.

**Why.** The previous commit made `/reply` *honest* but it still reported a miss — trace
`fe568a07`. The new trace step earned its keep immediately:

```
Provisions invoked:  1
Per provision:       Rule 4A(1)=LookupMissed
```

**The notice invokes `Rule 4A(1)`, not `Rule 4`** — every earlier diagnosis this session assumed
the latter. `LookupMissed` means the statute resolved and retrieval ran, so the failure was the
**verbatim-containment gate**. The E&D Rules print that provision as:

```
2[4-A.-(1) If in the opinion of the authorized officer there are sufficient grounds …
```

`norm(content).contains(norm("Rule 4A(1)"))` could never match it: there is **no literal "Rule"**
before the number (that lives in `chunks.unit_label`, which `retrieve_for_mapreduce` does not
return), and a `.` sits between the letter and the clause paren — `norm` strips whitespace and
hyphens but **not** `.`. The rule was in the corpus the whole time.

**Fix.** `provision_matcher()` builds a regex from the token's *shape* — number, optional letter
suffix (`4-A`/`4A`), then each clause paren tolerating the `.`/`-`/space noise between them —
with `chunk_contains_provision()` replacing the raw containment check.

⚠️ **A first attempt shipped a wrong-provision bug and the test caught it.** The Rule 4-A chunk
ends *"…in accordance with rule 5."* — a **cross-reference**. An unanchored fallback matched it
and would have quoted that chunk as "Rule 5". The matcher now anchors to a **defining position**:
start of chunk or line, optionally past a gazette footnote marker like `2[`, then either the kind
word (`Rule 4`) or the number opening a clause (`4-A.` / `4.`). Referring mentions no longer
match. `\b` before the number also stops `4A(1)` matching inside `24A(1)`.

**Test** `provision_matcher_finds_the_gazette_rendering` asserts against the **verbatim** line 184
of the E&D Rules, plus the ordinary `4. Penalties.- (1)` rendering, plus both false-positive
guards.

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- Still not verified live; `/reply` needs re-running against the same notice.
- The same containment weakness exists wherever else a provision is matched against chunk BODY
  text without `unit_label` — worth an audit.
- `retrieve_for_mapreduce` still does not return `unit_label`; plumbing it through would make
  this matching exact rather than shape-based.

## 2026-07-18 — Notice Assist: stop claiming a rule is absent when only the lookup missed

> ✅ VM worktree `/tmp/rrwt2` at `b568a0be`, `--no-default-features --features server`:
> `cargo check --lib` exit 0; **full suite 761 passed / 0 failed** (3 new tests).
> **NOT flag-gated** — the old message was factually wrong, so there is nothing to A/B.

**Why.** Trace `5471d1ec` (and `020ac9ac` before it) — `/reply` told an officer that
**"Rule 4 — not found in the indexed corpus"** while trace `29448bd5` was quoting that very
rule out of the very same corpus. `ground_one` collapsed four distinct failures into one
`found = false`, and `support_brief` rendered all of them as a claim about the CORPUS that the
code could not support: it only ever knew that *its own narrow lookup* missed.

⚠️ **This is the INVERSE of the same-day instrument-binding fix.** The main query path had **no**
instrument binding and answered out of the wrong Act (`bd0d16e1`, Food Authority). Notice Assist
has a **hard** binding (`instrument_scope`) and so denied a rule that exists. Two paths, opposite
failure modes, one underlying fact: a bare `Rule 4` is ambiguous across ≥5 instruments here.

**Fix 1 — say only what the code knows.** New `frame::GroundOutcome`
{`NotAttempted`,`Found`,`InstrumentUnresolved`,`LookupMissed`,`NotInScope`}, each with its own
wording. `LookupMissed` now reads *"could not be located in the indexed text of that statute"* —
a claim scoped to the lookup, not the corpus.
⚠️ `CitedRule.found` is **kept** so sessions persisted before this field still deserialize, but it
is now **derived** — set only by `CitedRule::grounded()` / `::missed()`, never assigned directly,
with a test (`ground_outcome_and_found_cannot_drift`) pinning the two together. This is
deliberately not a second source of truth.

**Fix 2 — an unresolvable statute is no longer a miss.** `ground_one` previously returned early
when `instrument_scope` returned `None`. It now **widens to the full scope** and flags the result
`InstrumentUnresolved`: the text is quoted (it is real corpus text) **and** the brief says
*"This text is from **&lt;document&gt;**, but the statute your notice names could not be matched
to an indexed document — confirm this is the instrument the notice relies on."* Among full-scope
hits it picks the document whose name best matches the reference (`instrument_score`) rather than
whichever Act ranked first — so widening does not resurrect the 2026-07-10 wrong-statute bug
silently. **Never guesses, never denies.**

**Fix 3 — the assist path is now traceable.** It emitted exactly ONE step, so `020ac9ac` could not
be diagnosed from the log at all (its `log::warn!` never reached the journal either —
`RUST_LOG` is unset in `noviq-server.service`). New step **"Notice Assist — grounding outcome"**
records each provision's outcome and the document its text came from.

**Files:** `notice_assist/frame.rs` (`GroundOutcome`, constructors, `is_quotable`),
`notice_assist/compose.rs` (`ground_one` widen+flag, `all_grounded`, `support_brief` match arms),
`notice_assist/mod.rs` (trace step).

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- Sessions persisted before today deserialize with `outcome = NotAttempted`; `is_quotable()`
  falls back to the legacy `found` flag so their briefs still render. Cosmetic at worst.
- `instrument_score`'s empty-`wanted` bug (abbreviated refs like "E&D Rules, 1973" return 0
  before `year_hit` is computed) now matters MORE here: it is what pushes a provision into the
  `InstrumentUnresolved` path. Worth fixing next.
- Not verified live — the `/reply` replay against a real notice has not been run.

## 2026-07-18 — Instrument-affinity re-rank + provision-label normalisation (both flag-gated, default OFF)

> ✅ VM worktree `/tmp/rrwt` at `943d115`, `--no-default-features --features server`:
> `cargo check --lib` exit 0; **full suite 759 passed / 0 failed** (6 new tests).
> Both flags default OFF ⇒ zero behaviour change until enabled.

**Why (two production traces, same root cause).** A bare provision token is ambiguous across
this corpus — `Rule 4` exists in the E&D Rules 1973, the APT Rules 1974, the Delegation of
Financial Powers 2019, the SLGA Compendium and SPPRA — and the main query path did nothing to
bind it to the statute the user named.

- **`bd0d16e1`** — *"Rule 4(1) sub rule 3 **from sindh civil servants efficiency and disciplane
  rules 1973**"*. Deep search assembled 22 passages: **7 Compendium, 5 E&D, 5 Delegation,
  4 APT**. The cited "Rule 4" chunks came from the **Sindh Food Authority Act**, and the answer
  explained that Rule 4(1) of the E&D Rules *"pertains to the designation of the Secretary to
  Government, Food Department"* — Food Authority composition served as disciplinary law, with
  20 citations. **A fluent, well-cited answer from the wrong Act is worse than a refusal.**
- **`99cdbff2`** — *"search for rule 4(I)(a) sub rule 3"* (no statute named). 32 chunks
  retrieved: Rule 5, Rule 35 (SPPRA blacklisting), Rule 5 — **zero Rule 4**. The words "sub
  rule" matched every chunk containing "sub-rule (2)". The model refused, correctly.
  **Retrieval failed, not the LLM.**

**⚠️ Constraint honoured — this is NOT the reverted `citation_fast_path`.** That fix (gate at
`query_router.rs:249`) *bypassed* vector search and picked a source by affinity alone, resolving
"rule 16" to the Secretariat Manual's "Steno Typist"; the architect turned it OFF with the ruling
*"every query uses the single hybrid-union retrieval path — no special-case citation routing."*
Retrieval here still runs in full; instrument match is folded in as **one more ranking signal**
next to salience and entity affinity, and **nothing is ever filtered out** — so a wrong guess
degrades ordering instead of producing the false *"not found in the indexed corpus"* that
`notice_assist`'s hard `instrument_scope` filter yields today.

**Fix 1 — instrument-affinity re-rank (`ECHO_INSTRUMENT_BOOST`, default 1.0 = off).**
- `query_router::instrument_ranks()` — scores each distinct document name against the **whole
  query** via the existing `notice_assist::compose::instrument_score`, returns `None` when
  nothing clears `>= 2` (the same bar `instrument_scope` uses). Shared by both paths so the
  threshold lives in one place.
- `query_router::apply_instrument_boost()` — graded positional re-score, wired as **S3c** right
  after `apply_entity_boost` (`query_router.rs` ~:1300).
- `deep_search::assemble::PassageSet::prioritize_instrument()` — called from
  `deep_search/mod.rs` **before `packed()`** (whose round sort is stable, so instrument order
  survives). Deep bypasses the normal path entirely, so wiring only one would have missed
  `bd0d16e1` — which is a deep-search trace.
- ⚠️ **`expand::detect_instrument` was evaluated and rejected** for this: its regexes require
  capitalised text (the real query is lowercase) **and it falls back to `"the applicable
  local-government rules"` for any input**, which would have fired the boost on every query.
  Scoring the raw query against the document name needs no extractor at all.
- Traces now print the **packed source mix** (`file×N`), not just a verdict — the `bd0d16e1`
  failure was invisible precisely because nothing recorded which documents won.

**Fix 2 — provision-label normalisation (`ECHO_PROVISION_NORM`, default off).**
`chunks.unit_label` is the **bare** provision (`"Rule 4"`), never `"Rule 4(1)(a)"`.
`augment_provision_terms()` appends the base label to the retrieval query (additive — the LLM
prompt still gets `query_text`). Reuses the existing `detect_citation`; no third citation scheme
was added. This also disposes of the `4(I)`-vs-`4(1)` typo for free, since the base label drops
clause parens entirely. ⚠️ A first attempt guarded on `query.contains(base)` and suppressed the
exact case it was meant to fix (`"rule 4"` *is* a substring of `"rule 4(i)(a)"`) — the
`base == cite` check alone is the correct one.

**Files:** `services/query_router.rs` (knobs, `instrument_ranks`, `apply_instrument_boost`,
`augment_provision_terms`, S3c wiring, trace); `services/deep_search/assemble.rs`
(`prioritize_instrument` + 2 tests); `services/deep_search/mod.rs` (call site + source-mix trace);
`services/assistant/capabilities/notice_assist/mod.rs` (`mod compose` → `pub(crate)` so the
primitive is shared rather than duplicated).

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- **Re-ranking is not recall.** `99cdbff2` retrieved *zero* Rule 4 chunks — boosting cannot
  surface what never entered the pool. Fix 2 targets that, and may not be sufficient; the next
  lever would be a targeted second retrieval pass on the canonical token.
- **`instrument_score` has a latent bug** (found separately): for an abbreviated reference like
  *"E&D Rules, 1973"* the `wanted` set collapses to empty (`E`/`D` ≤2 chars, `Rules` a stopword,
  `1973` all-digits) so it returns 0 **before** `year_hit` is computed. Both traces spell the
  statute out, so neither is blocked, but abbreviated queries get no boost.
- **Not yet verified live.** Unit-verified only; the end-to-end replay of both queries against
  the real corpus with the flags on has not been run.

## 2026-07-18 — Deep search: issue-driven facet expansion (flag-gated, default OFF)

> ✅ VM (worktree at `e01d1ff3`, `--features llm,server`): `cargo check --bin noviq-server` exit 0;
> `deep_search::expand` **6/6** (3 new). Flag `ECHO_DEEP_ISSUE_SPOTTING` default OFF — zero behaviour
> change until enabled.

**Symptom (case-study audit, SLGA-2013 omnibus resolution):** deep search fixed retrieval BREADTH
(single-pass cited a *definitions clause* as the auction rule → deep pulled 22 real citations, found the
actual auction/reserve rule, flagged a hallucinated figure) — but **both normal and deep missed the two
highest-value legal issues**: conflict of interest (the parking bidder is the Chairman's relative) and
quorum not maintained (members left before the vote). Also missed: omnibus-bundling / per-item
Government-vs-Council sanction.

**Root cause:** `deep_search/expand.rs::expand_query` is ITEM-driven. Its faithful-decomposition prompt
(`3c9037ad`) deliberately splits only explicitly-stated parts and FORBIDS inferring topics (to avoid the
old "always 4–6 facets" padding regression that pulled off-domain passages). So it decomposed the five
enumerated disposal items and retrieved their property rules, but never spun a facet for the legal issues
IMPLIED by facts buried in the prompt. Issue-spotting needs recognising those facts as issues — which
faithful decomposition forbids by design.

**Fix (NOT by loosening faithful decomposition — that re-breaks padding):** a gated, deterministic
issue-spotting stage. `expand.rs::spot_issues(query, instrument)` runs after the item facets (when
`issue_spotting_enabled()`) and appends a sub-question per latent issue **only when its trigger fact is
actually present in the prompt** — the inverse of the padding bug, so it stays faithful. Four trigger→
template rules (quorum · conflict-of-interest · write-off/sanction-limit · omnibus/Government-sanction),
each anchored to the named instrument via `detect_instrument` (acronym "SLGA 2013" / "<Name> Act…" /
Constitution / generic fallback). Capped at `ISSUE_MAX=3`, deduped against item facets, within the
`MAX_FACETS` budget. The enlarged sub-question set flows unchanged through the concurrent round-1
retrieval, the coverage check (drops any issue leg that retrieves nothing — safe), and synthesis.

**Flag:** `deep_search::issue_spotting_enabled()` (`ECHO_DEEP_ISSUE_SPOTTING`, default OFF), mirroring
`agentic_enabled()`. Rollout = config flip + restart, no rebuild. Design doc:
`specs/025-agentic-deep-search/issue-driven-facet-expansion.design.md`.

## 2026-07-17 (b) — Ordinal recall: prompt-injection lost to grounding; short-circuit instead

> ✅ VM (worktree at deployed `9b990879`, `--features llm,server`): `cargo check` exit 0;
> `assistant::memory` **20/20** (3 new). Follows the deploy of the (a) entry below, which FAILED
> the live replay — this is the fix.
> ✅ **DEPLOYED `e01d1ff3` on `release` + LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-17.** Fresh 8-question replay:
> **Q6 "what was my first question?" → the `recall` short-circuit fired: 3 ms, no retrieval, no
> model, correct Q1** (was a refusal on `9b990879`). Q1–Q5 unchanged. Q7 = accepted known limit
> (below). Confirmed from prod traces (`$ECHO_LOG_DIR/queries`, `Total time: 3 ms`, `Conversation
> recall` step, no citations).

**Symptom (live replay of `9b990879`):** the (a) fix injected the recalled turn into the grounded
system prompt and it landed cleanly (block present, overhead measured, no overflow) — but the model
**ignored it**. Q6 "what was my first question?" → **refusal** ("The retrieved documents do not
contain enough information"): the grounding prompt's refuse-if-not-in-documents rule outranks a
system-prompt note when no legal passage supports the question. Q7 "compare the first one with third
one" → the model compared **documents** (Constitution.pdf), reading "first/third one" as retrieved
passages. **A strongly-grounded RAG model must not be asked to recall conversation structure** (same
class as "never ask an LLM to count").

**Fix — deterministic short-circuit BEFORE capability dispatch (`mod.rs` `run_turn`):** a new
intercept `memory::direct_recall_answer(pool, conv, query)` in the same pre-dispatch chain as
`greeting`/low-signal/`count`, returning `TurnResponse { capability: "recall", citations: [] }` for a
PURE recall question — no retrieval, no model, no possible refusal (the shape of the deterministic
Count capability, ADR-0019). The existing tail persists + stamps it.

**`is_pure_recall(query, refs)` gate:** an ordinal turn-ref (`parse_ordinal_refs`) **plus** a
first/second-person anchor (`my`/`your`/`our`) **and** no comparison/summarise verb. So a legal "the
first schedule" (no turn noun) and the anchorless compound "compare the first one with the third one"
both fall through to normal retrieval — only "what was my first question?" / "read me your last
answer" short-circuit. Shared `fetch_turn_lists` helper (also refactored into the v1
`ordinal_recall_block`, which stays as best-effort for compound cases).

**Accepted known limit (user OK'd 2026-07-17):** Q7 "compare the first one with third one" routes to
retrieval and compares DOCUMENTS (live: "First Schedule vs Third Schedule"), because a bare "the
first one" — no `my`/`question`/`chat` — is genuinely ambiguous. **Naming the turns resolves it:**
the reworded Q8 "compare **my first question in this chat** with my third questions" compared the
real turns correctly (live). The disambiguator is the possessive anchor `is_pure_recall` keys on.
User's stance: fine as-is, just phrase it explicitly. Deferred fix option (NOT chosen): route a
compound compare-over-turns query to a transform-style no-retrieval path feeding only the two turns.

## 2026-07-17 — Ordinal turn-recall: "what was my first question?" named the wrong turn

> ✅ VM (worktree at `5783001b`, `--features llm,server`): `cargo check` exit 0; `assistant::memory`
> **17/17** (6 new); `query_router` regression green. Deterministic — no model in the recall path.
> Graph-memory **tier 2** (`Desktop\ui\GRAPH.png`): numbered turn nodes, looked up on demand.

**Symptom (prod replay 2026-07-17, `5783001b`):** Q6 *"what was my first question?"* answered
**"who is competent authority for that?"** — that was **Q3**, the oldest turn still inside the
4-pair verbatim window. Q1 had been evicted, so the model named the oldest turn it could still
*see*. **No window size fixes this:** an ordinal ("first", "third", "last") addresses a turn by
its POSITION, not content, so it can't be embedded (zero semantic overlap with "grounds for
penalty") and isn't in `recent_turns`. The chat store already holds every turn — `chat_message`
keeps a dense `seq` and evicted turns are only marked `summarized = 1`, never deleted. What was
missing was the **lookup**.

**Fix — `services/assistant/memory.rs::ordinal_recall_block(pool, conversation_id, query)`:**
a deterministic `seq` lookup. `parse_ordinal_refs` matches an ordinal token (`first`..`tenth`,
`1st`..`10th`, `last`/`previous`/`latest`) *adjacent to* a turn noun (`question`→user,
`answer`/`reply`/`response`→assistant, `one`/`thing`→whole exchange); a legal ordinal with a
non-turn noun ("first appeal", "first schedule") does NOT match. It reads the FULL turn history
including `summarized = 1` rows, **excludes the current in-flight user turn** (already appended
before this runs) from the question list so "first" = the real Q1 and "last" = the turn before
this one, quotes each resolved turn (300-char cap), and renders a non-citable
`=== EARLIER TURNS IN THIS CONVERSATION (recall) ===` block. Empty string when no ordinal is
referenced → zero cost on the common turn. Fixes Q6 *and* Q7 ("compare the first one with the
third one" → injects turn 1 and turn 3, both sides).

**Seam — why it's appended to `sys`, not `prior_turns_block` (`guidance.rs::run`):** the block is
`sys.push_str`-ed alongside `ATTACHMENT_SCOPE_OVERRIDE`, which `route_scoped`'s `law_overhead`
MEASURES (`est_tokens(system_prompt)`, query_router.rs:861), so the law budget shrinks to fit and
the prompt cannot overflow. This is the exact failure that got the earlier UNMEASURED
`memory_block` injection reverted (`80048b37`); measuring (`9f40d4aa`) is what makes the `sys`
seam safe now. `prior_turns_block` was the wrong home — it's a pure function over the capped
`history` slice and has neither DB access nor the evicted turns. Placed BEFORE the scope override
(override keeps the last word) and BEFORE the deep/single branch, so **both** paths get it (deep
wraps `{sys}`). Zero signature churn.

**Deferred:** cross-chat linking (explicitly not wanted — recall stays per-`conversation_id`);
turn→law / turn→entity graph edges ("which rule did you cite earlier?"); re-landing pinned-facts/
summary injection (same measured-`sys` seam now makes it safe, separate change).

## 2026-07-16 — A question mark was switching conversation memory off

> ✅ VM: `query_router::` **71/71**, `intent_router::` **47/47**, `cargo check` exit 0.
> ⚠️ Trace audit of a REAL 8-turn chat drove every fix here — not theory.
> **Read the traces at `$ECHO_LOG_DIR/queries`** = `/opt/noviq/echoAI/logs/ab_rerank/queries` in prod.
> `echoAI/logs/queries` is STALE (June) and misled me for ten minutes.

**Report:** "answers are also not connected with each other", and the new full-window banner never
fired after 8 questions. Audited the eight real traces. **Five of eight turns were broken, for FOUR
independent reasons**, and the banner was right not to fire.

| # | Question (as typed) | history | What happened |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "What penalties can be imposed under the E&D Rules?" | 0 | correct (first turn) |
| 2 | "and for bs-17 officer" | 177 | ✅ `and ` prefix |
| 3 | "who is the competent authority for that?" | **0** | ❌ RC1 punctuation |
| 4 | "what about the appeal timeline?" | — | ❌ RC2 — AmendmentChain, 0 links, **7 ms, no retrieval** |
| 5 | "can it be extended?" | 220 | ✅ ≤5 words |
| 6 | "what was my first question?" | 215 | ❌ RC3 — oldest visible turn was **Q4** |
| 7 | "compare the first one with third one." | **0** | ❌ RC1 vocabulary |
| 8 | "i was asking for my chat not the documents." | **0** | ❌ RC1 vocabulary |

### RC1 — a trailing `?` switched memory off (the big one)
`is_followup_query` built `padded = format!(" {lower} ")` from RAW text, then matched space-delimited
tokens: `" that "`. `"…for that?"` contains `" that?"` — **no match** → `prior_turns_block` returns
empty → **zero history reaches the model**. Word-boundary matching was running on non-word-boundaries.
**Fix:** normalise punctuation to spaces first (keep `-` for BS-17, `/` for n/a), then pad.
Vocabulary gaps killed Q7/Q8 too: only `"first question"` existed (not `"first one"`), only
`"i asked"` (not `"i was asking"`), only `"this chat"` (not `"my chat"`). All added.

**⚠️ KNOWN LIMIT left deliberately unfixed:** `names_own_subject` is case-sensitive, so
`"Who is the Competent Authority for that?"` still loses its history while the lowercase form keeps
it. I tried overriding when the query ENDS on a bare pronoun — **it broke the Q12 regression**
(`"…Principles of Policy, and whose responsibility is it to act on them?"` also ends on a pronoun,
but there it binds in-sentence). Telling them apart needs the antecedent, not the surface form. Every
real prod failure was lowercase, so this is not what broke the chat. Test
`known_limit_capitalisation_suppresses_anaphora` documents it. **Do not "fix" it with a trailing-word hack.**

### RC2 — bare "timeline"/"history" skipped the corpus entirely
`intent_router/classifier.rs` cue `\b(timeline|history|…)\b` @ weight 1.0 → `Intent::Timeline` →
`Capability::AmendmentChain` (`assistant/intent.rs:190`) = deterministic SQL/graph, **no retrieval, no
model**. So a cue hit does not mis-rank an answer, it **skips the law**. In this domain "timeline"
means a DEADLINE ("appeal timeline") and "history" a RECORD ("service history").
**Fix:** the bare words are gone; `timeline|history` must now be anchored to amendment/version
language (`amendment history`, `timeline of amendments`). `chronology|evolution|over time|when was|
since \d{4}` and the weight-0.9 amendment cue are untouched, so both existing expectations still pass.

### RC3 — the trace was lying, which is why nobody saw any of this
`("Prior turns", … history.chunks(2).filter(…).count().min(2))` counted the pairs the caller HANDED
us. It printed **"2 pairs from history" on the very turns that got `history 0`** — both numbers in the
same trace, contradicting each other, unread for weeks. Third instance of one disease this week
(hardcoded `law_overhead`; the citation-excerpt fill notice). **Fix:** derive it from the block that
is actually injected, and name the gate when it drops everything:
`"0 pair(s) injected (~0 tok) of 2 available  ⚠ DROPPED — is_followup_query judged this query self-contained"`.

### RC4 — the window: 2 → 4 exchanges (re-land of 325618ab)
`prior_turns_block` re-truncated to the last 2 pairs ON TOP of the caller's
`recent_turns_verbatim` (8 messages = 4 pairs) trim — two places deciding one window. That is why Q6
("what was my first question?") could only see back to **Q4**. Safe to re-land now: reverted in
`80048b37` when this block was unbounded AND unmeasured, but `law_overhead` MEASURES it since
`9f40d4aa`, so growth costs law passages instead of overflowing. Overhead 1937 → ~2317 (43% → 51%),
law −380 tok ≈ −3 passages. The bound now lives where it belongs: config window × the 600-char/turn cap.

**Test change worth flagging:** `measured_overhead_grows_…` asserted the block stays `< 700` tok — a
number that silently encoded the old 2-pair window. It correctly failed on this change. Rewritten to
assert the bound that is really this function's job (the 600-char/turn cap bites: 30k chars → ~945
tok), not a pair count that belongs to the caller.

### The banner (22e8335a) was right to stay quiet
Measured across the 8 real turns: overhead **1520–1735 tok = 34–38%** of the 4512 limit; 80% needs
~3610. **The chat never fills up** — history was capped at 2 exchanges, so it structurally cannot.
The premise behind the banner was inverted: the problem was never "too full", it was "remembers
almost nothing, and 3 times in 8 remembered *nothing*". After this change the ceiling is ~51% — still
under 0.80. **Left dormant deliberately as a safety net for the graph work. Do NOT lower the
threshold to make it fire** — that would warn about a chat that is fine.

### Still open (architect's call)
- **Ordinal recall** ("what was my first question?") is unfixable by ANY window size in a long chat —
  needs a `seq` lookup (the graph design, `Desktop\ui\GRAPH.png`).
- Carry-over into a new chat = the **summary** (the only honest "anything" mechanism) + pinned facts.
- Deep cost-guard.

## 2026-07-16 — The "context window full" notice has never once fired. Now it's measured.

> ✅ VM: `cargo check --lib --no-default-features --features llm,server` **exit 0**; `guidance::`
> **9/9** incl. both new tests. Frontend `tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run build` exit 0. VM copies
> md5-verified identical to the committed files.
> ⚠️ **NOT browser-verified**: nobody has watched the amber appear or the red block in a real long
> chat. That needs ~10 questions in one conversation.

### The bug: the notice measured the wrong thing, so it never fired

User report: testers watch a long chat quietly degrade into "no document found" / thin answers with
**no warning at all**. FR-018a's fresh-chat notice exists (`context_fill_threshold = 0.80`, banner in
`ChatPage.tsx`) — it just never showed.

`guidance.rs` built its fill number from **`qr.citations` excerpts** — the ~9 passages the model
QUOTED — not the ~33 chunks it READ:
```rust
let law: Vec<String> = qr.citations.iter().map(|c| c.excerpt.clone()).collect();
let plan = assistant::plan_budget(&EstimateCounter, window, cap, cfg, false, mem, text, &law);
```
That lands ~35% when the real prompt is at **94%**. It never crosses 0.80. **Dead feature.**
Same disease as the last two bugs: **two places measuring one thing, and the wrong one is on screen.**
`plan_budget` is a post-hoc audit that runs AFTER generation — it is the same object that reported
`summary_included: true` for a summary that was never injected.

### ⚠️ The trap: "just use the real prompt size" is ALSO wrong

The prompt is **~always ~100% full by construction** — `ctx_budget = window − answer − overhead`, then
law packs up to it. Prod traces across one six-turn chat: **94 / 95 / 99 / 101 / 96 / 98%**. A "real
prompt fullness" bar would warn on turn ONE, every turn, forever. Useless in the opposite direction.

**What actually degrades a long chat is the LAW BUDGET SHRINKING as history grows.** So fullness now
measures the non-law overhead against the point where the law budget hits its floor:

| Exchanges | Overhead | `used/limit` | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1,557 | 35% | quiet |
| 2 | 1,937 | 43% | today's default |
| 10 | 3,457 | **77%** | thinning |
| ~15 | 4,512 | **100%** | law floored → truncation → refusals |

`limit = gen_max_prompt − CONTEXT_TOKEN_BUDGET` — past it the floor itself overflows the cap (the
`⚠ BUDGET FLOORED` trace) and `llm.rs` head+tail truncation drops the law out of the middle. That is
the honest "this chat is full", and the existing 0.80 threshold fires at ~10 exchanges — which is
exactly where the architect's instinct put it independently.

### The fix — ship the measurement with the answer

- `query_router.rs`: new **`ChatFill { used, limit }`** + `QueryResponse.chat_fill`
  (`#[serde(default)]`). Computed ONCE next to where `law_overhead` is measured (9f40d4aa) and
  returned on **every** exit including the refusal paths — *a refusal in a nearly-full chat is exactly
  when the officer needs to be told the chat is out of room*. `check_cache()` and deep search return
  `None` (no single grounded prompt); deep is admin-only, so its stale estimate is contained.
- `assistant/mod.rs`: `AssembleInput.chat_fill` — measured value wins, `plan` stays as fallback.
- `guidance.rs`: `build_response(..., chat_fill, cfg)` threaded from `qr.chat_fill`.
- `ChatPage.tsx`: the notice moves OUT of the answer body (small grey text, once per answer — it would
  have repeated in every bubble once it started firing) to **one live banner at the composer**:
  amber at ≥80% ("this chat is N% full… replies may get thinner" + New chat), **red + `submit()`
  blocked at 100%** ("no room left to read the law properly"). Slash commands stay exempt (they never
  retrieve). Blocking is right at 100% *only* because the alternative there is a refusal anyway.
- **Deleted the lie.** The old banner said *"(your case facts carry over)"*. They do not: pinned facts
  are per-conversation AND are not injected at all (reverted in `80048b37`). The red banner now says
  plainly that you must restate anything Noviq needs.

**Tests:** `fill_notice_follows_measured_chat_fullness_not_the_prompt` (quiet at turn one, fires at
the floor) and `measured_fullness_overrides_the_post_hoc_estimate` (fails if anyone reverts to the
citation-excerpt estimate).

### 🔑 Process lessons from this change (three self-inflicted, all pattern-trust)
- A regex bulk-edit over `QueryResponse \{` matched **function signatures and the struct definition**,
  injected a field into a fn body and left a mangled `hat_fill`. Reverted both files; redone by hand
  with asserted-unique anchors. **Do not bulk-edit Rust literals with a loose regex.**
- The `AssembleInput` file list was built from a grep for `context_fill` — which only finds
  *consumers*. `transform.rs` and `summarize_doc.rs` **construct** it and never mention `context_fill`,
  so they were invisible. **Grep for the constructor (`AssembleInput {`), not for a field.**
- The Bash cwd **persists between calls**: a later `scp src-tauri/...` silently sent nothing because
  cwd had moved to `src-tauri/`, and the rebuild ran on stale files. Use absolute paths; verify the
  copy landed (md5) rather than trusting scp's exit.

### Follow-ups
- Deep search reports no measured fill (multi-round prompts) — still the old low estimate.
- "Continue in a new chat" carry-over is NOT built; until it is, the red banner sends the officer to a
  blank chat. **Carry-over = the summary (catches anything) + pinned facts (precision for the few
  patterns we can detect).** The three regex facts (grade / service / leave) are examples, NOT the
  memory — the architect was explicit that facts could be anything, and the summary is the only
  honest "anything" mechanism (LLM fact-extraction can confabulate; unacceptable for legal work).

> herring** on this Ubuntu-20.04 VM, *not* a code fault. Fix: pre-seed the install dir by copying
