### Smoke test results (shadow server, isolated PG, 2026-07-16)

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `assist_status` / `assist_exit` with **no token** | **401** both — auth enforced |
| 1 | login as seeded admin | 64-char bearer token |
| 2 | fresh conversation | `{"open":false}` |
| 3 | **`{"conversationId":…}`** (what the browser sends) | accepted — serde alias works |
| 4 | `/help` → `assist_status` | **`{"open":true}`** ← the desync fix, proven |
| 5 | `assist_exit` | `{"left":true}` |
| 6 | `assist_status` after exit | `{"open":false}` |
| 7 | `assist_exit` again (Leave clicked twice) | `{"left":false}` — idempotent, no error |
| 8 | `poll_turn` transcript after exit | latest turn is still **`/help`** — **`assist_exit` recorded NO chat turn**, which is the whole point of the fix |

Check 8 is the direct proof of the original complaint: leaving no longer runs a chat query. Check 4
is the direct proof that a reopened conversation can now be told it is in assist mode.

**Still unproven:** the browser UI itself — the A→B→A banner and the "Leaving…" button state have
not been clicked through. Only pure tests + HTTP were exercised.

### 1. Notice Assist "Leave" ran a whole chat query to exit (F022)

**Symptom (user):** "after we launch `/` commands assistant mode and while clicking on leave it
just not move out from assistant mode, it runs one chat query then comes out."

**Cause:** the button literally typed the command and pressed send —
`ChatPage.tsx`: `onClick={() => { setAssistMode(false); setInput("/cancel"); submit(); }}`.
So leaving posted a visible `/cancel` user bubble, spun the composer, round-tripped, and appended
an assistant reply. It is **cheap** (server `is_exit` → `session::delete` → early return; `reply()`
does **not** invoke the model, so no inference) — this was UX noise, not a slow turn.

**Why the obvious fix is wrong:** the assist session is **server state**
(`notice_assist_session`). While its row exists, `assistant/mod.rs:478` computes `assist_open` and
routes **every** turn in the conversation into the notice flow. `assistMode()` is only a *mirror*.
Deleting the `submit()` call would hide the banner while the session stayed open — and the
officer's next ordinary question would be silently hijacked into the notice flow. Strictly worse,
and invisible. (Same shape as the `/me` toggle race: one source of truth for session state; a
second, local copy drifts.)

**Fix:** give the button its own channel instead of making it impersonate a user.
- `api/query.rs` — **`POST /api/assist_exit`** `{conversation_id}` → `{left: bool}`. Loads (to
  report whether a session existed), deletes, returns. Idempotent; auth required, mirroring
  `cancel_turn`.
- `api/router.rs` — route registered next to `/cancel_turn`.
- `api/assistant.ts` — `assistExit(conversationId)` through the existing transport seam.
- `ChatPage.tsx` — `leaveAssist()` replaces the fake submit; `leaving()` disables the button
  ("Leaving…"); `leaveError()` renders **inside the banner**. On failure the banner deliberately
  **stays up** — the session is still open server-side, so hiding it would strand the officer in
  assist mode with no sign of it. (No silent `catch {}` — see the clipboard lesson.)

Typing `/cancel`, `/exit`, `/stop`, `/done` still works and is **unchanged**; the button just no
longer fakes a message to reach the same code.

### 1b. …and the same mirror was stale on every conversation SWITCH (fixed)

**Correction to the first draft of this entry**, which claimed a *page reload* stranded the officer
in assist mode. It does not: `onMount` always mints a **fresh** conversation id ("every launch
starts on a blank New chat"), so F5 lands in a new conversation where the hidden banner is correct.
The real defect is in the two paths that **switch** conversations, where `assistMode` was simply
never updated:

- **`newChat()`** reset turns/attachments/streaming but **not `assistMode`** → the 🛡️ banner
  followed the officer out of assist mode into a brand-new chat that has **no session**. The banner
  claimed a state that did not exist (false positive).
- **`selectConversation()`** never set `assistMode` at all → reopening a past conversation where
  `/help` had been typed showed **no banner while the session was still open**, so every question in
  it was still routed into the notice flow. Assist mode with no sign of it (false negative — the
  dangerous one). Reachable from the history list, which is also where you land after F5.

**Fix:** ask the server instead of guessing.
- `api/query.rs` — **`POST /api/assist_status`** `{conversation_id}` → `{open: bool}`. One indexed
  PK lookup; no model, no retrieval.
- `api/router.rs` + `api/assistant.ts` — route + `assistStatus()`.
- `ChatPage.tsx` — `refreshAssistMode(id)`; both switch paths clear the banner first (the previous
  conversation's value is *always* wrong for the new one) and `selectConversation` then corrects it
  upward from the server. `newChat` skips the round trip — a fresh UUID provably has no session.
  A stale in-flight reply can't clobber a conversation the officer has since left
  (`if (conversationId() === id)`).

On a failed status read the banner stays hidden (the common case, and the same state as before the
call existed) with a `console.warn` — not swallowed. Residual: if that read keeps failing, a live
session is invisible in the UI; the server still routes correctly.

### 2. Guardrail vocabularies moved into `bureaucrat.toml` (Constitution VI)

The greeting/probe fast-paths were already **live** (`is_greeting_or_intro`, `is_low_signal` →
nudge/greeting branches before retrieval; they also short-circuit the F025 deep loop). Their word
lists were hardcoded Rust `const`s — the Principle VI gap noted in PHR 0006's follow-up
("extend probe list from query_log if new filler shows up"), which needed a rebuild to do.

- `config/personas/bureaucrat.toml` — new **`[guardrails]`** section: `greetings` (12), `about` (16),
  `probes` (35), copied **verbatim** from the consts. Tunable via `ECHO_PERSONA_TOML` + restart.
- `persona.rs` — `Guardrails` struct + `Default` impl carrying the same lists.
- `intent.rs` — `is_greeting_or_intro` / `is_low_signal` now read `PersonaConfig::get().guardrails`
  and delegate to pure `*_with(query, lists…)` forms, so the rules stay unit-testable without
  loading the process-wide config. Signatures of the public predicates are unchanged.

**⚠️ The compatibility trap this was designed around:** `PersonaConfig::get()` falls back to the
embedded default **silently** on a parse error (log line only). A *required* `[guardrails]` field
would therefore make any pre-existing on-disk `ECHO_PERSONA_TOML` fail to parse and **silently
revert the whole tuned persona**. So the section and every field carry `#[serde(default)]`: an old
override file still parses, and a partial section (say `probes` only) keeps the built-in
greetings/about.

**Tests:** `embedded_guardrails_match_the_builtin_defaults` (the TOML *is* the old hardcoded list —
fails if one is edited without the other) and `guardrails_section_is_optional_for_older_override_files`
(parses `EMBEDDED` truncated at `[guardrails]`). Both **unrun** — see the status banner.

**Deliberately NOT done — the deep cost-guard.** The second known guardrail gap (a 1-word *real*
query like `penalties` running a ~135 s deep loop) is left alone: it is a **product decision**, not
an implementation (blocking a query the user explicitly asked for is a bad default), and deep search
is now **admin-only**, so the blast radius is one user. Wants a decision before code.

## 2026-07-16 — Structural fix: the law budget now MEASURES its overhead (and the [n] landmine is defused)

Fixes the two root causes behind the revert below. Both were **pre-existing**; today's memory work only made
them fire.

### Bug 1 — `law_overhead` was a hardcoded guess, and it was ALWAYS ~400 tokens short

`route_scoped_with_override` carved `law_overhead = 1500` for "system prompt + question + a little history",
then `ctx_budget = window − gen_max_tokens − law_overhead` (= 5412) and packed law up to it
(`build_context_pass` — the cut-from-the-bottom logic, which works fine). **Nothing ever measured the real
overhead.** Measured now:

| Component | Real |
|---|---|
| system prompt (persona 470 + guidance + grounding v5.4) | **1139 tok** |
| question | ~18 tok |
| history (2 pairs, 600-char/turn cap) | ~340 tok |
| scaffold (ChatML + demo + chars/4 margin) | 400 tok |
| **total** | **~1897** — vs the hardcoded **1500** |

So `ctx_budget(5412) + overhead(1897) = 7309 > 6912` cap. **The budget could always overflow** — it only
survived because law rarely packed to its full ceiling. When it did (prod T4) the prompt hit 101%, `llm.rs`
head+tail truncation dropped the MIDDLE (the law), citations collapsed 9→7→8→3→3→0, and the model refused.

**Fix:** measure, don't guess.
- New `est_tokens(s)` (chars/4 — the same unit `build_context_pass` and the trace already use, so the budget is
  measured in the units it is spent in).
- New **`prior_turns_block(query, history)`** — the history block extracted OUT of `build_rag_prompt` so the
  budget can measure exactly what will be injected. `build_rag_prompt` now calls the same function: **one source
  of truth**, so the budget can never disagree with the prompt.
- The effective `system_prompt` (override + deep breadth directive) is now resolved **before** the budget — it
  could not be measured while it was still being chosen 20 lines later.
- `law_overhead = est_tokens(system_prompt) + est_tokens(query) + est_tokens(prior_block) +
  PROMPT_SCAFFOLD_TOKENS(400)`.
- Now exact: `law(5015) + overhead(1897) + answer(1280) = 8192`. **Cannot overflow by construction**; the law
  budget shrinks to make room for history, which is the allocator's stated policy ("law outranks history").
- The overhead is now **traced every turn** ("Prompt overhead (measured)"), with a `⚠ BUDGET FLOORED` warning
  when `CONTEXT_TOKEN_BUDGET` (2400) kicks in. It went stale invisibly for months; it can't now.

### Bug 2 — the citation demo was switched on by prompt WORDING

`wants_index_citations = system_prompt.contains("[n]")` — a stringly-typed flag. Two failures:
1. It fired on any prompt that merely **mentioned** `[n]`, **including one that forbade it**: the reverted
   memory instruction "never attach a [n] citation marker" flipped the demo ON for the 8B (which had never had
   it — the full grounding v5.4 contains **zero** literal `[n]`), and the demo's leave example hijacked answers
   — a question about *rules of power* returned `## Authority to Sanction Leave` then refused.
2. It **contradicted its own comment**: the decompose/Lookup override (`intent_router/mod.rs:287,302`) says
   "end every claim with its citation [n]", so the sniff *included* the exact path the comment says to exclude.

**Fix:** gate on the real condition — `compact_prompt_profile()`. The demo exists for SMALL models (the 0.5B
ollama A/B, Phase-0 fix 0a); Qwen3-8B follows the `[n]` instruction natively. Behaviour on the 8B is unchanged
(it never had the demo); the landmine is gone, and the decompose path is now excluded as its comment always
intended.

**Tests (67/67 green):** `measured_overhead_grows_with_the_system_prompt_and_history` (overhead tracks its
inputs — a constant does not — and the block stays bounded under a 5k-char history),
`citation_demo_is_not_switched_on_by_prompt_wording` (a prompt that FORBIDS `[n]` must not summon the demo).

**This unblocks re-landing the reverted memory work** (4-pair history, pinned facts + summary): the budget now
absorbs them by trimming law instead of overflowing. Re-land them one at a time, watching the traced overhead.

## 2026-07-16 — ⚠️ REVERTED 325618ab + 68d4f71a: they overflowed the context window in prod

**What happened:** the two prompt-growing memory fixes below (4-pair history window, and injecting pinned
facts + summary) **broke multi-turn chats in production**. User report: "after four chats it is now throwing
[the insufficient-info refusal]". Both are reverted; the two token-*neutral* fixes (`ce8957fb` conversation-
reference gate, `b438a3d8` demo suppression) are KEPT.

**The audit that found it** (admin's real conversation, via `/api/query_traces/<id>`):

| Turn | Prompt tok | Cap | Use | Cites | Answer | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 disciplinary action | 6546 | 6912 | **94%** | 9 | 2874 | real answer |
| T2 grade 16 officer | 6572 | 6912 | 95% | 7 | 3217 | real answer |
| T3 purchase 5 GPU | 6848 | 6912 | 99% | 8 | 3057 | real answer |
| T4 town officer purchase | **7029** | 6912 | **101%** | 3 | 2378 | **OVER CAP** |
| T5 rules of power | 6665 | 6912 | 96% | 3 | **147** | **REFUSAL** |
| T6 what happened? | 6815 | 6912 | 98% | 0 | 82 | **REFUSAL** |

Citations collapse **9 → 7 → 8 → 3 → 3 → 0** as history accumulates and squeezes the law out.

**🔴 ROOT CAUSE (architectural, PRE-EXISTING — the revert only buys headroom, it does not fix this):**
the **law budget is computed independently of history**. `route_scoped_with_override` fixes
`ctx_budget ≈ 5412 tok / top-K=36` from `window - gen_max_tokens - law_overhead` BEFORE retrieval; then
persona (~530), citation demo, history, memory and question are all stacked **on top**. **Nothing subtracts
history from the law budget**, so the prompt can and does exceed the cap. When it does, `llm.rs` head+tail
truncation fires and drops the **MIDDLE — which is the law passages** → citations collapse → refusal.

**The system was already at 94% of cap on turn ONE with zero history.** There was only ~6% (≈366 tok) of
headroom; the two reverted commits spent ~540 tok of it (history 2→4 pairs ≈ +340, memory_block ≈ +200).
Even the restored 2-pair state is razor-thin: 6546 + ~340 ≈ 6886 of 6912.

**⚠️ ALSO FOUND — a SECOND, independent bug (NOT fixed here):** T5 refused at **96%**, i.e. UNDER the cap. Its
raw output was `## Authority to Sanction Leave for Officers` → refusal, for a question about *rules of power in
the local govt act*. "Sanction Leave" exists nowhere but the **citation demo**. `b438a3d8` only suppresses the
demo when history is injected; T5 is all-lowercase with no anaphora → `is_followup_query` false → no history →
**demo injected → it hijacked the answer's topic and forced a refusal.** The demo was justified by a **0.5B**
ollama A/B (2026-06-13); prod is now **Qwen3-8B-AWQ**, which follows the `[n]` instruction natively.
**Recommendation: drop the demo on the non-compact path entirely** — it poisons answers AND costs tokens.

**Before re-landing the memory fixes, the budget must become history-aware:** compute the history/memory block
first and subtract it from `ctx_budget` (the allocator's own doc already says "law outranks history" — today
nothing enforces that in the prompt builder). Note `plan_budget` does model this correctly but **runs AFTER
generation as a post-hoc audit** and never controls the prompt — see the entry below.

## 2026-07-16 — Fix: the citation demo masqueraded as conversation history

**Symptom (caught by the >8-turn eviction test):** after a 6-turn chat, *"What was the very first thing I asked
you about in this conversation?"* → **"Who can sanction 30 days leave?"** — a question the user never asked.
That is the **one-shot citation demo** (Phase-0 fix 0a, 2026-06-13), a synthetic `user`/`assistant` exchange
`build_rag_prompt` injects immediately **before** the real `prior` block:
```
<|im_start|>system … <|im_end|>
{citation_demo}   ← fake turn — the EARLIEST "user" message the model can see
{prior}           ← the real conversation
```
From the model's side it is indistinguishable from conversation, so its answer was *correct on the evidence it
had*. Worse than the wrong answer: the demo mentions "the Secretary" and "leave of up to 30 days", so a user
asking *"what did we discuss about leave?"* could be told about a conversation that never happened — a
confabulation vector straight out of the prompt.

**Fix (`query_router.rs::build_rag_prompt`):** suppress the demo when `prior_block` is non-empty —
`wants_index_citations && prior_block.is_empty()`. Rationale: once real turns are present the model already has
**better** few-shot examples (its own earlier answers, carrying real `[n]` markers over the real corpus), so the
synthetic demo is redundant there as well as harmful. Self-contained turns still get it — that is the case the
0.5B ollama A/B actually measured (no citations zero-shot → `[n]` with one example). Also saves ~40 tokens on
follow-ups.

**Tests (66/66 green):** `citation_demo_never_masquerades_as_conversation_history` — demo absent when history is
present, real turns still injected, demo still present on a zero-shot turn.

**Also verified by the same test run — the summary fix (`68d4f71a`) works end-to-end:** after 6 turns (12
messages, `keep_recent=8` → T1/T2 evicted), *"Earlier in this conversation, did I ask you about the E&D Rules
1973?"* → *"you asked: 'What are the grounds for penalty under the Sindh Civil Servants Efficiency and
Discipline Rules 1973?'"* — recalled **verbatim from the summary alone**, since T1 was no longer in the
verbatim window.

## 2026-07-16 — Fix: pinned facts + running summary were budgeted but never injected

**Symptom/why:** `memory::load_for_turn` returns `MemoryContext { pinned_facts, recent_turns, summary }` every
turn, and `plan_budget` counts all three — the audit even reports `summary_included: true`. But only
`recent_turns` ever reached the model: **`build_rag_prompt(query, context, history, system_prompt, focus_hint)`
has no parameters for pinned facts or the summary.** Verified: `query_router.rs` and `guidance.rs` contain zero
references to `pinned_facts`/`mem.summary` (the only `summary` hits are the unrelated `graph_summary` GraphRAG
table). So the officer's stated grade/length-of-service and the running summary of evicted turns were computed,
paid for in the budget, reported as included, and silently dropped. **The audit was lying.**

Structural note found while tracing: **`plan_budget` runs AFTER generation** (`guidance.rs:293`, on the
`qr` result at `:288`) — it is a **post-hoc audit**, not the allocator that builds the prompt. The real prompt is
assembled by `build_rag_prompt` inside `route_scoped_with_override`, which does its own budgeting. That gap is
how the two drifted apart unnoticed.

**Fix (`guidance.rs`):** new `memory_block(mem)` appended to `sys` — **the same seam as
`ATTACHMENT_SCOPE_OVERRIDE`**, so BOTH the deep loop (which wraps `{sys}` in its synthesis prompt) and the
single-pass path receive it with **no signature churn** through `route_scoped_with_override` (3 call sites) or
`build_rag_prompt` (4). Two blocks:
- `=== ABOUT THIS OFFICER ===` — pinned facts, always injected (the allocator's own doc calls them must-keeps).
- `=== EARLIER IN THIS CONVERSATION ===` — the running summary, capped at `SUMMARY_CHAR_CAP` (800 chars) so
  background can never crowd retrieved provisions out of the saturated 8192 window.

Both are explicitly marked **NOT law and non-citable** — they are the only prompt content that isn't retrieved
context, so without that instruction the model could attach a `[n]` marker to the officer's own grade. Appended
**before** the scope override, so the override keeps the last word (its text cancels earlier instructions).

**Risk considered:** the deep path's `foreign_number_in_prose` check could caveat figures from pinned facts
("BPS-17", "10 years") since they aren't in the retrieved passages. It is a **soft caveat, not a refusal**, and
deep is admin-only — accepted. The normal-path `citation_gate` checks *legal references*, not arbitrary
figures, so it is unaffected.

**Tests (16/16 green):** `memory_block_injects_pinned_facts_and_summary`, `memory_block_caps_a_runaway_summary`,
`scope_override_still_follows_memory_in_the_system_prompt`. Existing gate tests
(`ungrounded_reference_is_suppressed_and_flagged`, `definite_refusal_ships_no_citations`) still pass — the
citation guarantee is intact.

## 2026-07-16 — Fix: conversation memory was dropped for cross-turn reasoning ("compare X with Z")

**Symptom (caught on PROD, not in tests):** in one chat, asked X (E&D grounds) → Y (SPPRA thresholds) → Z (RSO
appeal), then *"Compare the findings of the first thing I asked you about with my third question. What is the
connection between them?"* — the model answered about **supplementary questions in the Legislative Assembly**
(Rule 19) and **development project review reports** (Manual §30), then invented a confident "connection"
between them. Neither topic was ever in the conversation: it had matched the literal words "first/third
question" against the corpus. **Control proof:** the same intent phrased as *"And compare those two."* (4 words)
answered correctly from memory (RSO 2000 vs E&D Rules 1973). Same conversation, opposite results — decided
purely by phrasing.

**Why:** conversation memory is loaded on every turn (`memory::load_for_turn` → `assistant/mod.rs:424`) but
`build_rag_prompt` injects it **only if `is_followup_query(query)`** (`query_router.rs:2705`), and the same gate
also controls retrieval carry-over (`:735`). The gate was tuned for *short anaphoric* follow-ups ("And for
BS-22?"), so a long, self-describing cross-turn question failed all three of its signals: >5 words, no
continuation prefix, and — the subtle one — `names_own_subject` saw the capitalised **"What" opening the second
sentence**, treated it as a proper noun, and *suppressed* the `" them "` anaphora it had found. History was
then silently discarded. The gate exists for a real reason (the 2026-05-10 drift bug: truncated prior answers
made 1.5B–3B models parrot the previous opener) — but it over-suppressed.

**Fix (`query_router.rs::is_followup_query`):** new `CONVERSATION_REFERENCE` marker set — explicit references to
the conversation itself ("you told me", "you said", "i asked", "asked you", "first/second/third question",
"we discussed", "previously", "this conversation", "your answer", …). These are **unambiguous** (a corpus
question never says "you told me"), so they are checked **before** the `names_own_subject` suppression: a query
may name its own subject and *still* depend on prior turns ("compare the E&D Rules with what you told me
earlier"). Deliberately **excludes** bare "compare"/"difference between" — those are perfectly self-contained.

**Tests (64/64 green):** `followup_detector_flags_explicit_conversation_references` (incl. the verbatim prod
failure) + `followup_detector_still_skips_self_contained_comparisons`. The Q12 false-positive regression and
both `build_rag_prompt` history tests still pass — the drift-bug guard is intact.

**Known adjacent issue (NOT fixed, deliberately out of scope):** `names_own_subject` only skips the first token
of the whole string, so any capitalised word opening a *later* sentence ("Then…", "What…") still reads as a
proper noun and suppresses anaphora. That's what masked this bug. Fixing it broadens follow-up detection for
many queries (affects retrieval too) — worth its own change + eval, not a rider on this one.

## 2026-07-16 — Fix: deep-search RESUME was unreachable dead code (stable thread_id + status filter)

**Symptom/why:** F026 Part 1 shipped checkpoint/resume/time-travel and the repo tests passed — but **resume
could never fire in production**. `guidance.rs` built the durable-thread key as `conversation_id:{handle.id}`,
and `handle.id` is a fresh `Uuid::new_v4()` minted per turn (`scheduler.rs::register`). So every attempt got a
brand-new `thread_id`, `resume_deep` → `checkpoint::latest(thread_id)` always returned `None`, and the
auto-resume branch was dead code. Enabling `ECHO_DEEP_CHECKPOINT` would have written ~6 checkpoints per deep
turn and resumed exactly zero times. **The unit tests missed it because they call the repository directly with
a fixed `thread_id` — they exercised the parts, never the wiring.** Found while preparing to test the feature
live (the flag was never on, so no user impact).

**Fix:**
- **Stable thread key** — new `deep_search::deep_thread_id(conversation_id, query_text)`:
  `conversation_id:<hash of normalized question>` (trim + lowercase + collapse whitespace). Semantics: *stop a
  deep turn, ask the same thing again in the same conversation → continue where it left off*. Different
  question or different conversation → different thread, so no collisions/bleed. `guidance.rs` now calls it
  instead of interpolating the workload id.
- **Status filter** — new `checkpoint::latest_resumable()`: the latest row for the thread **only if its status
  is `interrupted`**. Load-bearing: without it, re-asking a question whose thread already completed would
  "resume" the `done` checkpoint and replay the stored answer — an **accidental cache, not a resume**. Only the
  newest row decides (an older `interrupted` row behind a `done` is history, not an anchor). `resume_deep` now
  uses it; plain `latest()` stays for history/inspection.

**Tests (22/22 green on VM, was 20):** `deep_thread_id_is_stable_across_attempts` (same Q → same thread; case/
whitespace normalized; different Q/conversation → different thread) and
`latest_resumable_only_resumes_an_interrupted_thread` (interrupted resumes; **completed does NOT**, even with an
older interrupted row behind it; `latest()` unaffected) — the latter against real PG.

**Still flag-gated OFF** (`ECHO_DEEP_CHECKPOINT` unset in prod). Resume is now *reachable* but **has never run
live** — that needs the flag on + an interrupt→re-ask test. Known remaining gap: resume works within a process;
it is NOT tied to a page reload/reconnect (no stable turn id from the FE). ADR-0022's "negative" wording
understated this defect — it said resume needed a stable id for *cross-process reconnect*, when in fact the key
made **all** resume unreachable.

## 2026-07-16 — Fix: admin couldn't see the Deep-search toggle (duplicate /me race)

**Symptom/why:** after the admin-only gate shipped, a genuine admin's `/me` returned
`{role:"admin", deep_search_enabled:true}` (verified server-side) yet the Deep-search toggle stayed hidden.
Root cause: `ChatPage.tsx` ran its **own** second `GET /me` in `onMount` to populate a local `isAdmin` + the new
`deepEnabled` signal, wrapped in a silent `.catch(()=>{})`. That page-level fetch can resolve before/independently
of the canonical auth boot, and any hiccup left `deepEnabled=false` **permanently** with no error — the toggle
(and the admin Debug link, gated by the same call) just never appeared. The rest of the app already reads admin
state from the canonical store (`App.tsx`, `SettingsPage`, `IndexedFolders` import `isAdmin` from
`stores/auth`); ChatPage was the lone outlier duplicating it.

**Fix (frontend only):**
- `stores/auth.ts`: added `deep_search_enabled?` to `CurrentUser` (already returned by `/me`; login +
  `restoreSession` capture it) and exported `deepSearchEnabled()` derived from the boot-validated `currentUser`.
- `ChatPage.tsx`: deleted the local `isAdmin`/`deepEnabled` signals **and the duplicate `onMount` `/me` fetch**;
  now imports `isAdmin` + `deepSearchEnabled` from the store. App only renders ChatPage once `currentUser()` is
  set (`needsLogin` gate), so the value is present before first paint — no race. Added a `createEffect` that
  forces `deepSearch` off whenever `deepSearchEnabled()` is false (clears a stale ON pill), and removed the now
  unused `request` import.

**Lesson:** one source of truth for session/role. A per-page second `/me` with a swallowed catch is
indistinguishable from "feature not shipped" — the same silent-fallback trap as the clipboard fix earlier today.

## 2026-07-16 — Deep search gated to admins only (config-flagged rollout)

**Symptom/why:** the agentic deep loop is deployed and ON (`ECHO_AGENTIC_DEEP=1`) but still being smoothed —
the A/B verdict is "real but inconsistent", plus known open defects (synthesis garble tail, appeal-confusion,
and the resume dead-code found today). We want to keep exercising it in production without exposing an
unpolished feature to every user, and we want the eventual public launch to be a config flip, not another
CUDA redeploy.

**What:**
- **New gate helpers (`src-tauri/src/services/deep_search/mod.rs`):** `deep_audience_is_all()` reads
  `ECHO_DEEP_AUDIENCE` (`all`/`everyone`/`public` → open to everyone; unset/anything else → admin-only);
  `deep_enabled_for_role(role)` = admin OR audience-all. The pure decision is factored into `deep_enabled(role,
  audience_is_all)` so it's unit-testable without touching process env (new test `deep_audience_gate`, 20/20
  green on the VM).
- **Backend enforcement (`src-tauri/src/api/query.rs`):** `let deep = req.deep && deep_enabled_for_role(&user.role);`
  — a non-admin's `deep:true` (stale UI or crafted request) is **silently downgraded to a normal search** on the
  same line the flag is read. The UI toggle is never the enforcement point.
- **`/me` advertises it (`src-tauri/src/api/auth.rs`):** `MeResp.deep_search_enabled` computed server-side — one
  source of truth the UI reads.
- **Frontend (`src/pages/ChatPage.tsx`):** new `deepEnabled` signal set from `me.deep_search_enabled`; the "Deep
  search mode" menu item is `<Show when={deepEnabled()}>`, and `deepSearch` is forced off for non-admins. Default
  false, so a `/me` fetch failure hides the toggle rather than leaking the feature.

**Rollout later = flip one env var:** add `ECHO_DEEP_AUDIENCE=all` to prod `.env` + restart — no rebuild, instant,
reversible. Note: this gates who may *invoke* deep; the agentic loop still also requires `ECHO_AGENTIC_DEEP=1`.

## 2026-07-16 — Copy answer pastes as formatted text (rich clipboard), not raw markdown

**Symptom/why:** officers paste answers into Word. The Copy button wrote **text/plain only**
(`navigator.clipboard.writeText`), so a pasted answer arrived as literal markdown — `## Grounds and Penalties`,
`**Rule 3**`, `- Inefficiency` — which they then had to reformat by hand. The answer already renders as real
markdown on screen (`<AnswerBody>`: marked → DOMPurify → innerHTML); only the clipboard was lossy.

**Fix (`src/pages/ChatPage.tsx`):** put **both** flavours on the clipboard via `ClipboardItem` —
`text/html` + `text/plain`. Word and Google Docs prefer `text/html` and render real headings/bold/lists;
Notepad/terminals still take the plain text. Nothing is lost either way.
- New `answerHtmlForCopy(turn)` reuses the **same pipeline as `<AnswerBody>`** (marked → DOMPurify), plus an
  `escapeHtml` helper for citation fields. `gfm`/`breaks` are passed **explicitly** rather than inherited from
  AnswerBody's module-level `marked.setOptions`, so the copy still matches the render if that import ever goes.
- Deliberately parses the **raw** answer, not AnswerBody's linkified copy, so `[n]` markers paste as plain text
  instead of dragging the citation hover-popover markup into the document.
- The "Sources" block is carried into the HTML flavour too (`<p><strong>Sources</strong></p><ul>…`), preserving
  the copy-with-sources behaviour shipped in `bdf3ed98`.
- `copyAnswer(turn, id)` now takes the turn (was a pre-rendered string). **Falls back to `writeText`** when
  `ClipboardItem`/`clipboard.write` is unavailable or throws — it needs a secure context and is not guaranteed
  in the Tauri desktop webview, and a Copy button that silently does nothing would be worse than plain text.

**Verified:** `tsc --noEmit` clean; the marked→HTML transform checked against a realistic E&D answer →
`<h2>/<h3>/<strong>/<em>/<ul><li>` + Sources list, `&` escaped, `[n]` left as text. **NOT verified:** the actual
clipboard write and a real Word paste in a browser — needs a live click after deploy.

TMPDIR=/opt/noviq/tmp NOVIQ_TEST_PG_INSTALL_DIR=/home/appadmin/test-pg-install cargo test --lib

## 2026-07-15 — F026 Part 1: deep-search checkpoint / resume / time-travel (LangGraph-style)

**Symptom/why:** the agentic deep loop held all state in memory and ran linearly — a turn interrupted at ~135s
(restart, reconnect, Stop) lost everything and had to re-run from scratch (re-embedding every round). No way to
resume mid-graph or to re-run forward from an earlier decision (time-travel). We wanted LangGraph-style durable,
resumable, branchable state without adopting a graph runtime.

**What (backend `src-tauri`, NOT compiled/deployed — needs a VM CUDA build; flag-gated OFF by default):**
- **Migration `014_deep_checkpoint.sql`** (additive, new table only): `deep_checkpoint(id PK, thread_id, seq,
  node, parent_id, state_json, status, created_at)` + `ix_deep_ckpt_thread(thread_id, seq)`. `parent_id` forms
  the time-travel branch DAG. Mirrors the `one_ask_session` state_json convention (ADR-0014).
- **`deep_search/state.rs`** (new): `Node` (ordered completion marker: Start<Expanded<RetrievedR1<
  CoverageChecked<RetrievedR2<Synthesized<Done — so `state.node < Node::X` = "phase X not done yet") and
  `DeepState` (serializable: inputs + subs + passages + coverage + pending + partial answer + trace).
- **`deep_search/checkpoint.rs`** (new): repository (append / latest / load / history / next_seq /
  delete_thread) + `checkpoint_enabled()` flag (`ECHO_DEEP_CHECKPOINT`, default OFF). 2 repo unit tests
  (roundtrip+ordering+next_seq; load-by-id + thread isolation + delete).
- **`deep_search/mod.rs`** — added `serde` derives to `SubQuestion`/`Coverage`/`CoverageItem`/`Passage`/
  `PassageSet`/`DeepTrace`; **refactored `run_agentic_deep` into a checkpointed driver** (`drive`): each
  super-step is guarded by `state.node < Node::X` and writes a best-effort checkpoint after it completes, so a
  resumed `DeepState` skips completed phases. Final answer + citations are rebuilt deterministically from
  `state.passages` (`build_material` shared by synth + finalize), so a turn resumed at Synthesized/Done
  reproduces the same result with NO extra model call. New entry points **`resume_deep`** (from latest ckpt —
  wired as auto-resume at the top of `run_agentic_deep` when the flag is on) and **`resume_from`** (time-travel
  from a chosen ckpt; branches via next_seq + parent_id; admin trigger is a follow-up). Cancellation now
  checkpoints `interrupted` (so Stop → resumable) instead of dropping state.
- **`guidance.rs`** — passes a durable `thread_id = conversation_id + ':' + workload_id` to `run_agentic_deep`.

**Behaviour when OFF (default):** byte-identical to before — no checkpoint writes, no resume, driver runs
straight through. **Cross-cutting / follow-ups:** thread_id is per-turn (workload id), so cross-process
reconnect-resume needs the frontend to send a STABLE turn id (documented follow-up); time-travel (`resume_from`)
has no UI trigger yet (admin "↩ resume from node" affordance is next); housekeeping/TTL on `deep_checkpoint`
rows not yet added (history is retained for time-travel). ADR suggested: `stateful-deep-search-checkpointing`.

## 2026-07-15 — F026 Stop button (cancel a wrong / slow chat turn)

**Symptom/why:** there was no way for an officer to stop a running query. A wrongly-typed question — or a deep
search legitimately taking ~135s — had to be waited out; the composer stayed disabled the whole time. The
cancellation *engine* already existed (`Scheduler::request_cancel(Uuid)`, a live `CancellationToken` per
workload, cooperative `cancelled()` checks at every deep-loop round/generation boundary) — but nothing mapped a
**conversation** to its live workload id, and there was no UI trigger, so the token could never be fired from
the client.

**What (backend `src-tauri` + frontend `src/`, NOT deployed — needs a VM CUDA build):**
- **`services/scheduler.rs`** — new `chat_turns: DashMap<String, Uuid>` (conversation_id → current chat
  workload id) + three methods: `note_chat_turn` (record, last-writer-wins), `clear_chat_turn` (remove ONLY if
  the id still matches — a slow tail turn must not wipe a newer turn's mapping and silently disable Stop), and
  `cancel_conversation` (look up the id → `request_cancel` → return whether a live turn was found). 2 unit tests.
- **`capabilities/guidance.rs`** — `note_chat_turn(conversation_id, handle.id)` right after
  `scheduler.register(WorkloadKind::Chat)`, and `clear_chat_turn(...)` after `unregister`. Guidance is THE Q&A
  path (normal + deep), so this covers the expensive turns without touching the shorter capabilities.
- **`api/query.rs` + `api/router.rs`** — new `POST /api/cancel_turn {conversation_id}` (authed) →
  `scheduler.cancel_conversation`. Idempotent: `{cancelled:false}` just means the turn already finished. (The
  turn runs detached so a client disconnect does NOT cancel it — this is the *explicit* stop.)
- **`commands/query.rs` + `lib.rs`** — desktop `cancel_turn` Tauri command mirroring the endpoint (the shared
  guidance map is populated on desktop too), registered in the invoke handler.
- **`api/assistant.ts`** — `cancelTurn(conversationId)` client wrapper (routes through the transport seam →
  `/api/cancel_turn` on web, the Tauri command on desktop).
- **`pages/ChatPage.tsx`** — the send arrow becomes a red **Stop (■)** button while `busy()`; click →
  `stopInference()` sets a per-turn `stoppedThisTurn` flag and signals the server. `runInference` then renders a
  clean `_Stopped._` marker for BOTH the empty-answer (turn returned cancelled) and dropped-connection paths,
  and skips tunnel-recovery polling so a stopped turn is never "recovered" back.

**Cross-cutting / follow-ups:** transform/mapreduce register their own Chat workloads and are not yet in the
conversation map (only guidance is) — a running *summarize* wouldn't be stopped by this; fine for v1 (guidance
is the long path). Ownership check on `cancel_turn` is auth-only (conversation ids are unguessable per-user
UUIDs) — tighten to verify ownership if ever needed. This is **Part 2** of the F026 design (stop + LangGraph-
style checkpoint/resume/time-travel + deep cost-guard); Parts 1 & 3 (persisted `deep_checkpoint` + resume) are
still to build — ADR suggested (`/sp.adr stateful-deep-search-checkpointing`).

## 2026-07-15 — Attachment-scope grounding guard (stop the show-cause speculation)

**Symptom/why:** trace `376bc113` (conv `1ccae1b4`, "co-relate this document with procurement rules" on an
attached E&D show-cause notice) *looked* like a corpus search but the trace proved it scoped correctly to the
attachment (STEP 3 `Scoped to attachment: true`, 1 source; all retrieved chunks = the `SC02` notice). The real
defect: with only the notice in scope (which contains **no** procurement rules), the model **speculated** about
procurement law from its own training ("…may intersect… may involve procurement of travel-related services…")
instead of emitting the "not enough information" refusal it gave on the prior turn. Root cause: the bureaucrat
persona (`config/personas/bureaucrat.toml`) instructs "FIRST give a complete general answer: the standard
procedure and **the governing laws**" — that push overrides the strict-grounding rule when the only source is a
single attachment. So it read as an ungrounded/corpus answer to the user. Not a scoping bug — a grounding one.

**What (backend `src-tauri`, VM `cargo check --features llm,server` GREEN, 27.6s, no new warnings; NOT deployed):**
- **`capabilities/guidance.rs`** — `run()` gained a `scoped_to_attachment: bool` param. After building `sys`
  (persona + fragment + grounding), when true it appends new const **`ATTACHMENT_SCOPE_OVERRIDE`**: answer
  STRICTLY from the one attached document, do NOT add governing laws / standard procedure / speculation from
  memory, and if the file doesn't itself contain the asked-about rule reply with one clean sentence
  ("The attached document does not contain <subject>.") — the UI already shows the "Search all documents" widen
  button (`scoped_to_attachment=true`), so the officer gets the corpus path in one tap. Applied to `sys` BEFORE
  both the deep (`run_agentic_deep`) and single-pass (`route_scoped_with_override`) branches, so both honour it.
- **`is_bare_refusal`** — added `"does not contain"` so the override's refusal drops any stray attachment
  citation (clean refusal, no misleading source).
- **Threaded the flag** (explicit, not a hidden task-local, since all callers funnel through `guidance::run`):
  `additive::run` and `draft::run` gained the param and forward it; `run_turn` passes the already-computed
  `scoped_to_attachment` at all three dispatch sites. `route_scoped_with_override`/`run_agentic_deep` unchanged
  (they receive the already-tightened `sys`).
- **Behaviour when NOT attachment-scoped:** byte-identical (flag false → no prompt change). Honours the same
  Notice-Assist exemption as scope resolution (a `/help` turn is `notice_flow` → not attachment-scoped).

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- Prompt-level guard — verify live post-deploy that the show-cause "co-relate/what rules apply" case now refuses
  cleanly + the widen button pulls the real procurement rules from the corpus (needs VM CUDA build + smoke).
- Heuristic edge: a *large* attachment that genuinely DOES contain the asked law still gets the strict prompt —
  acceptable (it can still answer from its own passages; the override only forbids OUTSIDE law).
- Phase-3 "smart widen guard" (proactively offer corpus when the file can't answer) is now partly realised by
  the clean refusal + always-on button; the proactive "your file cites but doesn't contain these rules" message
  is still not built.

## 2026-07-15 — Scope routing: narrow-first attachment + "Search all documents" widen button; copy-with-sources

**Symptom/why:** attaching a file and asking a *legal* question about it ("what procurement **rules** apply?")
searched the WHOLE CORPUS, ignoring the attachment. Root cause: attachment scoping was gated on
`intent::wants_attachment_only(text)` = `references_attachment && !seeks_legal_authority`, so any legal word
(rules/section/act/…) flipped `seeks_legal_authority` true → the gate failed → the turn fell through to the
full corpus. Scope was **inferred from wording**, not set explicitly. Also: the "Copy" button copied only the
prose, so a pasted answer lost its authorities.

**What (backend `src-tauri`, `tsc` green; Rust compile-safe by review — NOT yet VM-built):**
- **`services/assistant/mod.rs` scope block** — replaced the wording heuristic with **NARROW-FIRST**: a chat
  with a live attachment scopes to that attachment **by default, regardless of wording**. Precedence:
  `widen || notice_flow || explicit-selection` → `narrow_to_selection` (honours ticks/@); else a live
  attachment → scope to it (`scoped_to_attachment=true`); else the @-mention safety net; else full corpus. An
  explicit tick/@ on another doc **overrides** the attachment (dead-simple, no combining).
- **Notice-Assist exemption** — `/help` (and an open assist session) deliberately keep the whole corpus (the
  officer's defence needs the STATUTE, not just the notice), so `notice_flow` skips the attachment default.
  Moved the `assist_open` load above the scope block; removed the later duplicate.
- **Widen path** — new `widen: bool` param on `run_turn` (threaded from `api/query.rs` `QueryReq.widen` and the
  desktop `send_message` command); when true, ignores the attachment default → full visible corpus.
- **`TurnResponse.scoped_to_attachment`** (`#[serde(default)]`) — set on the response only for retrieving turns
  (guarded against greeting/low-signal). Drives the UI widen affordance. Trace step now reports it.
- Retired `intent::wants_attachment_only` as the scope gate (kept `#[allow(dead_code)]` for tests/reference).

**What (frontend `src`, `tsc --noEmit` green):**
- **`pages/ChatPage.tsx`** — extracted the send/append/tunnel-recovery tail of `submit` into shared
  `runInference(masked, maskedItems, {deep, sourceIds, widen})`; each assistant turn now stores `query`
  (the masked question) so widen re-runs it verbatim (privacy-safe, no re-masking). New `widenSearch(turn)`.
- **"Search all documents" button** — rendered under an answer when `resp().scoped_to_attachment`
  ("Searched only your attached file. [Search all documents]"); click re-runs the same question `widen:true`.
- **Copy-with-sources** — `answerForCopy(turn)` appends a "Sources:" block (`[n] instrument — path (p.X)`) so a
  pasted answer is self-contained; answers with no citations copy prose alone.
- **`api/assistant.ts`** — `sendMessage(...,widen?)` + `TurnResponse.scoped_to_attachment?`.

**Cross-cutting / follow-ups:** (1) NOT yet VM-built/deployed — needs the CUDA build + a live smoke test
(attach a show-cause, ask "what rules apply" → answer scoped to the file, widen button pulls the corpus).
(2) `poll_turn` recovery rows don't carry `scoped_to_attachment`, so a tunnel-recovered attachment-scoped turn
won't show the button (edge case). (3) FUTURE (saved, not built): a general-help door (invoke help → attach →
free-form query); entry point undecided, scope = same narrow-first. (4) Phase 3 "smart widen guard" (when the
file can't answer, proactively offer the corpus instead of a dead-end) not yet built.

## 2026-07-14 — Low-signal / probe guardrail (nudge instead of a junk answer)

**Symptom/why:** a content-free turn — a stray single character (`a`), a bare `test`/`asdf`/`qwerty`, pure
digits (`123`), or punctuation only (`...`) — fell straight through to full retrieval + a ~30 s inference,
which then "answered" the probe from whatever chunks matched lexically and attached junk citations. Wasteful
and confusing (and, with deep mode toggled on, a ~130 s agentic loop over nothing).

**Fix:**
- **`services/assistant/intent.rs`** — new `is_low_signal(query)`: true for empty/punctuation-only input, a
  ≤2-char alphanumeric skeleton (`a`, `ab`, `1`, `42`), pure digits, or an exact match against a small
  probe/filler list (`test`, `asdf`, `qwerty`, `abc`, `blah`, `dummy`, `sample`, `lorem ipsum`, …).
  **Deliberately conservative** — a single MEANINGFUL word (`penalties`, `misconduct`, `SPPRA`) or any real
  question (`test the SPPRA rules`) is NOT caught, so lazy-but-real queries still route to retrieval. Unit
  test `low_signal_matches_probes_not_real_questions` pins both directions.
- **`services/assistant/mod.rs`** — new `nudge` capability branch in `run_turn`, placed right after the
  greeting branch (so slash / open-assist-session / prebaked-summary / greeting all still win first, and an
  open Notice-Assist session still captures short replies like "ok"). Returns the short `NOVIQ_NUDGE` message
  (example questions + the `@`-scope hint), no retrieval, no citations; traced as `Low-signal / probe`.

**Cross-cutting:** sits BEFORE capability dispatch, so it also short-circuits the F025 agentic deep-search
loop for probes (no 3-call / 2-round run on `test`). Mirrors the existing greeting fast-path shape exactly.
Follow-up: none required; extend the probe list if new filler patterns show up in query_log.

## 2026-07-13 — Feature 024: deterministic table-name enumeration (kill hallucinated entries)

**Symptom/why:** the whole-document summary's table segment listed **"Department Zoonology"** and
**"Department Z"** for RoB — neither exists. DB-verified (source `d207c986…`): `table_row` chunks contain 0
"department z" and exactly one "zoo" hit, which is a *function* line ("all matters relating to animal
husbandry, **zooids**…", + "Zoological Gardens"), not a department. Root cause: `build_table_segment`
(`services/summary_builder.rs`) fed the 50 messy `table_row` chunks to the LLM and asked it to *"LIST THE
ENTRIES BY NAME"* — a re-rendering step where the model confabulated names from garbled cell text and padded
the list with an alphabetical placeholder ("…Department Z").

**Fix (`services/summary_builder.rs`, deterministic — no LLM):**
- New `table_row_name(content)` extracts the entry name **verbatim** from column 1 of the ` | `-delimited
  row: drops any `render_row_with_header` header-label prefix and cross-page `": "` cell bleed (keep text
  after the last `": "`), cuts amendment/editorial tails (`(Substituted`, `(Inserted`, `vide Notification`,
  `Deleted vide`, …), and rejects the header row (`Secretariat Department`/`S. NO.`), serial-only, and
  non-alphabetic cells. Order-preserving dedup.
- `build_table_segment` now assembles the segment in code: *"The document's schedules and tables list N
  distinct named entries, including: A; B; …."* — no model call, so **fabrication is impossible** (only real
  cell text can surface) and the earlier CoT-leak surface ("Okay, let's tackle…") for this segment is gone.
- Signature dropped `model_slot`/`tier` (single caller in `build_document_full` updated).
- Tests: `table_row_name_extracts_department_verbatim`, `table_row_name_rejects_header_and_non_entries`
  (incl. the zooids→NOT-a-department regression).

**Cross-cutting / follow-ups:** entry-name *cleanliness* is still bounded by feature-023 limits — pdfplumber
splits RoB Schedule-I across per-page tables and `table_row` conflates schedules, so a few names carry
cross-page residue (real text, not invented). Multi-page table stitching + schedule labeling remain the 023
follow-up. Deploy: build on VM (`cargo test --lib … table_row_name`) then re-run `build_summaries` so stored
`document_full` segments regenerate.

## 2026-07-12 (latest15) — Feature 023: general structured-table capture at ingestion

**Why:** PDF tables (e.g. RoB Schedule-I 39-department distribution-of-business table) were detected by the
pdfplumber sidecar as structured `SidecarTable{header,rows}` but that structure was only linearised to prose
then discarded; the clause parser shredded the linearised rows into hundreds of micro-chunks (RoB → 292), so
no single unit held the whole table → "how many departments" answered 12–14 not 39, list-all was incomplete,
and whole-document summaries dropped table content. GENERAL fix (any table, any doc type), spec-driven under
`specs/023-structured-table-capture/` (spec+plan+tasks, PHRs 0001–0003). Branch `023-structured-table-capture`.

**What (deterministic, no LLM; additive migration; 697 lib tests pass, 0 regressions):**
- **migration `013_table_units.sql`** — additive: widen `chunks.unit_type` + `graph_nodes.node_type` CHECK
  to include `table`,`table_row` (superset).
- **`parsers/table.rs`** — `ExtractedTable{id,page,header,rows}` + in-band region markers
  `⟦TBL:{id}⟧…⟦/TBL:{id}⟧` (`table_open_marker`/`strip_table_markers`/`parse_table_marker`).
  `reflow_with_sidecar` now returns `(text, rows, Vec<ExtractedTable>)` and wraps each table's linearised
  rows with markers; `emitted` rows exclude markers. Threaded onto `ParsedDocument.tables` through all
  extraction constructions; `extract_document` returns the tables (carried on the pdfplumber-PRIMARY path).
- **`structured_importer.rs`** — `strip_table_regions` lifts marker regions out of the body BEFORE heading
  detection (mirrors `strip_chrome`/`strip_front_matter`/`strip_back_matter`; recomputes page offsets),
  eliminating the shredding without offset drift. New `persist_table_units` (called from `persist(...,
  tables)`) emits per detected table: ONE whole-table chunk (`unit_type='table'`, `render_table_markdown` =
  header + separator + all rows) + one chunk per row (`unit_type='table_row'`, `render_row_with_header`
  labelled cells, amendment note retained) + a graph `table` node that `contains` its `table_row` children
  under the document root; `block_class='table'`.
- **`summary_builder.rs`** — `load_content_for_summary` includes the whole-table chunk (summaries now cover
  table content) but excludes the per-row duplicates (`unit_type != 'table_row'`).
- **Tests** — markdown 39-row count (C-1), row header-labels + amendment note, blank-header synth, strip
  region-only, strip no-op on prose-only (SC-004), marker round-trip (C-4).

**Scoping notes:** deterministic Track-1 counting (counting.rs) NOT wired to tables — mapping an arbitrary
subject noun ("department") to `table_row` isn't general; the whole-table chunk (all rows in one chunk) is
retrieved and the LLM counts/lists from it. Structured tables ride the pdfplumber-PRIMARY extraction path
(pdftotext tier discards them). **Pending: live validation** (deploy branch → `POST /api/reindex_structure`
→ verify RoB `table`=1 / `table_row`=39 / "how many departments"=39). Graph-guided summarizer (feature 024)
consumes these table nodes next.

## 2026-07-12 (latest14) — Server-side structure re-index endpoint (headless re-extract gap)

**Why:** deploying the item-1 parser fix + bumping `STRUCTURED_IMPORTER_VERSION` 1→2 did NOT re-index
anything in prod. Root cause (diagnosed on the live server): the startup re-extract enqueue
(`enqueue_structure_reextract`) lives inside `lib.rs::setup_models_and_watchers`, which is
`#[cfg(feature = "desktop")]` — the headless `noviq-server` never calls it, and the server also runs no
background worker for `pending` sources (it indexes only on API upload). So the version-bump mechanism is
desktop-only; on the server a parser change can never reach already-indexed documents.

**What:**
- `services/indexer.rs::reindex_structure_all(pool, embedder, tier)` — selects every indexed PDF with
  `structure_importer_version < STRUCTURED_IMPORTER_VERSION`, and for each re-runs `do_index` (re-parses
  the stored file with the current parser, re-chunks, re-embeds; idempotent — clears the source's old
  chunks + graph first, and bumps the version on success so it won't loop). Serialised on `indexing_sem`.
  Returns `(attempted, ok, failed)`.
- Admin **`POST /api/reindex_structure`** (`api/system.rs`) — background task (re-embed is slow), returns
  `{status:"started"}`, guarded by `REINDEX_RUNNING` (one at a time). Progress visible via
  `sources.indexing_status`.
- Rollout for a parser change is now: deploy → `POST /api/reindex_structure` → wait for all `indexed` →
  `POST /api/build_summaries` → `POST /api/rebuild_graph` → verify.

## 2026-07-12 (latest13) — Pre-baked-summary items 1–3: parser citation fix + build guard + ingest dedup

Resumes the pre-baked whole-document-summary follow-ups parked before the GraphRAG detour.

**Item 1 — generic amendment-footnote parser fix (all rules docs).** Amendment-compiled OCR prefixes
inserted provisions/schedules with a superscript note marker glued to a `[` → a leading DIGIT before the
bracket (`5[12. Constitution of anti-corruption council`, `1[SCHEDULE (See Rule 10)`). Three deterministic
paths missed it (→ E&D missing Rule 12, dup Rule 7, spurious Part IV). Fixed generically (not per-doc):
- `doc_profiles/rules.rs` — the 2 heading patterns carrying `\[?` now use `(?:\d*\[)?` (tolerate the
  footnote digit before the bracket) so `5[12.` is detected as Rule 12.
- `parsers/back_matter.rs::boundary_kind` — same `\[?`→`(?:\d*\[)?` so `1[SCHEDULE` opens a back-matter
  boundary.
- `heading_detector/regex_pass.rs::scan_structural_boundaries` — added `(?:\d*\[)?` prefix (consumed, not
  captured, so labels stay clean).
- **Gazette-footnote Part suppression** (`regex_pass.rs::scan_with_profile_unit`): drop Part-level hits
  whose own line is a gazette/notification/date citation (`line_is_gazette_footnote` = `dated \d|gaz.|
  notification no|extra-ordinary`) — kills the spurious "Part IV" minted from `Part IV-A, dated 9-7-1985,
  the Sindh Govt. Gaz., …` that stole Rule 12's clauses. New helpers `line_at`/`line_is_gazette_footnote`.
- **GraphRAG synergy:** the graph overlay is built from provision citations, so this fix also corrects
  E&D's graph node labels — after re-index, re-run `POST /api/rebuild_graph`.
- Tests: back_matter `1[SCHEDULE`→schedule; regex_pass `5[12.`→Rule 12 + gazette-Part suppressed.

**Item 2 — `build_summaries_all` indexed-source guard (`summary_builder.rs`).** Was `SELECT DISTINCT
source_id FROM chunks` (any source with chunks, incl. mid-ingest/failed). Now joins
`sources.indexing_status = 'indexed'` so a partial ingest can't bake an incomplete whole-doc summary.

**Item 3 — ingest-time dedup for stored `document_full` (`summary_builder.rs`).** The stored summary kept
reworded tail echoes that only the query-time presentation pass hid. New `finalize_segments` applies the
SAME near-dup dedup (`summarize_doc::dedupe_repeats`, now `pub(crate)`) to each segment before storage and
drops emptied segments; wired into all `build_document_full` return paths.

**Pending:** VM build/test; then item-1 needs a corpus re-index (all rules docs) to regenerate chunks +
`POST /api/build_summaries` + `POST /api/rebuild_graph`, then verify E&D (Rule 12 present, no dup Rule 7,
no Part IV). **Item 4** (decide `ECHO_SUMMARY_RECALL` on/off) still open.

## 2026-07-12 (latest12) — GraphRAG: rebuild_graph endpoint (regenerate overlay, no re-ingest)

**Why:** the generalised provision-kind overlay (latest9) and cross-doc overlay (latest11) are built at
INGEST / via `link_graph`, but the live corpus was indexed BEFORE the generalisation → Article-only
(constitution-only) overlay. A full re-index (re-OCR/re-embed) just to regenerate edges is wasteful — the
edges are a pure function of already-persisted chunk text + nodes.

**What (`services/graph_linker.rs::rebuild_overlay` + `api/system.rs::rebuild_graph`):**
- `rebuild_overlay(pool)` — regenerates the WITHIN-document overlay for the whole corpus from existing
  `graph_nodes` + `chunks.content`, running the SAME extraction as `graph_builder` (`provision_refs` →
  provision-head index via `citation_key`; self/enclosing guard via the node's own `citation_key`;
  `non_obstante` on "notwithstanding"). Idempotent — `graph::delete_intra_doc_overlay_edges` wipes the
  intra-doc overlay first (disjoint from the cross-doc delete; leaves `contains` + cross-doc intact).
- `provision_refs` exposed `pub(crate)` for reuse (alongside `provision_key`/`citation_key`/`provision_ref_re`).
- Admin **`POST /api/rebuild_graph`** — one-shot: `rebuild_overlay` (intra) THEN `link_corpus` (cross-doc),
  deterministic + inline, returns `{intra_doc_edges, cross_doc_edges, instruments_targetable, sources}`.
  **No re-OCR/re-embed** — the fast path to bring an already-indexed corpus up to the full overlay.
- Rollout now: deploy (flags OFF = no behaviour change) → `POST /api/rebuild_graph` → audit `graph_edges`
  (expect per-doc overlay 0→real, E&D 12+, cross-doc SLGA/SPP-Act) → flip `ECHO_GRAPH_EXPAND`/
  `ECHO_AMEND_NOTES` → A/B eval (tier `hybrid+graph`). ADR + PHRs still owed.

## 2026-07-12 (latest11) — GraphRAG Phase 3: corpus cross-document linker

**Why:** `graph_builder` runs per-doc with a per-doc citation map, so it can only build WITHIN-document
edges (live audit: every overlay edge was intra-doc, 0 cross-doc). The high-value cross-doc relationship
in a legal corpus is **subordinate Rules → their enabling Act**: the Compendium names "Local Government
Act" 24×, SPPRA Rules name "Public Procurement Act" 3×, Delegation 2019 1×, RoB 2× — and those Acts (SLGA
2013, SPP Act 2009) ARE in the corpus. This is the "the answer to X changes when the parent Act's Y is
involved" case. Architect-confirmed: strategy (b) title+provision → (a) exact-title fallback, **NO fuzzy**;
title derived from `file_name`; bare "the Act" deferred; runs as an admin endpoint (not per-doc auto).

**What (`services/graph_linker.rs`, new + wiring):**
- `link_corpus(pool)` — post-ingest corpus pass. Builds a target registry: per source a distinctive
  title regex (`title_signature`) + document node + provision-head index (`citation_key`). Scans every
  source's chunk text for references to OTHER instruments' titles; on a match, resolves a provision named
  just after the title via `provision_ref_re`+`provision_key` against the target's head index (**b**), else
  falls back to the target's `document` node (**a**); inserts a cross-doc `cross_reference` edge
  (referencing chunk's node → target node). Deduped by `(from,to)`; skips self-source; UTF-8-boundary-safe
  window. **Phase 0's `graph::expand` already follows `cross_reference`, so cross-doc edges activate for
  retrieval with no extra wiring.**
- `title_signature` — derives `(?i)\b(?:sindh\W+|the\W+)?<core>\b` from the file name: strips numeric
  prefix + year, drops leading geo/article words (sindh/the/of/government), requires an instrument type
  word (act/ordinance/rules/order/regulations) + ≥2 core tokens (else `None` — too generic to match
  safely, e.g. "Rules of Business"). `\W+` between core tokens absorbs the commas/parens/spaces real
  citations insert. 3 unit tests (optional prefix, needs-type-word/2-tokens, punctuation tolerance).
- `graph::delete_cross_doc_cross_reference_edges` — deletes ONLY edges whose endpoints span sources →
  idempotent re-run, leaves the Phase 1 within-doc overlay intact.
- Admin endpoint **`POST /api/link_graph`** (`api/system.rs::link_graph`, route in `api/router.rs`) —
  deterministic + fast (no model), runs inline, returns `{edges_inserted, instruments_targetable,
  sources_scanned}`. Run after a corpus re-index.

**Pending:** VM build; then the single deploy + full re-index (regenerates Phase 1 intra-doc overlay) +
`POST /api/link_graph` (cross-doc) + `POST /api/build_summaries` + audit `graph_edges` + turn on
`ECHO_GRAPH_EXPAND`/`ECHO_AMEND_NOTES` for A/B eval. ADR + PHRs owed (GraphRAG-on-Postgres-not-Neo4j).

## 2026-07-12 (latest10) — GraphRAG Phase 2: amendment-awareness annotation (NOT amended_by edges)

**Why the pivot:** Phase 2 was planned as `amended_by` graph edges. The `amendment_events` audit
(108 rows: 98 constitution, 8 APT, 1 SPPRA, 1 E&D) killed that premise — **every `by_instrument` is an
instrument OUTSIDE the corpus** (constitutional amendment Acts like "the Constitution (Eighteenth Amdt.)
Act, 2010"; P.O. No. 14 of 1985; S&GAD gazette notifications; "Act No. IV/13"). None match our 16 docs,
so an `amended_by` edge has **no in-corpus `to_node`** and would produce **zero edges** — exactly the
reason `graph_builder` skipped it originally, now confirmed on live data. Building it = dead machinery.

The completeness intent still holds ("the answer to X changes when X was amended"), so Phase 2 pivots to
**amendment-awareness annotation** (architect-approved): when a provision that reaches the LLM context has
recorded `amendment_events`, annotate it so the answer flags the base text may be superseded. Reuses the
F013/F015 provenance; no dead edges. `amended_by` stays in the Phase 0 edge list (harmless, free-activates
if a future corpus ever contains an amending instrument).

**What:**
- `db/repositories/graph.rs::amendment_rows_for_chunks(pool, chunk_ids, scope_source_ids)` — joins
  `amendment_events → graph_nodes → chunks`, returns `(chunk_id, kind, by_instrument, effective_date)`.
  Scope-clamped (note names instruments/dates = answer content, FR-001; mirrors the `_scoped` variant).
- `services/query_router.rs` — after `build_context`, when `ECHO_AMEND_NOTES` is on, fetch the rows for
  the final context chunk ids and build a per-chunk note `[⚠ Amendment history: this provision was
  <kind> by <instrument>, <date>; … — the text above may be superseded; verify the current version.]`
  (instrument truncated to 90 chars, events deduped). Traced "Amendment-awareness (Phase 2)".
- `build_context_string` now takes an `amend_notes` map and appends the note under the matching `[N]`
  passage (empty map = no-op when disabled). Both call sites (main + grounding-retry) updated.
- **Flag-gated `ECHO_AMEND_NOTES` (default OFF)** — A/B alongside `ECHO_GRAPH_EXPAND`.
- Follow-up: grounding system-prompt could instruct the model to *surface* the note rather than treat it
  as citable text; extractive-answer path (off in prod) not yet annotated. Prod uses the LLM path.

## 2026-07-12 (latest9) — GraphRAG Phase 1+0: generalized edge extraction + seed-and-expand retrieval

**Why:** decided (this session, with architect) to build our own Postgres GraphRAG rather than adopt
Neo4j (fixes none of our real pains; `graph::expand` recursive-CTE already does bounded multi-hop at our
scale — see the Neo4j eval, recommendation = don't). The motivating gap: pure vector similarity retrieves
what's *semantically similar to the query*, NOT what's *legally connected* to the answer — an amendment or
a `notwithstanding` override that flips the answer is rarely lexically similar, so it's never retrieved.
**Live edge audit (port 34213, db echo) exposed the blocker:** the relational overlay barely existed —
`contains` 6,649 (all 13 docs) but `cross_reference` 99 + `non_obstante` 17 **all belonged to
`constitution.pdf` alone**, `amended_by` **0**, and **every overlay edge was within-document** (zero
cross-doc). Root cause in `graph_builder.rs`: the reference extractor matched **`\bArticles?\s+N` only**
(Constitution vocabulary) — every "Rule 16"/"Section 9" produced no edge.

Build order agreed: **1 → 0 → 2 → 3** (Phase 2 = wire `amended_by` from `amendment_events`; Phase 3 =
corpus cross-doc linker, strategy (b) title+provision resolution → (a) exact-title fallback, **no fuzzy**).

**Phase 1 — generalized, doc-agnostic edge extraction (`services/graph_builder.rs`):**
- `provision_ref_re` replaces `article_ref_re`: matches `article|section|rule|regulation|clause|chapter|
  part|schedule` + arabic number (`\d+[A-Za-z]?`). **Arabic-only in v1 on purpose** — matching bare romans
  (`i`/`v`/`x`) against ordinary words would mint false legal edges, which are worse than none. Roman-
  numbered Parts/Schedules = a scoped follow-up.
- References AND stored citations both collapse to a normalized key via `provision_key` (lowercased kind,
  trailing plural `s` stripped, upper-cased number, no separators) + `citation_key` (parses the head before
  the first `(`): `Rules 3` and `Rule 3` → `rule3`; `Rule 5(6)` → `rule5`; `Article 19a` → `article19A`.
  So the target format is **not hardcoded per doc-type** (stored citations vary: `Rule 5(6)`, `Section 142`,
  `Schedule-II`, `Article 19A`). References resolve against a **provision-head index** (article-level nodes
  only), so a text ref always targets the provision head, never a sub-clause.
- Self-reference + self-loop guards preserved (now key-based). 3 new unit tests: cross-kind extraction,
  key normalization, synthetic Rule 4 → Rule 12 edge (a case that produced **0** edges before).
- Runs on all 3 ingest paths (`indexer`, `structured_importer`, `doc_ir/dispatch`) → re-index regenerates.

**Phase 0 — seed-and-expand retrieval arm (`services/query_router.rs`):**
- New arm AFTER the hybrid union/RRF merge (mirrors the summary-recall arm): top-`ECHO_GRAPH_SEED_K` (8)
  merged chunks → `graph::node_ids_for_chunks` → `graph::expand` over
  `cross_reference/non_obstante/amended_by` at `ECHO_GRAPH_HOPS` (1, capped 3) → fetch the new reached
  provisions (cap `ECHO_GRAPH_K` 12) → **scope-clamp (FR-001 defence-in-depth, matters once Phase 3 crosses
  sources)** → `union_merge` into the pool → traced "Graph expansion (legal overlay)", tier `hybrid+graph`.
- **Flag-gated `ECHO_GRAPH_EXPAND` (default OFF)** — safe A/B like `ECHO_HYBRID`; also a no-op on any corpus
  whose overlay edges aren't built yet, and decoupled from the (disabled) citation fast-path where the only
  prior graph use (`expand_citation_neighbours`, 1-hop) was trapped.

**Not yet verified:** committed to `feat/document-full-summary` for a VM build (`cargo test --lib
graph_builder`) + the real proof — re-index E&D 1973 and re-audit `graph_edges` (expect 0 → real overlay).
Phases 2 & 3 pending. NO Neo4j — final.

## 2026-07-12 (latest8) — Composer UX: loosen name masking + resizable query box

Two parallel UI asks (frontend only; `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vitest run` 6/6).

**1. Loosen confidential masking (`src/lib/maskEngine.ts`).** Name detection auto-masked EVERY

## 2026-07-12 (latest7) — Structure-tolerant whole-document summaries (content, not labels)

**Why:** the E&D-1973 whole-doc summary was the one eval failure (latest6 follow-up #1). Root cause
found by inspecting the live chunks: NOT the summary layer and NOT a foreign/merged document — the
*amendment-compiled* PDF prefixes inserted provisions/schedules with a superscript footnote marker
that OCR renders as a **leading digit before `[`** (`5[12. Constitution of anti-corruptions council`,
`1[SCHEDULE (See Rule 10)`). That shape breaks three deterministic-parser paths → **missing Rule 12**
(its anti-corruption-council text glued onto Rule 11 = the "Repeal-gist-says-council" symptom),
**duplicate "Rule 7"** (schedule serial `7. Chief Minister…` minted as a rule), and a spurious
**"Part IV"** (from a `Part IV-A, dated…` gazette footnote) that stole Rule 12's clauses.

Architect decision (do NOT revert): **do not hand-fix the parser per document** — it doesn't scale to
the future 1000s of docs, and the summary is **citation-free** so exact rule numbering doesn't matter
for it. Instead make the whole-doc summary **structure-tolerant**: reduce over the document's CONTENT,
not the parser's provision labels. The mislabelled text is still *present*, so the LLM summarises it
faithfully regardless of the mis-parse. (Also settled: **Mistral "Deep re-index" tier is abandoned** —
never propose it for any document; fast-tier + robust generation only.)

**What (`src-tauri/src/services/summary_builder.rs`; VM-verified: `cargo test --lib summary_builder`
`--no-default-features --features llm,server,cuda` → 7 passed):**
- **`build_document_full`** (new) — the `document_full` summary now reduces over `load_content_for_summary`
  (every non-boilerplate chunk except `block_class IN ('chrome','footnote')`, label-prefix stripped,
  in `chunk_index` order) instead of over the per-provision gists. Small/medium docs = one reduce call;
  long docs = windowed hierarchical reduce (`pack_windows` → tier-1 `summarize_content_window` partials
  → tier-2 reduce into 1 segment, or ≤3 ordered segments when partials overflow). `DOC_FULL_INPUT_CHARS
  = 24_000` (replaces `GISTS_PER_DOC_SEGMENT`).
- **`summarize_document_full`** generalised: "per-provision topic notes" → "material" (works for raw
  content or partials); input cap `MAX_PROVISION_CHARS*4` → `DOC_FULL_INPUT_CHARS`.
- **Structure-less coverage:** provision-gist recall index (Track 2) still gated on `unit_type='article'`
  (unchanged), but `document_full` now runs even with 0 provisions, anchored on the `document` chunk or
  the first chunk. **`build_summaries_all` broadened `WHERE unit_type='article'` → all sources** — so a
  structure-less upload (200-page meeting minutes) finally gets a whole-doc summary. `skipped` now means
  "no content at all".
- Unit tests added: `pack_windows_*`, `strip_label_prefix_*`.

**Query-time presentation pass (`summarize_doc.rs` + `assistant/mod.rs`; VM tests → 18 passed):**
`try_prebaked` now takes `model_slot`/`tier` and runs the stored `document_full` summary through the prose
model (`present_summary`, `PRESENT_MAX_TOKENS=800`) with a STRICT grounding prompt — present only the
stored text, add no facts/numbers/dates, no citations, tailored to the user's phrasing. `strip_think`
guards a leaked reasoning block; ANY generation failure / empty output falls back to the verbatim stored
summary (never worse than before). This is the "intelligence at answer time" the earlier deterministic
serving lacked, and it also smooths residual ingest-parse artefacts. No longer "no model" — the trace step
records LLM-presented vs verbatim-fallback.
**Loop fix (post-deploy, live-verified):** the first prod E&D query showed the small model produced a
perfect first paragraph then fell into a restate-the-same-points loop to the token cap. Added
`dedupe_repeats` (GLOBAL sentence dedup on the presented output), tightened the prompt ("a SINGLE concise
summary; do not repeat points"), and lowered `PRESENT_MAX_TOKENS` 800→500. Test `dedupe_repeats_kills_restated_sentences`.

**Cross-cutting / follow-ups:** (2) `build_summaries_all` now touches EVERY source incl. user uploads — heavier on the
next full rebuild; single-source build (`{"source_id":…}`) unaffected. (3) verify E&D: regenerate its
`document_full` with the new code + re-run `research/summarize-eval/`. (4) parser mis-parse still affects
CITATION flows (notice-assist `/help`, RAG) — separate systemic track, NOT per-doc regex.

## 2026-07-11 (latest5) — Pre-baked whole-document summaries (summarize → ingest-time summary)

**Why:** architect decision. With map-reduce disabled in prod (`NOVIQ_MAPREDUCE=off`), a
"summarize <document>" turn fell through to single-pass **Guidance** (bounded top-K) → only a
PARTIAL summary of a whole act/rulebook. The user wants whole-document summaries generated ONCE at
ingest and served directly. Distinct from the Track 2 recall index (011): the `level='document'`

Design settled with the user: whole-document only (no part/chapter tier), single segment (2–3 for
long docs), **no citations**, synthesized prose. Generated by REDUCING over the per-provision gists
we already have (NOT a live map-reduce — that sweep is the killed slow path).

**What (VM-verified: non-cuda `cargo check` EXIT 0; `summary_builder`/`intent`/`summarize_doc` lib
tests 1+20+1 pass):**
- **migration 012** — widen `graph_summary.level` CHECK to add `'document_full'` (additive).
- **`summary_builder.rs`** — `build_document_full`: reduce over the provision gists into 1 segment
  (most docs) or 2–3 (Constitution/Compendium; `GISTS_PER_DOC_SEGMENT=120`), higher token budget
  (`GEN_DOC_FULL_MAX_TOKENS=700`), presentational prompt (officer-facing prose, no numbering).
  Rows are **NOT embedded** (`insert_document_full` bypasses `summary_embeddings`) → stay out of the
  recall pool. `SummaryStats.doc_full` added; `POST /api/build_summaries` log includes it.
- **`summarize_doc::try_prebaked`** — named-doc match (reuses `counting::best_source_match`, so
  topical summaries with no named doc fall through) → returns the concatenated `document_full`
  segments deterministically (no model, no citations). Trace step "Pre-baked document summary".
- **`assistant::mod::run_turn`** — captures `requested_summarize` BEFORE the `NOVIQ_MAPREDUCE`
  kill-switch rewrites SummarizeDoc→Guidance, then intercepts with the pre-baked path (after
  slash/assist, before transform/additive/dispatch).

**Follow-ups:** (1) generalize to NON-legal user uploads (e.g. 200-page meeting minutes) — reduce
over CHUNKS not `article` provisions + auto-trigger at index time + hierarchical reduce for size +
optional per-meeting sectioning; currently structure-less docs are skipped → summarize still falls to
Guidance for them. (2) after deploy, re-run `build_summaries` to populate `document_full` for the 13
structured docs. (3) the existing `level='document'` recall gist leaks the echoed prompt

## 2026-07-11 (later) — Title-based doc_type + attachment-safe corpus counts + prod cleanup

**Why:** verifying the count capability (below) against prod surfaced two data-quality bugs that
made corpus counts wrong. (1) `sources.doc_type` is auto-detected by **body-word frequency**, which
misclassified `03_Sindh_Public_Procurement_Act_2009` as `manual` (its body repeats "instructions" /
uppercase `CHAPTER`; it never says "Ordinance", and the `act` profile had no self-signal for the word
"Act") — and any naive "this Act" body signal would wrongly pull `05_Compendium_Rules_under_SLGA`
(legitimately `rules`) to `act`, because that compendium says "this Act" 47×. (2) The same PDF

attachments are pre-created with an empty `file_hash` that the re-index branch never backfills), and
those per-conversation attachment rows were being counted as corpus documents.

**What (code, branch `feat/adr0019-structured-counting`, VM-verified: cargo check clean + 57 tests):**
- `doc_profiles/mod.rs` — new `doc_type_from_title` + `detect_profile_titled`: **title-first**
  classification, authoritative over body scoring (title states the instrument type unambiguously and
  is immune to body-reference noise). Priority rules/regulations > manual > act/ordinance. Tokenizes on
  non-alphanumerics (NOT regex `\b`, which treats `_` as a word char → fails on `_Act_`). Body scoring
  stays the fallback for type-less titles. `structured_importer.rs` ingest now calls the titled entry.
  Locked with tests over the exact live corpus filenames incl. the Compendium regression guard.
- `counting/mod.rs` — `count_by_doc_type` now filters `conversation_id IS NULL` (corpus = shared
  library only; per-conversation chat attachments excluded).

**What (prod DB, live now — NOT via code):**
- Purged 2 of 3 duplicate `SC02_Azra` attachment rows (kept newest) + their chunks/embeddings/mentions

- Corrected 2 mislabeled rows to match the new title logic: SPPA-2009 `manual→act`, RoB-1986
