## 2026-07-11 (latest) — Deterministic count/list capability (ADR-0019) + pipeline map

**Why:** count/list questions ("how many rules are in the SPPRA Rules?", "how many acts do we
have?") were routed through the LLM, which cannot be trusted to count. A 2026-07-11 code+prod-DB
audit (GraphRAG usage) established: `graph_nodes.node_type` is a purely STRUCTURAL level word
(`document|part|chapter|article|clause|subclause` — see `structure_parser.rs:51`), NOT semantic;
`sources.doc_type` is the semantic classifier (act/rules/manual/generic); the officer's unit word
("rule"/"section"/"article") lives in `DocProfile.level_vocab`, not in `node_type`. Naive `COUNT(*)`
over Constitution articles = 332, but the graph builder emits a DUPLICATE node per chunk occurrence
of a multi-chunk provision → only `COUNT(DISTINCT citation)` = 283 ≈ the real 280 (+ inserted arts
like 10A). Departments ("sum of all departments") are NOT in `graph_nodes` — trapped in RoB
Schedule-I tables; the `entities` table is near-empty (19 dates, 2 refs) → that case is blocked on
the table-chunking fix.

**What:**
- `services/counting/mod.rs` (new) — pure, fully unit-tested: `node_type_for_unit(doc_type, word)`
  (profile-vocab first, then fixed structural words, then a `para`/`paragraph`→primary-provision
  alias for the future GFR/SFR Para-N books); `is_structural_count_query` (the PRECISE routing gate —
  requires a countable unit noun, so "how many members must be present" / "how many days to appeal"
  do NOT hijack); `count_by_doc_type`, `count_units_in_source` / `list_units_in_source`
  (`COUNT(DISTINCT citation)` / natural-sorted labels), `structural_breakdown`, `sources_for_matching`
  + `best_source_match` (names an in-scope doc from the query, stopword-guarded), `doc_type_category`,
  `pluralize`, `doc_type_label`.
- `services/assistant/capabilities/count.rs` (new) — the live **Capability::Count** handler,
  mirroring `amendment_chain` (the other zero-model capability): structured facts → deterministic
  prose → grounded response (context = answer, self-grounded by construction). Within-doc count/list
  or corpus `doc_type` histogram; no retrieval, no LLM.
- Wiring on the **client-server path only** (`assistant::run_turn`): `Capability::Count` added to
  `intent.rs` enum + `as_str` + `classify_capability` (gated on `is_structural_count_query`, before
  the LLM capabilities); `persona.rs` `capability_prompt` arm (falls back to guidance — never used,
  deterministic); `run_turn` match arm (`emit_phase("count")` → `count::run`); `src/api/assistant.ts`
  Capability union gains `"count"`. The legacy desktop `intent_router::dispatch` path was intentionally
  NOT wired (product is client-server) — an initial wiring there was reverted, classifier restored.
- `history/adr/0019-structured-counting-and-verbatim-synthesis-retrieval.md` (new, Proposed).
- Pipeline architecture map published as an Artifact (granular routing diagram; printable to PDF).

**Verification:** ⚠ **NOT built** — no local cargo toolchain (Windows box). Needs VM `cargo check` +
`cargo test --lib counting:: assistant::intent::` + `npm run build` before any merge. The counting
module has ~18 pure unit tests; the SQL fns mirror queries already run successfully against prod
`echo` (port 40509). Commit to a SIDE BRANCH — never `release` (auto-deploys unverified).

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- Fix ~2 `doc_type` misclassifications before trusting corpus counts (SPPA-2009 tagged `manual`; see
  MEMORY doc-depth). Latent bug: `graph_builder.rs` emits duplicate nodes (DISTINCT masks it).
- Pure "list all rules" (no "how many") still routes to the LLM ListChildren/Guidance path — extend
  the gate to list-triggers later if desired.
- ADR-0019 Track 2 (verbatim synthesis) + Track 3 (department tree, blocked) + granular tracing/admin

## 2026-07-10 — Attachment size limit + audit-para corpus coverage map

**Why:** two F022 follow-ups. (1) `/help` on a 200-page report attached a huge PDF that ran OCR +
embed **synchronously** before replying, and extraction read only its front matter — an attachment
is meant to be one notice / one para, not a full document. (2) Audit paras cite financial rulebooks
(GFR, Sindh Financial Rules, Treasury Rules) that are **not indexed**, so they failed to ground.
Architect decision: cap attachments small (the model then reads the whole thing — **no para picker
needed**); index the missing rulebooks so citations resolve.

**What:**
- `api/uploads.rs` — `attach_limits()` (env `NOVIQ_ATTACH_MAX_PAGES` default **15**,
  `NOVIQ_ATTACH_MAX_MB` default **8**) + `pdf_page_count()` (lopdf structure-only, no OCR; works on
  scans). `attach_document` rejects an oversize file with **413 `attachment_too_large`** and a
  message pointing to *My Documents* (byte cap checked first so a huge PDF isn't parsed). Non-PDFs
  fall to the byte cap. 3 unit tests. **The `upload_documents` (My Documents) path is unchanged** —
  full documents belong there.
- `notice_assist/extract.rs` — `MAX_DOC_CHARS` **14_000 → 40_000**. Coupled to the 15-page cap: a
  capped-small attachment must be read **whole**, else the front-matter bug returns.
- `notice_assist/compose.rs` — `provision_tokens()` Pass-B regex now recognises **`paragraph|para`**
  (longer form first) so GFR's para-numbered citations ("Para 213(5) of GFR") tokenise instead of
  being a false miss. `[-\s]*[0-9]` guard keeps "parameter"/"paramount" out. New test.
- `docs/corpus-coverage-checklist.md` (new) — the rulebook coverage map for a **Sindh govt** officer:
  two-jobs framing (ground what's cited / surface the officer's shield), tiered list, per-book
  definition-of-done, guardrails (edition risk, one-tier-at-a-time indexing), and located official
  `.gov.pk` source URLs for every missing book (S1–S10, edition NOT yet verified).

**Empirical basis:** `pdftotext` over the 4 AGP gold reports → citation frequency: SPPRA ~70
(indexed), GFR ~44, Sindh Financial Rules ~25, SLGA ~11, Treasury 3, P&D 3. So the real gap is
**two books** (GFR Vol-I + Sindh Financial Rules Vol-I), not four.

**Verification:** ⚠ **NOT built** — no local cargo toolchain (Windows box); Rust changes await VM
`cargo check` + `cargo test --lib uploads:: notice_assist::` before merge to `release`. Committed on
a side branch (not `release`) to avoid auto-deploying unverified code.

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- Source + **edition-verify** GFR Vol-I and Sindh Financial Rules Vol-I, then index shared (like
  E&D/RSO). Everything else is Tier 2/3. (`Para N` tokenizer now DONE — see compose.rs above.)
- Open scoping question: primary user Secretariat vs local-government (council) officers — reshuffles
  SLGA/local-council rules into Tier 1.

## 2026-07-10 — Slash commands must never reach retrieval or the LLM

**Why:** after leaving assist mode, `/cancel` ran a **full inference turn** and answered from the
SPPRA rules about the *"cancellation of a bidding process"*. Proven in `query_log`:

| turn | latency | answer |
|---|---|---|
| `/cancel` (session open) | **250 ms** | "Left assist mode." |
| `/cancel` (**no** session) | **38,801 ms** | "## General Answer … Cancellation of Bidding Process …" |

Only `/help|/reply|/audit` were recognised as commands (`is_notice_assist_command`). Every other
slash command fell through the `run_turn` intercept into ordinary capability dispatch → hybrid
retrieval + generation on the literal word "cancel".

**What:**
- `intent::is_slash_command()` — ANY leading `/<alpha>` token. `intent::is_assist_exit_command()` —
  `/cancel|/exit|/stop|/done`, recognised **even with no session open**.
- `assistant/mod.rs` — the intercept is now `is_slash_command(text) || assist_open`, so a slash
  command can never reach capability dispatch.
- `notice_assist::run` — exit works with or without a session (distinct message for each); an
  unrecognised slash command returns "Unknown command" + the command list, with **zero retrieval and
  zero generation**.
- Composer `/` palette gains `/cancel`.

**Verification:** VM `cargo check` EXIT 0; `assistant::intent` + `notice_assist` = **38 passed / 0
failed** (new `every_slash_command_is_kept_away_from_retrieval`); `npm run build` EXIT 0; deployed
(`907dec1`), `/api/health` 200.

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- `/help` on a **long** document reads only the first `MAX_DOC_CHARS = 14_000` chars in
  `chunk_index` order — on a 200-page audit report that is the cover/TOC, not the para. Audit flow
  needs a para picker (see memory `project_022-notice-assist`).
- Attaching a 200-page PDF runs OCR + embed **synchronously** before the response; needs a size
  guard/warning.

## 2026-07-10 — Notice Assist: support-while-writing (no questionnaire, no ready-made reply)

**Why (officer feedback):** it re-pasted the allegation every turn, asked too many questions, quoted
rules from the **wrong statute**, and produced a template letter. "We want support while writing the
reply — share the rules that protect him — not a ready-made reply."

**Two real grounding bugs:**
1. `compose::ground_one` matched the **entire** reference verbatim inside a chunk — a notice says
   *"Rule-4 of the Sindh Civil Servants (Efficiency & Discipline) Rules-1973"*, which never occurs as
   one string → **every rule returned `found=false`**. New `provision_tokens()` splits the reference
   into `Rule 4`, `Rule 4A(1)`, `Rule 5(3)` and verifies each. (Tests caught two more: `Rules-1973`
   parsed as "Rule 1973"; `sub-rule (3) of rule 5` parsed as "Rule 3" instead of `Rule 5(3)`.)
2. `Rule 4` exists in many statutes, so retrieval over the whole corpus **quoted rules the notice
   never invoked**. New `instrument_scope()` pins retrieval to the statute the notice *names* (word +
   year overlap on the document name; E&D **1973** beats APT **1974**). An unresolvable statute is a
   **MISS**, never a guess.

**New product shape:**
- `ground_support()` — retrieves the provisions that **protect** the officer (inquiry, right of
  hearing, penalty scale, appeal, the conduct rule) from the **same** statute, verbatim + cited.
- `support_brief()` — charge (once), provision invoked `[n]`, provisions in his favour `[n]`, what to
  put on the record. **No questions asked.**
- `Phase::CoWrite` — every later turn is a paragraph of HIS reply; `critique()` (local model,
  provisions-only context) returns **Support / Needs evidence / Risk / Sharper wording**. It declines
  to write the reply. `ask.rs` (questionnaire) and `draft()` (template letter) **deleted**.
- UI: top bar shows the logo instead of the "Noviq" wordmark; the chat rail keeps the wordmark and
  drops the duplicate logo.

**Verification:** VM `cargo check` EXIT 0; notice_assist + intent = **37 passed / 0 failed**;
`npm run build` EXIT 0; deployed (`f7f40c5`).

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- The five `ground_support` topic queries are heuristic; if a safeguard section comes back empty the
  queries need tuning against the E&D chunks.
- Audit paras cite instruments not in the corpus (SFR, GFR, Treasury Rules, P&D directives) — they
  now fail honestly (⚠) instead of quoting SPPRA, but give no support until indexed.
- `Phase::Gather|Ground|Draft|Done` are retained only so old sessions deserialize; they are
  normalised to `CoWrite` on load.

## 2026-07-10 — Attach: circular progress ring + tunnel-safe progress polling

**Why:** attaching a document showed a pulsing `⋯` with no sense of completeness. A ring driven by
the existing `/api/index/events` SSE stream would have been a lie: the **Cloudflare quick tunnel
buffers that stream indefinitely**, so a browser behind it never receives a tick and the ring could
only ever spin (same class as the `poll_turn` issue).

**What:**
- `components/ProgressRing.tsx` (new) — SVG ring; **determinate** (arc sweeps from 12 o'clock,
  `stroke-dasharray`) when a percent is known, **indeterminate** (spinning quarter-arc) when it is
  not; `active|done|error` colours, optional numeric label.
- **Real upload progress:** `transport.attachDocuments()` switched from `fetch` to
  **`XMLHttpRequest`** — `fetch` cannot report upload progress, `xhr.upload.onprogress` can, and it
  survives the tunnel. At 100 % (bytes on the server) the ring flips to indeterminate while the
  server parses/OCRs/embeds, because `attach_document` responds only when indexing is done.
- **Real index progress without SSE:** `indexer::emit_progress` now also records the latest tick per
  source in a process-wide map (`latest_progress()` / `progress_for()`), exposed by new
  **`POST /api/index_progress {sourceIds}`** (owner-scoped; `documents::index_progress`). ChatPage
  polls it every 1.5 s while a chip is indexing. **Sources with no tick are ABSENT from the
  response** so the ring stays indeterminate rather than showing a misleading 0 %.
- Chips: ring while indexing → **green tick** when ready → **red ✕** on failure; the paperclip button
  itself becomes a ring during upload.

**Verification:** `npm run build` EXIT 0; deploy `frontend=1 backend=1`; `/api/health` 200;
`POST /api/index_progress` → `200 []` for an idle source (and `401` without a token — route mounted
behind auth, not 404).

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- `latest_progress()` entries are pruned at 100 % on read; a source that dies mid-index leaves a
  stale entry until process exit (bounded, harmless).
- Desktop (Tauri) still uses the event channel; the poll is a no-op there.
- The 1.5 s poll only runs while a chip is pending/processing.

## 2026-07-10 — OCR: PP-OCR on ONNX Runtime (tesseract eliminated) + Notice Assist question policy

**Why (one bug, two layers).** Testing `/help` on a real scanned Sindh show-cause notice (SC02),
Noviq asked *"What specific misconduct is alleged against you?"* — but the misconduct **is written
in the notice**. Two causes:

1. **OCR destroyed the evidence.** The deploy VM's vCPU is masked to Core2 (`sse4_2`, **no AVX/FMA**).
   `import paddle` raises **SIGILL and kills the process** — not a catchable exception — so
   `paddle_ocr_enabled()` was true, PaddleOCR crashed on every scan, and `pdf.rs`'s `.or_else()`
   silently fell back to **tesseract**. Tesseract mangled the page and dropped the whole
   *"The allegations of your alleged misconduct are as under:-"* block. The model therefore only ever
   saw the word "misconduct". **The official `paddlepaddle` `noavx` wheel (2.4.2) imports but still
   SIGILLs on the first matmul** — no paddle build runs on this host.
2. **The model asked a question it must never ask** — one whose answer is in the document.

**What:**
- `sidecars/ingestion-sidecar/ingestion_sidecar.py` — `_ocr_backend()` (`ECHO_OCR_BACKEND` forces
  `rapidocr|paddleocr`; otherwise prefer RapidOCR when importable) + split `_ocr_rapidocr()` /
  `_ocr_paddleocr()`. **RapidOCR runs the SAME PaddleOCR (PP-OCR) det/rec models on ONNX Runtime**,
  which has no AVX requirement. Wire schema unchanged (`pages[].text`, `pages[].mean_conf`), plus a
  `backend` field. **Never probe `paddle` first — the import is fatal.** (`import os` was missing.)
  Installed `rapidocr-onnxruntime` into the prod OCR venv (`ECHO_OCR_PYTHON`).
- `notice_assist/extract.rs` — prompt gains strict **QUESTION RULES** (ask only for facts the
  *officer* holds; never what is alleged / which rule / who issued / the deadline). Because prompts
  aren't guarantees, `is_document_content_question()` **drops such questions after parsing**, and
  `default_officer_questions()` substitutes the standard officer-fact set if none survive.
- `notice_assist/frame.rs` — `source_chars` + `poorly_read()` / `allegation_details_missing()`;
  `mod.rs` now warns *"I could not read the specific allegation — attach a clearer copy"* instead of
  interrogating the officer when the scan is bad.

**Verification:** production sidecar on the SC02 page → `backend: rapidocr`, **1,703 chars, mean_conf
0.943**, and the full allegation ("Ex-Pakistan … remained absent till … 21.12.2020") is recovered —
tesseract had lost all of it. VM `cargo check` EXIT 0; `assistant::intent` + `notice_assist` tests =
**40 passed / 0 failed** (4 new, incl. the exact SC02 case). Deployed (`backend=1`), `/api/health` 200.

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- Documents ingested **before** this change hold tesseract-quality chunks — **re-attach / re-index**
  them (chunks are not retro-fixed).
- `ocr::paddle_ocr_enabled()` / `ocr_pdf_paddle()` are now misnomers (the sidecar chooses the
  runtime); rename when convenient.
- On an AVX host the paddle runtime is still selectable via `ECHO_OCR_BACKEND=paddleocr` (GPU build).

## 2026-07-10 — Settings: admin uploads were invisible; "index a file" was impossible

**Why:** as admin, indexing a document "didn't work" — nothing appeared. It had actually
**succeeded**: `api/uploads.rs:240` deliberately indexes an admin's uploads into the **shared
corpus** (`owner = None` when `user.role == "admin"`), so the row carries `owner_id = NULL` and the
`LEFT JOIN users` yields `owner_username = NULL`. The frontend listed "My documents" via
`myFolders() = all.filter(f => f.owner_username === currentUser().username)` → the admin's own
folder never matched → **silent success that looked like failure**. Separately, the folder input had
`webkitdirectory` set unconditionally in `onMount`, so the picker **refused single files** — hence
"index file not working".

**What (`src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx`, `src/api/index.ts` — frontend only):**
- The single `webkitdirectory` input is split into **"Add files"** (files) and **"Add folder"**
  (directory); the attribute is toggled by a `pickDirectory()` signal in a `createEffect`. Admin's
  button reads "Add files (shared)" with an explanatory title.
- **"My Documents" stays owner-scoped** (documents you own). For an admin it is empty *by design* —
  their uploads belong to the shared corpus and are managed under **Indexed Folders**. An admin
  note + admin-specific empty state explain this, so an empty pane no longer reads as a failed
  upload.
- Usage/quota bar hidden for admins: `usage_for_owner(user.id)` is always 0 when their docs are
  `owner_id NULL`, so it was reporting a meaningless 0.
- (`Source` TS type gains `owner_id`, already serialized by the Rust struct.)

**Correction (same day):** the first attempt matched the admin's `uploads/<username>` folder **by
path** so it would appear under "My Documents". That **duplicated the entire shared corpus** into
that pane — the same files "Indexed Folders" already lists. Reverted to the owner-based filter; the
explainer above is the fix instead. A redundant "Shared corpus" badge was also dropped (the row
already carries a Shared/Private toggle).

**Verification:** `npm run build` (tsc + vite) = EXIT 0; deployed to `release`
(`deploy done … frontend=1 backend=0`), `/api/health` = 200. Confirmed in the live DB that the two
Notice-Assist rulebooks were already indexed shared (E&D Rules 1973 = 172 chunks/172 embeddings;
RSO 2000 = 80/80), which is what proved the "failure" was cosmetic.

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- `myUsage()` for an admin reports 0 (quota is `usage_for_owner(user.id)`, and admin docs are
  `owner_id NULL`) — the usage bar is meaningless for admins; hide or special-case it.
- Path-basename matching would also claim a *shared* folder coincidentally named after the user;
  acceptable, but an explicit `is_own_upload_dir` flag from the API would be cleaner.
- Admin uploads remain global by design (architect confirmed) — the badge is the only guard.

## 2026-07-10 — F022 Notice Assist: `/help` officer-defense flow (MVP, branch `022-notice-assist`)

**Why:** honest officers who acted under political pressure receive show-cause notices, warnings
and audit paras, and file weak un-cited replies. Noviq already grounds answers in verbatim corpus
citations — this turns that into a guided path from "here is the notice against me" to "here is my
procedurally-correct, cited reply". Design problem: we cannot predefine intake fields because the
document type/structure is unknown. **Solution = two layers:** a tiny universal *argument frame*
(the only predefined structure) + the **local model DERIVES** the allegations and the questions
from the document itself.

**What (`services/assistant/capabilities/notice_assist/`, new):**
- `frame.rs` — `NoticeAssistState`/`Frame`/`Allegation`/`SlotQuestion`/`CitedRule` + phase machine
  (Analyze→Gather→Ground→Draft→Done). All `serde(default)`, unknown-key tolerant.
- `session.rs` — additive migration **010 `notice_assist_session`**; save/load/delete (one_ask seam).
  Resumable, tunnel-safe (no reliance on live SSE).
- `extract.rs` — **local-model** analysis via `query_router::generate_direct` (vLLM/llama.cpp —
  **never the remote engine**, so the sensitive notice stays on-box even when chat is on Groq).
  Free-text JSON (**no llguidance** — it crashes), tolerant parse: strips fences/prose, first
  balanced `{…}`, unknown `document_kind`→`other`, clamp confidence, **retry once**, then a
  single-question **fallback** (never a fabricated frame).
- `ask.rs` — slot loop: `record_answer`/`mark_gap`/`is_skip`("N/A")/`wants_draft`. A `Filled`/`Gap`
  slot is never re-asked.
- `compose.rs` — **grounding** retrieves each invoked rule from the **corpus** (the notice is the
  *premise*, per the 2026-07-10 attachment-vs-corpus rule) and accepts it only when the retrieved
  provision **verbatim contains** the normalized reference ("Rule-12 (2)" ≡ "rule 12(2)"). A miss ⇒
  `found=false` ⇒ explicit ⚠ "not found in the indexed corpus", **never quoted from model memory**.
  `draft()` is **deterministic assembly (no LLM)**: show-cause and audit-para templates + a
  documents-to-attach checklist; unanswered slots render as ⚠ gaps.
- `intent.rs` — `is_notice_assist_command` (`/help|/reply|/audit`). `assistant/mod.rs` — `run_turn`
  intercept (command OR open session) alongside transform/additive.
- Frontend — `/` command palette in `ConfidentialComposer` (mirrors the shipped `@`-mention
  machinery) + assist-mode banner in `ChatPage`.

**Integrity leash:** the reply asserts no fact the officer didn't supply and no rule the corpus
didn't supply; the political-pressure case is handled via the lawful **written-orders doctrine**,
never concealment. Grounded rules carry `[n]` citations gated against their own verbatim text.

**Verification (VM, glibc runbook `NOVIQ_TEST_PG_INSTALL_DIR`):** `cargo check --features
llm,server,cuda` = **EXIT 0**; `cargo test --lib -- assistant::intent assistant::capabilities::notice_assist`
= **35 passed / 0 failed** (17 notice_assist tests: parse-tolerance incl. `garbage_returns_none_not_a_fabricated_frame`,
slot loop, grounding-miss flagging, audit-vs-show-cause template). Frontend `npm run build` = EXIT 0.

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- **Principle VI deviation:** the analysis prompt + reply templates are **code constants**, not TOML
  config fragments (tasks T002/T027 still open). Move them to `config/personas/` before GA.
- **GA gate (T040):** grounding is only trustworthy if the E&D rules, audit/PAC rules, Rules of
  Business and Civil Servants Act are indexed. Un-located rules degrade honestly (⚠), but confirm
  coverage before launch. Also open: T038 prompt-eval on real notices, T030/T035 smoke checks.
- Extraction quality is unmeasured on real documents (only fixtures); run T038 before promoting.

## 2026-07-10 — Intent: titled-role obligation questions now route to ActionItems

**Why:** the full-suite run surfaced `intent_router::classifier::action_items_what_must_officer_do`
failing — and it was a REAL routing gap, not a stale test. The ActionItems phrasal cue only
allowed a bare role word right after "the" (`what must the (officer|secretary|director|department)`),
so a titled role — "the **Information** Officer", "the **Chief** Secretary", "the **Deputy**
Commissioner" — missed it and fell through to `Lookup`. Genuine "what must X do" obligation
questions weren't getting the ActionItems capability.

**What (`services/intent_router/classifier.rs`):** broadened the cue to `what (must|should)
<determiner> ([a-z]+ ){0,3} <role>` with an expanded role set (officer/secretary/director/
department/commissioner/authority/official/head/registrar/collector/minister/chairman/board/
agency). The **determiner+role frame is retained**, so the `f8828a02` bare-"must" false-positive
fix still holds ("must be advertised" / "must it go higher" do NOT match). Added regression tests
`action_items_titled_roles_route_correctly` + `bare_must_is_not_action_items`.

**Verification:** `intent_router::classifier` = **11 passed / 0 failed** on the VM (incl. the two
new guards). This closes the one failure from the full-suite run below → suite now fully green.

## 2026-07-10 — Test-PG runnable on the glibc-2.31 CI VM (NOVIQ_TEST_PG_INSTALL_DIR)

**Why:** `cargo test --lib` on the deploy VM (Ubuntu 20.04, **glibc 2.31**) failed every
PG-backed test with `initdb: libssl.so.3: cannot open shared object file`. libssl was a
red herring: providing it surfaced the real blocker — `postgresql_embedded` (0.20.4,
`bundled`) DOWNLOADS a PG 17.10.0 build that needs **glibc 2.34**, which cannot run here.
Production works because it reuses a pre-provisioned COMPATIBLE install
(`/opt/noviq/data/pg/install/17.10.0`, glibc ≤2.29 + **system OpenSSL 1.1**); tests
re-download the incompatible build into a fresh `/tmp` dir every run.

**What (`src-tauri/src/db/mod.rs` `testing::engine()`):**
- New env `NOVIQ_TEST_PG_INSTALL_DIR`: when set, it becomes `Settings.installation_dir`
  so `setup()` reuses the pre-seeded compatible binaries instead of downloading; the
  vendored-pgvector copy is skipped (already present + avoids a parallel-copy race).
  Default path (fresh per-pid install) unchanged.
- One-line fix: `create_dir_all(&root)` before `setup()`. The download path created the
  per-pid `/tmp/echoai-test-pg-<pid>/` root as a side effect of extraction; the reuse
  path skips extraction, so writing `root/.pgpass` + `root/data` failed with a bare
  `IoError("No such file or directory")` until the root is created explicitly.

**VM test runbook (glibc-2.31 host):** seed once
`cp -a /opt/noviq/data/pg/install/17.10.0 /home/appadmin/test-pg-install/17.10.0`, then
`export NOVIQ_TEST_PG_INSTALL_DIR=/home/appadmin/test-pg-install` and run
`cargo test --release --no-default-features --features llm,server,cuda --lib`. No
`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` needed (prod binaries link system OpenSSL 1.1).

**Verification:** full lib suite = **625 passed / 1 failed / 5 ignored**. The lone failure
`intent_router::classifier::action_items_what_must_officer_do` is **pre-existing** (stale
assertion after commit `f8828a02` "bare-'must' misroute"; my branch touches no
`intent_router/` file) — needs a separate test/assertion update. All 11 `assistant::memory`
PG tests, previously erroring on libssl, now pass.

## 2026-07-10 — Composer document scope: checkboxes now apply, @-mention typeahead, attachment-aware retrieval

**Why:** three linked bugs in "which documents does a turn search."
1. The right-rail document-tree checkboxes did **nothing** — `ChatPage` rendered
   `<DocumentTree />` with no `onSelectionChange`, and the whole request path
   (`sendMessage` → `/api/query` → `run_turn`) had **no parameter** to carry a
   chosen subset. Retrieval always ran over the full visible set regardless of
   ticks ("still searching unselected documents").
2. "Summarize/brief **this document**" / "from this" never resolved to the
   attachment → answered from the whole corpus (the audited summarize failure).
3. No way to point a turn at one named document.

**What:**
- **Scope plumbing (fixes #1).** `run_turn` gains `selected_source_ids:
  Option<&[String]>`; new private `narrow_to_selection()` intersects it with the
  F021 `visible_source_ids` privacy set (only narrows, never widens — a
  forged/stale id can't reach an unauthorized doc). `QueryReq.source_ids`
  (`sourceIds` alias) + the desktop `send_message` command arg thread it through.
  Frontend: `DocumentTree` now reports selection via `onSelectionChange` (wired in
  ChatPage) + emits its catalog via new `onCatalog`; `sendMessage(convId, text,
  sourceIds?)` sends the subset only when not "all selected."
- **Attachment-aware scope (fixes #2).** `intent::references_attachment()` detects
  "this/the attached document", "from this", "I uploaded…"; `run_turn` scopes
  **strictly to the conversation's live attachment** (`sources::attachment_source_ids`)
  when the turn wants the doc's OWN content. **Gated by
  `intent::seeks_legal_authority()`**: a turn that references the attachment but
  asks for external law ("which laws support this show-cause / audit para?") keeps
  the corpus in scope — the attachment is only the premise; the governing law
  lives in the corpus. `wants_attachment_only = references_attachment && !seeks_legal_authority`.
- **@-mention typeahead (fixes #3).** `ConfidentialComposer` gains a "@" document
  picker (`documents`/`onMentions` props): typing "@" opens a name typeahead;
  picking inserts "@Full Name" and scopes retrieval to that source **only**.
  Mentioned ids are derived statelessly from the text (edit-safe). A "Answering
  only from: <chips>" strip shows the active scope. Precedence in the composer:
  @-mention → checkbox subset → all.

**Files:** `services/assistant/mod.rs` (run_turn param + narrowing + `narrow_to_selection`),
`services/assistant/intent.rs` (`references_attachment`, `seeks_legal_authority`,
`wants_attachment_only` + tests), `db/repositories/sources.rs` (`attachment_source_ids`),
`api/query.rs` (`QueryReq.source_ids`), `commands/assistant.rs` (`send_message` arg),
`src/api/assistant.ts` (`sendMessage` sourceIds), `src/components/ConfidentialComposer.tsx`
(@-mention), `src/components/DocumentTree.tsx` (`onCatalog`), `src/pages/ChatPage.tsx` (wiring + scope hint).

**Verification:** frontend `npm run build` (tsc + vite) = **EXIT 0**. **Rust not yet
checked** — no toolchain on the Windows dev box; run on the VM before deploy:
`cargo check --no-default-features --features llm,server,cuda` +
`cargo test --lib -- assistant::intent assistant::tests::narrow_to_selection`.

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- Selecting "None" in the tree currently falls back to "all" (empty subset =
  no restriction, both FE and BE) — deliberate, but revisit if users expect
  none=nothing.
- Attachment-only detection is regex/heuristic; a novel phrasing may miss (falls
  back to full scope — safe) or the law-gate may misfire on an odd query.
- HyDE query expansion (requested) is NOT in this change — separate retrieval-
  quality feature; noted for a follow-up.

## 2026-07-09 — Multi-provider remote engine: Google Gemini (Gemma 4) + provider/model dropdowns

**Why:** the admin could point the remote engine only at providers that nest their route under
`/v1` (Groq, OpenRouter, Together). Google's Gemini OpenAI-compat layer is
`https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/chat/completions` — **no `/v1`** — so it
404'd against the hardcoded path. Goal: serve Gemma 4 12B (and any Gemini id) through the same
`NOVIQ_INFER_ENGINE=remote` seam, and let the admin pick a **provider** that auto-fills base
URL/prefix and shows a **per-provider model dropdown**.

**What:**
- `services/inference/remote.rs` — `Endpoint::path()` → `route()` now returns the version-less
  route (`/chat/completions`); the version segment moved to a new `RemoteConfig.api_prefix`
  (default `/v1`, seeded from `NOVIQ_REMOTE_PREFIX`). Requests hit `{base_url}{api_prefix}{route}`
  and health probes `{base_url}{api_prefix}/models`. New `pub fn normalize_prefix()` (empty stays
  empty → Gemini; `"v1"`→`"/v1"`). Added tests: prefix shapes + a Gemini URL assertion (no double
  version segment). **Default `/v1` keeps every existing provider + the stored Groq config working.**
- `services/inference/runtime.rs` — persist/load `remote_prefix` in `db_config`; `InferenceStatus`
  gains `remote_prefix`.
- `api/admin.rs` — GET returns `remote_prefix`; `SetInferenceReq.prefix` (Option) — `Some("")` sets
  it empty (Gemini), `None` keeps the stored value.
- `src/pages/Admin.tsx` — **Provider** dropdown (Groq / Google Gemini / OpenRouter / Custom) with a
  `PROVIDERS` catalogue: selecting one adopts its base URL + prefix + swaps the **Model** dropdown
  to that provider's curated ids (with an "Other…" free-text escape). Base URL/prefix/endpoint are
  auto-managed for known providers, editable only under Custom. Load path infers provider from the
  stored base URL and preserves an intentional empty prefix.

**Verification:** frontend `npm run build` (tsc + vite) = EXIT=0. **Rust not yet checked** — no
toolchain on the Windows dev box; run `cargo check --no-default-features --features llm,server,cuda`
+ `cargo test --lib -- inference::remote` on the VM before deploy.

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- OpenRouter catalogue intentionally omits `gemma-4-12b-it` (its slug returned "not available" as of
  2026-07-09) — verify/refresh provider model lists as availability changes.
- Gemini free-tier rate limits are tight; the evidence-leashed persona/citation density should be
  re-checked on Gemma 4 12B before making it prod default.
- Model dropdowns are static client-side lists (not fetched from each provider's `/models`) — a
  future refinement could populate them live via the existing health/`/models` path.

## 2026-07-08 — Admin toggle: local GPU (vLLM) ⇄ hosted API (Groq) + runtime engine config

**Why:** let an admin switch chat generation between the local A40 (vLLM) and a hosted
OpenAI-compatible API (Groq) — inserting the API key from the dashboard — **without a restart**.
Engine choice was env-captured in `OnceLock` generators (restart-only); this adds a runtime-mutable
config the dashboard drives. Builds on the remote-engine + structured-output work (same session).

**What:**
- `services/inference/runtime.rs` (new) — `RwLock` holding the **active** engine + `RemoteConfig` +
  a cached `Arc<dyn TextGenerator>`, seeded from env, overridable at runtime. `current_engine()`,
  `http_generator()`, `status()` (never exposes the key — only `has_api_key`), `apply()` (rebuilds
  the generator immediately), `load_from_db()`/`save_to_db()` persist to `db_config`
  (`infer_engine`, `remote_base_url`, `remote_model`, `remote_endpoint`, `remote_api_key`).
- `services/inference/mod.rs` — `engine_from_env()` now returns the **runtime-active** engine (so
  every `is_http()`/dispatch/health/budget gate honours a live switch); `engine_from_env_raw()` is
  the env seed; `parse_engine()`/`engine_str()` helpers; `http_generator()` returns `Arc<dyn>` (not
  `&'static`) so the generator can be swapped at runtime.
- `api/admin.rs` — `GET /api/admin/inference` (engine + remote config, no key) and
  `POST /api/admin/inference` (switch engine / set key/model/URL/endpoint; merges onto stored config
  so a blank key is preserved; rejects selecting remote with no key; persists + applies + audits).
- `api/router.rs` — mounts `/admin/inference`. `api/health.rs` — reports the runtime-active engine.
- `bin/noviq-server.rs` — `runtime::load_from_db()` at startup applies a saved override (no-op if none).
- `src/pages/Admin.tsx` — "Inference engine" card: Local GPU (vLLM) ⇄ Hosted API select, +
  write-only API-key field, model, base URL, endpoint; loads status on mount, POSTs on save.

**Verification:** VM `cargo check --no-default-features --features llm,server,cuda` = EXIT=0;
frontend `npm run build` (tsc + vite) = EXIT=0. Groq path itself proven live end-to-end earlier
(`remote::live_provider_stream` against real Groq).

**Security / behaviour:**
- API key stored in `db_config` (bundled Postgres — same trust boundary as the corpus); **never**
  returned by the read path. Consider encrypting-at-rest later.
- **Inert by default:** startup finds no saved override → stays on env `NOVIQ_INFER_ENGINE=vllm`.
  No behaviour change until an admin flips the toggle.

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- Deploying the toggle necessarily ships the (inert) remote-engine + agent scaffolding it depends on.
- When switched to Groq, the vLLM sidecar keeps holding VRAM (not stopped) — acceptable; a future
  refinement could pause it.
- Key-at-rest is plaintext in `db_config`; rotate the Groq key if the DB is ever exposed.

## 2026-07-08 — Senior-bureaucrat persona (evidence-leashed advisor voice)

**Why:** upgrade the assistant voice from a plain "bureaucrat assistant" to a **senior, seasoned
civil servant / advisor to top executives** (user-supplied persona, `Desktop/persona.txt`) — richer
institutional reasoning (issue → governing provision → application → exceptions/authority → risk)
for complex cases, while **preserving the evidence-first invariant**.

**What (`config/personas/bureaucrat.toml`, `[persona].full` + `.compact`):**
- `full` = the user's senior-bureaucrat identity paragraph **+ a grounding-leash paragraph** that
  keeps the richer voice from leaking parametric legal knowledge: authority comes ONLY from
  retrieved context; state every rule/number/authority verbatim + cite; flag gaps instead of
  filling them; **never cite a rule/judgment/precedent not in context**; separate law STATED
  (cited) from ANALYSIS (reasoning), and **every analytical sentence must rest on a cited
  provision** (closes the gap where the citation gate passes ungrounded, citation-less analysis).
- `compact` = short evidence-leashed variant for small models (the profile prod uses on Gemma).

**Design note:** the leash matters MORE at 8B than at 1B — a bigger model has more law to leak.
`GROUNDING_SYSTEM_PROMPT` v5.4 and all capability fragments are **unchanged**; only the persona
voice changed. For the current 8B use the **full** profile (`NOVIQ_PROMPT_PROFILE` unset/≠compact).

**Verification:** VM `cargo test --lib -- assistant::persona` = **5 passed / 0 failed** (TOML
parses via `include_str!`; guard assertions hold). Also delivered `Desktop/complex_queries.md` —
5 executive-grade multi-hop test queries + a scoring rubric.

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- Not yet run against the live 8B — verify citation density stays ~1.5/answer (advisor tone must
  not lower it) and Analysis stays tethered; use the 5 queries in `complex_queries.md`.
- Persona references judiciary/precedents but the corpus has no case law → leash forbids inventing
  it; indexing judgments is a separate corpus task if precedent reasoning is wanted.
- Executive answer-structure fragment (Bottom line → Basis → Analysis → Risks → Next step) drafted
  but NOT added — persona-only change for now; add as a capability fragment if desired.

## 2026-07-08 — Structured-output seam + agentic loop foundation (F017)

**Why:** the constrained legal-retrieval agent (spec `017-legal-retrieval-agent`, FR-003/014)
needs (1) the inference seam to emit **validated JSON** for control decisions (not brittle prose
parsing) and (2) a bounded LLM-controller / Rust-executor loop. Built both as a compiling,
unit-tested foundation on top of the F016 `TextGenerator` seam and the new remote engine.

**Layer 1 — structured output (seam extension):**
- `services/inference/mod.rs`: `ResponseFormat` enum (`Text` | `JsonObject` | `JsonSchema{name,schema}`),
  a `GenParams.response_format` field (default `Text` = unchanged chat), and a **non-streaming
  `complete()`** trait method (default impl drains `generate_stream` with a no-op sink, so both HTTP
  engines inherit it).
- `services/inference/remote.rs`: chat/completions bodies attach OpenAI `response_format`
  (`json_object` / `json_schema` with `strict:true`); `chatml_to_messages` now falls back to a
  single user message for plain (non-ChatML) prompts (agent control calls use plain prompts).
- `services/inference/vllm.rs`: maps `JsonObject`→`response_format`, `JsonSchema`→`guided_json`
  (vLLM guided decoding).
- `services/query_router.rs`: `vllm_infer` `GenParams` literal gains `..default()`.

**Layer 2 — agent orchestrator (`services/agent/`, server-only `#[cfg(feature="server")]`):**
- `tools.rs`: `Tool` trait (name/description/async run→`ToolResult{observation, evidence_ids}`) +
  fixed `ToolRegistry` (closed tool set — no open-ended/internet tools, spec Out-of-Scope).
- `mod.rs`: `run_agent()` bounded loop — builds a ChatML controller prompt, calls `complete()`
  with a `JsonSchema` action constraint, `parse_action()` (balanced-brace extractor tolerant of
  ```json fences; rejects unregistered tools), dispatches to Rust tools, accumulates evidence.
  Enforces: hard `MAX_ITER` cap (`NOVIQ_AGENT_MAX_ITER`, default 3, FR-005), **no-progress stop**
  when an iteration adds no new evidence (FR-007), **grounded refusal** on no-evidence/malformed
  output (FR-006, never fabricate), bounded control-call retry (FR-003). Final answer via a
  `synthesize()` call over the gathered evidence.

**Verification (VM, `--no-default-features --features llm,server,cuda`):** `cargo check` EXIT=0,
`cargo test --no-run` EXIT=0, and **`cargo test -- services::agent services::inference` = 29
passed / 0 failed**. Loop logic tested against a scripted mock generator + mock tool (tool→finish,
no-evidence refusal, no-progress stop, malformed-output safety, schema/format bodies).

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- **Not wired into the live chat path.** No real tools yet (retrieval/cross-ref/expansion), no
  `chat://` status emit (FR-010), no agent on/off flag (FR-012), no fast-path gate (FR-013). Next
  step is a `HybridSearchTool` wrapping the existing retrieval + wiring `run_agent` behind a flag.
- Structured output unverified against a live provider — vLLM `guided_json` vs remote
  `response_format` should be smoke-tested for actual JSON conformance.
- No golden-set eval yet (spec FR-016) — gains are unmeasured until F018 eval exists.

## 2026-07-08 — Remote OpenAI-compatible LLM API inference engine

**Why:** add a third inference backend so the server can generate through a *hosted*
OpenAI-compatible API (OpenRouter/Groq/Together/Fireworks/DeepInfra/DeepSeek/…) — e.g. a
free-tier GPU API — without local weights, alongside the existing vLLM sidecar and in-process
llama.cpp GGUF. Selected with `NOVIQ_INFER_ENGINE=remote` (or `api`).

**What (files):**
- `services/inference/remote.rs` (new) — `RemoteGenerator` implementing `TextGenerator`.
  Mirrors `vllm.rs` raw-byte SSE line buffering + cancel + per-delta `on_token`. Adds (1)
  bearer auth from `NOVIQ_REMOTE_API_KEY` (`.env` only — never hardcoded, Constitution) and
  (2) two endpoint shapes: `chat` (default, `/v1/chat/completions`, `messages` + `delta.content`)
  vs `completions` (`/v1/completions`, raw prompt + `choices[].text`, byte-identical like vLLM).
  In chat mode `chatml_to_messages()` parses the hand-built ChatML prompt back into role/content
  messages (strips the Qwen no-think prefill; drops the trailing `<|im_start|>assistant` gen cue
  so providers don't reject a trailing assistant turn). Config from `NOVIQ_REMOTE_*` env. 9 unit tests.
- `services/inference/mod.rs` — `EngineKind::Remote`; `EngineKind::is_http()` predicate
  (`Vllm | Remote`) that captures the real meaning of the old `== Vllm` gates ("out-of-process
  HTTP engine, not the in-process GGUF slot"); `remote_generator()` OnceLock; `http_generator()
  -> Option<&dyn TextGenerator>` single dispatch point; `engine_from_env()` maps `remote`/`api`.
- `services/query_router.rs` — `vllm_infer` now resolves the generator via `http_generator()`
  (serves both HTTP engines through one path); `try_llm_infer_streaming` gate + the FR-011
  friendly-error check use `is_http()`; "Send to LLM" trace adds a `Remote` arm (reports
  `NOVIQ_REMOTE_MODEL`).
- `services/assistant/{mapreduce.rs,mod.rs}` — window resolution gates on `is_http()`; window
  precedence `NOVIQ_REMOTE_MAX_MODEL_LEN` → `NOVIQ_VLLM_MAX_MODEL_LEN` → 8192.
- `api/query.rs` — width-1 `gen_gate` permit skipped for any HTTP engine (remote handles its
  own admission), via `is_http()`.
- `api/health.rs` — `/api/health.engine` reports `{kind:"remote", ready}` (readiness = `GET
  /v1/models`, which also validates the key).
- `deploy/noviq-server.service` — documents the `NOVIQ_REMOTE_*` env block.

**Cross-cutting:** `EngineKind` gained a variant → all three exhaustive matches (health, trace
labels, `http_generator`) handle `Remote`; all other sites were `== Vllm` comparisons now
folded into `is_http()`. No DB/schema change. Desktop default unchanged (llama.cpp).

**Follow-ups / risks (≤3):**
- Chat vs completions: `chat` double-templates a provider's chat template around our content;
  `completions` preserves byte-identical prompts but not every hosted API exposes it — default
  is `chat` for breadth. Verify answer/citation quality per provider before prod.
- Not yet compiled (no Rust on Windows — compile on VM per runbook) nor live-smoke-tested
  against a real provider. Owed: VM `cargo check` + a streamed turn against one free API.
- Secrets: key is env-only; confirm `.env` stays git-ignored on the VM.

## 2026-07-06 — Map-reduce kill-switch + trace labels reflect real engine/DB

**Trace labels (`afb10055` release, `services/query_router.rs`):** query traces printed the
on-disk GGUF slot filename (`Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M.gguf`, or the `qwen2.5-1.5b` fallback) as the
generation model even under vLLM — where the GGUF never loads — and hardcoded `sqlite-vec`
/ `FTS5` although the build is PostgreSQL-only (pgvector + `websearch_to_tsquery`). Fix:
- "Send to LLM" step now branches on `inference::engine_from_env()`: vLLM reports the served
  `NOVIQ_VLLM_MODEL` (reconstructing the HF repo id when it's an offline snapshot path);
  llama.cpp reports the GGUF filename. Emits `Engine` + `Model` facts (was `Model file`).
- Vector-search `Engine`: `sqlite-vec ANN` → `pgvector ANN (cosine)`.
- Keyword-search title: `FTS5` → `PostgreSQL full-text`.

**Map-reduce kill-switch (`6458cb28` release, `services/assistant/mod.rs`):** the map-reduce
capabilities (SummarizeDoc/Compare/Conflict/ActionItems) run a multi-batch provision sweep
that over-builds context — a live SPPRA "responsibilities … bid evaluation reports"
ActionItems query gathered 67 provisions and took **82.6 s** on the 8B. New
`map_reduce_enabled()` reads env `NOVIQ_MAPREDUCE` (default ON); when `off`/`0`/`false`/`no`,
a `Capability::is_map_reduce()` cap is downgraded to `Capability::Guidance` **before** dispatch
so it uses one bounded top-K retrieval (the single-pass guidance path). Default keeps
map-reduce on for the desktop build; **prod sets `NOVIQ_MAPREDUCE=off` in `.env` (+ both model
backups)**. Verified via admin `/api/query`: same query now `capability:"guidance"`, HTTP 200
in **26.1 s** (from 82.6 s), coherent cited answer.
**Tradeoff:** single-pass may reduce breadth on "list all X" questions vs the provision sweep;
reversible per-deployment via the env var with no rebuild. Owed: PHRs for both commits.
**Ops note:** prod chat model temporarily flipped Gemma 4B → Qwen3-8B-AWQ this session for a
user A/B (restore `.env.bak.gemma4b.20260706` + restart noviq-vllm, noviq-server to revert).

## 2026-07-06 — Map-reduce now retrieval-scoped: doubled-K hybrid slice, one tranche

**Why:** map-reduce capabilities gathered EVERY leaf chunk of the user's visible corpus
(`gather_provisions` over `visible_source_ids` — no document narrowing at all). A topical
"responsibilities … bid evaluation reports" question planned 61+ sequential map batches,
ran 10+ minutes, then died on a Gemma token-overflow 400 (14,880 real tokens vs 14,336
window on ONE batch) with the error unlogged (detached task) — browser saw nothing, no
query_log row, no trace. Architect decision: map over the retrieval slice instead;
officer-driven "dig deeper" iterations (next tranche on request, merge with prior
findings, stop offering at exhaustion) DEFERRED as the follow-up design.
**Fix (`0a1a9fda` release):**
- `query_router::retrieve_for_mapreduce` — same hybrid vec+FTS5+union/RRF path guidance
  uses, at `ECHO_MAPREDUCE_K_MULT` (default 2.0) × `ECHO_VEC_K`/`ECHO_FTS_K`, scoped to
  the caller's visible sources. ~96 chunks → ~4-6 batches ≈ 1-2 min vs 10+.
- `capabilities::gather_provisions_retrieved` — builds provisions+citations from the
  slice (unit_label via one batched IN lookup). `run_mapreduce_capability` + the four
  capability `run()`s + dispatch now take `embedder`. `gather_provisions` kept
  (dead_code-allowed) for the deferred whole-document audit path.
**Impact:** SC-009 "full coverage by construction" per turn is intentionally relinquished
for map-reduce turns — coverage follows query relevance (per-turn); the interactive
deepening design will restore completeness across turns. Summaries of a named act are now
retrieval-biased toward the query wording — acceptable per architect for this iteration.
**Still open underneath:** Gemma-aware token estimate + vllm.rs real-token clamp (a
single mis-planned batch can still 400), detached-task error logging, scheduler workload
cleanup on error.

## 2026-07-06 (later) — Gemma 3 4B LIVE via bitsandbytes 4-bit + tunnel-timeout fix (detach + poll_turn)

**Why:** bnb 4-bit (the one untried 4B quant) dodges the fp16 AWQ/Marlin kernels that NaN'd —
bnb dequantizes in bf16. Staged + verified on prod: weights 3.57 GiB, smoke completion has
finite logprobs, SPPRA answers cited (grounding up to 1.50/15 citations), out-of-corpus refusal
correct, gen 60–66 tok/s. Full report: `docs/gemma-4b-staging-report-2026-07-06.md`.
**Config (live `.env`):** `NOVIQ_VLLM_MODEL=<local HF snapshot path>` (NOT the repo id — vLLM's
bnb loader lists the repo tree online and crashes under `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`; a local dir path
keeps the offline invariant), `NOVIQ_VLLM_QUANT=bitsandbytes`, `NOVIQ_PROMPT_PROFILE=full`
(compact was a 1B workaround; 4B's best grounding came under full v5.4.0),
`NOVIQ_VLLM_LEN_HEADROOM=6144` → serve_len 14336. Headroom raised because the Rust char-based
token estimate under-counts the Gemma tokenizer by up to ~60% on dense legal chunks (measured
13,243 real tokens vs ≤8192 budget) → vLLM 400s killed map passes. Proper fix still open:
clamp `max_tokens` against the real prompt count in `services/inference/vllm.rs`.
**Tunnel-timeout fix (branch `fix-tunnel-detach-poll`):** Cloudflare quick tunnel kills HTTP
requests at ~100 s and axum cancels the handler on disconnect → map-reduce turns (minutes by
design) were aborted mid-pipeline with nothing persisted (`error_apierror` in browser).
- `api/query.rs::query` — turn now runs in a detached `tokio::spawn` (gen-gate permit acquired
  INSIDE the task so the llama.cpp width-1 invariant holds across disconnects); always persists
  to `query_log` on success.
- `api/query.rs::poll_turn` + route `/poll_turn` — recovery read, scoped user_id+conversation_id
  with `since_ms` guard (never serves a stale turn).
- `db/repositories/query_log.rs::latest_since` — the scoped query.
- `src/api/assistant.ts::pollTurn`, `src/pages/ChatPage.tsx::recoverTurn` — web-only: on send
  failure poll every 6 s ≤12 min, render recovered answer (masking refill applied); server-side
  failures still surface (no row ⇒ timeout ⇒ original error).
**Impact:** delivery-path only — zero change to model output. `query_log` now doubles as the
recovery store (retention follow-up). Live token streaming over the tunnel still broken (SSE
buffered) — WS remains the proper fix. Revert paths: 1B = MODEL/QUANT/PROFILE keys; 8B =
`.env.bak.qwen8b.20260706`.

## 2026-07-06 — Gemma 3 4B staging: FAILED on vLLM 0.8.5 (NaN int4 kernels / bf16 OOM) — do not retry these variants

**Why:** user asked to stage 4B (int4 ~3GB < Qwen3-8B-AWQ ~5.7GB, so it "should fit" — size is
fine; kernels are not). 4B is multimodal `Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration`; the text-only 1B is a
different arch and works.
**Evidence (all on prod VM, vLLM 0.8.5 + A40 sm_86 + cuda-compat):**
- `gaunernst/gemma-3-4b-it-qat-autoawq` (AWQ) — loads, generates EMPTY text; `logprobs=1` →
  500 "Out of range float values are not JSON compliant" = NaN logits.
- `ISTA-DASLab/gemma-3-4b-it-GPTQ-4b-128g` — config is compressed-tensors (explicit
  `--quantization gptq_marlin` errors; `NOVIQ_VLLM_QUANT=none` auto-detects) — loads, same
  empty/NaN output.
- `unsloth/gemma-3-4b-it` bf16 (8.1GB) — "No available memory for the cache blocks" crash-loop
  even at util 0.92 + 7168 window + 4 seqs (~1GB other-process VRAM overhead).
**Untried:** bitsandbytes 4-bit (non-marlin kernels). Prep done: venv310 pip bootstrapped via
`ensurepip` (uv venv shipped without pip), live `/opt/noviq/vllm-scripts/run-vllm.sh` handles
`NOVIQ_VLLM_QUANT=bitsandbytes` (`--load-format bitsandbytes`) — repo `deploy/vllm/run-vllm.sh`
NOT yet synced with that line. Real fixes if bnb fails: vLLM upgrade (torch/CUDA/transformers
chain on driver-locked VM) or Qwen3-4B-AWQ (ChatML-native, proven quant path).

SPPRA query answers with 3 citations. All three 4B checkpoint downloads retained in the HF cache.

## 2026-07-06 — Compact prompt profile for small models (v5.5.0-compact, Gemma-1B fix)

**Why:** entry below — Gemma-1B systematically refused answerable queries under the ~530-token
persona+guidance+v5.4 prompt stack while answering the same context correctly under a short
instruction. Live prompt A/B against the vLLM sidecar isolated two causes: (1) v5.4's up-front
refusal rule over-triggers on a 1B; (2) the one-sentence citation demo anchors 1B answers to one
sentence, dropping every condition.
**Fix (`242699a2` on release; branch `compact-prompt-profile`; user-approved prompt):**
- `services/llm.rs` — `GROUNDING_SYSTEM_PROMPT_COMPACT` (+`_VERSION "5.5.0-compact"`, audit-logged),
  `compact_prompt_profile()` (env `NOVIQ_PROMPT_PROFILE=compact`), `grounding_system_prompt()` /
  `grounding_prompt_version()` selectors. Compact prompt keeps literal `[n]` (demo-injection
  trigger) and the canonical refusal sentence byte-identical to `INSUFFICIENT_INFO_MSG` (unit test).
- `assistant/capabilities/guidance.rs::system_prompt` — compact profile absorbs persona voice +
  guidance refine-offer into the single compact prompt; non-guidance capabilities keep their task
  fragment. Default profile byte-identical.
- `query_router.rs` — Regular queries use the selector; version logging uses the active version;
  richer worked citation demo (cited condition LIST + refine offer) under the compact profile.
**Verified live (prod `/api/query`, profile active):** both previously-refusing SPPRA queries now
answer with citations; out-of-corpus question still refuses correctly. Residual 1B comprehension
errors remain (e.g. invented "Tax-Free Procurement" label, partial condition lists) — prompt
ceiling reached; that's the model. `.env` now: MODEL=unsloth/gemma-3-1b-it, QUANT=none,
PROMPT_FORMAT=gemma, PROMPT_PROFILE=compact. Full revert to 8B = `.env.bak.qwen8b.20260706` keys +
drop/ignore PROMPT_PROFILE (chatml default) + restart both services.

## 2026-07-06 — Prod chat model swap: Qwen3-8B-AWQ → Gemma 3 1B (user decision) + Gemma prompt-format seam

**Why:** user chose to run Gemma 3 1B as the production chat generator (advised it is a quality
step down from Qwen3-8B for citation-grounded legal answers — decision recorded; revert is an
`.env` flip). Blocker found first: every prompt builder emits **hand-built ChatML** (Qwen
markers) sent byte-identical to vLLM `/v1/completions` — Gemma 3 uses `<start_of_turn>` turns,
so a bare model swap would feed it foreign control tokens and its stop token would never fire.
**Fix (`77d8f12a` on release; branch `gemma-1b-integration`):**
- `services/inference/vllm.rs` — `NOVIQ_VLLM_PROMPT_FORMAT=gemma` (default `chatml` = byte-identical
  to before) translates at the single `VllmGenerator::generate_stream` choke point instead of
  touching ~5 prompt builders: leading system block folded into first user turn (Gemma has no
  system role), `user/assistant` → `user/model`, `<|im_end|>` → `<end_of_turn>` (prompt + stop
  list), Qwen3 `NOVIQ_NO_THINK` prefill `<think>\n\n</think>\n\n` dropped. 4 unit tests.
- `deploy/vllm/run-vllm.sh` (repo + live `/opt/noviq/vllm-scripts/` copy, backup
  `run-vllm.sh.bak.20260706`) — `NOVIQ_VLLM_QUANT=none` omits `--quantization` for unquantized
  bf16 checkpoints; repo copy reconciled to live reality (`--kv-cache-dtype auto` +
  `--enable-chunked-prefill`; fp8 KV crashes Triton fp8e4nv on sm_86 — F016 finding).
**Ops:** weights = `unsloth/gemma-3-1b-it` (bf16, 1.9GB; `google/` repo is HF-gated → 403 without
a licensed token) in `/opt/noviq/model-library/hf-cache`. `.env`: `NOVIQ_VLLM_MODEL=unsloth/gemma-3-1b-it`,
`NOVIQ_VLLM_QUANT=none`, `NOVIQ_VLLM_PROMPT_FORMAT=gemma`. Revert = restore those three keys to
`Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ`/`awq`/`chatml` + restart noviq-vllm, noviq-server.
**Cross-cutting:** llama.cpp fallback path untouched (still ChatML + Qwen GGUF). Output scrubbers
in `llm.rs` unchanged — vLLM trims `<end_of_turn>` server-side via the stop list. Expect quality
regression vs 8B on synthesis/citations; latency and concurrency should improve.
**Verified live 2026-07-06:** integration CORRECT (env in server process, translated prompt
accepted, retrieval + citations intact, turn latency ~2s vs ~6s on 8B). BUT the predicted quality
regression is immediate and systematic: on both smoke queries (Rule 16 direct contracting /
alternative methods) Gemma-1B returned the v5.4 refusal line despite the correct chunks being
retrieved and cited (3 citations each). Direct probe against vLLM with the SAME context but a
short instruction → correct grounded answer with [n] citation. Root cause: the ~500-token
multi-part v5.4 system prompt over-triggers the strict refusal rule on a 1B model — not a
retrieval or format bug. Options: Gemma-tuned shorter system prompt, or revert (3-key `.env`
restore: `.env.bak.qwen8b.20260706`). Gotcha logged: `scp` from Windows carried CRLF into
`/opt/noviq/vllm-scripts/run-vllm.sh` → systemd 127 crash-loop on `env: 'bash\r'`; fixed with
`sed -i "s/\r$//"`.

## 2026-07-05 — Web polling fallback for indexing status (SSE-tunnel workaround)

**Why:** the finding below — trycloudflare quick tunnel delivers 0 SSE body bytes, so
`/api/index/events` never reaches the browser and indexing statuses ("processing" folders,
My-documents rows, chat attach chips) looked frozen until a manual page revisit.
**Fix (frontend only, web-only via `!isTauri()` guard; desktop Tauri events untouched):**
- `src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx` — `indexPollNeeded` memo (any folder OR myDocs source
  pending/processing) drives a `createEffect` interval: every 5s call `loadFolders()` (which
  also reloads myDocs+usage on web) and `refreshFolderSourcesIfOpen` for still-active folders.
  Interval self-clears when nothing is pending (memo flips false → effect cleanup).
- `src/pages/ChatPage.tsx` — `attachPollNeeded` memo (any attachment pending/processing)
  polls `loadAttachments(conversationId())` every 4s, same self-clearing pattern.
**Notes:** SSE listeners kept — direct/desktop access still gets live per-file progress bars;
polling only converges statuses (no percent updates through the tunnel). Chat *token* streaming
through the tunnel is still broken (separate concern — needs WS or chunked fallback).

## 2026-07-05 — F021 usage queries: SUM(bigint) decodes as NUMERIC, not i64 (browser-test blocker)

**Symptom:** first F021 browser test (quickstart §1, My documents upload) failed with
`ApiError: mismatched types; Rust type Option<i64> (INT8) is not compatible with SQL type NUMERIC`.
**Root cause:** PostgreSQL's `SUM()` over a `BIGINT` column returns `NUMERIC`, but both usage
queries decoded column 0 as `Option<i64>`. Hit on every quota check (`check_quota` →
`usage_for_owner`) and the admin usage view. Not caught earlier: scope_tests use embedded PG
(unrunnable on VM glibc 2.31) and don't cover the usage queries.
**Fix:** `::BIGINT` cast on the SUM in `src-tauri/src/db/repositories/sources.rs::usage_for_owner`
and `src-tauri/src/api/admin.rs::usage`.
**Lesson:** PG aggregate return types differ from the column type — SUM(int8)→numeric,
SUM(int4)→int8, AVG→numeric. Always cast aggregates in `query_as` decodes.

## 2026-07-05 — F021 deploy crashloop: migration 009 vs pre-existing visibility column (fix `b557891b`)

**Symptom:** after merging F021 to release (`bf3e82f9`), noviq-server crash-looped at boot
("column visibility of relation sources already exists"), bundled PG down with it → site 502.
**Root cause:** migration **005** (F014) had already added a nullable, unused
`sources.visibility TEXT`; 009's plain `ADD COLUMN visibility` failed atomically, so
owner_id/conversation_id were never created either. Not a partial-apply — first boot error was literal.
**Fix:** 009 rewritten idempotent (`IF NOT EXISTS` on all columns/indexes) and it now ADOPTS
the existing column: `UPDATE NULL/legacy → 'shared'`, then `SET DEFAULT 'shared'` + `SET NOT NULL`.
No CHECK constraint (ADD CONSTRAINT has no IF NOT EXISTS; API enforces the two-value rule).
Dry-run against live prod PG in BEGIN/ROLLBACK: clean (11 docs → shared). Manual-PG repair
runbook (pg_ctl on 5432) proven and recorded in memory `project_021-user-documents.md`.
**Lesson:** grep prior migrations for column names before writing ALTERs — 005 also has
other speculative columns.

## 2026-07-05 — Sign-in always lands on Chat (stale-URL redirect fix)

**Why (user):** signing in dropped users onto whatever URL the browser was left on —
`LoginScreen` is a full-screen overlay OUTSIDE the Router, so after auth the Router
mounted at the stale path (e.g. `/settings` from a previous admin session, bookmark, or
refresh). Normal users stranded on Settings hit the admin-gated fetches → "authentication
error"; even admins landing on Settings was wrong UX. Every sign-in must land on Chat.
**Change:** `src/components/LoginScreen.tsx` `handleSubmit` — after `login()` succeeds,
`window.history.replaceState(null, "", "/")` before the app shell mounts, so the Router
always starts at `/` (Chat). `replaceState` (not push) so Back doesn't return to the
stale path. Session *restore* (`restoreSession`) intentionally untouched — an already
signed-in user refreshing on `/settings` should stay there.
**Verify:** `tsc --noEmit` exit 0. Browser: log out on /settings → sign in as normal
user → lands on Chat, no auth error.

## 2026-07-03 — Confidential-detail masking in chat (F020 Phase 1, client-side)

**Why (user):** every query is persisted verbatim in `query_log`/traces/`chat_message`,
so any CNIC/name/salary an officer types lives in PG forever + is visible to admins. The
LLM is self-hosted, so the risk is *storage*, not third-party leakage → mask before send.
Spec `specs/020-confidential-masking/spec.md` (Phase 2 = names via GLiNER + /api/detect_pii).
**Change (frontend only — `src/`; deploy rebuilds `dist`):**
- **`src/lib/maskEngine.ts`** — regex detectors (CNIC `\d{5}-\d{7}-\d`, PK phone, money
  `Rs…`, file/case no., email, date; **legal tokens Rule/Article/Section deliberately NOT
  matched** so retrieval is unaffected). `MaskSession`: reversible label map (`[CNIC_1]` —
  same value → same label), `mask(raw, ranges)` (right-to-left splice), `refill(text)`,
  sessionStorage-serialisable. Verified round-trip via esbuild+node (6/6 types, Rule 16 preserved).
- **`src/components/ConfidentialComposer.tsx`** — composer with a highlight **overlay**
  (transparent textarea over a mirrored tinted layer — a text box can't colour substrings),
  a **chip tray** (tap to keep/mask each detected item), and **"+ Mask selected"** (select
  text → manual mark; every occurrence masked). Enter submits, Shift+Enter newline.
- **`src/pages/ChatPage.tsx`** — `submit` now masks `input()` with the active ranges BEFORE
  `sendMessage` (server/DB/logs see labels only); the user bubble shows the RAW text; answers
  + live stream are `refill()`-ed for display. Map is per-conversation, session-only (key
  `noviq_mask_<id>`), loaded on mount/newChat/selectConversation. Composer `<input>` → the
  new component (send button now `type=button` calling `submit()`).
**Privacy note:** local `turns` (localStorage history) still hold real values — that's the
officer's own machine; the *server* never receives them. Encrypting/masking local history is
a Phase-3 item.
**Verify:** `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; `vite build` exit 0; engine round-trip test PASS. Visual
overlay alignment + chip/selection interactions need a browser eyeball (this deploy).

**Revision 1 (same day, user browser feedback):**
- **CNIC regex** was missing plain/spaced forms → broadened to `\d{5}[-\s]?\d{7}[-\s]?\d`
  (dashes, spaces, or 13 plain digits). Verified all 3 forms.
- **Masking confirmation UI** (user: "how do users confirm it worked?") — the sent user
  bubble now **highlights the masked values** (emerald `<mark>`) + a "🔒 N details masked
  before sending" caption; the answer **highlights the refilled values** (`highlightMarkdown`
  → inline `<mark>` survives marked+DOMPurify) with a "highlighted = your masked details"
  note. New helpers `maskedItemsFromRanges`/`highlightSegments`/`highlightMarkdown`; `Turn`
  gained `masked?: MaskedItem[]` (stored on both user+assistant turns at submit).
- **Composer auto-grows** to ~3 lines (80px) then scrolls (was 1-line hidden-scroll).
- **Removed the top context-window bar** (reclaimed vertical space per user).
- **Edit query button** now always visible (was opacity-0 hover-only); **restored a Copy
  button** on every answer (copies the refilled text; "Copied" flash).
- Names still Phase-2 (GLiNER) — manual "Mask selected" covers them for now.

**Revision 2 — Phase 2a: automatic name detection (client-side heuristic).**
Server GLiNER (spec's Phase-2 plan) is a heavy lift on THIS VM (no-AVX CPU → prebuilt
ML wheels SIGILL, as llama-cpp-python did; GPU VRAM ~1.3 GB free under the 8B). So name
masking ships now as a tuned client-side heuristic (`detectNames` in `maskEngine.ts`):
runs of Title-Case tokens minus a legal/govt/geographic **stoplist**, plus single names
after an honorific/**trigger** (Mr/Dr/Syed/…); honorifics trigger but aren't masked
(mask "Bilal", not "Mr. Bilal"); trailing punctuation trimmed. Verified: catches
"Ahmed Khan"/"Syed Ali"/"Ayesha Siddiqui", ignores "Government of Sindh"/"Chief
Minister"/"Request for Quotations". False positives handled by the existing exclude
chips. **Bug fixed in-flight:** `NAME_TRIGGERS` `.split(" ")` bound to only the 2nd
string literal (precedence) → Set of chars not words → single-name+trigger never fired;
wrapped in parens. Model-based upgrade (Phase 2b GLiNER, higher recall) deferred until
it can be validated on the VM. `tsc` + `vite build` green.

**Revision 3 (browser feedback):**
- **Single + lowercase names** ("shahid", "Shahid", "yasir") were missed (heuristic
  needed 2+ Title-Case words). Added a curated **`NAME_GAZETTEER`** (~200 common Pakistani
  first/last names, case-insensitive) + `isNameToken`; a run is accepted if it contains a
  known name OR is 2+ Title-Case words OR is a single word after a trigger. Catches
  shahid/Shahid/yasir/Yasir Khan; still ignores Government of Sindh / Request for
  Quotations / Peshawar. **Still code, not an LLM** (Phase 2b GLiNER = the model path).
- **Copy-answer button** moved inline with Cited/Confidence badges, right-aligned
  (`ml-auto`), same badge style (was a separate line under the answer).
- **ChatGPT-style scroll:** on a new turn, pin the latest USER question near the TOP of the
  transcript (`data-role="user"` + getBoundingClientRect) and stop auto-following streaming
  tokens — was jumping to the bottom (feedback panel) of long answers.

**Revision 4 — Option A: high-recall name masking + word-scale amounts.**
- **Names inverted to a BLOCKLIST** (user: "dictionary isn't catching all names; names are
  open-ended"). `isNameToken` now flags any capitalised word that is NOT a common English
  word (`COMMON_WORDS`, ~400 terms) and NOT a legal/govt/place term (`NAME_STOPLIST`, +PK
  cities +currency) — plus known names via the gazetteer for lowercase. Every run of name
  tokens is accepted (high recall; masking is privacy → a missed name is worse than an
  over-mask the officer can un-tap). Catches novel names (Kashif Mehmood, Ali Raza); still
  ignores Rule 16 / SPPRA / Sindh Local Government Act / Karachi. Trigger-gating removed.
- **Amounts** now match word-scales with/without currency: `Rs 5 lac`, `2 million`,

- **Bug fixes:** "Rs" was flagged as a name → added currency tokens to the stoplist;
  `mergeSpans` tie-break now keeps the LONGER span on equal start (money "Rs 5 lac" beats
  stray name "Rs"). `tsc` + `vite build` green.

## 2026-07-03 — Disable citation fast-path: single hybrid path for all queries

**Symptom (user, live):** after re-indexing SPPRA, "rule 16" questions were
refused — `"The retrieved documents do not contain enough information…"`.
**Root cause (DB + trace `3fb64c8d`):** SPPRA Rule 16 is indexed correctly
(`Part_II/Rule_16/(1)/(a)/(ii)` present, 607 chunks, all embedded, maxlen 1411 —
nesting fix verified live). The failure was the **citation fast-path** (STEP 6):
a bare "Rule 16" triggered `citation_fast_path`, which resolves by `unit_label`
and **bypasses vector search + reranker + hybrid union**. "Rule 16" collides
across 4 instruments (SPPRA 24, Secretariat Manual 27, SLGA Compendium 21,
Delegation 3). Source-affinity disambiguation (`source_affinity_tokens`) scored
by token overlap of query vs filename+head_text, but its stopword list only
drops legal-structure words (rule/section/article) — generic English
(under/use/method/conditions) survives and polluted the vocab, so the Secretariat
Manual's "Rule 16 — Steno Typist" won (overlap > 0 → scope-guard fallthrough
never fired) even when the query said "sppra". The correct SPPRA Rule 16 never
entered the pool because hybrid was short-circuited.
**Fix:** per architect — one retrieval path for every query. New gate
`citation_fast_path_enabled()` (`ECHO_CITATION_FAST_PATH`, default OFF) in
`services/query_router.rs`; the call site (`answer`/retrieval, ~line 640) now
forces `citation_ids = None` unless the flag is set. All queries fall through to
hybrid-union (`ECHO_HYBRID=union`, cosine-first) which already answers general
SPPRA questions correctly (trace record 6). Legacy behaviour recoverable via the
env flag.
**Scope/follow-ups:** also disables the chapter-index enumeration fast-path
(`detect_chapter_index_citation`) — acceptable per single-path directive; revisit
if "list all articles in chapter N" enumeration regresses. Reranker still gated
by `ECHO_RERANK`; enabling it would further sharpen the now-unified pool. No DB
or migration change. Requires rebuild+deploy on VM (auto-deploy on push to
`release`).

## 2026-07-02 — SPPRA nesting: L6 roman items + sequence disambiguation

**Why:** SPPRA evidence (PDF census + live DB): romans nested inside alpha
sub-clauses (`Rule 16(1)(a)(ii)`, `Rule 2(1)(l)(i)–(iv)`) were flattened —
`(i)/(v)/(x)` matched the single-alpha SubClause pattern and persisted as
SIBLINGS with colliding paths (`(1)/(i)` ×4, parent lost); `(ii)+` and the
`(aa)–(hh)` doubled definition run were absorbed into the previous chunk.
**Change:** (1) `NodeLevel::Item = 6` (structure_parser) — persists as
`unit_type='subclause'` (PG CHECK unchanged); depth lives in `unit_path`
(`Rule_16/(1)/(a)/(ii)`); `resolve_bare_citations` chains the citation
automatically ("Rule 16(1)(a)(ii)"). (2) rules-profile patterns: alpha
`[a-z]{1,2}` (catches `(aa)–(hh)`) + roman Item pattern (i–xv). (3) NEW
`regex_pass::resolve_ambiguous_sub_markers` — `(i)` after `(h)` = alpha run
continuing; `(i)` under `(l)` = roman list opener; `(ii)` after `(hh)` =
doubled alpha; stray `(v)/(x)` keep the legacy alpha reading; roman-run
continuation wins over alpha. Offset-dedup keeps the deeper reading, resolver
demotes contextually. CAPS `(A)–(E)` (5 instances) stay in-leaf under their
roman. Coalescer safe (romans 200–450c > MIN 120). Tests:
`nesting_tests::{roman_items_nest…, ninth_alpha…}` (e2e tree) +
`regex_pass::tests::{ambiguous_markers…, stray_v…, alpha_and_roman…}`.
**Scope:** rules profile only (act/manual/generic unchanged — same bug exists
there; extend when those docs are re-indexed). User re-indexes SPPRA via
browser to apply.
