## 2026-07-02 — Carry-over noise fix (generic-legal boilerplate blocklist)

**Why:** the follow-up "who has power to approve this note" carried over `Draft,
Chief, Secretary, note` (Step 3 keyword carry-over), dragging clerical
draft-signing chunks (Rule 79/93/187) into retrieval and steering the answer to
"who signs the office draft" instead of "who has procurement approval authority"
(grounding 0.21). `extract_carryover_keywords` prioritises capitalised "proper"
tokens, so generic gov titles ranked as if they were entities. **Change:** added a
`GENERIC` blocklist (roles/titles, jurisdiction, doc-structure/correspondence
boilerplate) filtered alongside STOPWORDS in `extract_carryover_keywords` — only
distinctive topic terms (Canon, e-Daftar, SPPRA, BS-19, dates, places) carry over.
Dashed/alnum tokens (e.g. `ex-pakistan`) are exempt. Test
`carryover_drops_generic_legal_boilerplate`. Domain-topical words (procurement,
leave, approval, contracting) intentionally NOT blocked.

## 2026-07-02 — Hybrid Union: vector-cosine-first ordering (citation + relevance)

**Why:** live traces (union active) showed two coupled defects: (1) the model
defaults to citing `[1]`, so with union's unranked interleave the best chunk wasn't
at `[1]` → mis-citations (Rule 16(1)(b) cited as `[1]`=Rule 14/17); (2) union with
no ranking flooded context with FTS keyword-noise (addressee lists, clerical
draft-signing rules) → the model answered "how to sign a draft" instead of "who has
financial authority to approve", grounding 0.20. **Change:** `union_merge` now
orders **all vector hits first (cosine-descending, so best semantic match → `[1]`),
then FTS-only hits appended** (was: vec/fts interleave). Recall unchanged (FTS-only
still included); dedup + caps unchanged. Fixes citation-default + demotes keyword
noise in one deterministic, no-model change. Test updated. Deferred if insufficient:
citation re-anchor (map each prose ref to the chunk that contains it) and/or reranker.

## 2026-07-01 — Citation gate: env-gate + disable (over-strips correct refs)

**Why:** live trace evidence — the citation gate (`assistant/citation_gate.rs`,
applied in `assemble_response`) deleted correct, grounded sentences from the UI
answer while the pre-gate trace answer was right. Root cause: `normalize()`
collapses whitespace/hyphens but NOT the space before a parenthesis, so the model's
compact `Rule 11(1)` / `Rule 16(1)(b)` never matches the source's `Rule 11 (1)` /
`Rule 16 (1) … (b)`; compound sub-clause refs are also non-contiguous in source and
can never match. Result: false-positive "Could not find X" flags + whole sentences
stripped (SPPRA direct-contracting answer gutted). **Change:** `citation_gate_enabled()`
env flag (`ECHO_CITATION_GATE`, default ON); `assemble_response` skips
`redact_ungrounded` when `ECHO_CITATION_GATE=0`, shipping the full answer with no
flags. **Activated on VM:** `.env` `ECHO_CITATION_GATE=0`. Proper fix (deferred):
normalize space-around-parens + verify base provision, not the full compound ref.

## 2026-07-01 — Noviq Hybrid Union: flag-gated alternative to RRF fusion (experiment)

**Why:** the June Rule 16 audit showed RRF *demotes* a chunk strong in one modality
but absent from the other (Rule 16 = vector rank 3, FTS-absent → demoted → falls
past the greedy budget cutoff). Live DB evidence this session: chunks are now small
(mean ~74 est-tok, p90 ~141, max 1636; 91.5% ≤150 tok), so a union of top-20 vec +
top-20 fts (~35 unique after id-dedup, ~2.6k tok) fits the ~5.4k evidence budget
easily — union is now practical where it wasn't when chunks were ~2.8k tok.
**Change (flag-gated, RRF stays default):** new `hybrid_union_enabled()`
(`ECHO_HYBRID=union`) + `union_merge(fts, vec, fts_k, vec_k)` in `query_router.rs`
— deduped UNION (by chunk_id), vec-first interleave, per-list depth = ECHO_VEC_K /
ECHO_FTS_K. Wired at both hybrid merge sites (main `:753`, retry `:1345`). Same
chunk in both lists kept once; near-identical text from different docs intentionally
kept (per design decision). Unit test `union_merge_dedups_interleaves_and_caps`.
Downstream salience/entity boosts + `build_context` (ctx_top_k + token budget) are
unchanged — to isolate the union variable, also set ECHO_SALIENT_BOOST=1.0 /
ECHO_DEFINITIONAL_BOOST=1.0 / ECHO_ENTITY_BOOST=1.0. **Activate on VM:** `.env`
`ECHO_HYBRID=union`, `ECHO_VEC_K=20`, `ECHO_FTS_K=20`, restart. A/B vs RRF on the
32-Q set. Related open finding: the `ctx_top_k = ctx_budget/150` heuristic assumes
150 tok/chunk but live mean is ~74, so RRF path under-fills the window to ~49%.

## 2026-07-01 — One-click GPU re-embed (admin button) + hide global folder from non-admin Settings

Two changes, both server-deployed (VM CUDA build via push→poll-timer).

### Admin "GPU re-embed corpus" button
**Why:** admin browser-indexing embeds on CPU (~32 min/corpus); the GPU path is
~50× faster on the embed step but was SSH-only. Proven this session: GPU embed =
3.6s/529 chunks vs 182s CPU (`METRIC embed_done_ms`), `Successfully registered
CUDAExecutionProvider`. Full reindex stays CPU-extraction-bound (pdftotext/
pdfplumber) — GPU only accelerates embed (+ OCR-of-scans, not wired).
**Fix:** `api/admin.rs::gpu_reindex` (AdminUser-gated) drops a trigger sentinel
`{NOVIQ_DATA_DIR}/GPU_REINDEX_REQUESTED` (refuses 200 `ok:false` if `DEPLOYING`
banner already up); route `POST /api/admin/gpu_reindex` (`api/router.rs`);
frontend button + confirm in `pages/Admin.tsx`. Orchestration runs OUT of process
(it restarts noviq-server, so it can't run inline): VM `/opt/noviq/gpu-reindex.sh`
(self-healing `trap` restore: stop vLLM → set `ORT_DYLIB_PATH` in `.env` to the
GLIBC-2.27 spike GPU lib + `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` drop-in → restart → reindex 11 admin
sources → restore CPU+vLLM) launched by systemd `noviq-gpu-reindex.path` (watches
the sentinel) → `noviq-gpu-reindex.service` (`Type=oneshot`, `TimeoutStartSec=
infinity`). **Gotcha proven:** `ORT_DYLIB_PATH` MUST be in `.env` (app force-loads
`.env`, clobbering a systemd drop-in `Environment=`); only `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` goes
in the drop-in. The `Embedding model ready (gpu=true)` log echoes the env flag, not
real EP success — verify via ort's `Successfully registered CUDAExecutionProvider`.

### Hide the global admin folder from non-admin Settings
**Why:** admin-indexed folders are `owner_id NULL` (global); `folders::
list_for_owner` returned `owner_id = $1 OR owner_id IS NULL`, so every regular user
saw the admin corpus folder in Settings **with a delete button** (revoke was already
403-guarded server-side, but the UI still showed it — confusing + wrong).
**Fix:** `db/repositories/folders.rs::list_for_owner` now `WHERE owner_id = $1`
only. Non-admins see just their own folders; the corpus is still fully searchable in
chat (retrieval is whole-corpus). Admins keep the full list via `list()`.

## 2026-07-01 — Chunking audit follow-ups: RC-H de-hyphenation, RC-F footnote anchoring, RC-E table-row citability

Three deferred defects from `docs/chunking-audit-2026-06-29.md`, each a small,
deterministic, unit-tested fix. (RC-C was already resolved; RC-PG/A/B/D shipped
earlier.) RC-T and LG-Act page overshoot are NOT included — they need live-data
reproduction on the VM (RC-T also rebuilds the frozen sidecar binary and its
merged-cell fill risks inventing cell values, against the verbatim contract).

### RC-H — complete de-hyphenation (`text_normalizer.rs`)
`hyphen_join` was `[a-z]-\n[a-z]` — it required the newline immediately after the
hyphen and a letter immediately after the newline, so it missed the ~150 residual
line-break hyphens (constitution 42, Compendium 43, RoB 16) where the PDF
continuation line is indented or the hyphen carries a trailing space. Broadened to
`[a-z]-[ \t]*\n[ \t]*[a-z]`. Also extended `repair_spaced_words` to rejoin a
same-line break-hyphen (`Govern- ment` ×14 in Delegation, no newline for the regex
to see) — dictionary-gated on `JOIN_TARGETS`, so a real compound ("Director-General")
is never fused.

### RC-F — footnote → clause anchoring (`structured_importer.rs`)
`anchor_citation_for_page` returned `None` whenever a page held >1 distinct
provision (the common case), so most of 600+ footnotes never produced an
`amendment_event`. Added `footnote_marker` (leading ordinal, tolerant of a `[`
opener) + `anchor_citation_for_footnote`: keeps the conservative single-provision
fast path, and on an ambiguous page rescues a precise anchor by matching the
footnote's marker digit to the in-body amendment marker (`N[` / `]N`), anchoring
only when exactly one same-page provision carries it (refuse-or-flag otherwise).

### RC-E — table-row citability (`structured_importer.rs`)
Delegation 57% / APT 58% of table rows were `label_status='unresolved'` because
the tree-level `resolve_bare_citations` only qualifies against `named_provision`
(`keyword<space>ordinal`), missing a table hung off `SCHEDULE-I` / `ANNEXURE-A` /
a descriptive title. New `nearest_named_ancestor` walks `parent_chunk_id` to the
first non-bare ancestor (skipping the filename-titled `unit_type='document'` root
so a row never cites the PDF filename); a tagged row with a bare/absent label is
relabelled `"<ancestor> — <serial>"` + `label_status='resolved'`. Never invents —
a row with no meaningful ancestor stays unresolved.

## 2026-07-01 — Oversize chunks: recursive split_long_text + size-cap front/back-matter persist

### Symptom (still-big chunks after RC-D + re-index)
Operator re-removed all docs and re-indexed several times, yet the live corpus
still held 35k–42k-char chunks. RC-D (`79070306`) did **not** solve it — two
distinct leaks survived, both diagnosed live on the GPU VM (2026-06-30):
- **A — persist paths bypass the splitter.** Front/back-matter blocks are
  persisted OUTSIDE the DocNode tree (`persist_front_matter_chunks` /
  `persist_back_matter_chunks` in `structured_importer.rs`), inserting
  `b.content` WHOLE — never routed through `finalize_tree`/`split_oversized_leaves`.
  Offenders: constitution TOC `front_matter`=42,658c; schedules
  `back_matter`=17,708/10,504c.
- **B — `split_long_text` didn't enforce its threshold on pieces.** Branches
  0/1/2 (clause-marker / paragraph / sentence) returned pieces AS-IS; only the
  final char-cut (branch 3) honoured the limit. A body with ≥2 paragraphs where
  ONE paragraph was itself 35k (OCR run / list, no internal `\n\n` or sentence
  break) shipped that 35k piece whole. Proof: Manual `Section_30/p1` = 35,604c
  `provision` (the `/p1` shows it went through the splitter). Table-row 27k and
  RC-D container splits inherited the same leak (they call `split_long_text`).

### Fix
- **`structure_parser.rs::split_long_text`** — new nested `enforce()` recursively
  re-splits any returned piece still over `threshold` (each recursion operates on
  a strictly smaller slice and bottoms out at the char-cut, so it always
  terminates with pieces ≤ `threshold`). Applied to the marker, paragraph, and
  sentence branches.
- **`structure_parser.rs::split_block_for_persist`** (new `pub(crate)`) — applies
  the tree's oversize policy to a standalone block body: ≤ `oversize_hard_ceiling()`
  (8000c) kept whole; above it, `split_long_text(_, long_chunk_threshold())` into
  ≤1500c pieces.
- **`structured_importer.rs`** — `persist_front_matter_chunks` /
  `persist_back_matter_chunks` now expand each block through
  `split_block_for_persist` before insert, with a running `chunk_index`. Returned
  counts already feed the next `start_index`, so downstream indexing stays
  consistent. `block_class` / `section_kind` / `unit_label` unchanged (kept
  retrievable). TOC/schedules split-and-kept rather than excluded.

### Tests
- `split_long_text_enforces_threshold_on_giant_paragraph`,
  `split_block_for_persist_splits_above_ceiling_keeps_small_whole`.

### Still open (deferred)
Re-index the corpus on the GPU VM to clear the stale oversize rows. Constitution
TOC is split-and-kept for now; whether to instead mark it boilerplate/exclude is
an orthogonal call for the operator. RC-E/RC-T/RC-H/RC-F from the 2026-06-29 audit
remain.

## 2026-06-30 — Chunking RC-D: oversized container split + drop empty/label-only chunks

### Symptom (from live-DB chunk audit)
Operator inspected the live corpus and found defects the codebase thought were
solved: (a) 40k+ char chunks shipping whole (35,604c Manual, 42,866c constitution
per `docs/chunking-audit-2026-06-29.md` H2/RC-D); (b) huge empty chunks and chunks
whose only content is a bare provision number ("Rule 2" body == "2"); (c)
coalescing not absorbing these. Most heading/page/label defects were a **stale
live DB** (predates the 2026-06-29 RC-A/RC-B/RC-C/RC-PG fixes — VM re-index clears
them), but RC-D + the empty/label-only scraps were **genuinely open in code**.

### Fix (`src-tauri/src/services/structure_parser.rs`)
- **RC-D oversize containers** — `split_oversized_leaves` early-returned for
  `Document|Part|Chapter` so a table/absorbed-provision body hung off a container
  shipped as one uncitable 40k chunk. Now it returns only when the body is ≤
  `oversize_hard_ceiling()` (new helper, default 8000c, `ECHO_OVERSIZE_CEILING`);
  above that it falls through to `split_long_text(text, long_chunk_threshold())`,
  producing context-sized **≤1500c** `… part N` pieces. Normal short child-indexes
  (≤ ceiling) untouched — Fix-B invariant preserved.
- **Empty / label-only leaves** — new `is_empty_or_label_only_leaf` + a `.filter`
  in `coalesce_undersized_leaves` drops blank/whitespace-only leaves and pure
  label-echo leaves (text == normalized label, ≤8 alnum chars) before merging.
  Conservative: real short clauses (text beyond their number) are kept.

### Context-window note
RC-D pieces are capped at `long_chunk_threshold()` (1500c ≈ 375 tok), and the
split→coalesce ordering in `finalize_tree` re-merges any tiny sentence fragments
back up to `hard_max` (1500c). Net: no 40k blobs, no scraps — TOP_K stays
context-sized.

### Tests
- `coalesce_drops_empty_and_label_only_leaves`,
  `split_oversized_container_splits_pathological_body_but_keeps_short_index`.
- `cargo test --lib structure_parser::` → **29/29 passed**.

### Still open (deferred — need live rows / sidecar, not rushed under budget)
RC-E (table-row citability), RC-T (page-spanning table headers / merged cells),
RC-H (hyphenation), RC-F (footnote→clause anchoring). The "two garbage chunks
where size/unit_label/page hold content" need the actual rows to diagnose. **And:
re-index the corpus on the GPU VM** to clear all the stale RC-A/B/C/PG defects.

## 2026-06-29 — Retrieval forensic audit: SPPRA Rule 16 "Direct Contracting" miss (root-caused, live DB)

### Why Rule 16 never reaches the LLM — answered against the live `echo` PG + trace
**Symptom:** the test draft query ("…direct contracting with the sole distributor of
Canon scanners…") returns Rule 17/55/Delegation/Manual; **Rule 16 absent**. Filled
the `docs/retrieval-audit-2026-06-29.md` questionnaire end-to-end (no code change —
diagnosis only).
**Finding (evidence in the doc):** Rule 16(1)(b) "Direct Contracting" (`0bb1e977`,
255 chars) **IS retrieved — vector rank 3 of 72** (exact KNN; the HNSW index is
unused — it's on `halfvec_cosine_ops` but the query uses `<=> $::vector`). It dies
**downstream of retrieval**:
- **RC-1 (Critical, ~65%):** `build_context_pass` (`query_router.rs:3524-3535`)
  token-budget starvation. One Delegation table chunk `f53c2c6d` = 11,313 chars ≈
  2,848 tok = **53% of the ~5,412-tok budget**; five oversized chunks exhaust it,
  leaving ~5 tok, so the 83-tok Direct-Contracting chunk hits the `continue` at
  `:3533` and is skipped. Only **5 chunks** reach the LLM (trace `ee0615b7` STEP 10).
  The F015 per-chunk-cap removal is what lets one table monopolize the budget.
- **RC-2 (High, ~25%):** `rrf_merge` demotes the FTS-absent vector-only chunk
  (RRF 1/63=0.0159) below both-list chunks (Delegation 0.0269) and vec-rank-1
  Rule 17 (0.0164) → lands RRF ~pos 6-8, behind the budget-fillers.
- **RC-3/RC-4 (Medium):** no legal-synonym expansion ("sole distributor"↛"single
  source"; FTS ranks it 177/1494) + provision fragmentation (Rule 16 = 7-tok heading
  shell + 12 tiny sub-clauses).
**Template hypotheses:** OBS-1 (pool cutoff) **REFUTED** (rank 3); OBS-2 (AND-FTS)
**REFUTED** — `fts5_retrieve:1671` OR-joins tokens → 1,494 matches, not 0; OBS-3
(scores discarded, 5-tuple return) **CONFIRMED**; OBS-4 (`:715` stale "sqlite-vec
ANN" label vs pgvector `<=>`) **CONFIRMED**.
**Fix order (Phase 17, not yet applied):** per-chunk budget cap (`:3524-3535`) →
split oversized table chunks at ingestion → RRF recall-guarantee slot for top-N
vector → procurement synonym expansion → score instrumentation (Retrieval Debugger)
+ fix the `:715` label. SPPRA source id is now `c41e3209-…` (re-indexed; memory's
`9e43e5ac` stale). Live PG port ephemeral (was 46233); trace dir
`ECHO_LOG_DIR=/opt/noviq/echoAI/logs/ab_rerank`.

## 2026-06-29 — Chunking audit fixes: page-number realignment (RC-PG) + heading detection for `(i)`/`[` openers (RC-A)

**Why:** Forensic chunking audit of the live 11-doc corpus (`docs/chunking-audit-2026-06-29.md`)
found two broad defects:
- **RC-PG — every document's `page_number` is wrong**, compressed and worsening
  with depth (SPPRA Rule 17 real p13 → stored p5; Rule 50 p35 → p14; SPSC Reg 100
  p59 → p26). Root cause: `structured_importer::import` runs `text_normalizer::normalize`
  (collapses 3+ space gutters, blank-line runs, leading tabs — legal `-layout` PDFs
  are mostly gutter padding) and THEN strips chrome using the caller's
  `page_offsets`, which are byte offsets into the **raw** (pre-normalize) text. The
  shorter normalized text makes every byte-start point too far ahead → each
  provision stamps to an earlier page, error accumulating with depth. Verified the
  page map entering the chain is correct (pdfplumber reports the right pages) — the
  drift is purely the normalize/offset mismatch.
- **RC-A — heading detector misses provisions whose line doesn't start `N. <Capital>`.**
  The bare-number patterns require `[A-Z]` right after `N. `, and the `N. (sub)`
  patterns only accept numeric `(1)`. So: (a) amendment-INSERTED rules whose bracket
  precedes the number (`[18. Response Time …]` — SPPRA Rules 18, 32) and (b) provisions
  whose body opens with a roman/alpha sub-marker (`3. (i) There shall be …` — Sindh
  Rules of Business Rules 3-8/13/14/…) were never detected and were absorbed verbatim
  into the preceding provision.

**Change (smallest-diff):**
- `parsers/pdf.rs` — `pdftotext_page_offsets` made `pub(crate)`.
- `services/structured_importer.rs` — `import` re-derives `page_offsets` from the
  **normalized** body via `pdftotext_page_offsets` when it contains form feeds
  (normalize preserves `\x0c`); single-page/`.txt` bodies keep the caller's offsets.
  New test `page_offsets_realigned_after_normalize_no_compression` (gutter-padded
  3-page fixture; Rule 3 must stamp p3 — fails pre-fix).
- `doc_profiles/{rules,manual,act}.rs` — bare-number + `N. (sub)` heading patterns
  gain an optional leading `\[?\s*` (amendment-bracket openers) and the `(sub)`
  patterns accept roman `(i)`/alpha `(a)` in addition to numeric `(1)`. `manual`
  also gains a dedicated `N. (sub)` opener pattern (it had none).
- `heading_detector/regex_pass.rs` — tests `amendment_bracket_inserted_rule_detected_rc_a`
  and `bare_number_with_paren_sub_opener_detected_rc_a`.

**Cross-cutting / follow-ups:** Requires a **re-index** of the corpus on the VM
(GPU embed) for the fixes to take effect in the DB, then re-run the audit scripts
to confirm the page map and the absorbed provisions are recovered. Still OPEN from
the audit: RC-B (constitution Articles 55–76 missing — needs separate root-cause),
RC-C (RoB duplicate `Section 30/31/32` from schedule renumber), RC-D (oversized
35k/42k chunks), RC-E (uncitable table rows), RC-F (footnote→amendment anchoring),
RC-T (spanning-table header misattribution + 40-54% empty cells), RC-H (residual
hyphenation). `printed_page` vs `pdf_page` distinction (audit §6) not yet added —
current fix makes `page_number` the correct PDF sheet index. KNOWN minor edge
(separate from the gross compression this fixes): a provision sitting exactly on a
page top — only a form feed/whitespace before it — still binds ±1 page early
because the heading regex's `^\s*` consumes the leading form feed; real pages carry
a running header between the break and the first provision, so impact is small.

## 2026-06-29 — Ingestion: pdfplumber promoted to PRIMARY text+table extractor (pdftotext → fallback)

**Why:** `pdftotext -layout` mis-shapes some pages (column interleave, scrambled
table bands) → poor chunks. pdfplumber reads layout-preserving page text AND
returns structured table *cells*, so it both reads prose better and linearises
ruled tables. The pdfplumber sidecar already existed (Phase 9a) but was used
**only for tables**; pdftotext was still primary for text.

**Change (smallest-diff, reuses the proven table reflow):**
- `sidecars/ingestion-sidecar/ingestion_sidecar.py` — new `extract_document` op:
  per 1-based page returns full `text` (`extract_text(layout=True)`, flow-extract
  fallback) + the same `above/below/tables` band the tables op emits.
- `parsers/table_sidecar.rs` — `extract_document()` client: assembles the
  form-feed-joined page layout (matches the `pdftotext -layout` page convention)
  and runs `table::reflow_with_sidecar` to linearise tables in place → returns
  `(text, reconstructed_rows)`. `None` ⇒ unavailable/failed/no-text ⇒ fall back.
- `parsers/pdf.rs` — **Tier 0** = pdfplumber (quality-gated by `score()`); a
  `Good` result wins, anything weaker or a missing/failed sidecar falls through to
  Tier 1 pdftotext, then lopdf, then OCR. Toggle `ECHO_PDFPLUMBER_PRIMARY=0`.
  Sets `extraction_method`/`reconstruction_method = "pdfplumber"`.

**Graceful degradation:** if the server runs the new code against an OLD sidecar
binary (no `extract_document` op), the sidecar returns `{ok:false}` → Rust falls
back to pdftotext. So deploy order is safe.

**Build/deploy steps (VM):** (1) `sidecars/ingestion-sidecar/build.sh` rebuilds
the frozen PyInstaller binary (its own pinned pdfplumber 0.11.5 venv) →
`src-tauri/binaries/ingestion-sidecar-<triple>` (already the `ECHO_INGESTION_SIDECAR`
path). (2) rebuild server. (3) re-ingest corpus (~32 min). (4) A/B + chunk export
diff. **Validate the op on ONE PDF before the full re-ingest.**

## 2026-06-29 — Fix: "View latest trace" 404 on the headless/browser build

**Symptom:** browser "View latest trace" (Settings) → "read failed api error".

**Root cause:** `read_latest_query_trace` (+ the `download_*_query_trace*` helpers)

no route → 404 → the UI's "read failed". Not caused by any recent change; latent gap
since F014.

`resolve_log_dir(&None)` returns early on `ECHO_LOG_DIR`, so no AppHandle needed) and
registered `POST /api/read_latest_query_trace`. Returns `[filename, body]` matching the
frontend's `[string, string]`; empty pair when no trace exists yet. Backend-only.

**Trace downloads (web) — added same day:** the three download buttons
(`Download latest/all/recent`) were also desktop-only — they get a `dest` from the
Tauri `save()` dialog, which throws in the browser → "Download failed". Added GET
endpoints `/api/traces/latest`, `/api/traces/all`, `/api/traces/recent?limit=N`
(`api/system.rs`, concatenation format mirrors the desktop commands) and branched the
`SettingsPage` handlers on `isTauri()`: web now streams via `transport.downloadAuthed`
(authed fetch → blob), desktop keeps the save-dialog path. Frontend + backend change.

## 2026-06-29 — Fix: bare-"must" misroute to whole-corpus ActionItems map-reduce (5 eval timeouts)

**Symptom:** 5 of 30 eval questions (Q01/Q04/Q16/Q19/Q30) timed out on **both**
engines — `<ERR timed out>` at exactly the client ceiling (60s vLLM run / 200s
llama.cpp run). Engine-independent + client-side cutoff ⇒ the *server* was running
far longer than a single generation. The 26 that passed all recorded
`capability=guidance`; the 5 had a blank capability (no response ⇒ nothing recorded).

**Root cause (deterministic, pre-existing — predates F017):** the `ActionItems`
classifier cue (`intent_router/classifier.rs:52`, weight 1.0) listed `musts?|shall do`
as standalone alternatives. A bare "must" appears in countless ordinary factual
questions ("must it go higher", "must be advertised", "members must be present").
Match ⇒ `Intent::ActionItems` ⇒ `Capability::ActionItems` ⇒ `is_map_reduce()` ⇒
`run_mapreduce_capability` fans out **one LLM call per window-sized batch over every
in-scope provision** (~8,425-chunk corpus ⇒ dozens–hundreds of sequential
generations) ⇒ runs until the client disconnects. Perfect 1:1 correlation: the cue
fires on exactly the 5 timeout questions and on none of the 26 that passed (all 5
contain "must"; none of the others do). The F017 chunker change only widened the gap
(bigger chunks ⇒ slower per-pass) — it did not cause this.

**Fix:**
- `services/intent_router/classifier.rs` — removed `musts?|shall do` from the
  ActionItems cue. The `what (must|should) i do` / `what (must|should) the
  (officer|secretary|director|department)` phrasal forms remain and still capture
  genuine action-extraction requests. Validated: 0 ActionItems hits across all 30
  eval Qs; the 3 genuine action-item phrasings still match.
- `services/assistant/intent.rs` — regression test `bare_must_does_not_trigger_
  actionitems_mapreduce` pins all 5 questions to `Capability::Guidance` (and asserts
  `!is_map_reduce()`); `genuine_action_item_requests_still_route_to_actionitems`
  guards the other direction.
- `services/assistant/mapreduce.rs` — **defense-in-depth backstop** (the classifier
  is the real cure): bound the map phase by `NOVIQ_MAPREDUCE_MAX_BATCHES` (default
  64) AND `NOVIQ_MAPREDUCE_BUDGET_SECS` (default 600). On cap, stop mapping, reduce
  the partial extracts, and append a coverage note — graceful degradation instead of
  a hang. Defaults are generous enough for a legitimate single-document summary.

**Follow-ups:** (1) Rust not buildable on Windows — `cargo test -p <crate>
services::assistant::intent` + `intent_router::classifier` must run on the VM.
(2) Re-run the A/B; the 5 should now answer (quality of those answers is a separate
question — they are hard boundary/refusal/conflict items). (3) The map-reduce cap
defaults are untuned; revisit if a legitimate large scoped summary ever truncates.

## 2026-06-29 — Ingestion overhaul — chunker over-segmentation fix + Mistral path removed (single deterministic path)

**Why:** A documents-grounded audit of the legal-RAG answers traced wrong/conflated
answers (e.g. Q02 "who approves Rs 10,000M" → answered *ECNEC*, should be *CDWP*) to
the **chunker**, not retrieval. Two defects: (1) `structure_parser::split_long_text`
treated `.`+whitespace as a sentence boundary, so **"…costing upto Rs. 10,000 million"
was severed** into "…Rs." | "10,000 million…" — the operative figure landed in a chunk
that didn't co-retrieve with its subject (CDWP §2.6 → ECNEC rule, DB chunks 62/63);
(2) `ECHO_LONG_CHUNK_THRESHOLD` **defaulted to 500 chars**, shredding ordinary provisions
into 3-4 fragments. Corpus-wide: 26% of chunks were ≤3 tokens. NOTE: tables (pdfplumber
sidecar) and boilerplate (`is_boilerplate` filtered at retrieval) were NOT the problem —
verified via `reconstruction_method='pdfplumber'` on table chunks + the retrieval filter.

**Fix (chunker — `src-tauri/src/services/structure_parser.rs`):**
- **Fix A** — `split_long_text` sentence splitter is now abbreviation/number-aware: never
  breaks at `.` when the next non-space char is a DIGIT (covers "Rs. 10,000"), or after a
  known abbreviation (`Rs/No/Sec/Art/Annex/i.e/e.g/viz/vs…`) via new `ends_with_abbreviation`.
  Regression test `split_keeps_currency_figure_with_lead_in`.
- **Fix B** (baked into defaults = future-proof for any upload, not just server `.env`):
  `long_chunk_threshold` 500→**1500** (whole provision stays one chunk), `coalesce_params`
  target 600→900 / hard_max 800→**1500**; `MIN` kept 120 (no SC-005 regression). Updated the
  one test whose fixture assumed the 500 ceiling.

**Mistral/doc_ir removal (single ingestion path):** one-ask drafting (F010) + template
ingestion (F009) are RETIRED (F015 T030 — `commands/{drafting,one_ask}` already undeclared/
dormant), and the LLM-IR ingestion branch was `#[cfg(desktop)]` (never in the headless
server). So the Mistral GGUF was dead weight. Removed from compilation:
- `services/mod.rs` (`pub mod doc_ir` commented), `commands/mod.rs` (`importer`),
  `db/repositories/mod.rs` (`ir_cache`), `services/indexer.rs` (Feature-006 deep-tier block),
  `services/legal_ir/mod.rs` (dead `doc_ir` re-exports), `commands/system.rs` (Mistral
  `ModelSpec` + `discover_ir_builder_gguf` branch), `lib.rs` (`importer::cancel_import`).
  doc_ir/importer/drafting/one_ask source files left dormant on disk per the additive policy.

  `NOVIQ_VLLM_MAX_MODEL_LEN` by *its* token estimate; vLLM enforces with the *exact* Qwen tokenizer;
  the few-hundred-token mismatch overflowed a zero-margin 8192 window → 400 on 5 large-context Qs.
  Fix: `run-vllm.sh` now serves `MAX_LEN + NOVIQ_VLLM_LEN_HEADROOM` (default 2048). Follow-up: clamp
  `max_tokens` vs real prompt count in `vllm.rs`.

  / p95 28.6s / 20.9 req/min (1.58×, FAILS SC-003); util 0.80: p50 15.0s / p95 25.8s. Correlated
  sampling: vLLM admits only **4→6** concurrent (GPU 95–98%), processing in waves. **KV is NOT the
  limit** (6 short reqs = 3,900 of ~39,000 KV tokens); the ceiling is **vGPU compute / vLLM prefill
  scheduling** on the time-sliced slice. Embedder serializes via a global Mutex but is **CPU** (default
  fastembed EP) and ~0.2s — secondary. Engine-only hit 10-in-8s only because the server was stopped
  (whole slice + util 0.88). **SC-002 (p95 ≤ 10s) not met co-resident.** Next: tune vLLM
  `max_num_batched_tokens`/chunked-prefill; quantify the vGPU floor; then decide cutover vs. renegotiate
  the target. Rollback stays one env flip.

## 2026-06-28 — Chat UI: fix "reopened chat is empty", drop top settings/“model not loaded”, split rail scroll windows

**Symptom/why (3 issues reported on the deployed chat tab):**
1. **Reopening a past chat showed nothing** — the conversation appeared in the history
   list but its transcript was blank. Root cause: each assistant `Turn` persisted the full
   `TurnResponse`, including every citation's `verbatim` (full quoted legal passages). Long
   legal sessions bloat `localStorage` past its ~5 MB quota → `saveTurns` hits its silent
   `catch` and the transcript never persists, while the tiny conversation-meta list (a few
   strings) still saves — hence "listed but empty".
2. The top bar showed a **model-settings gear** and an alarming **"model not loaded"** text.
3. The left rail's **Chats** list (`max-h-56`) and **Files** (DocumentTree) weren't balanced
   dedicated windows; a long chat history could obscure the indexed-documents section.

**Fix (`src/pages/ChatPage.tsx`):**
- `trimForStorage()` strips per-citation `verbatim` before `saveTurns` (citations still render
  n/instrument/path/page; verbatim only feeds the right-rail blurb + clipboard of the *live*
  session, so losing it on a reopened chat is harmless). Slashes the persisted payload so the
  quota is no longer hit.
- Persistence effect switched to `createEffect(on(turns, …))` so merely *switching*
  conversations can never re-save with stale turns (defensive against any non-batched clobber).
- Removed the top-bar settings gear; replaced the "model not loaded" fallback with a neutral
  `context window —` `Stat` (kept the context-window readout for development/state visibility).
- Left rail: **Chats** and **Files** are each now a `flex-1 min-h-0 flex flex-col` with an
  internal `overflow-auto` body and a fixed header → two equal, independently-scrolling
  windows that never overlap; the indexed-documents section is always visible.

**Verification:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (exit 0). Behavioural check (reopen a long chat,
confirm transcript restored) to be done on the deployed build. **Deploy:** lands only when the
branch reaches `release` (poll-timer rebuilds `src/` → dist). Currently committed on
`016-vllm-serving`.

## 2026-06-27 — Perf — Qwen3 no-think switch (`NOVIQ_NO_THINK`) + audit of default-off knobs

**Why:** Qwen3-8B lookup latency on the A40 was ~14 s vs ~4–6 s for Mistral-7B.
Root cause is Qwen3's **thinking mode is ON by default** — the model generates a
`<think>…</think>` reasoning chain on every turn. The streaming filter in `llm.rs`
*discards* that text, but the model still spends the tokens (and wall-clock) to
produce it. Qwen3's official off-switch is the chat-template flag
`enable_thinking=false`, which simply pre-closes an empty `<think>\n\n</think>\n\n`
block right after the assistant tag. This codebase builds ChatML prompts by hand
(does not call `apply_chat_template`), so we reproduce that flag ourselves.

**Fix:** new `query_router::no_think_assistant_prefix()` returns
`"<think>\n\n</think>\n\n"` when env `NOVIQ_NO_THINK` ∈ {1,true,on,yes}, else `""`.
Appended after the final `<|im_start|>assistant\n` in **`build_rag_prompt`** (covers
main answer gen, retry, and both map-reduce passes which call it) and
**`build_judge_prompt`**. The empty block is *prompt* text (not generated) so it
never leaks into output. **Default OFF** — Mistral (current chat model) and any
reasoning-dependent flow are untouched; the operator sets `NOVIQ_NO_THINK=1` in the
VM `.env` when Qwen3 is the active model. This is the gated return of the old
unconditional `<think></think>` short-circuit that was removed (see 2026-06-… entry)
because it broke LFM2.5 — gating makes that regression opt-in.

**Audit of "is it off?" knobs (requested):**
- **Reranker** — OFF (hardcoded; `query_router.rs:814`, `ECHO_RERANK=1` to override).
- **Reviewer/judge** — OFF (`reviewer_enabled()` = `ECHO_REVIEWER=1`; default off).
- **NER Pass 2 (LLM)** — OFF (hard-disabled `indexer.rs:1009`; Pass 1 regex still runs). Index-time only, not a chat-latency factor.
- **Query cache** — ⚠️ **ON in release/production** (`query_cache_enabled()`: env unset → `!cfg!(debug_assertions)`; OFF only in debug). `ECHO_QUERY_CACHE=0` to force off. **Important for the Qwen3 re-test: use fresh/uncached queries or set `ECHO_QUERY_CACHE=0`, else repeated queries return cached answers and the latency number is meaningless** (the earlier T028 capture used fresh conversations for this reason).

**RESULT — DEPLOYED + Qwen3-8B is now the production chat model (2026-06-27).**
Pushed to `release` (commit `f0f8a6fe`), VM poll-deploy rebuilt the CUDA binary
(`deploying → ok`). Swapped active model Mistral → `Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M.gguf` via
`use-model.sh` (loads **37/37 layers on GPU**, all KV on CUDA0). Set
`NOVIQ_NO_THINK=1` (permanent) in the VM `.env`. Measured on the A40-12Q, fresh
uncached conversations (temporarily `ECHO_QUERY_CACHE=0`, since cache is ON in
release — see audit above; reverted after timing):
- **Qwen3-8B no-think: lookups 3.8 / 4.3 / 5.1 / 5.6 s (avg ~4.7 s)** — clean,
  `[n]`-cited, no `<think>` leak.
- vs **Qwen3-8B thinking-on baseline ~14 s** → **~3× faster**; now on par with
  Mistral (~4.3–6.6 s). **Decision (architect): keep Qwen3-8B, do NOT restore
  Mistral** (parked in `/opt/noviq/model-library/`).
- **Gotcha found mid-test:** the first swap-restart silently failed (`sudo -S … 2>/dev/null
  && echo` swallowed the error), so an initial timing run (9–17 s) hit a stale
  process with the old env / model. Re-restarted cleanly, verified `NOVIQ_NO_THINK=1`
  in `/proc/<pid>/environ`, then re-measured — hence the numbers above.

## 2026-06-27 — Perf — Topical "summarize …" mis-routed to whole-corpus map-reduce (7 min → ~6 s)

**Symptom:** chat queries containing "summarize/overview/…" took **7+ minutes**
(measured on the GPU VM: a single "Summarize the approval limits of the DDWP and
CDWP" turn = **428,643 ms** on Mistral; even worse on Qwen3-8B). Lookup queries
were fine (~6.6 s). Confirmed slow on **both** models — not model-specific.

**Root cause:** `assistant::intent::classify_capability` mapped *any*
`Intent::Summarize` to `Capability::SummarizeDoc`. `run_turn` then runs that
capability over `all_indexed_source_ids` (the **whole corpus**) via
`capabilities::run_mapreduce_capability` → `mapreduce::run`, which gathers **every
in-scope leaf provision** ("full coverage by construction") and does **one LLM pass
per window-sized batch**. On a large corpus + the A40-12Q vGPU that is ~12 full-window
context builds (32,768 cells / 4 GB KV each, ~25 s/build) per turn. A *topical*
question that merely contains "summarize" (no document named) was paying the
whole-corpus cost when the user wanted a targeted answer.

**Fix:** `intent.rs::classify_capability` — `Intent::Summarize` now routes to
`SummarizeDoc` **only** when the query names a document (`parse_document_scope`
non-empty) OR is an explicit broad/whole-corpus overview (new `is_broad_overview`
helper: "all documents", "entire corpus", "everything", "table of contents", …).
Otherwise → `Capability::Guidance` (fast hybrid RAG, ~6 s). Existing
`SummarizeDoc` cases (named instruments, e.g. "summarize the Sindh Local Government
Act 2013") are unchanged; added regression tests
(`topical_summary_without_document_scope_is_guidance`,
`broad_overview_still_maps_to_summarize_doc`).

**Impact/follow-ups:** Compare/Conflict/ActionItems still map-reduce the whole
corpus — same latency cliff if mis-triggered; they at least imply ≥2 docs. The
deeper structural fix (scope map-reduce to retrieved-relevant provisions, cap batch
count, and move inference to vLLM for the 10-concurrent-user requirement) is tracked
in `specs/014-server-thin-client/WINDOWS_CLAUDE_FOLLOWUPS.md` + the architecture
review. `gen_gate = Semaphore::new(1)` still serializes generation (≈3–4 concurrent
users at 4–6 s).

## 2026-06-27 — F014 — Admin-indexed docs are now global; remove dead server-path UI

**Request (architect):** documents an **admin** uploads/indexes from the browser
must be visible to **all** users; they were scoped to the admin's personal folder
(`/uploads/admin`) and invisible to regular users. Also remove the "server index
folder path" text input + (disabled) "Index server path" button next to Upload —
"neither for user nor admin"; and delete leftover test-corpus docs.

**Root cause:** `add_indexed_folder`/`upload_documents` set
`indexed_folders.owner_id = Some(uploader.id)` for everyone, and
`folders::list_for_owner` returned only `owner_id = $1` — so regular users never
saw admin-owned **or** global (NULL-owner) folders. Retrieval (`query_router`) is
NOT owner-scoped, so chat already used these docs; only the folder *list* hid them.

**Fix (3 code + 2 data):**
- `api/uploads.rs` + `api/documents.rs`: admin → `owner_id = None` (global = shared
  with everyone); regular user → `Some(user.id)` (private). NULL already means
  "global" in this schema (`folders::owner_of` comment).
- `db/repositories/folders.rs::list_for_owner`: `WHERE owner_id = $1 OR owner_id
  IS NULL` so users see their own + shared folders. Admins still see all via
  `list`. `can_manage_folder` unchanged → users can VIEW but not delete shared docs.
- `pages/SettingsPage.tsx`: removed the admin server-path input + button (and the
  now-dead `webFolderPath` signal + `handleAddFolderWeb`). Upload-folder stays.
- Live DB: `UPDATE indexed_folders SET owner_id=NULL WHERE owner_id=<admin>` (the
  11 existing admin docs); deleted the `testcorpus` folder via the
  `revoke_indexed_folder` admin API (proper cascade — chunks/embeddings/graph).

Verified on VM: `cargo check --no-default-features --features llm,server` + `tsc
--noEmit` both 0 errors. NOTE: deep-reindex stays a secondary/opt-in path — normal
indexing uses the simple tier first; do not force `deep_index_folder_source`.

`build.sh` pinned `pdfplumber==0.11.10`, which hard-requires
`pdfminer.six==20260107` — a version with no installable files on PyPI (latest is
20250324); 0.11.6+ are likewise unsatisfiable (==20250327 / 20251107 …). The
PyInstaller freeze failed at dependency resolution. Pinned `pdfplumber==0.11.5`
(`pdfminer.six==20231228`, published); table API unchanged for our extract_tables

## 2026-06-27 — F014 — Admin param-routes never matched: axum-0.8 `{id}` syntax on axum 0.7 (Task 3)

**Symptom:** the admin **Activity**/**Export** panels returned the SPA `index.html`
(HTTP 200) instead of JSON, and the unauth route-probe in WINDOWS_CLAUDE_FOLLOWUPS
§3 showed `activity`/`export` as 405 (read as "old binary"). **Root cause (real
bug, not deploy lag):** `src-tauri/src/api/router.rs` registered the four
`/admin/users/{id}/{disable,enable,activity,export}` routes with axum **0.8**
brace-param syntax (`{id}`), but the crate depends on **axum 0.7.9**
(`src-tauri/Cargo.toml`), where `{id}` is a *literal* path segment. So none of
those param routes ever matched a real id — every request fell through to the
static SPA fallback (GET → `index.html` 200; POST → 405 because the static service
rejects non-GET). This silently broke the **entire** admin per-user surface
including the older enable/disable, not just the new activity/export.

**Fix:** `{id}` → `:id` on router.rs:86-90 (axum-0.7 colon syntax). Handlers use
`Path(id)` extraction, which is unchanged. Verified with an incremental
`cargo check --no-default-features --features llm,server` on the VM (Finished,
0 errors). NOTE for Task 4 / future axum 0.8 upgrade: revert to `{id}` at that time
(it's the 0.8 idiom). The follow-up doc's "405 = old binary" heuristic was wrong —
405 here is the static fallback rejecting POST, not a registered route.

## 2026-06-27 — F014 — Deploy banner sentinel merged into the operational poll script (Task 2)

**Symptom/goal:** the "Noviq is updating…" banner + post-deploy auto-reload are
coded (server `/api/health` reads a `DEPLOYING` sentinel under `NOVIQ_DATA_DIR`),
but the live `/opt/noviq/deploy.sh` never wrote the sentinel. **Finding:** the
in-tree reference `deploy/deploy.sh` *does* write it — but it rebuilds frontend +
backend and `systemctl restart`s **unconditionally on every poll** (no
change-detection/early-exit). The operational poll script (runs every ~2 min) has
the incremental change-detection the reference lacks; copying the reference over it
(as the follow-up doc literally instructed) would restart the live server every
2 minutes. **Decision:** surgically merge — keep the operational script's
fetch/early-exit/FE-BE change-detection, and inject the sentinel
(write after `OLD != NEW`; `trap cleanup EXIT`; clear before each restart). Backed
up the prior script to `/opt/noviq/deploy.sh.bak.<ts>`; `bash -n` clean. Sentinel
path resolves from `.env` → `/opt/noviq/data/DEPLOYING`, matching what
`/api/health` reads. The in-tree reference is left as-is (it's a one-shot, not the
poller).

## 2026-06-27 — F014/F012 — Ingestion pipeline: design already coded; gap is sidecar provisioning on the VM

**Question from architect:** make the pipeline = digital text `pdftotext`; tables
`pdfplumber` → fallback `pdftotext -bbox`; scanned/image `PaddleOCR` → fallback
`tesseract`. **Finding: this is already implemented in code, default-on** —
- Tables (`parsers/pdf.rs::maybe_reflow_tables`): `table_sidecar::extract_tables`
  (pdfplumber, `ECHO_TABLE_SIDECAR` default-on) first; falls through to the
  `pdftotext -bbox` projection engine.
- OCR (`parsers/pdf.rs` Tier 3 + `ocr::paddle_ocr_enabled`): PaddleOCR
  (`ECHO_PADDLE_OCR` default-on, gated on the sidecar venv being present) first;
  tesseract fallback on any failure / venv absent.

So why it wasn't "working": both sidecars **silently fall back when not installed
on the host**. The pdfplumber frozen binary (`src-tauri/binaries/ingestion-sidecar-<triple>`,
built by `sidecars/.../build.sh`, git-ignored) and the PaddleOCR venv (built by
`setup-ocr-venv.sh`, at `~/.cache/echo-ocr-venv-build/.ocr-venv`) had never been
provisioned on the GPU VM → every doc used `-bbox` + tesseract.

**Action:** wrote VM provisioning steps to `~/Desktop/vm_setup_sidecars.txt` (build
both sidecars as `appadmin`, set `ECHO_INGESTION_SIDECAR` / `ECHO_OCR_PYTHON` /
`ECHO_PADDLE_OCR=1` / `ECHO_TABLE_SIDECAR=1` in the server `.env`, restart,
re-index). The binary + venv survive `git reset --hard` (untracked), so it's a
one-time setup. **Code change here is comment-only** — corrected three stale
"PaddleOCR is opt-in" comments (`pdf.rs`, `ocr_sidecar.rs`, `setup-ocr-venv.sh`) to
say default-on; no behavior change, so NOT promoted to `release` (avoids a needless
CUDA rebuild). NOTE: sidecars run at **index time** only — existing docs must be
re-indexed to benefit.

## 2026-06-27 — F014 — Auto-reload after deploy keyed off the sentinel (version field never changed)

**Symptom:** after a deploy, the browser kept running the OLD frontend bundle —
"deployed but no changes show up" — until a manual hard-refresh. **Root cause:** the
auto-reload in `stores/serverStatus.ts` only fired when `/api/health`'s `version`
changed, but `version` is hardcoded `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` = `"0.1.0"` and never
changes; and a frontend-only deploy doesn't restart the backend at all, so there was
no signal to detect.

**Fix:** reload off the **deploy sentinel** instead. When the poller ever sees
`status:"deploying"` and the server next returns `ok`, it reloads once. This catches
both frontend-only and backend deploys (the sentinel spans the whole deploy
regardless of what changed). Removed the dead `version`-comparison path. NOTE: this
only fires once the VM's operational `deploy.sh` actually writes the sentinel (see
`vm_enable_deploy_banner.txt`); until then, hard-refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R) is still
needed to pick up a new bundle.

`tsc --noEmit` → 0.

## 2026-06-27 — F014 — Cycling "working…" status during generation (web had a bare spinner)

**Symptom:** in the browser, while the answer generates (~tens of seconds on
Mistral-7B) the chat showed nothing interactive — just a pulsing block. **Why:**
the live phase (`classify/retrieve/generate`) and token-stream events are
Tauri-only; the web transport returns the whole `TurnResponse` at once, so
`phase()`/`streaming()` stay empty in the browser.

**Fix (`ChatPage.tsx`, frontend-only):** added a `statusIdx` signal driven by a
`createEffect` that, while `busy()`, cycles a friendly message list every 5s
("Reading your documents…" → "Thinking…" → "Thinking some more…" → "Connecting the
rules…" → "Drafting the answer…" → "Polishing the wording…" → "Almost done…",
clamped at the last). The busy block now shows three bouncing dots + the current
status. Desktop still shows the real `phase()` when events are present (the cycling
text is the fallback). No backend change.

`tsc --noEmit` → 0.

## 2026-06-27 — F014 — Expose model-status + chat-mode over HTTP (browser couldn't see the model / toggle)

**Symptom (live server, browser):** chat header showed "model not loaded" and the
Chat Answer Mode toggle was stuck on "Extractive … Recommended" and did nothing —
even though `/api/health` reported `gpu:true, layers:999` (a model IS loaded on the
A40). **Root cause:** `modelStatus()`, `getChatExtractive()`, `setChatExtractive()`
route through `transport.call` → `POST /api/<cmd>` on web, but **those routes were
never mounted** on the server (they only existed as desktop Tauri commands). Every
call 404'd → the chat fell back to "model not loaded" and the toggle read its
default. So the prior change flipped the *backend* default but left the browser
unable to see or change anything.

- **New `api/system.rs`** with three command-named handlers mounted in the
  authenticated subtree (`api/router.rs`): `POST /api/model_status` (active model +
  derived window, mirrors `commands::assistant::model_status`), `POST
  /api/get_chat_extractive`, `POST /api/set_chat_extractive`. Getter/status take any
  `AuthUser`; the setter persists `db_config.chat_extractive` and returns the new
  value (JSON body so `transport.call` has something to read). No frontend wiring
  change needed — `assistant.ts`/`index.ts` already `import { call as invoke }`.
- **`App.tsx`:** gated `<ModelDownloadBanner>` behind `isTauri()`. It calls the
  desktop-only `check_model` and is about downloading a model to *this* machine —
  meaningless (and another 404 source) in the browser, where the model lives on the
  server.
- **`SettingsPage.tsx`:** default the `chatExtractive` signal to `false` (LLM) so the
  pre-fetch state matches the new default, and reworded the mode descriptions —
  AI-model is now "Default", extractive is "a fallback for when no capable model is
  loaded" (the "Recommended" tag no longer sits on the bypass).

**Confirm a backend deploy landed from a URL-only box** (health's `version` is
static, so it can't): `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST
<url>/api/model_status` → **401** = new binary live (route exists, needs auth);
**404** = old binary still running (deploy/rebuild not finished). After it's live,
reload the page: the chat header shows the model name and the toggle works.

`cargo check --features llm,server` → 0; `tsc --noEmit` → 0.

## 2026-06-27 — F014 — Force LLM chat + indexing progress in browser + per-user usage panel

Three operator-reported issues on the live server, fixed together.

**1. Chat was bypassing the LLM (no way to switch back).** Root cause: the
`chat_extractive` flag in `db_config` **defaulted ON** (`query_router.rs`
`chat_extractive_enabled` returned `unwrap_or(true)`), so chat composed verbatim
provisions and "skips the LLM entirely." The only toggle was two **Tauri desktop
commands** (`get/set_chat_extractive`) that were never exposed over HTTP — so on
the browser/server deploy there was no control to turn it off.
- Flipped the default to **OFF** (LLM): `chat_extractive_enabled` now returns
  `unwrap_or(false)` and only the literal `'1'` re-enables the extractive bypass
  (`query_router.rs`, and the matching desktop getter in `commands/system.rs`).
- **Migration `007_query_log_usage.sql`** also resets any stored row to `'0'`
  (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET value='0'`) so the *live* DB switches
  to the model on deploy, not just fresh installs. Extractive code is retained but
  dormant.

**2. Indexing progress bar never showed in the browser.** `SettingsPage.tsx`
(which owns the browser upload via `uploadDocuments`) tracked per-file progress
only through the Tauri `listen("source:indexing-progress")` event — which never
fires for web clients. Swapped that subscription to the cross-transport
`onIndexProgress` helper (already in `transport.ts`): Tauri event on desktop,
`/api/index/events` **SSE** in the browser. Same callback body, now fed from `p`
directly. The folder-scan `listen("folder:progress")` is unchanged.

**3. Per-user usage + activity in the admin panel.** Built on the existing
`audit_log` user events; added a dedicated per-turn log.
- **`query_log` table** (migration 007, additive): `user_id`, `conversation_id`,
  `question`, `answer`, `citations_json`, `latency_ms`, and peak `cpu_pct` /
  `ram_mb` / `gpu_util_pct` / `gpu_mem_mb`.
- **Resource sampler** `services/usage_sampler.rs`: a background `spawn_blocking`
  loop samples the server process (sysinfo CPU%/RSS, 250 ms) and the GPU
  (`nvidia-smi`, ~1 s) and reports the PEAK. Generation is serialized behind the
  gen gate, so the peak attributes cleanly to the one running query.
- **Wired into `api/query.rs`**: sampler wraps `run_turn`; on success it writes a
  `query_log` row (best-effort — never fails the user's turn).
- **Repository** `db/repositories/query_log.rs`: `insert`, `list_for_user`,
  `export_for_user`, and `usage_by_user` (per-user rollup: count, last active, avg
  CPU/GPU, peak RAM, avg latency — cast to int8/float8 in SQL to avoid numeric
  decode).
- **Admin API** (`api/admin.rs` + `api/router.rs`): `GET /admin/users` now returns
  the usage rollup per user; new `GET /admin/users/:id/activity` (recent 200
  turns) and `GET /admin/users/:id/export?format=json|csv` (full history, served
  as a download with `Content-Disposition`).
- **Admin UI** (`Admin.tsx`): widened table with Queries / Last active / Avg CPU /
  Peak RAM / Avg GPU / Avg ms columns; an **Activity** expander showing each
  recent query (question, answer, latency + CPU/RAM/GPU per turn); and **JSON** /
  **CSV** download buttons. Auth'd downloads use a new `transport.downloadAuthed`
  (bearer header + blob object-URL, since `<a download>` can't carry the token).

**Verify:** `cargo check --no-default-features --features llm,server` → 0;
`tsc --noEmit` → 0. Note GPU columns read `—` on CPU-only hosts (no `nvidia-smi`);
on the A40 VM they populate. Deploy via `make deploy` (migration applies on
startup; additive, rolls back cleanly per FR-017).

## 2026-06-27 — F014 — Restore the `release` deploy model (VM verified + repointed)

**Context:** the committed deploy scripts said `BRANCH=release` but the live VM had been
deploying `014-server-thin-client` directly (a shortcut taken when the login/upload/
per-user-folder work needed to go live and `origin/release` was 26 commits behind). Two
questions got resolved today: (1) is the VM's deploy loop safe? (2) which branch model do
we keep — track the feature branch directly, or restore `release` as a stable deploy ref?

**VM verification (`appadmin@10.150.0.100` — see
`specs/014-server-thin-client/VM_HANDOFF_VERIFY_DEPLOY.md`):**
- `noviq-deploy.service` `ExecStart=/opt/noviq/deploy.sh` — **out-of-tree ⇒ Case A
  DECOUPLED.** `git reset --hard` in the loop can't touch the operational script, so the
  in-tree/live branch mismatch was never an actual footgun, only misleading docs.
- `noviq-deploy.timer` healthy (~2-min poll, no errors); repo at `/opt/noviq/echoAI`.

**Decision (architect):** restore the **`release`** model. The server tracks one stable
branch forever; you develop on feature branches (`014`, `015`, …) and `make deploy`
promotes the current branch → `origin/release`. The VM is never reconfigured when a new
feature branch starts — the friction that the direct-tracking shortcut would have caused.

**Actions taken:**
1. **Promoted `release`:** fast-forwarded `origin/release` `b57b6436 → 477364a0` (gained 26
   commits incl. login/upload/per-user-folders). Clean FF — `release` was an ancestor of `014`.
2. **Repointed the VM (out-of-tree op script):** `/opt/noviq/deploy.sh` `BRANCH` back to
   `release` (backup saved `deploy.sh.bak.<ts>`); `git checkout -B release origin/release`
   in the VM repo so its branch ref tracks `release` (the script only `reset --hard`s, never
   checks out). Both refs were already at `477364a0`, so the next poll was a clean no-op —
   verified `up to date (477364a)`, no rebuild, no restart. Live site unaffected.
3. **In-tree reference scripts** (`deploy/deploy.sh`, `deploy/check-release.sh`, `Makefile`,
   `deploy/noviq-deploy{.timer,-check.service}`): kept on `release` (now truthful), but
   **parameterised** so the branch is overridable via `BRANCH=` / `DEPLOY_BRANCH=` env
   instead of hardcoded, and headers document the out-of-tree-copy + promote-via-`make deploy`
   model. (Note: an earlier commit `477364a0` this morning had flipped these to `014` to match
   the then-current shortcut; this entry supersedes that — we standardised on `release`.)

**Impact / how to deploy now:** push WIP to your feature branch freely; run `make deploy`
when a build is tester-ready → it pushes `HEAD:release`, the VM picks it up within ~2 min
and rebuilds only what changed. `test_deploy_rollback.sh` already exercises `BRANCH=release`
against its own throwaway repo, so it's unchanged and still valid.

  build` (updates served `dist/`), `src-tauri/` → cuda `cargo build` + `systemctl restart noviq-server`.

## 2026-06-26 — F014 — Add web login screen (US2 gap: browser had no way to authenticate)

**Symptom:** the browser thin client showed "Not authorized — admin access required" on
`/admin` (and silently failed other authed calls). **Root cause:** the web build had **no
login UI** — `transport.setAuthToken()` was defined but **never called anywhere**, and there
was no username/password form. Meanwhile the server gates every route except `/health` and
`/login` behind `require_auth` (`api/router.rs:66`). So the browser never sent a bearer token
→ `GET /api/me` 401'd → `Admin.tsx` left `isAdmin=false`. Backend auth was fine (verified:
admin login → 200 + token; `/me` → `role:"admin"`; `/admin/users` authorized).

**Fix (new files):**
- `src/stores/auth.ts` — persists the session token in `localStorage` (`noviq:authToken`),
  restores it into the transport **synchronously at module load** (so early authed requests
  carry it), exposes `currentUser`/`authReady`/`isAdmin`, and `login`/`logout`/`restoreSession`.
- `src/components/LoginScreen.tsx` — username/password form → `POST /api/login` → store token
  → load `/me`. Friendly errors for 401 / 429 / network.
- `src/App.tsx` — web-only auth gate: `restoreSession()` on mount; show a "Loading…" splash
  until `authReady`, then `LoginScreen` until `currentUser` is set. Desktop (Tauri) bypasses
  the gate entirely (no auth there).

Token is in-memory in the transport + localStorage for reload-survival. `tsc --noEmit` → 0;
`vite build` → 0 (needed a one-off `@rollup/rollup-win32-x64-msvc` install for the Windows
native binary). Built `dist/` deployed to the VM at `/opt/noviq/echoAI/dist` (served fresh by
axum ServeDir, no restart). Reached over an SSH tunnel (`-L 8080:127.0.0.1:8080`) because the
IBA firewall only forwards 22/ICMP, not 8080.

## 2026-06-26 — F014 — DECISION: "index folders, no notebooks" (analysis only, no code change)

**Why:** architect decided the thin client stops creating notebooks/adding individual files —
users **index a folder** (a path on the server/VM, the central corpus). This retires the T053 gap
(no create-notebook HTTP route) instead of building that route. Full analysis + next-session plan in

- **Folder indexing already works server-side.** `db/repositories/folders.rs::insert` creates the
  `indexed_folders` row **and** a stub `notebooks` row `__folder__<id>` (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) in

  `notebooks::list` hides `__folder__%`/`__batch__%` stubs. So `POST /api/add_indexed_folder` is the

## 2026-06-26 — F014 — VM STANDUP COMPLETE: full stack runs on the A40 (GPU LLM + PG + ORT + systemd)

**Why:** finish the GPU-VM standup — turn the green CUDA build into a running, durable server.
Four more runtime blockers surfaced and were resolved; the server now answers `/api/query` over the
A40 under systemd. Resolves the PG/glibc blocker noted in the entry below.

**Blocker 1 — bundled PG vs focal glibc (resolved by source build).** The theseus-rs
`postgresql_embedded` PG 17.10.0 binaries need glibc 2.32–2.34 + OpenSSL 3; the IBA VM is Ubuntu
20.04 (glibc 2.31 + OpenSSL 1.1). PGDG has **dropped focal** (only jammy/bullseye remain — also too
new), so no prebuilt works. Fix: **built PostgreSQL 17.10 + pgvector 0.8.1 from source on the VM**
(`/opt/noviq/build_pg.sh`), focal-native, into `…/pg/install/17.10.0/`. `postgresql_embedded::setup()`
skips its own extraction when `installed_dir()` finds a version-matching subdir (verified in the 0.20.4
source), so the app uses the source-built engine with **no code change**. Needed `bison`+`flex` (apt);
configured `--with-openssl --without-readline --without-zlib --without-icu`. The app's vendored-pgvector
copy lands in flat `lib/`/`share/extension/` but source-built PG's `pkglibdir`/`sharedir` are
`lib/postgresql`/`share/postgresql`, so the copy is inert and PG loads the correctly-installed focal
`vector.so`. Boot now logs `Created chunk_embeddings vector table … halfvec HNSW index`.

**Blocker 2 — SIGILL on model load (Illegal instruction).** The IBA vCPU is masked to a pre-AVX
**Core2 (no AVX/AVX2/FMA/F16C/BMI2)**; ggml-cpu's default build enables AVX2 → `SIGILL` the moment a
model loads (CPU-side dequant runs even with full GPU offload, so it killed BOTH the GPU and CPU
paths). Fix: build with `RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native"`, which `llama-cpp-sys-2`'s build.rs detects
to set `GGML_NATIVE=ON` so ggml compiles for THIS CPU only (the build.rs else-branch can only turn
features *on*, never off, so it can't disable ggml's AVX2 default — native is the only env lever).
Build host == run host on the VM, so native is correct; `deploy.sh` now exports it. After this:
`load_tensors: offloaded 25/25 layers to GPU`, `CUDA0 model buffer size = 373.73 MiB`.

**Blocker 3 — missing ONNX Runtime.** `ort` uses `load-dynamic`; the embedder (fastembed) + reranker
need `libonnxruntime.so` (1.20.x for ort rc.9). Vendored the MS `libonnxruntime.so.1.20.1` to
`/opt/noviq/.ort-runtime/` and set `ORT_DYLIB_PATH` in `.env` (so the systemd EnvironmentFile carries
it). ORT's MLAS runtime-dispatches, so it runs on the AVX-less CPU. Query then returned **HTTP 200**.

**Blocker 4 — orphan PG after a crash.** A crashed `noviq-server` leaves its `postgres` child running
(`pkill noviq-server` doesn't reap it) → next boot fails `another server might be running`. Operational
note for the runbook: on a hard crash, `pkill -9 -f '17.10.0/bin/postgres'` + remove
`…/pg/data/postmaster.pid`. (No code change; the desktop path has orphan-adoption, server relies on
clean systemd stop.)

**Durability — systemd.** Installed/enabled `noviq-server.service` as `User=appadmin` (no `noviq` user
exists on the VM; binary needs only `libcuda.so.1` from the default loader path — cudart is static).
Server is `active`, `enable`d (survives reboot), `Restart=on-failure`. Verified `/api/health`
(`gpu:true, layers:999`) and `/api/query` (HTTP 200) under systemd. Unit files updated in-repo:
`User=noviq`→`appadmin` across all three; deploy + check units now `ExecStart=/bin/bash -lc …` so the
CUDA build/poll get cargo/cmake(3.30)/node/git from `~/.profile`.

**Standup prerequisites recorded (one-time, on the VM):** CMake 3.30 at `~/.local/cmake-current` on
PATH; `bison`+`flex`+`libssl-dev`+`pkg-config` via apt; PG17+pgvector source-built into the install
dir; `libonnxruntime.so.1.20.1` vendored + `ORT_DYLIB_PATH`. Admin seeded (`admin` / see `.env`).
`NOVIQ_BIND=0.0.0.0:8080` for direct VPN browser access.

**Still open (validation, not blockers):** T028 GPU-vs-CPU latency needs an indexed doc (empty-corpus
queries short-circuit before generation); the `#[ignore]`d server-side tests (T021/T048); enabling the
poll-timer deploy + full SC-001..010 acceptance (T052).

**GAP found while attempting T028 (T053, new):** `POST /api/add_sources` accepts `{notebookId,
filePaths}` and indexes, but indexing fails `notebook_sources_notebook_id_fkey` — the notebook row must
pre-exist and **the headless API exposes no create-notebook route** (router has only
`list_notebook_sources`). Desktop creates notebooks via a Tauri command not surfaced over HTTP. To make
the browser client able to index (the pilot requirement — users index into the central DB), the server
needs a `create_notebook` (and probably list/delete) endpoint, OR indexing should upsert a default
notebook. For a one-off T028 measurement, a notebook row can be inserted directly (bundled PG listens
on an ephemeral port from `…/pg/data/postmaster.pid` line 4; password in `…/pg/.pgpass`, user
`postgres`, db `echo`). Not yet implemented.

## 2026-06-26 — F014 — T026 CUDA build GREEN on the A40 VM (+ deploy.sh fix); PG/glibc blocker found

**Why:** first real `cargo build --release` (not just `cargo check`) of the decoupled tree with
CUDA on the Ubuntu-20.04 GPU VM. Three environment/toolchain gaps surfaced, all now resolved; the
`noviq-server` binary builds and links CUDA. A separate **runtime** blocker (bundled PG vs focal
glibc) is documented at the bottom for the next decision.

**Build gap 1 — CMake too old.** `ggml-cuda/CMakeLists.txt` needs CMake ≥ 3.18; focal ships 3.16.3.
Installed the official CMake 3.30.5 binary into `~/.local/cmake-current` (no sudo) and prepended it
to PATH in `~/.profile`. (Also fixed a self-inflicted `~/.profile` PATH line from this session that
had been mangled by shell-escaping and was dropping `~/.cargo/bin`.)

**Build gap 2 — stale CMake cache.** The first (failed, CMake-3.16) configure left a `CMakeCache.txt`
in `target/release/build/llama-cpp-sys-2-*/out/build` that produced no Makefile on the retry
(`make: Makefile: No such file`). Fix: `cargo clean -p llama-cpp-sys-2` + `rm -rf` the build dir
before each retry.

**Build gap 3 — non-PIC CUDA objects (the real one).** Final link of the position-independent target
failed: `rust-lld: relocation R_X86_64_PC32 cannot be used against symbol 'stderr'; recompile with
-fPIC`, from nvcc-compiled `mmq-instance-*.cu.o` in `libllama_cpp_sys_2.rlib`. CMake compiled the
C/C++/ASM with `-fPIC` but not the CUDA host code. Fix: `export CUDAFLAGS="-Xcompiler -fPIC"` (CMake
seeds `CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS` from it) + build `--bin noviq-server` only (headless needs no desktop
`cdylib`). Clean rebuild → **Finished in 8m19s, EXIT=0**. Binary is 612 MB, `ldd` shows
`libcuda.so.1`, `strings` shows `ggml_cuda_*`. Boots and detects the A40 (tier 5, VRAM 11.8 GB).

**`deploy/deploy.sh` fix (real bug).** Line 59 ran `cargo build --release --features "server,cuda"`
**without** `--no-default-features`, so the poll-timer production deploy would have re-added the
`desktop` default feature → tauri/webkit → fail on the headless box (the exact thing the decoupling
removed). Rewrote it to `--no-default-features --features "llm,server,cuda" --bin noviq-server` and to
export `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86` + `CUDAFLAGS="-Xcompiler -fPIC"` (env-overridable) so the
automated build reproduces the working manual build. The full standup env (CMake 3.30 on PATH) is a
documented VM prerequisite.

**`.env` created on the VM** (`/opt/noviq/echoAI/.env`): DATA_DIR=/opt/noviq/data,
WEB_DIR=.../dist, BIND=0.0.0.0:8080 (direct VPN browser access during acceptance), GPU_LAYERS=999,
admin seeded from env on first boot.

**RUNTIME BLOCKER (open) — bundled PG vs focal glibc.** On boot the server reaches DB setup and the
theseus-rs `postgresql_embedded` PG 17.10.0 binaries fail: `initdb`/`libpq.so.5` need GLIBC_2.32/2.33/
2.34 and `libssl.so.3` (OpenSSL 3) — focal has **glibc 2.31 + OpenSSL 1.1**. The vendored pgvector
`.so` is almost certainly built the same way (would fail `CREATE EXTENSION vector` too). So the fully
bundled/offline DB (FR-004) can't run as-is on this box. `postgresql_embedded::setup()` skips its own
extraction when `installed_dir()` finds a version-matching subdir, so a focal-compatible PG 17 +
pgvector placed at `…/pg/install/17.10.0/` would be used without a code change — pending the standup
decision (PGDG focal packages vs from-source vs container). Nothing committed for this yet.

**Why:** first real compile of the decoupled tree on the Ubuntu-20.04 GPU VM (no local Rust
toolchain on the laptop). `cargo check` surfaced env + layering gaps the Windows-only build never hit.

**VM env:** installed `libssl-dev` + `pkg-config` (openssl-sys had no headers).

**Fix 1 — audio deps gated (`Cargo.toml`):** `cpal` pulled `alsa-sys`, which failed (no ALSA on the
headless VM). Made the Meeting-Agent audio crates (`cpal`, `webrtc-vad`, `rubato`, `hound`) `optional`
and added them to the `desktop` feature. All consumers (`meeting/*`, `stt_sidecar`) are already
desktop-gated, so the server build now links no audio stack.

**Fix 2 — indexing layering (`services/indexing.rs` NEW):** `api/documents.rs` (server) imported
`SourceDto`/`FolderDto`/`EntityDto` + `index_sources`/`index_folder` from `crate::commands::*`, but
`commands` is now desktop-only → `E0433 cannot find commands`. These are shared "one implementation,
two transports" pieces that were mis-homed in `commands/`. Moved them to a new always-compiled
`services::indexing` module (AppHandle → compat); `commands/{sources,folders,entities}.rs` now
`pub use` them (desktop back-compat) and `api/documents.rs` imports them directly. No behavior change.

**Fix 3 — llm-gated re-export (`services/legal_ir/mod.rs`):** `pub use doc_ir::mistral_builder` was
ungated but `mistral_builder` is `#[cfg(feature="llm")]` → broke the no-llm fast loop. Mirrored the
`llm` gate. (Desktop/llm consumers reference `doc_ir::mistral_builder` directly, unaffected.)

**Verify (ON THE VM):** `cargo check --no-default-features --features server` → Finished, 0 errors;
`cargo check --no-default-features --features llm,server` → Finished, 0 errors (1m37s). Remaining VM
work is unchanged: the real `cargo build --release --features llm,server,cuda` (CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86)

behind a `desktop` feature; shim the shared service layer via `crate::compat`; gate desktop-only
modules. (Prior session did Cargo.toml/build.rs/compat.rs/lib.rs/services/mod.rs/indexer.rs/
query_trace.rs/llm.rs/query_router.rs/scheduler.rs — see `RESUME_DECOUPLING.md`.)

**This session — finished the remaining shared-layer files:**
- `services/analysis_engine.rs` (3), `entity_extractor.rs`, `intent_router/mod.rs`: pure
  `tauri::AppHandle` → `crate::compat::AppHandle` param/import swaps (no state/Manager).
- `services/cloud_llm.rs`: import split (`compat::{AppHandle,Emitter}` + desktop-gated `Manager`);
  `settings_path` body gated — desktop uses `app.path().app_data_dir()`, headless derives from
  `NOVIQ_DATA_DIR` (default `.noviq-data`). `load_settings`/`save_settings` stay defined in BOTH
  builds because `entity_extractor`'s `Some(a)` branch must compile on the server (dead at runtime —
  server always passes `None` → `load_settings_cached`).
- `services/assistant/{mod,mapreduce}.rs` + `capabilities/{action_items,conflict,compare,
  summarize_doc,mod,draft,guidance}.rs`: AppHandle/Emitter → compat (no state/Manager).
- `services/doc_ir/{progress,cache,dispatch}.rs`: AppHandle/Emitter → compat; `cache::cache_dir`
  gated like `cloud_llm::settings_path` (desktop path-API vs `NOVIQ_DATA_DIR/ir_cache` headless).
  `doc_ir` is server-reachable (indexer → `dispatch`), so it is NOT module-gated — only the
  `Manager` import and the `cache_dir` body are.

**Invariant established:** every `tauri::` path reachable from `--features server` is now either
compat-shimmed or `#[cfg(feature="desktop")]`-gated. Verified by sweep — remaining raw `tauri::`
refs live ONLY in desktop-gated modules (`commands/*`, `meeting`, `batch_processor`, `stt_sidecar`)
or behind explicit desktop cfgs (lib.rs, indexer NER fns, the three `Manager` imports). Server
caller `api/query.rs::run_turn(.., None, ..)` matches the new `Option<&compat::AppHandle>` sig.

**Verify:** NO local Rust toolchain — must `cargo check --no-default-features --features server` ON

event bus, and a headless trigger to start indexing, before moving to the GPU-VM tasks.

**Key finding (smaller than feared):** indexing progress already funnels through one
`AppHandle`-optional fn, `indexer::emit_progress(app: &Option<AppHandle>, …)`. So the SSE half is
surgical, not a rewrite. **No `AppState` changes** were needed either: `index_file`'s `TaskBudget`
arg is unused (`_task_budget`), and the folder `FileWatcher` stays in the desktop command — so a
throwaway `TaskBudget::new()` suffices in the shared service fns.

**Broadcast channel (T024):** `indexer::index_progress_channel()` — a process-wide
`tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<IndexingProgress>` (OnceLock, 256 buffer). `emit_progress` now
publishes to it **and** (when `app` is `Some`) emits the Tauri event — desktop unchanged, web gets the
same ticks. Concurrency stays bounded by the existing `indexer::indexing_sem()` (no new job queue
needed; documented as the equivalent).

**SSE endpoint:** `api/index_events.rs` → `GET /api/index/events`. **Auth nuance:** the browser
`EventSource` API can't set an `Authorization` header, so the bearer token rides in `?token=` and the
handler resolves it via `auth::resolve_token` — this route is mounted in the **public** subtree
(outside the bearer middleware) for that reason. Stream built with `futures::stream::unfold` over a
`broadcast::Receiver` (skips `Lagged`, ends on `Closed`), `KeepAlive` default.

**Triggers + service extraction:** `commands/sources.rs::index_sources` and
`commands/folders.rs::index_folder` extracted (both take `app: Option<AppHandle>`); the Tauri commands
delegate (`Some(app)`), the new `POST /api/add_sources` / `POST /api/add_indexed_folder` handlers in
`api/documents.rs` pass `None` (+ audit `action="index"`, T038). Folder-level `folder:progress` events
are desktop-only (guarded `emit_folder_progress`); web relies on the per-file SSE stream.

**Frontend (T025):** `src/api/transport.ts::onIndexProgress(cb)` — Tauri `listen("source:indexing-
progress")` on desktop, `new EventSource("/api/index/events?token=…")` on web; returns a sync
unsubscribe. `components/notebook/SourceList.tsx` rewired from the raw `listen` to `onIndexProgress`
(dropped the now-unused `@tauri-apps/api/event` import).

**Verify (single pass):** `cargo check --features server --bin noviq-server` + `cargo check --lib`
(desktop) + `cargo test --features server --test api_admin --no-run` all exit 0; `tsc --noEmit` clean —
only the 2 pre-existing dead-code warnings. **All local F014 tasks are now done;** remaining work is
GPU-VM-gated (T026–T028 cuda build/latency, T035 deploy rollback test, T051 runbook, T052 acceptance,
+ run `api_admin` green against bundled PG).

## 2026-06-26 — F014 — US6 deploy path (T029–T034) + "server is updating" browser banner

**Why:** the GPU server needs an unattended update path (no manual SSH build per change), and during
a deploy the browser testers must see *what's happening* instead of a dead/erroring page.

**Deploy path (Stream B, all local files — installed on the VM later):** `deploy/deploy.sh`
(fetch→checkout `release`→`npm ci && build`→`cargo build --release --features server,cuda`→restart
→`/api/health` probe→auto-rollback to prev binary+commit on fail), `noviq-server.service`,
`noviq-deploy.service` (oneshot, decoupled so the restart can't kill the build, FR-015),
`noviq-deploy.timer` + `noviq-deploy-check.service` + `check-release.sh` (poll `origin/release`
every ~2 min = PRIMARY trigger, VPN-gated VM has no inbound webhook), `sudoers.noviq` (tight
NOPASSWD: restart server + start deploy unit only), root `Makefile` `deploy:` (push current branch
→ `origin/release`). Matches `deployment-and-updates.md`.

**"Server updating" notification (new requirement):** `deploy.sh` touches a `DEPLOYING` sentinel
under `NOVIQ_DATA_DIR` at build start and clears it before the restart + on any exit (trap).
`src-tauri/src/api/health.rs` now reports `status:"deploying"` while that file exists (else `ok`) —
so the still-running OLD binary advertises the in-progress deploy for the whole (minutes-long) CUDA
build. Frontend: `src/stores/serverStatus.ts` polls `/api/health` **web-transport only** (`isTauri()`
→ no-op), mapping deploying / fetch-failure(restart blip) → an amber banner
(`src/components/ServerStatusBanner.tsx`), and auto-`location.reload()`s when a NEW `version` returns
so testers pick up the rebuilt frontend bundle. Wired in `App.tsx` (`startServerStatusPolling` in
`onMount` + `ServerStatusBanner` next to `ModelDownloadBanner`).

**Sentinel ordering matters:** cleared BEFORE `systemctl restart` so the freshly-started binary
probes `status:"ok"` (FR-017) rather than tripping its own rollback; the EXIT trap covers the
build-failure path (banner never sticks, old server keeps serving).

warnings); `tsc --noEmit` clean; `bash -n` on both scripts OK. **Pending (needs the VM):** T035

## 2026-06-25 — F014 — Update/deploy path designed (auto-deploy on push, server is CUDA build host)

**Why:** Spec 014 (server/thin-client) said nothing about how code authored on the laptop reaches
the running GPU server. Needed a repeatable update path before the pilot — every fix was otherwise
a manual SSH build.

**Decisions** (with the architect): build host = the GPU server (CUDA/cuBLAS must compile where the
toolkit+driver live; laptop pushes source only); trigger = **auto on push to a `release` ref**
(signed GitHub webhook `/__deploy`, HMAC-SHA256; server-side poll-timer fallback for VPN-gated
boxes); downtime = brief restart OK (single binary serves API **and** the built static frontend →
no API/UI version skew).

**Key design constraints baked in:** (1) a Rust process can't restart itself — the webhook only
*triggers* a decoupled `noviq-deploy.service`; the build/restart lives outside the server's process
tree and survives the bounce. (2) `release`-branch trigger (not every push) so slow CUDA rebuilds
aren't thrashed. (3) failed post-deploy health probe auto-rolls-back to previous binary+commit;
migrations stay additive so the older binary is safe on a newer schema. (4) models (`*.gguf`) and
secrets never in git — models transferred out-of-band via rsync, `.env` via systemd EnvironmentFile.

**Files:** `specs/014-server-thin-client/deployment-and-updates.md` (NEW — full design + `deploy.sh`,
systemd units, sudoers drop-in, webhook handler spec, laptop `make deploy`). `spec.md` gained
US6 (update from local dev), FR-013…FR-018, SC-007/008. No code yet — 014 has no HTTP server crate
(`grep axum/actix/hyper::Server` over `src-tauri/` = none); this is the deploy seam, to be built
alongside the FR-001 HTTP-API split. Reachability behind IBA VPN must be confirmed (webhook vs poll).

## 2026-06-22 — F015 — Chat history list (ChatGPT/Claude-style) in the left rail

**Symptom**: after an app restart the transcript reloaded with the user's
questions but the answers appeared missing/empty. Root cause: the previous design
auto-restored a single fixed conversation (`noviq:conversationId` + one
`noviq:turns:<id>` record) on startup; a partial overwrite of that one record left
questions without answers, and the single-conversation model couldn't keep more
than one past chat anyway.

**Fix** (`src/pages/ChatPage.tsx`):
- Removed `CONVERSATION_KEY` / `ensureConversationId` auto-restore. Startup now
  always opens a fresh blank chat (`newConversationId()` + empty turns), like
  ChatGPT/Claude.
- Added a persisted, ordered conversation list (`noviq:conversations` →
  `ConvMeta[]` of `{id,title,updatedAt}`), with `loadConversations`/
  `saveConversations`. A conversation enters the list only once it has ≥1 turn
  (blank New-chat sessions never clutter the rail). Title = first user message
  (≤60 chars).
- Persistence `createEffect` now saves turns *and* upserts the conversation meta
  (most-recent-first); a second effect persists the list.
- New handlers: `newChat` (no longer deletes the old chat), `selectConversation`
  (reopens full Q+A from `noviq:turns:<id>`), `deleteConversation` (removes record
  + meta; falls back to a new chat if the active one is deleted).
- Left rail: prominent "New chat" button + a scrollable **Chats** history section
  (capped `max-h-56`) above the existing **Files** tree; old bottom "New chat"
  button removed, Help kept.

**Cross-cutting**: client-only (localStorage); no backend/command/migration
changes. `tsc --noEmit` clean; no dangling refs to removed symbols.
