## 2026-06-21 — Feature 015 Phase 7 — Conversation memory polish (T043–T046, T052)

**What**: the conversation-memory layer that makes long sessions reliable —
deterministic pinned-fact extraction, summarize-old-turns eviction, the
context-fill notice + fresh-chat carry-forward, and three acceptance gates.

**Why**: US3. A session that runs many windows long must never lose load-bearing
situational facts (grade/length-of-service/leave type) to summarization, and must
nudge the officer to a fresh chat before quality degrades — carrying their facts
forward so they don't restate them (FR-017/FR-018/FR-018a/FR-018b/FR-021).

**Fix / files**:
- `services/assistant/memory.rs`:
  - **T043** `extract_facts` (deterministic labelled regexes: grade/BPS,
    length-of-service, leave type) + `record_pinned_facts`/`capture_pinned_facts`
    (supersede earlier value on restatement; same-value restatement is a no-op) +
    `load_pinned_facts`. `load_for_turn` now fills the always-present pinned slot
    and excludes `summarized=1` turns from the verbatim set.
  - **T044** `evict_old_turns(keep_recent)`: folds the oldest non-summarized turns
    into `conversation_summary` (deterministic compact extract; LLM-assist can
    swap in later) and marks them `summarized`; pinned facts (separate table) are
    exempt. Idempotent + incremental (summary accretes).
- `commands/assistant.rs`: `send_message` now captures pinned facts after the user
  turn and runs eviction after the assistant turn; new **T045**
  `new_chat_from_notice` command (carries non-superseded facts into a fresh
  conversation + builds a recap), registered in `lib.rs`.
- Frontend: `components/ContextFillNotice.tsx` (non-blocking nudge + "New chat"
  button) wired into `ChatPage.tsx` (`startFreshChat` swaps the conversation and
  seeds the recap); `api/assistant.ts` gains `newChatFromNotice` + `confirmDocuments`.
- `tests/bureaucrat_chat_acceptance.rs`: **T046** SC-004 (early facts honored after
  a 40-turn session with eviction) + SC-008 (notice at threshold + facts carry to
  a fresh chat); **T052** FR-021 (write → drop pool → reconnect a second
  independent pool to the same durable DB → conversation reloads intact). These
  are the file's first DB-backed gates (`db::testing::test_pool`), still no LLM.

**Cross-cutting**: no migration (reuses `pinned_case_fact` from migration 004 +
`conversation_summary`/`chat_message.summarized` from baseline). Tests: `cargo
test --lib assistant` 69/0; `cargo test --test bureaucrat_chat_acceptance` 16/0.

(MODULAR_IMPROVEMENT_LOG), T050 (full-suite green gate).

## 2026-06-21 — Feature 015 Phase 5 — Whole-doc summarize + amendment chain (T032–T037)

**What**: shipped the F015 P2 map-reduce layer — a sequential **map-reduce driver**,
a whole-document **summarize-doc** capability over it, and a deterministic
**amendment-chain** capability + `get_amendment_chain` command built from F013
provenance. Two new acceptance gates prove 100% document coverage and amendment
fidelity, both without a live LLM.

**Why**: whole-/cross-document work (summarize a book, amendment history) cannot
fit one window and must read everything without skipping (US6/FR-005d) while the
amendment chain — the highest-confabulation-risk surface — must be structural,
not generated (US8/FR-005f). F013 is already in this branch's history, so the
provenance the chain needs is present.

**Changes**:
- **T032 — map-reduce driver** (`services/assistant/mapreduce.rs`, new): pure
  `plan_batches(counter, provisions, per_batch_overhead, window, gen_reserve)`
  packs atomic provisions into window-sized batches — **no provision split, every
  provision in exactly one batch in document order** (the full-coverage invariant;
  an oversized-alone provision gets its own singleton rather than being dropped).
  async `run(...)` resolves the model + dynamic window (T029), runs one grounded
  extract pass per batch on the single slot via `infer_with_cancel_temp` (temp 0),
  then a reduce/synthesis pass (skipped for a single batch); streams
  `assistant://progress {phase:"map"|"reduce", batch, total}`. Reuses
  `query_router::build_rag_prompt` (made `pub(crate)`) so citation formatting
  matches the single-pass path. 5 unit tests.
- **T033 — summarize-doc capability** (`capabilities/summarize_doc.rs`, new):
  `gather_provisions` reads each in-scope source's **leaf** chunks (a chunk that is
  not the parent of any other — so a container's text is not double-counted; flat
  docs keep every chunk) in document order, runs them through the map-reduce driver
  with the summarize persona fragment, then gates + assembles the cited summary
  over the full source text. Coverage is guaranteed by the batcher. Wired into
  `send_message` (`Capability::SummarizeDoc`).
- **T034 — amendment-chain capability** (`capabilities/amendment_chain.rs`, new):
  **provenance lives in the `amendment_events` table** (migration 020 / pg
  baseline), keyed `node_id → graph_nodes.citation` — NOT the `amended_by` edges /
  `footnote_refs` the tasks.md text guessed. Pure `build_chain(provision_ref,
  events)` orders events oldest→recent by `effective_date` (undated sink to the end
  stably); `render_prose` renders citation-grade text grounded in the chain's own
  facts (re-gates clean by construction); empty → "no amendments recorded" (never
  invented). 0 model-invented links. 4 unit tests. Wired into `send_message`
  (`Capability::AmendmentChain`, provision extracted via new
  `intent::extract_provision_ref`).
- **T035 — `get_amendment_chain` command** (`commands/assistant.rs` + new
  `graph::amendment_events_for_provision` repo fn): case-insensitive citation/
  legal-path match → `build_chain` → `{chain[], ordered:"oldest_to_recent",
  narration:null}`. Deterministic, no model. Registered in `lib.rs`.
- **T036/T037 — acceptance gates** (`tests/bureaucrat_chat_acceptance.rs`, NO live
  LLM): SC-009 builds a 60-section act, asserts the batcher spans multiple passes
  and the union of all batch indices is exactly `0..N` (100% coverage, none
  skipped/sliced); SC-010 feeds out-of-order provenance and asserts the chain is
  ordered oldest→recent with every link's instrument/action/date matching a source
  row (0 invented/dropped), plus the "none recorded" path.

**Verification**: `cargo build --lib` clean (only the 2 pre-existing dead-code
warnings). `cargo test --lib assistant::` 58/0 (+11). `cargo test --test
bureaucrat_chat_acceptance` 11/0 (+3).

**Follow-ups**: Phase 6 (T038–T042 compare/conflict/action-items) reuses this
map-reduce driver. The amendment-chain `send_message` path currently renders the
chain deterministically (safe, citation-grade); optional LLM narration over the
already-ordered chain (persona fragment exists) is a future enhancement. Frontend
wiring for `get_amendment_chain` is not yet done (T035 is the command only).

## 2026-06-21 — Feature 015 Phase 4 — Drafting + hot-swap model (T026–T031, T051)

**What**: shipped the F015 P2 layer — a dedicated **draft** capability (plain-prose
cited Summary/Note with the larger generation reserve), `export_draft` +
`model_status` commands, reasoning-span stripping at the generation boundary, and
the **retirement** of the legacy slot/template/docset/gap/finalize drafting path
from the user-facing surface. Two new acceptance gates prove the window scales with
the model and grounding is model-independent.

**Why**: drafting is no longer a separate pane — it is one intent-routed capability
of the unified assistant (US4). Hot-swapping a bigger GGUF must widen the usable
window without changing grounding (US5). Thinking models must render clean prose.

**Changes**:
- **T028 — `<think>` stripping at the boundary** (`services/llm.rs`): new
  `strip_reasoning_spans(text)` (module-level, unit-tested) removes
  `<think>…</think>` (and tolerates unclosed/orphan tags) from
  `infer_with_cancel_temp`'s returned `output` at **every** return point (normal,
  `<|im_end|>` break, mid-stream cancel). The streaming filter already hid think
  tokens from the live `chat://token` stream; this guarantees the **returned
  string** — the user-facing answer AND the citation-gate input — is clean
  regardless of caller (FR-009/R7). The IR-builder grammar path is left raw
  (JSON). +3 unit tests.
- **T026 — draft capability** (`services/assistant/capabilities/draft.rs`, new):
  `run(...)` is a dedicated dispatch seam delegating to the capability-generic
  single-pass engine (`guidance::run`) with `Capability::Draft` — which selects
  the draft persona fragment (body prose only, no letterhead/salutation/signature),
  the larger `gen_reserve_draft` (FR-013), and suppresses the offer-to-tailor. +3
  unit tests (draft fragment present, no offer, reserve larger than QA).
- **T027 — `export_draft` command** (`commands/assistant.rs`): fetches the persisted
  assistant turn by `(conversation_id, message_id)` and renders it to plain text by
  wrapping the prose in a single `Block::Prose` → `drafting::export::draft_to_text`
  (reuse, no letterhead/signature, FR-022). `TurnResponse` gains a `message_id`
  field (stamped after persistence); `memory::append_turn` now returns `(seq, id)`.
- **T029 — `model_status` command** (`commands/assistant.rs` + `ModelSlot::window_info`
  in `llm.rs`, real + non-llm stub): returns `{ model_file, n_ctx, trained_ctx,
  ram_clamped, source }`. `window_info` loads (caches) the active model, reads
  `n_ctx_train()`, and runs the RAM/VRAM clamp (`n_ctx::for_model`); `source` is
  `ECHO_N_CTX` when overridden else `auto`; `ram_clamped` = resolved < trained and
  not overridden (FR-019/FR-010).
- **T030 — retire the legacy drafting path** (`lib.rs`, `commands/mod.rs`, frontend):
  removed all `drafting::*` (Feature 009) and `one_ask::*` (Feature 010) command
  registrations + the `DraftSessions` managed state, and dropped the
  `commands::{drafting,one_ask}` modules from compilation. The command files +
  `services::drafting` tables/services are left **dormant on disk** per the additive
  policy (the citation gate and `export.rs` were extracted and are reused). Frontend:
  deleted `pages/Drafting.tsx`, `components/drafting/*`, `api/{drafting,oneAsk}.ts`,
  `stores/{drafting,oneAsk,oneAsk.test}.ts`; **`ChatPage` is now the single `/`
  surface** (was unrouted) and the `/drafting` route + nav button are gone. Added an
  "Copy draft as plain text" button on draft turns and a model-status line in the
  chat header (`api/assistant.ts` gains `exportDraft`/`modelStatus`/`ModelStatus`).
- **T031/T051 — acceptance gates** (`tests/bureaucrat_chat_acceptance.rs`, NO live
  LLM): SC-007 asserts a larger window retains ≥ as much law + history (and strictly
  more of one) while the gated answer/flags are unchanged; FR-020 runs an
  in/out-of-corpus set under two windows (model proxies) and asserts the gate verdict
  (verbatim kept, ungrounded flagged + offer-to-index, prose re-gates clean) is
  byte-identical regardless of model. Windows are passed directly to the allocator

**Verification**: `cargo build --lib` clean (only pre-existing dead-code warnings,
now incl. dormant one-ask `lexical_query`). `cargo test --lib assistant::` 47/0
(+3 draft); `cargo test --lib strip_reasoning` 3/0; `cargo test --test
bureaucrat_chat_acceptance` 8/0 (+2). `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 errors.

**Follow-ups**: Phase 5 (T032–T037) needs the F013 rebase (amendment provenance) +

## 2026-06-21 — Feature 015 Phase 3 — Grounded no-truncation MVP (T016–T024)

**What**: shipped the F015 MVP — the single-pass **guidance** capability with
general-answer-first + offer-to-tailor, model-independent ungrounded-claim
**suppression**, and the four P1 acceptance gates (SC-001/002/003/005). Phase 2
wired one guidance turn inline in the command; Phase 3 extracts it into a real
capability handler and proves the hardest invariants without a live model.

**Why**: this is the product (US1/US2/US3). A grounded answer on turn one, zero
fabricated citations, and a provable no-truncation guarantee are the contract;
everything in Phases 4–7 rides on this MVP.

**Changes**:
- **T018 — citation-gate suppression** (`services/assistant/citation_gate.rs`):
  new `redact_ungrounded(answer, context)` splits prose into sentences and drops
  any sentence asserting a provision the retrieved context does not support
  verbatim, returning the cleaned answer + the suppressed refs. The shipped prose
  re-gates clean by construction — even a weak/hot-swapped model cannot leak a
  fabricated citation (FR-006/FR-007). `assemble_response` (`mod.rs`) now routes
  through it (universal across all capabilities per FR-005c) instead of only
  flagging. +2 gate unit tests.
- **T016/T017/T019 — guidance capability** (`services/assistant/capabilities/{mod,guidance}.rs`,
  new): `system_prompt(cfg, cap, compact)` = persona + capability fragment +
  the existing `GROUNDING_SYSTEM_PROMPT` (the `[n]` citation machinery is kept
  verbatim so retrieval-side citations still resolve); `build_response(...)` runs
  the gate + assembler with offer-to-tailor only for `Guidance`; `run(...)` is the
  async single-pass orchestration (retrieve+generate via
  `route_scoped_with_override` → allocate → gate → assemble), streaming
  `assistant://progress`. It serves **every** capability for now (the Phase-3
  bridge) — specialised draft/map-reduce handlers replace specific caps in later
  phases. 5 unit tests.
- **command dispatch** (`commands/assistant.rs`): `send_message` is now a thin
  dispatcher — classify → persist user turn → load persona+memory → build history
  → `guidance::run(...)` → persist assistant turn. The inline retrieve/allocate/
  gate body moved into the handler; behaviour change vs Phase 2 is that the turn
  now uses the **bureaucrat system prompt** (persona + guidance fragment) instead
  of the bare auto prompt.
- **T020 — frontend**: already satisfied by Phase 2's `ChatPage.tsx` (renders
  offer-to-tailor, ungrounded flags + offer-to-index, context-fill meter); no
  change needed.
- **T021–T024 — acceptance gates** (`tests/bureaucrat_chat_acceptance.rs`, new,
  NO live LLM): SC-003 stress conversation (200 turns × 6 provisions) asserts
  `Σ prompt + reserve ≤ window` every turn; SC-002 asserts retrieved provisions
  are atomic (whole or wholly absent, never sliced) + law-outranks-history; SC-001
  asserts in-corpus answers keep every ref and out-of-corpus answers flag + emit
  zero fabrications (shipped prose re-gates clean); SC-005 asserts a complete
  cited answer + offer-to-tailor on turn one with no clarifying-question gate.

**Verification**: `cargo build --lib` clean (pre-existing dead-code warnings only).
`cargo test --lib assistant::` 44/0 (was 37; +5 guidance +2 gate). `cargo test
--test bureaucrat_chat_acceptance` 6/0.

## 2026-06-21 — Feature 015 Phase 2 — Foundational spine (T004/T008/T011–T015)

**What**: completed the F015 foundational spine — the unified bureaucrat chat
assistant now round-trips a guidance turn end-to-end (classify → retrieve →
allocate → generate → gate → assemble) on one conversational surface, with an
audited budget plan proving `Σ prompt + reserve ≤ window`.

**Why**: Phase 2 is the BLOCKING shared spine for all F015 stories (MVP guidance,
drafting, summarize, compare/conflict, action items). Phases 3–7 ride on top.

**Changes**:

  for everyone — re-run the 22-prompt eval if oversized TOC/cover chunks resurface

  Explicit non-zero values pass through untouched, so every legacy call-site keeps
  its exact behaviour. With the allocator guaranteeing fit pre-generation, the
  head+tail truncation becomes the unreachable safety net.
- **T012 — persona config** (`services/assistant/persona.rs`, new): typed loader

  `load_for_turn` (recent turns most-recent-first + running summary) and

- **T004** (`commands/assistant.rs` + registration in `commands/mod.rs` + `lib.rs`).
- **T015 — frontend** (`src/api/assistant.ts` + `src/pages/ChatPage.tsx`, new):

## 2026-06-21 — Feature 013 Phase 9b — PaddleOCR scan sidecar (opt-in)

**What**: an optional, indexing-time, deterministic (NO LLM) OCR path that runs **PaddleOCR**
(3.7.0) instead of tesseract on scanned PDFs. Replaces the Tier-3 tesseract call when opted in.
**ON by default**; `ECHO_PADDLE_OCR=0` opts out. Safe as default-on because it ALSO requires the
sidecar venv (`available()`) — machines without it use tesseract — and the OCR tier only fires for
genuinely scanned docs. Tesseract stays the fallback on any failure. (CPU ~1.7 min/page; the GPU
server is fast.) Flipped to default-on per user request 2026-06-21.

**Why**: the spike (`~/Desktop/modular_diagnosis/03_paddleocr_spike`) proved tesseract **invents
numbers** on scans (`Nov. 02, 2013` → `2613`; `02, 2013` → `7013`) — the root cause of the corpus
false citation "Section 20413". PaddleOCR reads them correctly. Confirmed live this session:
page 3 read `Nov. 02, 2013` ✓, page 7 read `02, 2013` (not `7013`) ✓, mean_conf 0.98–0.99.

**Decisions** (user, 2026-06-20/21): scope = 9b now; runtime = **Python venv, NOT frozen** (Paddle
is heavy + finicky to freeze, and the IBA GPU server — where OCR belongs — runs Python directly, so
freezing buys nothing; freezing stays an optional escape hatch for off-server distribution).
GPU auto-detected (CPU here). Rust owns rasterisation (reuses the existing `pdftoppm` path);
sidecar receives page PNGs.

**Files**:
- `src-tauri/sidecars/ingestion-sidecar/ingestion_sidecar.py` — new `ocr` op: PaddleOCR over page
  images → per-page `{text, mean_conf}`. **`enable_mkldnn=False`** dodges the PaddlePaddle 3.x
  oneDNN/PIR crash (`ConvertPirAttribute2RuntimeAttribute`) — the env var `FLAGS_use_mkldnn=0` is
  NOT honoured by the 3.x PIR executor; the **constructor kwarg is** (key finding). Doc-orientation/
  unwarping/textline-orientation sub-models disabled (faster, unneeded). Lazy paddle import → the
  frozen 9a binary (no paddle) fails the op gracefully.
- `src-tauri/sidecars/ingestion-sidecar/setup-ocr-venv.sh` — reproducible venv (paddleocr 3.7.0 +
  paddlepaddle).
- `src-tauri/src/services/parsers/ocr_sidecar.rs` — Rust client: discover venv python
  (`ECHO_OCR_PYTHON`, else `~/.cache/echo-ocr-venv-build/.ocr-venv/bin/python`) + script
  (`ECHO_OCR_SIDECAR_SCRIPT`, else in-repo), spawn `python script` with `op=ocr` + image paths,
  parse JSON, generous per-page timeout, every failure → `None` (→ tesseract fallback). `available()`
  gate. `#[ignore]` smoke test `smoke_ocr_images` (verified: 2 pages, conf 0.98–0.99, reads `2013`).
- `src-tauri/src/services/parsers/ocr.rs` — `paddle_ocr_enabled()` gate + `ocr_pdf_paddle` (reuses
  `rasterise`, `extraction_method="paddleocr"`, counts low-confidence pages <0.80).
- `src-tauri/src/services/parsers/pdf.rs` — Tier-3 prefers Paddle when enabled+available, else
  tesseract; preserves the real `extraction_method` (was hardcoded `"ocr"`).

**Verification**: sidecar op end-to-end (JSON stdin→stdout) on scan pages 3 & 7 — correct numbers,
no oneDNN crash. Rust client end-to-end on rasterised pages — reads `2013`, conf 0.98–0.99,
~1.9 min/page. `cargo test --lib` 533/0, 2 ignored (manual harnesses).

**Follow-ups / deferred**: full-document app re-index with `ECHO_PADDLE_OCR=1` on doc 04 (user step);
GPU paddlepaddle build on the IBA server for speed; low-confidence → `label_status='unresolved'`
chunk flag (mean_conf is captured + logged, but not yet threaded to per-chunk flagging);
PP-Structure for scanned *tables*; reading-order sort of PaddleOCR lines (currently detection order).

## 2026-06-20 — Feature 013 Phase 9a — pdfplumber table sidecar (digital PDFs)

**What**: an optional, indexing-time, deterministic (NO LLM) Python sidecar that extracts
real table *cells* via **pdfplumber** (MIT), replacing the geometric projection engine for
digital PDFs with ruled/grid tables. **ON by default**; `ECHO_TABLE_SIDECAR=0` opts out.
Safe as default-on because an absent binary / no tables / any failure falls through to the
projection engine (a missing sidecar never changes behaviour).

**Why**: the table spike (`~/Desktop/table_ingestion_test/spike_results/`) proved that on
digital ruled tables pdfplumber returns correct cells where `pdftotext -layout` interleaves
columns into wrapped text the Rust projection engine must reverse-engineer (and sometimes
scrambles). pdfplumber == PyMuPDF in quality but is MIT (PyMuPDF is AGPL). See
`specs/013-ingestion-hardening/phase9-extraction-sidecars.plan.md`.

**Decisions** (plan §5): scope = **9a only** (9b PaddleOCR deferred); runtime = **PyInstaller
frozen binary** (user choice); process model = **v1 one-shot CLI** (JSON on stdin → JSON on
stdout); discovery = binary next to exe / `binaries/` (like `pdftotext`, no `AppHandle`); cell
format = **reuse the existing `linearize`** so the golden row format is identical regardless of
extractor.

**Files**:
- `src-tauri/sidecars/ingestion-sidecar/ingestion_sidecar.py` — `extract_tables` op: per page →
  structured verbatim rows + header labels + table bbox + prose `above`/`below` the table band
  (cropped by bbox y-bounds). One-shot CLI; any failure → `{ok:false}` so Rust falls back.
- `src-tauri/sidecars/ingestion-sidecar/build.sh` — freezes to
  `binaries/ingestion-sidecar-<triple>` with PyInstaller. **Builds on a NATIVE fs**
  (`$HOME/.cache/...`): ntfs-3g returns spurious ENOSPC on the data partition despite free
  space; only the final binary is copied back. Records `BUNDLED_LICENSES.md`.
- `src-tauri/src/services/parsers/table_sidecar.rs` — discover + spawn (`std::process::Command`,
  300 s watchdog) + `parse_response`; returns pure `table::SidecarPage`s; every failure path
  returns `None` (→ projection-engine fallback, never fails the index).
- `src-tauri/src/services/parsers/table.rs` — pure `SidecarTable`/`SidecarPage` types +
  `reflow_with_sidecar`: drops the `(1)(2)(3)(4)` enumerator, collapses single-populated-cell
  rows (spanning `Note:` / wrapped continuations) to a clean standalone line, strips the
  pdfplumber serial dot (`"1."`→`"1"`) so `linearize` re-adds `". "` (avoids `"1.."`), splices
  `above + rows + below` per page. Unreported pages kept byte-for-byte.
- `src-tauri/src/services/parsers/pdf.rs::maybe_reflow_tables` — when the sidecar yields tables,
  use it; else fall through to the projection engine. Now returns the **extractor name** alongside
  the rows (`"pdfplumber"` vs `"schema_anchored"`).
- **`reconstruction_method` provenance plumbing**: new `ParsedDocument.reconstruction_method`
  field (all 9 parser construction sites set it), threaded `indexer → structured_importer::persist
  → tag_table_row_chunks`, which now writes `chunks.reconstruction_method = $method` instead of a
  hardcoded `'schema_anchored'`. So after re-index, sidecar rows are tagged **`pdfplumber`** and
  projection rows `schema_anchored` — the sidecar's coverage is measurable:
  `select reconstruction_method, count(*) from chunks where block_class='table_row' group by 1;`
- `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` — registered `binaries/ingestion-sidecar` in `externalBin`.
- `.gitignore` — the 29 MB frozen binary + build dirs are ignored (rebuildable via `build.sh`);
  source + build script are tracked.

**Verification** (frozen binary → Rust reflow, 4 spike docs):
- Delegation: 75 tables / 796 rows, cells verbatim + schema-anchored
  (`"1. Creation of Post — To whom delegated: …; Extent: Full Powers."`).
- SPPRA: `extract_tables`→`None` (no machine-detectable tables) → projection-engine fallback. ✓
- Compendium: 29 tables / 82 rows; PC-I Manual: 63 tables / 373 rows.
- Tests: `cargo test --lib` 529 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored. New: 4 unit tests +
  `golden_delegation_p8_reflow` (drives the captured real p8 JSON fixture through
  `parse_response`+`reflow_with_sidecar`, asserts exact rows) + an `#[ignore]`d real-binary
  harness (`ECHO_SPIKE_PDF=… cargo test … -- --ignored`).

**Table-row tagging — segment matching (2026-06-20, follow-up):** live re-index showed the
sidecar reflows all rows (Delegation log: "796 rows across 75 pages") but only 146 chunks got
`block_class='table_row'` — 57 row-bearing `provision` chunks were missed. Root cause: the
structured tree-builder *fragments* a row across chunks (serial+description → heading, the
`— To whom delegated: …` body → child) or merges several rows, so the old whole-row substring
test under-tagged. Fix (`structured_importer.rs`): `row_match_keys(norm_row)` now emits the full
row **plus** its HEAD (before the ` — ` em-dash) and BODY (after) as verbatim match-keys, each
≥12 chars; `chunk_is_table_row` matches any key. Recovers the fragmented/merged row-bearing
chunks while staying verbatim-only (no fuzzy heuristics). Tests: `cargo test --lib`
(+`chunk_is_table_row_catches_fragmented_rows`, +`row_match_keys_drops_short_segments`).
**Live re-index result (Delegation):** table_row 146→**208**, leakage 57→**5** provision chunks.
**Whitespace-insensitive follow-up:** the last 5 missed because `normalize` keeps newlines, so a
reflowed cell joined with spaces (`in a case. Total …`, `Rs. 0.015`) didn't substring-match a
chunk holding the source line breaks (`in a case.\nTotal …`, `Rs.\n0.015`). `collapse_ws` now
collapses all whitespace to single spaces on BOTH keys and chunk content before matching
(+`chunk_is_table_row_is_whitespace_insensitive`). 2nd re-index: table_row 208→220, leakage 5→**2**.
**Body-cell follow-up:** the last 2 were long rows truncated at a chunk boundary
(`… Finance Department Govt.` while the emitted row runs on) / with inherited descriptions, so
neither full row nor full body was a substring. `row_match_keys` now also emits each folded body
CELL (split at the `; ` tail separator, e.g. `To whom delegated: Ombudsman`) as a key
(+`chunk_is_table_row_matches_truncated_long_row_by_cell`). `cargo test --lib` 533/0/1. Expect
leakage→0 on next re-index.
**Takes effect on re-index** (tagging runs in `persist`). Chosen over splitting each row into its
own chunk (user decision: keep chunk granularity, tag all row-bearing chunks — DB stays ~150
table_row chunks, each may hold several rows, none mislabeled).

**Follow-ups / deferred**: 9b PaddleOCR scan sidecar (heavy: bundled model, ~1.7 min/page,
v2 long-running + progress/cancel, on-demand/deep tier); default-on for digital after live
re-index verification; borderless-table recall (pdfplumber "stream" weaker — projection
engine stays as fallback); cross-platform frozen binaries (only linux-x86_64 built).

## 2026-06-19 — Feature 012 Wave D — Phase 1: Schedule-Aware Heading Suppression (Rule-N misattribution)

**Symptom**: in `09_Sindh_Delegation_of_Financial_Powers_2019.pdf` (132 rows; Compendium 8, SPSC 7),
Second-Schedule delegation-table serial entries (`3. Leases of land`, `17. WORKS AND SERVICES
DEPARTMENT`) were stored as `Rule 3` / `Rule 17`. The formfeed fix only rescued rows whose nearest
boundary was a Part/Schedule; most delegation rows sit under TOP-LEVEL `Part-II`/`Part-I` (DB: 201/162
chunks) — NOT nested under a `SCHEDULE` node — so a schedule-ancestor anchor would miss them.

**Root cause (structural, not lexical)**: each departmental table restarts serials at `1,2,3…`, and
the doc also has real Rules 1–37. A serial `3. Leases of land` is textually identical to a real rule
`3. Title`, so neither the bare-number regex nor `drop_out_of_sequence_articles` can reject it.

**Fix** (`heading_detector/regex_pass.rs`): `suppress_schedule_table_serials(text, &mut hits)`, called
in `scan_with_profile` after dedup, before the sequence filter. It splits the document into spans
between structural boundaries (levels shallower than Article — Part/Chapter/Schedule), and within any
span whose text carries a **delegation-table signature** (`is_delegation_table_context`: `To whom
delegated` | `Nature of power` | `Sr. #` | a TIGHT `(1)(2)(3)(4)` column header) it drops the
Article-level bare-number headings. The serial rows then attach to the nearest container (`Part-II` /
`Second Schedule`) — the desired fallback. **Discriminator is the table signature, not the schedule**,
so it works whether the container is labeled `Part-II` or `Second Schedule`.

**Why it's safe**: the signature never appears in ordinary rule prose, so main-body rules and
non-table schedules are untouched; the tight `(1)(2)(3)(4)` form (only spaces/tabs between) matches a
column header, not spread-out sub-clauses. Failure mode = fewer headings inside one delegation table,
never a false Rule citation, never an effect outside such a table.

**Tests** (`regex_pass::tests`): `delegation_table_serials_not_promoted_to_rules`,
`real_bare_number_rules_outside_table_still_detected`, `rules_then_delegation_schedule_suppresses_only_table`,
`schedule_without_table_context_keeps_numbered_headings`.

**Gate**: `cargo test --lib` = **489 passed, 0 failed** (was 484).

**LIVE-VERIFIED (2026-06-19, after forced re-index)**: Delegation table-serial mislabels (`Rule N` +
"to whom delegated") **158 → 0**; genuine `Rule 1…37` headings preserved (37 distinct, no
over-suppression); serial rows now fall under `Part-*`/`Schedule`/sub-markers. **Ops note**: the fix
did NOT apply on the first re-index — incremental indexing (`indexer.rs:504`) dedup-skips files whose
content hash is unchanged + status=`indexed`, so a chunker CODE change never reprocesses them. Forced
it by flipping the 3 affected sources to `indexing_status='pending'` (defeats the skip → `do_index`
deletes old chunks + re-chunks). Residual follow-up: rows land mostly under bare sub-markers
(`(i)`/`(b)`) not `Part-II` — safe (no false citation) but a candidate Phase-1.5 refinement (suppress
table-internal Clause/SubClause enumerators too).

## 2026-06-19 — Feature 012 Wave D — US6 formfeed boundary fix (schedule misattribution)

**Symptom**: after the Wave-D re-index, 11/12 `table_row` chunks still carried `Rule N` instead of
`Second Schedule`/`Part-I`. Not chrome (SECOND SCHEDULE rows are real provisions).

**Root cause**: `FIRST/SECOND SCHEDULE` / `PART-I` headings sit at the TOP of a page, immediately
after a formfeed (`\x0C`) rather than a newline. `scan_structural_boundaries` anchors with `(?m)^`,
which matches after `\n` but NOT after `\x0C` → the boundary was missed → the schedule's rows inherited
the preceding Rule's label.

**Fix** (`heading_detector/regex_pass.rs::scan_structural_boundaries`): scan on
`text.replace('\u{0c}', "\n")`. `\x0C` and `\n` are both single UTF-8 bytes, so every `m.start()`
offset stays valid against the ORIGINAL text (verified by the new test asserting the offset realigns).
Regression test `detects_schedule_boundary_after_formfeed` added.

**Tests**: single full build `cargo test --lib` = **484 passed, 0 failed** (was 483; +1 formfeed test).
Index-time → effect on the next attended re-index: schedule chunks should label as `Second Schedule`/
`Part-I`, not `Rule N`.

## 2026-06-18 — Feature 012 Wave D — US6 schedule boundaries (T038–T040) + chrome chat-exclusion (T028)

**Why (US6)**: schedule/annexure content inherited the PRECEDING rule's label (live: Delegation
Second Schedule rows tagged `Rule 27(5)` / `Rule 22(v)`) because `SECOND SCHEDULE` / `PART-I` were
never detected as structural boundaries. **Why (T028)**: chat retrieval (`query_router`) didn't
exclude chrome — only the one-ask drafting path did.

**US6 (`heading_detector/regex_pass.rs`, FINAL §C)**:
- `scan_structural_boundaries`: ALL-CAPS standalone-line lexicon — `(FIRST..TENTH) SCHEDULE`,
  `SCHEDULE/ANNEXURE/APPENDIX`, `PART-<n>`, `FORM <id>` — document-CLASS grammar, NO per-document
  keywords. The all-caps full-line anchor is the heading-vs-reference disambiguator: a mid-sentence
  mixed-case "…the Second Schedule…" never matches. Merged into `scan_with_profile`.
- Emitted at `NodeLevel::Part` (shallower than `Article`) so `build_tree_from_headings` opens a new
  container and `drop_out_of_sequence_articles` resets the numeric run; `resolve_bare_citations`'s
  nearest-named ancestor becomes the schedule → schedule content stops inheriting `Rule N`. Reused
  the existing `Part` level (smallest viable diff) rather than net-new node kinds. `titlecase_boundary`
  normalizes labels (`SECOND SCHEDULE`→`Second Schedule`, `PART-I`→`Part-I`).
- Test: `detects_schedule_boundaries_not_inline_references`.

**T028 (`query_router.rs`)**: added `AND c.is_boilerplate = FALSE` to all 4 chat retrieval queries
(FTS scoped/unscoped + vector scoped/unscoped). Chrome excluded from chat ranking; `table_row`
chunks stay retrievable (is_boilerplate=FALSE).

**Deferred (with rationale)**: T036 (cross-page row continuation — current page-break spill orphans a
cell tail to pre-prose, contract-safe/not-scrambled; re-adding cross-page state not worth regression
risk before the attended re-index); T041/T042 (curation — blocked on manual data; implement once the
re-index identifies residual fallback pages).

**Tests**: single full build `cargo test --lib` = **483 passed, 0 failed** (no regressions). Index-time
→ effect on this re-index: schedule chunks should label as `Second Schedule`/`Part-I`, not `Rule N`.

## 2026-06-18 — Feature 012 Wave D (US5 v2) T034–T035: recurrence DELETED → schema-anchored reconstruction

**Why**: post-re-index (T031–T033) proved the safety gate worked (confident-garble signature 121→2;
COLLEGE EDUCATION garble→0) but the still-present recurrence detector kept emitting
**column-garbled rows that pass the monotonic-serial gate** (e.g. `12. … — To whom delegated excess
over the amount for which not exceed ten (10) per cent.` and a numbered officer LIST reconstructed as
a table). The gate is a floor, not the fix — only reading the document's declared schema fixes
columns. Decisive datum: the Delegation header + `(1)(2)(3)(4)` enumerator repeat ~55× (one per page).

**Change (`parsers/table.rs` — DELETE recurrence, BUILD header+enumerator anchoring, FINAL §A)**:
- **Deleted** `detect_columns` (frequency/projection), `detect_continuation`, `line_aligns`,
  `take_header`, `starts_with_digit`, and the cross-page `head.cols` stitch loop. `reflow_tables_with_rows`
  is now a per-page loop (each Sindh schedule page re-declares its schema, so pages self-anchor).
- **Added** `detect_schema` (an enumerator line `(1)…(N)` whose preceding line is an N-cell header →
  column COUNT + LABELS), `group_cells` (header→cells), `body_column_lefts` (column left-edges from the
  page's serial-led DATA rows only — body cells are left-aligned so left edge = min cell-start; keep the
  N strongest clusters, **NO fractional support threshold** ⇒ the sparse Extent column survives and the
  over-split `(i)` cluster drops), `is_serial`. `detect_page_table` rewired: schema → anchor rows →
  body lefts → region-bound (serial-led + wrapped continuations, STOP at the first non-serial leading
  column = Note/heading/prose) → `build_rows` → `verify_table` → `linearize(schema.labels)`.
- Rejected (FINAL §G): deriving bands from header/enumerator x-positions — headers are CENTERED while
  the body is LEFT-aligned (page-8: `Extent`@495 vs body `Full Powers`@429), which re-splices Extent
  into the authority column. Body anchor-row left-edges + `col_index` is the correct reference.
- Consequence: a table WITHOUT a `(1)(2)(3)(4)` enumerator no longer reconstructs (falls back to
  `-layout`). Conservative + correct for this corpus; non-enumerator tables/lists → curation (T041) or
  a future enhancement. Cross-page row spill (a cell crossing the page break) currently orphans its
  tail to pre-prose (contract-safe, not scrambled) — proper row continuation is T036.

**Tests (TDD)**: `table_without_enumerator_falls_back` written RED (recurrence wrongly reconstructed
it), now GREEN. `real_delegation_page8_reconstructs_first_row` (verbatim page-8 geometry) passes under
schema-anchoring. `each_page_self_anchors_with_repeated_header` replaces the deleted cross-page-stitch
test. `heading_inside_table_band` + `non_monotonic_serials` now carry enumerators so they exercise
`verify_table` (not the no-schema path). `cargo test --lib parsers::table` = **8/8**; full lib compiles.
Index-time → next re-index should reconstruct Delegation schedule rows correctly and drop the
recurrence column-garble.

## 2026-06-18 — Feature 012 Wave D (US5 v2) T033: table-row provenance / visibility

**Why**: `reconstruction_method` was null for all 5929 chunks — we couldn't measure which chunks
came from table reflow, so we were blind to coverage/regressions. The reflow runs inline in
`pdf.rs` (text replacement), so provenance was lost before persist.

**Change (rewrite-stable, normalize-safe — touches 8 files, no migration)**:
- `parsers/table.rs`: `reflow_tables_with_rows(words, layout) -> (String, Vec<String>)` returns the
  emitted verbatim row lines; `reflow_tables` kept as a `.0` wrapper (7 existing tests unchanged).
- `parsers/mod.rs`: new `ParsedDocument.reconstructed_rows: Vec<String>`; populated on the pdftotext
  reflow path (`pdf.rs`), `Vec::new()` on every other constructor (lopdf/ocr/ocr_skipped/image/
  audio_video/text/document).
- `pdf.rs`: `maybe_reflow_tables` now returns `(String, Vec<String>)`.
- `structured_importer.rs`: `persist(.., reconstructed_rows: &[String])` → `tag_table_row_chunks`
  marks chunks `block_class='table_row'` + `reconstruction_method='schema_anchored'` (UPDATE mirrors
  `persist_chrome_chunks`). Match is a verbatim substring of the **normalized** row in the chunk
  content (reflow runs pre-normalize; rows ≥12 chars to avoid prose collisions). Tagged rows stay
  **retrievable** (NOT boilerplate) — they are real, citable content.
- `indexer.rs`: passes `&parsed.reconstructed_rows` to persist.

**Tests (TDD)**: pure `chunk_is_table_row_matches_emitted_row_verbatim` (verbatim match hits its
chunk; prose does not). `cargo test --lib parsers::table` 7/7 + classifier green; full lib compiles
clean across all 8 files. **Index-time** → takes effect on the next re-index (after which
`SELECT reconstruction_method, count(*) FROM chunks GROUP BY 1` becomes the coverage metric).
Design note: verbatim-substring tagging is deliberately rewrite-stable — T035 still emits row lines,
so this provenance survives the recurrence→header-anchored rewrite.

## 2026-06-18 — Feature 012 Wave D (US5 v2) T031–T032: table-reflow safety contract

**Why**: the Wave C re-index proved the recurrence/projection column detector emits **confident
garble** on the real Sindh schedules — NOT a missed reconstruction. Live DB: 121 chunks carry the
linearizer signature; rows scrambled (`COLLEGE EDUCATION DEPARTMENT — Extent: work`), section
headings linearized as rows, sparse `Extent` column dropped, schedule content mis-attached to
preceding rules (`Rule 27(5)`, `Rule 22(v)`). Full root-cause + tech-lead decisions in
`docs/US5_table_reflow_diagnosis.md`, `docs/US5_table_reflow_design_review.md`,
`docs/US5_table_engine_FINAL_DECISIONS.md`. Decisive datum: the Delegation PDF repeats its
`Sr.# | Nature of power | To whom delegated | Extent` header + `(1)(2)(3)(4)` enumerator **55×** —
an explicit, self-declared schema the recurrence model was needlessly trying to infer.

**Change (Wave D, safety-first — `src-tauri/src/services/parsers/table.rs`, pure, NO re-index yet)**:
- `reflow_tables` is now a **total verifiable function** (FINAL §B): a detected table's rows pass
  through `verify_table(rows)` before `linearize`; on failure the page run keeps its `-layout` text
  byte-for-byte. "A missed table is acceptable; a confident scramble is not" is now *enforced*, not
  aspirational — the old gate checked shape pre-build and never re-checked the output.
- `verify_table`: requires ≥2 rows whose col-0 is a strictly-increasing integer serial, and rejects
  any row whose cells absorbed a section heading (`contains_heading_run` = ≥2 consecutive ALL-CAPS
  ≥4-letter words; body cells are Title Case). Helpers `parse_serial`, `contains_heading_run` added.

**Tests (TDD)**: `heading_inside_table_band_forces_fallback` + `non_monotonic_serials_force_fallback`
written RED first (verified failing: heading folded into a row; serials emitted 1,3,2), then GREEN.
`cargo test --lib parsers::table` = **7/7** (5 prior reconstructions unaffected — they carry
monotonic serials + Title-Case cells, so they still reconstruct). Change is additive (new pure fns +
one gate call; no API change) → other modules unaffected.

**Cross-cutting / follow-ups (Wave D, tasks.md Phase 9–11)**: T033 tag row-units
`block_class='table_row'`/`reconstruction_method` (visibility); T034 **delete** recurrence
(`detect_columns`/`detect_continuation`/`head.cols` carry); T035–T037 header+enumerator-anchored
reconstruction (count/validation ← header+enumerator; positions ← body anchor-row left-edges — NOT
header x-positions, which are centered while the body is left-aligned); T038–T040 US6 schedule/
annexure boundary nodes + label-inheritance reset; T041–T042 manual-curation backstop. After T032
ships, the next re-index should collapse the 121 garble chunks to honest `-layout` fallback.

## 2026-06-18 — Feature 012 Wave C (US5) + US3: cross-page table engine + label≠content flag

**Why (US5/D1)**: the carried table reflow detected columns/rows per page and required ≥3
multi-cell lines per page — so a REAL Sindh table (e.g. Delegation of Financial Powers) whose
rows span the `\x0c` page break has too few lines per page and never fired ("R1 did not fire"
live). **Why (US3/D4)**: a chunk whose content starts with a provision number ≠ its label is a
silent mislabel; it was only warned, never flagged.

**US5 — Rust-native cross-page table engine** (`parsers/table.rs`, confident-only → NO prose regression):
- **Projection-profile column detection**: `detect_columns` now projects every word's x-extent
  from tabular lines onto the x-axis, merges occupied bands, and splits on whitespace gutters
  ≥ col_gap → column x-starts. Robust to borderless / multi-level headers (replaces per-line
  cell-start clustering).
- **Cross-page stitching**: `reflow_tables` detects a per-page anchor (strong ≥3-multi-line
  threshold), then appends rows from following pages via `detect_continuation(words, anchor_cols)`
  — a relaxed, column-signature-keyed parser that requires the continuation to start at the top
  and align to the anchor's columns. Repeated headers dropped (`take_header`); **continuation
  post-prose preserved** (never lost). Shared `build_rows` used by both anchor + continuation.
- Confident-only: a page that does not anchor (or a ragged region) keeps its `-layout` text
  byte-for-byte — a missed table is acceptable, a scramble is not.
- Tests: new `cross_page_table_stitches_rows_across_break`; existing single-page +
  prose-unchanged + too-few-lines-fallback preserved.

**US3 — label≠content invariant promoted to a flag** (`structured_importer.rs`, index-time):
- `flag_label_content_mismatches` sets `label_status='unresolved'` on any chunk whose content
  begins with a provision number disagreeing with its label (reuses `detect_label_mismatches`
  per chunk for the row id). Refuse-or-flag — never a confident-but-wrong citation. The full
  re-segmentation split is deferred (more invasive).

**Post-re-index fix (real geometry)**: the Wave C re-index showed the Delegation table still
garbled. Diagnosed against the actual PDF (`pdftotext -bbox` page 8): the Second Schedule has TWO
header rows — the column titles AND a `(1)(2)(3)(4)` enumerator sub-header — and `take_header`
removed only one, so the enumerator row survived as data (`"(1). (2) (3) (4)"`). Columns detect
fine (col3/col4 gutter ≈11pt > col_gap). Fix: generic `is_enumerator_row` (every non-empty cell is
a parenthesised/bare small number or roman numeral) dropped before linearize, in both the anchor
and continuation paths. Locked by `real_delegation_page8_reconstructs_first_row` — a unit test
built from the EXTRACTED page-8 coordinates (header folded, `(1)(2)(3)(4)` dropped, col-3 wrapped
cell + "Extent: Full Powers" verbatim). Chrome rose 362→696 across re-indexes but is correct
(genuine form-field junk: nomination forms with `____` fill-blanks, mostly Compendium); not over-strip.

**Tests**: `cargo test --lib` = **477 passed, 0 failed** (table 5/5 incl. real geometry). Both are
INDEX-TIME → take effect on the next re-index (Wave C), which also clears the cosmetic `label_status`

**Why**: the live prod DB (post-US8) proved the downstream boilerplate flag matched
**0/4277** — junk (mastheads, "P a g e", "Contact Us", form fields) was swept UNDER
real provisions and had already inherited their labels, so a label-based flag could
never catch it (it was the source of the ¶2 fabricated citation). The defect (D3) is
**upstream of tree-build**; the fix must be too. Plus D5: bare sub-marker citations
(`(i)`, `(d)`) cite nothing real. Feature 012 spec/plan/research drove this; SDD.

  lists, in power order: (1) cross-page positional repetition (digit-stripped key so
  "P a g e 3/4" and page-numbered running headers collapse to one recurring key;
  threshold `max(3, 40% of pages)`), (2) margin geometry (geometry-optional `y_band`),
  (3) form-field structure (`is_form_field`: fill-blanks/dotted leaders, email/URL/phone

- **`structured_importer::import`** now takes `page_offsets` and runs `strip_chrome` BEFORE
  profile/heading/tree so chrome never reaches tree-build; stripped blocks returned on
  `ImportOutcome.chrome_blocks`. Env-gated `ECHO_CHROME_STRIP` (default on). `indexer`
  threads `parsed.page_offsets`.
- **`persist`** writes chrome blocks as separate chunks `block_class='chrome'` +
  `is_boilerplate=TRUE` (kept, auditable, **excluded from retrieval** via the existing

  flag: removed `flag_boilerplate_chunks`/`has_provision_identity`/`dry_run_boilerplate`/
  `BoilerplateCandidate`. `parsers/boilerplate.rs` kept (unused) for reference.

**US2 — hierarchical label resolution (fixes D5, core)**:
- **`structure_parser::resolve_bare_citations`** runs in `build_tree_from_headings` BEFORE
  coalescing: a bare sub-marker citation is qualified by its nearest named ancestor
  (`(i)` under `Rule 27` → `Rule 27(i)`); named provisions untouched; no named ancestor
  ⇒ left bare (never invented). `is_bare_marker` helper (pub). 2 unit tests.
- **`structured_importer::flag_unresolved_labels`** sets `label_status='unresolved'` (+ warn)
  on persisted chunks whose `unit_label` is still bare — uncertainty as a first-class state.

**Migration `pg/migrations/003_chunks_provenance.sql` (additive)**: `block_class` (default

## 2026-06-17 — US8 (re-scoped): ingestion structural quality — tabular module + year-rule + boilerplate flag

**Why**: the prior "US8" (TAB band-aid in `text_normalizer`) was confirmed insufficient live — §3
Delegation-of-Financial-Powers still garbled ("11. Power to declare (i) Administrative Full powers.
motor vehicles") because `pdftotext -layout` discards column geometry and reads left-to-right, so a
wrapped cell interleaves its row. Plus two index-time data defects: 39 year-as-rule labels ("Rule 2017"
from "…Rules, 2017…") and 101 junk chunks ("Contact Us"/page markers) indexed as retrievable provisions
(the source of the ¶2 fabricated citation). Post-meeting roadmap (`docs/post-meeting-roadmap-2026-06-17.md`)
re-scoped US8 to absorb the former US11 data-hygiene scope so ONE re-index fixes all three. SDD, not TDD
(user direction).

**R1 — robust ingestion**:
- **`parsers/table.rs` (new)** pure `reflow_tables(words, layout_text)`: detect table regions from
  `pdftotext -bbox` word geometry (≥3 consecutive ≥2-column lines), assign words to columns by
  greatest-start-≤-x, group logical rows (non-empty col-1 starts a row; empty col-1 = wrapped
  continuation), and linearize each row headers-folded + VERBATIM cells
  (`"11. Power to declare surplus motor vehicles — Authority: …; Extent: …"`). Confident-only: any
  ambiguous/ragged region keeps the original `-layout` text (a missed table is acceptable; a scramble
  is not). Pure core, no IO → 3 unit tests.
- **`parsers/pdf.rs`** IO shell: `extract_with_pdftotext_bbox` + `parse_bbox` (XML→`WordBox`) +
  `maybe_reflow_tables` wired into Tier-1, behind `ECHO_TABLE_REFLOW` (default ON, `=0` disables for
  A/B + revert without rebuild); `page_offsets` recomputed from reflowed text.
- **Year-rule** (`heading_detector/regex_pass.rs`): `looks_like_year` guard in `scan_with_profile`
  drops a bare 1800–2099 `num` capture so no "Rule 2017"/"Section 2010" is minted (index-time mirror of
  the runtime `decompose` guard, which never saw stored labels). Real ordinals (260/25A) still parse.

**R2 — generic boilerplate de-prioritisation (flag-not-delete)**:
- **`parsers/boilerplate.rs` (new)** pure `is_boilerplate(content, has_provision_identity)`: structural
  signals only (page markers, email/URL/phone, low prose-content ratio), short-fragments-only, NO per-doc
  keyword list. **Provision-label-keep invariant** hard-returns false for any chunk with a provision
  identity. Deliberately conservative (keep-bias): dropping a real provision is silent + unrecoverable.
- **Migration `pg/migrations/002_chunks_boilerplate.sql`**: additive `chunks.is_boilerplate BOOLEAN
  DEFAULT FALSE`. `structured_importer::flag_boilerplate_chunks` sets it at persist time — **flags, never
  deletes** (reversible + auditable).
- **`drafting/retrieval.rs`**: `AND c.is_boilerplate = FALSE` on both lexical and KNN-hydration queries
  so flagged chunks never rank (scoped to the one_ask drafting path where the ¶2 junk appeared; general
  chat `query_router` NOT yet filtered — follow-up).
- **`structured_importer::dry_run_boilerplate`**: read-only would-flag list (id/source/label/snippet) =
  the FR-013b iv pre-re-index review gate; must show zero false positives before a re-index is trusted.

**Tests**: `cargo test --lib` = **451 passed, 0 failed** (was 441; +10: 3 table, 6 boilerplate, 1 year).

## 2026-06-17 — Fix perpetually-failing manual detection test (category error; product unchanged)

**Why**: `doc_profiles::manual::detection_matches_manual_corpus` failed on every full `cargo test --lib`
run for weeks and was repeatedly waved off as "pre-existing/unrelated" instead of diagnosed.

**Root cause**: the test asserted heading-shaped strings (`"1. RECEIPT AND DESPATCH"`,
`"1.2 Indexing of files"`) against `MANUAL.detection_patterns`, which by design only identify the
document *type* (Manual / Instruction / Secretariat / CHAPTER). A bare `"1. TITLE"` is a *heading* and
appears in Acts/Rules too, so it correctly is NOT a manual-detection signal — the test encoded a
category error. Product behaviour was right all along.

**Fix** (`doc_profiles/manual.rs` tests only): assert detection strings (`"Manual of Secretariat
Instructions"`, `"CHAPTER II"`) against detection_patterns, and the heading strings against
`heading_patterns` in a new `heading_patterns_match_manual_headings` test. Suite now **441/0**.

## 2026-06-16 — Heading-mislabel defect: Fix-1 detection + Fix-2 invariant guard + US8 tabular de-interleave (index-time)

**Why**: live drafts cited `Rule 54` for content reading `"55. Entry into Force…"`, `Part II(3)` for
`"50. Publication…"`, `Rule 3(i)` for `"2. Sanction of Director General…"` — the stored chunk's
`unit_label` provision number disagreed with the provision number that *begins its own content*.
Deterministic (metadata, not model) → a citation-grade data bug. Full corpus diagnosis written to
`docs/heading-mislabel-defect-diagnosis.md`: ~530 mislabeled chunks, **every one on the `rules` profile**
(Delegation 22%, SPSC 15%, Compendium 11%, SPPRA 5%); `act`/`manual` = 0%. Root cause: `rules.rs`
recognised bare-number `N. Title` headings only via 4 narrow special-cases; the dominant Sindh style
`N. Title - body` (single dash) and plain `N. Title` (`6. Language`) matched none, so those headings were
invisible and swept under the preceding `(N)` sub-clause, inheriting its label. `act.rs`/`manual.rs` each
carry one general bare-number pattern → 0% defect; `rules.rs` was the only profile missing it.

**Change** (index-time — requires ONE re-index to take effect):
- **Fix-1 detection** (`doc_profiles/rules.rs`): added the general high-recall pattern
  `^\s*(?P<num>\d+[A-Z]?)\.\s+(?P<title>[A-Z][^\n]{2,})` modelled on `act.rs:46`. High recall by design
  (also matches schedule form-fields `1. Name` and footnotes `3. Subs. Ibid.`) — filtered generically next.
- **Fix-1 sequence filter** (`heading_detector/regex_pass.rs`): `leading_provision_number()` +
  `drop_out_of_sequence_articles()`, wired into `scan_with_profile` after dedup. GENERIC, no vocabulary
  list: a Part/Chapter heading resets the run; an Article whose number jumps **far backwards**
  (`n*2 < max_num`) is a form/footnote restart and is dropped. The half-of-max ratio tolerates ordinary
  subsection jitter (`9.11` after `9`). Drops the `1. Name`/`2. Address` form cluster amid rules
  `149/150/151` without promoting them to fake rule headings (Compendium regression guard).
- **Fix-2 invariant guard** (`structure_parser.rs` `detect_label_mismatches()` + `log::warn!` in
  `structured_importer.rs::persist`): pure function mirroring the diagnosis SQL — flags any persisted chunk
  whose content begins with an `N. Title` provision heading whose number is absent from its label.
  Conservative substring test (`Rule 155` vs content `55` never flagged). Index-time warning + unit test
  assertion = a future doc that regresses is caught mechanically, not by a human noticing a wrong citation.
- **US8 tabular de-interleave** (`text_normalizer.rs` `collapse_columns_per_line()`): `pdftotext -layout`
  aligns table columns with space gutters; the historical blanket collapse of 3+ spaces → single space
  fused a row's cells into a false sentence (the live Delegation-of-Financial-Powers garble "…Full Powers
  within the allocated expenditure … item year"). Generic geometry rule: a line with ≥2 gutters that is
  **adjacent to another** ≥2-gutter line is a multi-row table row → gutters become interior TABs (preserved
  by normalization, cells stay verbatim, never fuse); every other line keeps the single-space collapse, so
  prose, the 2-space act.rs marginal-label boundary, and existing collapse tests are untouched.

**Verification**: logic for all three pre-verified in a standalone `regex_lite`-only project (seconds, no
monolith rebuild) against the real-DB line shapes; then `cargo test --lib` = **428 passed, 1 failed** —
the single failure is the long-standing pre-existing `doc_profiles::manual::detection_matches_manual_corpus`
(`"1. RECEIPT AND DESPATCH"`), unrelated to this change. New tests: 2 in `rules`/`regex_pass`, 1 in
`structure_parser::label_invariant_tests`, 2 in `text_normalizer` (all green).

**Follow-ups / risk**: US8 is **not yet validated against the real Delegation `-layout` bytes** (PG was
down at implementation; built the safe generic version that is a proven no-op on prose). After re-index,
re-run the corpus mismatch scan in the diagnosis doc — target **0** on every `rules`-profile doc — and
spot-check §3 financial cells live before trusting those citations. Build-ops: a stray rust-analyzer
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets` was running on the shared target dir and was killed first
(documented hazard) so the test build owned the target.

  Legal hints replace the dev-scheme phrase with generic procurement-method vocabulary ("procurement

  sanction") to stop the Dev-Manual bias and bias toward procurement-method provisions.

## 2026-06-16 — Secretariat-summary refactor, Slices 1–2 (style/structure + citation caps & single-section dedup)

**Why**: higher-ups' brief — turn one-ask drafts from a "legal/research narrative" into a Government
of Sindh secretariat summary (concise, ≤3 citations, no duplication, no filler). SDD artifacts:
`specs/010-one-ask-drafting/{spec,tasks}-secretariat-summary-refactor.md` (locked decisions:
D1 verbatim-compressed citations — NOT model-paraphrased; D2 generic domain logic, no keyword lists;
D3 one skeleton + type profiles; D4 structural now / precision after re-index).

**Slice 1 — style & structure (compose.rs, skeleton.rs, verify.rs)**:
- `compose.rs build_section_prompt`: replaced the writer rules with a "Government of Sindh Secretariat
  summary" style block — concise/formal/decision-oriented; bans advocacy, greetings,
  "we request/kindly/we humbly/we await/we appreciate", academic commentary, repetition. (T009)
- Non-Background sections get an explicit "Do NOT restate the proposal/urgency/departments" line; only
  §1 establishes the case. (T010)
- Prayer guidance → one sentence, no citations/figures (skeleton §5). (T011)
- Financial fallback when no officer figure: structured "met from the approved budget allocation …
  detailed cost estimates placed on record before issuance of the purchase order" instead of "to be
  determined later". (T012)

## 2026-06-16 — Root cause of garbled quotes + broken labels: lopdf word-fragmentation; prefer pdftotext

**Symptom**: after a full re-index on the rebuilt binary, live drafts STILL quoted garbled verbatim
("Procurements over **o ne** hundred thousand", "Form of contract is a draft contract **agr eement**",
"sha ll", "t he Authority") and showed broken labels ("Rule **2017**(4)", bare "(m3)"/"(1)"). US2's
`repair_spaced_words` (committed `68e05669`) was proven by unit test yet had zero effect on the corpus.

**Diagnosis (evidence-based, not theory)** — live DB query (PG port from `ps`, db `echo`) + extractor
A/B on the real PDF:
- The stored chunk for that provision is **exploded one-token-per-line**: `Procurements over\no\nne\n
  hundred thousand`. The fragments are separated by **newlines**, while `repair_spaced_words` only joins
  a **single space** (`&input[we..ns] == " "`). The US2 unit test used a space (`"o ne hundred"`), so it
  passed while never matching real data. The snippet renderer collapses the newlines to spaces AFTER
  storage → "o ne".
- That doc (`02_SPPRA_Rules_2010`) was extracted by **lopdf** (Tier 1). Running `pdftotext -layout` on
  the same PDF yields the provision **clean and whole** ("…over one hundred thousand rupees and up to
  one million rupees shall be advertised…"). Line-shape A/B: **lopdf 42% of lines ≤3 chars, mean 16
  chars; pdftotext -layout 2% tiny, mean 71.** lopdf is the root cause.
- The quality gate (`text_quality::score`) was **blind** to this: it tokenises across newlines, so a
  fractured page still tokenises into mostly whole words → lopdf scored `Good` (1.0) → `pdf.rs` returned
  at Tier 1 and **pdftotext was never tried**.
- Same root cause breaks labels: the per-line explosion wrecks heading/structure detection → bare
  "(1)"/"(c)" unit labels and "…Rules, 2017" mis-captured as a "Rule 2017" content prefix at index time
  (US3's year-guard lives in query-time `decompose`, not the index-time parser). **Labels deferred** per
  architect — re-evaluate on the cleanly re-extracted corpus first.

**Fix (one coherent thing: stop using fragmented extraction; generic, no document-specific terms)**:
- `parsers/text_quality.rs` — per-line fragmentation signal: over ≥`FRAGMENT_MIN_LINES`(20) non-empty
  lines, if >`TINY_LINE_RATIO_MAX`(0.30) are ≤3 chars → `Suspect` (score 0.35). Threshold sits in the
  42%↔2% gap. Gated on line count so snippets/fixtures are never judged on line shape. +3 unit tests.
- `parsers/pdf.rs` — reordered tiers: **pdftotext primary → lopdf no-poppler fallback → OCR → best-of.**
  lopdf kept (not deleted) as the dependency-free safety net for poppler-less machines; on any machine
  with poppler (which OCR already requires via `pdftoppm`) pdftotext now wins. Module doc updated.

**Cross-cutting**: index-time — **requires one re-index** to re-extract the corpus before drafts
improve. After re-index, re-evaluate (a) residual labels and (b) the off-topic-card / writer-gloss
issue seen in the 2026-06-16 live drafts (writer forcing irrelevant cards like the taxation-gazette
Rule 7(2) into the matter) on clean text.

**Tests**: `cargo test --lib parsers` 18/18 green (incl. 3 new fragmentation tests); no regressions.

## 2026-06-15 — Re-chunk extension Slices 2–4: Fix #3 lexical weighting (US5) + clean quotes (US2) + year-guard labels (US3)

**Why**: continuing the citation-grade re-chunk extension after coalescing (Slice 1). Three
correctness fixes, all generic (no hardcoded/document-specific lists), batched per the architect's
"one cargo test at slice end" cadence.

**Fix #3 — corpus-rarity lexical weighting (US5, FR-013, SC-007)** — `drafting/one_ask/research.rs`.
`ts_rank_cd` has no IDF, so a chunk matching many COMMON query words ("secretary", "department")
out-ranks the one chunk matching the RARE words that identify the provision ("contracting",
"distributor"). Split `lexical_query` → pure `lexical_tokens` + pure `select_discriminative_terms`
(drop df==0 and df>50%, keep rarest `LEXICAL_MAX_TERMS`=8) + async `discriminative_lexical_query`
(one corpus-DF lookup per draft via `unnest($1::text[]) LEFT JOIN chunks … plainto_tsquery`), wired
into `research()` once (section-independent). Graceful fallback to the plain token OR on any DB
hiccup so retrieval never breaks. **Formalized into SDD**: ranking was previously a non-goal — added
spec US5/FR-013/SC-007 + tasks T022–T024. (Was uncommitted "off-SDD Fix #3"; architect approved.)

**US2 — clean, paste-ready quotes (FR-004, T013/T014)** — `text_normalizer.rs`. New
`repair_spaced_words`: verbatim-safe intra-word-space repair that DELETES a stray single space
("o ne"→"one", "sha ll"→"shall", "Gov ernment"→"Government") ONLY when the two fragments rejoin into
a known word (`JOIN_TARGETS`, generic number/legal/governance vocabulary). Never changes a letter;
single-space guard means ≥2-space boundaries (act.rs marginal-label `\s{2,}`) are untouched; runs
after hyphen-join, before structure detection; idempotent; leaves clean text byte-for-byte. Two
legitimate adjacent words ("in formation", "the cat") are never merged.

**US3 — year-not-an-ordinal label guard (FR-006, T016/T017)** — `intent_router/decompose.rs`.
`provision_label` gained `looks_like_year`: a bare 4-digit number in 1800–2099 (no sub-letter) in a
heading is a YEAR ("…Rules, 2017…"), not a provision number, so it no longer mints "Rule 2017" /
"Section 2010" → returns None (caller flags/falls back). Real ordinals (3-digit "Article 260",
sub-lettered "25A", out-of-range "1500") still parse. (Hierarchical bare-marker qualification
"(i)"→"Rule 27(5)(i)" already shipped in `card_label`.)

**Tests**: new unit tests in all three modules (research.rs discriminative-terms ×2 already green;
text_normalizer repair ×3; decompose year-guard ×1). Single `cargo test` at slice end across
`one_ask::research`, `text_normalizer`, `decompose`, `structure_parser`. Tasks T013/T014/T016/T017/
T022–T024 done; T002/T004/T005 goldens covered by equivalent in-module coalescing tests. Remaining:
T008–T010 dedicated re-index command/UI (convenience — Index-Folder already applies the new chunker),
live gates T012/T012a/T015/T018. Spec/tasks: `specs/010-one-ask-drafting/*-rechunk-reindex-extension.md`.

## 2026-06-15 — Re-chunk extension Slice 1 (coalescing): coalesce_undersized_leaves (heading-path only)

**What**: implemented the small-leaf COALESCING pass that cures chunk fragmentation (the
confirmed root blocker — corpus median 41c, 55% <50c, provisions shredded into scraps). In
`structure_parser.rs`: `coalesce_undersized_leaves` — the inverse of `split_oversized_leaves`,
a post-order transform that merges RUNS of ≥2 adjacent under-`MIN` (default 120c, env
`ECHO_COALESCE_MIN/TARGET/HARD_MAX`=120/600/800) leaf siblings under the same parent into coherent
units (≤ hard_max), inheriting the parent's provision citation. Isolated short clauses and any leaf
≥MIN are left untouched; `/p{N}` paragraph-split children are skipped so coalescing never undoes an
oversize split.

**Key design correction during implement (TDD caught it)**: first wired `finalize_tree`
(split+coalesce) into ALL three finalize sites — that regressed the Constitution (2 existing tests
went RED: 361→356 chunks; Preamble `/p2`→`/m1`). Root cause: `parse_tree` (site ~147) ingests the
**clean, pre-structured constitution IR** and must NOT be coalesced; only `build_tree_from_headings`
(structured_importer path, sites ~376/470) carries the OCR fragmentation. Fix: coalescing runs ONLY
on the heading-detected path; `parse_tree` reverted to plain split. This is cleaner than the plan
assumed — fragmentation is confined to the heading/OCR path, so the cure is too. MIN set to 120 (not
the spec's ~300): Constitution clauses cluster 80–300c and a higher MIN over-merges them (SC-005).

**Tests** (one cargo run, build cadence honored): `cargo test --lib structure_parser` 18/18 green —
6 new coalescing tests (merge-run, boundary, isolated-preserved, no-regress SC-005, hard_max cap,
oversize-still-splits FR-003) + the 2 Constitution tests restored. Tasks T001/T003/T003a/T006/T007
done; T002/T004/T005 goldens, T008/T009 re-index command, T010 frontend, T012/T012a live gate
deferred. NOTE: the existing "Index Folder" flow already routes through the heading path, so a
re-index applies coalescing even before the dedicated T008 command. Spec/plan/tasks:
`specs/010-one-ask-drafting/*-rechunk-reindex-extension.md`. See `project_noviq_fragmentation_confirmed_blocker`.

## 2026-06-15 — Fix #1: lexical leg = officer subject-nouns only (drop section role-hints) + fragmentation root-cause

**Symptom**: a "direct contracting / sole distributor" procurement note retrieved only generic
Rules-of-Business boilerplate (Schedule V, Section 30/46/22/27); the governing SPPRA Direct
Contracting rule was never cited though it exists in the corpus.

**Fix #1 (universal, no hardcoding)**: `one_ask/research.rs::lexical_query` now tokenizes ONLY the
officer's sentence, not `section.role_hints`. The role-hints ("rules of business", "competent
authority", "approval", "routing") are generic governance vocabulary; under `ts_rank_cd` (no IDF)
they let common boilerplate outscore the officer's discriminative subject nouns. Role-hints stay
on the VECTOR leg (`section_query`). Test `lexical_query_keeps_officer_subject_drops_money_and_role_hints`
asserts the universal property. `cargo test one_ask::research` 7/7 green.

**But Fix #1 cannot rescue this query — and the live re-run proved why.** Trace (`logs/dev-…`) +
live DB query (port 41063, db `echo`) showed the Direct-Contracting provision is SHREDDED:
`"(1) Direct Contracting"` (22c), `"(1) and obtainable only from one source,"` (41c),
`"(1) certifies in writing the proprietary nature…"` (81c) — no single chunk holds the operative
rule. Corpus-wide: 20,817 chunks, **median 41 chars, 55% under 50 chars**. Tiny chunks →
meaning-poor, look-alike embeddings → non-discriminative vector distances (the earlier H finding) →
the only well-formed retrievable chunks are full RoB paragraphs, so every draft pulls them.

**Root cause of the fragmentation**: `structure_parser.rs` emits ONE chunk per parsed node
(`collect_chunks`), the parser makes a node per marker `(1)/(i)/(a)`, dirty OCR/pdftotext extraction
broke provisions across lines (over-segmenting), and `split_oversized_leaves` SPLITS big leaves but
there is **NO inverse to MERGE small leaves**. Design assumed clean structure (works on the
Constitution); the Sindh OCR corpus violates it. **Conclusion: retrieval tuning has hit its ceiling;
the cure is re-chunk + re-index** (coalesce small leaves → ~300–800c provisions + OCR/newline repair
+ hierarchy-label fix + re-embed). See `project_noviq_fragmentation_confirmed_blocker` (memory) and
the new re-chunk SDD spec. Fix #1 kept regardless — it is a genuine improvement for non-fragmented asks.

## 2026-06-15 — Fix: one-ask draft wiped on tab navigation (state moved to module store)

**Symptom**: while a one-ask summary was composing, switching to another tab and returning
wiped the whole drafting UI (progress, live writing pane, activity feed, finished draft) — even
though the backend job kept running. User report: "everything wipes out … running in background
but not showing in the UI."

**Root cause** (traced through all four boundaries): `OneAskView.tsx` held the entire run state
in component-local signals (`draftId`/`progress`/`view`/`busy`/`notes`/`liveSections`/`basePct`/
`tokenPct`/`startedAt`/`finishedAt`) and tore down its three Tauri listeners in `onCleanup`. The
SolidJS router (`App.tsx` `<Route>`s) unmounts the Drafting page on tab switch → signals
destroyed + listeners removed → every `drafting://one-ask-progress|complete` and `chat://token`
event fired while away was dropped. On return a fresh component mounted empty; `busy` is only ever
set by `submit()`, so the writer-token guard (`!busy() || stage!=="composing"`) silently discarded
the live stream. The backend job (`start_one_ask` detached `async_runtime::spawn` keyed by
`draft_id`, persisting via `state::save`) is decoupled from the webview, hence "running in
background." Same class already fixed for Chat (module store, rehydrate-if-empty).

**Fix** (frontend-only, no backend change):
- New `src/stores/oneAsk.ts` — module-level signals (survive unmount) + pure reducer functions
  (`applyProgress`/`applyComplete`/`applyToken`/`beginAsk`/`resetOneAsk`) + `initOneAskListeners`
  (idempotent, registers the 3 listeners ONCE at module scope; dynamic-imports the api wrappers so
  the module stays loadable under a plain Node test runner). Section-progress bookkeeping
  (`sectionBasePct`/`sectionSpanPct`/`sectionTokens`) became module mutables.
- `src/components/drafting/OneAskView.tsx` — deleted the local run-state signals and the listener
  `onCleanup` teardown; now reads from the store and `onMount`s `initOneAskListeners()`. Only
  UI-transient signals stay local (`copied`, ticker `now`). `submit()` calls `beginAsk()`.

**Verification**: `src/stores/oneAsk.test.ts` 4/4 (vitest `--environment node` — repo default
vitest env is jsdom which isn't installed; the store test is DOM-free); `tsc --noEmit` exit 0.
Live GUI tab-nav verification still pending (app + dev server were down).

**Scope decision**: user chose "just the wipe fix." Draft *history* (browse/reopen/edit past
drafts) is a separate, larger feature — the data is ALREADY persisted (`one_ask_session` mig 025 +
`chat_message` mig 023) and `state::list` exists in `one_ask/state.rs:167` but is NOT exposed as a
Tauri command, and there is no history UI. Deferred to a future SDD spec.

**Symptom/why**: 15-trace eval (rebuilt app, 0a active) proved two independent problems.

E14 2→20), spanning multiple unrelated docs, with marker numbers not matching the displayed
list and half-sentence excerpts. Cause: resolver re-matched the cited chunk's filename+page
against ALL retrieved chunks, and `page` is NULL corpus-wide → `(None,_)=>true` matched every
chunk of the document. (2) The 0.5B fabricates over CORRECT context (E03 ctx had "10,000
million"→said "30M"; E11 ctx had "10%" at rank 1→said "15%"; E14 fabricated quotes) — proven
model ceiling, not retrieval.

**Fix (Phase-0e, `query_router.rs`)**:
- `indexed_citation_markers()` — resolve each `[n]` to the EXACT chunk `chunks[n-1]`, 1:1,
  deduped, in order; renumber prose `[old]`→`[new]` to match the displayed list; drop
  out-of-range markers. Kills the 1→11 explosion + marker≠display.
- `citation_snippet()` — sentence-bounded (≥12 words, 220 cap, no mid-word cut), replaces
  `truncate(content,300)`. No-marker → top-3 fallback preserved (decompose path depends on it);
  legacy `[file,page]` path kept.
- Fixed stale `context_builder_token_budget_drops_large_chunk` fixture (chunks now ≥50c to
  clear the anchor filter; budget 400 so per-chunk cap doesn't pre-empt the budget test).
- `extract_indexed_citations` retained (tests) under `#[allow(dead_code)]`.

**Tests**: `cargo test --lib query_router::tests` 59 passed / 0 failed.

harness `tests/rag_eval.rs` (real FTS+vector+RRF+0.5B via `intent_router::dispatch`).

## 2026-06-13 — DIAGNOSIS (no code change): chunk fragmentation = RAG answer-quality root cause

**Symptom/why**: two live chat traces (saved at `~/Desktop/final testing/`) — one wrong
("Rule 2017 of the Sindh Civil Services Rules", a fabricated rule+source), one right-answer
but wrong-citations. Deep evidence-based investigation (live PG corpus + code) proved the
dominant cause is **indexing/chunking**, not the model/prompt/retrieval ranking.

**Findings (hard data)**: 20,817 chunks, **median 41 chars**, 73% <100 chars, 55% <50 chars;
`06_Manual…PC-I.pdf` = 7,964 chunks @ 56 chars avg. A single provision ("…competent to approve
development projects costing up to **Rs. 10,000 million, provided no external funding**") is
shredded across 6 chunks (idx 962–967); the retrieved chunk stops at "Rs. 10,000" — "million"
is in the next, un-retrieved chunk. So the complete answer exists in NO single chunk. Hierarchy
mislabeled: `unit_path = Rule_2017/(2)/(e)` — a YEAR captured as a Rule. RULED OUT: question
truncation (ChatML puts question at tail `query_router.rs:1844`; `llm.rs:541‑555` keeps
head+tail; prompt 2364<2500 cap → not truncated; both answers on-topic) and model capability
(answered correctly when given the intact `Rule 4` chunk).

**Mechanism**: `heading_detector/*` over-detects (every OCR line/year → heading) →
`structure_parser::build_tree_from_headings`/`collect_chunks` emit one chunk per leaf; the only
size-normalisation is downward (`split_oversized_leaves`) — there is **no merge for undersized
leaves**. OCR newlines (`develop\nment`, `Rs\n.\n10,000`) compound it.

**Preferred remedy** (full write-up + acceptance criteria in `docs/chunking-fragmentation-issue.md`):
ingest-side re-chunk (OCR newline repair + heading-label sanitisation rejecting years/page-nums
+ a new small-leaf coalescing pass to ~300–800-char provision units) → re-index OCR PDFs; plus
