## 2026-06-13 — Draft quality Fix H (hybrid retrieval + anti-starvation) + F2 (money-figure canonicalization)

**Symptom/why**: H diagnosis (live log data, 30 candidates) proved embedding distance cannot
carry relevance — distances cluster 0.2475–0.3100 and irrelevant money-vocabulary neighbours
INTERLEAVE with relevant ones (forest-bond clause at 0.2696 beat a relevant chunk at
0.2764); margin tuning was a dead end. Separately, every remaining figure flag was a
formatting variant of a source-backed figure ("Rs. 10 million" vs "Rs.10.00 million",
OCR'd "Rs . 10,000").

**Fix H** (`retrieval.rs`, `research.rs`):
- `retrieval::lexical()` — `websearch_to_tsquery` over the existing generated `tsv` GIN
  index, same indexed/watched-folder filters as `knn`; `distance` carries `ts_rank_cd`
  (order-only contract).
- `lexical_query()` — OR-joined SUBJECT tokens from ask + role hints; money/magnitude
  vocabulary excluded (LEXICAL_STOP) — that exclusion IS the discriminator.
- `rrf_merge()` (k=60) — both legs fetch 2× the card budget; chunks found by BOTH legs
  outrank single-leg ones; vector margin kept as safety net only.
- **Anti-starvation**: cap consumption is first-come-first-served in skeleton order; a
  section whose every hit is already cap-consumed force-adopts its top hit (one bounded
  cap exception). Total starvation observed on the fixture corpus; live prayer-paragraph
  thinness is the same shape.

**Fix F2** (`verify.rs`): `money_key()` canonical figure key (numeric value + magnitude
word; f64 Display trims "10.00"→"10", commas/OCR spaces ignored). Applied to the
officer-figure check and a figures-ONLY card-backing path — provision numbers can never
pass via money backing ("Article 27" vs "27 million" pinned by test).

**Tests**: lib `drafting::one_ask` 46/46 (6 new), `one_ask_acceptance` 3/3 (fixture cites
re-mapped to post-hybrid assignments via temp dump, removed).

**Cross-cutting/follow-ups**: (a) next live run should show subject-relevant cards —
if misattribution persists even with relevant cards, narrow the F allowance to the
adjacently-cited card (contract decision); (b) `lexical()` is one_ask-scoped today but
seam-shaped for reuse; (c) LEXICAL_STOP is English+PK-money specific — revisit if corpus
language broadens.

## 2026-06-13 — Draft quality Fixes G+I + H relevance instrumentation (010 research/verify/compose)

**Symptom/why**: post-D1–F live gate run (2026-06-13) — large improvement (flags 17→7,
connective prose back, no quote >2 paragraphs, "Section 2.10" label proven correct) but:
(1) bare sub-clause `unit_label`s ("(1)", "(i)", "(5)") render without authority AND defeat
the Fix-F echo-allowance (prose "Rule 27(5)" flagged because the card label was "(i)");
(2) cap-cut snippets strand connectives ("…50 million to Rs.") with no cut marker;
(3) writer emitted a malformed marker "[FIG:x]" which shipped as literal prose;
(4) DOMINANT/contract-critical: irrelevant cards (SPSC forest-bond clause in a
schools-funding summary) survive the Fix-A margin, and the writer stitched a verbatim-backed
but WRONGLY-ATTRIBUTED claim ("concept clearance proposals over twenty five thousand
rupees") — semantic failure passing mechanical gates.

**Fix G** (`research.rs`): `card_label(unit_label, unit_path, content)` — bare "(…)" labels
qualified from the `unit_path` hierarchy (`Rule_27/(5)/(i)/p2` → "Rule 27(5)(i)"; `_`→space,
`pN` page-marker segments dropped); noun-labelled leaves ("Section 2.10") stand alone; no
named ancestor → content-prefix fallback → bare label. Repairs both display and F's
echo-matching.

**Fix I** (`verify.rs`, `compose.rs`): cap-cut snippets back off trailing connectives
(SNIPPET_TRAIL_STOP) and append a display ellipsis "…"; `quote_verifies` strips the ellipsis
before the verbatim check (decoration, not quoted text). `parse_markers` scrubs malformed
marker shapes (`[FIG:x]`, `[CITE:]`) from prose — never rendered.

**H instrumentation** (`research.rs`): every KNN candidate logged per section —
`one_ask research [Section] dist=… best=… KEEP/DROP chunk=… :: head` — so the next live run
shows exactly where the forest-bond-class cards score and where the cutoff should sit.
NO behavior change to retrieval yet; margin decision follows the data.

**Tests**: `card_label` hierarchical cases + cap-cut/ellipsis + sentence-cut-no-ellipsis +
malformed-marker scrub. `drafting::one_ask` lib + `one_ask_acceptance` green (see commit).

**Cross-cutting/follow-ups**: (a) H decision pending live log data — likely tighter margin
or lexical-overlap filter; (b) OPEN CONTRACT QUESTION: Fix-F allowance lets the writer
misattribute verbatim-backed numbers across cards in the same section — consider narrowing
to the adjacent quote's card if live runs keep producing wrong claims; (c) "Rule 2023"-style
junk anchors in unit_path are upstream (F007) and out of scope here.

## 2026-06-12 — Draft quality Fixes D1+D2+E+F (010 verify gate + research), DB-cross-verified

**Symptom/why**: live re-run after Fixes A–C still unusable; before coding, every hypothesis
was cross-verified against the bundled PG (`echo` DB) + the persisted `one_ask_session`
state. Findings: (1) the "same quote ×3 paragraphs" was NOT a dedup/cap failure — one chunk,
one card, correctly capped to 2 sections, but `verify.rs` resolved `[CITE:n]` against the
FULL card vec with no section check, so a hallucinated global id rendered a real card from
another section; (2) card labels came from `provision_label(content)` — content prefixes are
index-time prepends and can be junk ("Section 2010" = mis-captured year) while
`chunks.unit_label` held the real "Section 6.20"; (3) 14 of 17 flags were ECHOES — prose
provision numbers/figures matching labels/excerpts of cards cited in the same paragraph,
killing the writer's connective sentences; (4) 26 citation runs / 5 paragraphs, stacked
back-to-back = quote salad; (5) 1,271 duplicate-content groups in `chunks` are nearly all
<200-char boilerplate (backlog, not a draft-quality cause).

**Fix** (batch, user-directed single red-green cycle):
- **D1** `verify.rs`: a `[CITE:n]` whose card isn't assigned to the paragraph's section →
  Flag ("belongs to a different section"), never rendered.
- **D2** `verify.rs`: quote-stack collapse — drop a citation directly following another
  citation, and repeat cites of the same card within a paragraph (style drop, no flag).
- **E** `research.rs`: `card_label()` prefers `chunks.unit_label` (fetched with page_number)
  over content-prefix parse; `verify.rs::citation_snippet` strips the leading provision-label
  prefix from the quote (it duplicates `rendered_label`; falls back to full excerpt when
  label-only).
- **F** `verify.rs::foreign_number_in_prose`: prose numbers/figures verbatim-backed
  (normalized) by a label/excerpt of a card ASSIGNED TO THIS SECTION are allowed; true
  foreigners still flagged. Scoped per-section so cross-section echoes stay flagged.
- Acceptance fixtures updated to cite in-section cards (they predate section scoping;
  ground truth obtained via a temporary research-dump test, removed after use):
  legal→[CITE:3], financial→[CITE:2], proposal→[CITE:4]+[CITE:5].

**Tests**: 8 new in `verify.rs`, 1 in `research.rs`; `drafting::one_ask` 36/36;
`one_ask_acceptance` 3/3.

**Cross-cutting/follow-ups**: (a) empirical gate = live summary re-run vs the 2026-06-12
baseline (user-attended); (b) backlog: index-time content-prefix mis-capture ("Section 2010"
baked into chunk text — F007 stream) and ~4k duplicate boilerplate chunks; (c) F's allowance
uses normalized containment against section cards — if too loose in practice, tighten to
exact label equality.

## 2026-06-12 — Draft quality Fix B: short verbatim citation snippet (010 verify gate)

**Symptom/why**: T018 live draft spliced the WHOLE chunk excerpt at every `[CITE:n]` marker

  `citation_quote_stops_at_first_sentence_boundary`. `drafting::one_ask` 26/26,
  `one_ask_acceptance` 3/3.

authority; only the quoted span shrank. Queued next: Fix C (Flag runs at paragraph end),
then ONE live summary re-run vs the 2026-06-12 baseline.

## 2026-06-12 — Draft quality Fix A: retrieval relevance cutoff + section-reuse cap (010 writer pipeline)

**Symptom/why**: First post-port live draft (T018) was citation-safe but unusable: KNN always
returns the k nearest chunks NO MATTER HOW FAR, so off-topic provisions became citation cards
(Rule 39 disability compensation in a development-funds summary); and card dedup merged one
generic chunk into every section that retrieved it (same Rule 6 quote in 4 of 5 paragraphs).

**Fix** (`services/drafting/one_ask/research.rs`):
- `relevant_hits()`: relative cutoff — drop hits whose cosine distance exceeds the section's
  best hit by > `DISTANCE_MARGIN` (0.15). Relative, not absolute, so no per-embedder calibration.
- `MAX_SECTIONS_PER_CARD = 2`: a card may serve at most 2 sections; stops one chunk dominating
  the whole draft.
- Unit tests for the filter; `cargo test --lib drafting::one_ask` 24/24,
  `one_ask_acceptance` 3/3, `one_ask_knn_parity` 2/2.

**Follow-ups (queued, one commit each)**: Fix B — splice a SHORT verbatim snippet per citation
instead of the whole chunk excerpt (`verify.rs` `quoted = card.excerpt.clone()` is the raw-dump
cause); Fix C — collect Flag runs at paragraph end instead of mid-sentence. Empirical gate
after B+C: re-run one live summary and compare against the 2026-06-12 baseline draft.

## 2026-06-12 (T018 live gate) — engine password persistence fix + gate PASSED

**Symptom/why**: T018 live run. (1) First launch: engine setup EINVAL — app_data_dir is a
symlink onto NTFS (`home-overflow`); PG cannot live on fuseblk. Env fix (no code): real ext4
dir `~/.local/share/echoai-pg`, symlinked as `{app_data_dir}/pg`. (2) oomd killed the scope
at model load (pressure 79% > 50%/20s) — the 2026-06-11 prescribed root drop-in was finally
applied: `/etc/systemd/system/user@.service.d/99-echoai-oomd.conf`
(`ManagedOOMMemoryPressureLimit=95%`) + oomd restart. (3) Relaunch then failed
"password authentication failed for user postgres".

**Fix (code)**: `db/pg/engine.rs::ensure_running` — `Settings::default()` generates a NEW
random superuser password every call; initdb stamps the first run's password into the
cluster, so later launches must reuse it. Now reads `{pg_root}/.pgpass` (trimmed) when
present and sets `settings.password` before `PostgreSQL::new`.

**Gate results (SC-001/SC-002 first data points)**: 10 docs / ~20.8k chunks fresh-indexed;
DB write phase 1–20 s/doc (was minutes on vec0); store 278 MB vs 65 GB (≈230×). One-ask
draft end-to-end: research KNN 2.0 s (was 1678 s — ≈800×), 0 oomd kills, draft completed.
Startup warm-up KNN absorbs the 18 s cold-cache cost by design.

**Cross-cutting/follow-ups**: (a) draft QUALITY is now the blocker (010 writer pipeline,
NOT 011): raw chunk-dumps w/ OCR artifacts instead of prose, irrelevant picks (Rule 39
disability in a funds summary; same Rule 6 quote ×4), flags interleaved mid-sentence.
Verbatim/refuse-or-flag gate held (all invented refs caught). (b) T021 must detect
non-POSIX FS under pg_root and surface plain-language remediation. (c) ext4 root has
~9 GB free; full-corpus future may need a loop-mounted ext4 image on the NTFS volume.

## 2026-06-11 — 010 UX: ETA → elapsed stopwatch; "killed at 7%" diagnosed (systemd-oomd, not crash)

**Symptom/why**: (1) Live run showed "~500–600 min remaining" — the linear ETA
(`elapsed×(100−p)/p`) extrapolated honestly from a pathologically slow research stage; user
wants a plain elapsed timer instead. (2) Yesterday's live run "killed at 7%": journal shows
`systemd-oomd` killed `echoai-dev.scope` (119 processes) at 19:25:38 PKT — user-slice memory
pressure 57.01% > 50% for >20 s. NOT a panic, NOT kernel OOM, NOT the tauri file-watcher,
NOT battery (shutdown came 24 min later). The `run-dev.sh` scope wrapper with
`ManagedOOMMemoryPressureLimit=100%` does NOT protect: oomd monitors the parent
`user@1000.service` (Ubuntu 50% default) and picks the heaviest descendant as victim;
`ManagedOOMPreference=avoid` on user units needs systemd ≥252 (machine has 249).
**Root driver**: the vec0 KNN `MATCH ?/k=?` research queries took **1678 s and 1247 s each**
on the live 65 GB `chunk_embeddings` (log `dev-20260611-181141.log`, sqlx slow-statement) —
sqlite-vec 0.1.x vec0 is optimized brute force, not ANN, so each query reads the whole table
from disk → page-cache thrash → sustained memory pressure → oomd kill. T035's "research ≤15 s"
gate is currently failing by ~100×; the 281 s brute-force number was NOT fixed by the KNN seam
on real data.

**Fix (UI only this entry)**: `OneAskView.tsx` — `etaLabel` replaced by `fmtDuration`/
`elapsedLabel` stopwatch (`m:ss`, `h:mm:ss`); progress card shows `{pct}% · ⏱ {elapsed}`;

to Copy. tsc clean; drafting lib 70/70 + one_ask_acceptance 3/3 re-run GREEN (closes the
pending verification on commit 43ce1354).

**Impact/follow-ups**: (1) research-stage perf is now the blocking 010 issue — needs real
ANN/partitioning/pre-filter strategy (feeds the parked Postgres+pgvector pivot decision);

## 2026-06-11 — 009 Phase D fix: ingest parser rejects array-valued fields the 7B actually emits

**Symptom/why**: First live manual ingest of the real gold failed all 3 attempts with
"invalid type: sequence, expected a string" — refusal path worked (FR-010b, no schema), but
the model output was unparseable every time. Root cause (evidence: spike artifact
`~/Desktop/Noviq Documents reports/option_c_ingestion_spike_20260610/raw/mistral7b_freetext.output`
line 1273): Mistral-7B emits list-like regions (C.C. distribution lists, multi-line paragraphs)
as JSON **arrays of strings** (`"provision": ["C.C to:-", "1. The Section Officer…", …]`), but
`ModelProposedSlot` typed `label`/`provision`/`text` as `Option<String>` and the tolerant chain
only handled control chars + trailing commas, not type shape. The spike never exercised the
parser (output was read by eye), so this slipped through.

**Fix**:
- `services/drafting/ingest.rs` — `string_or_lines` deserializer (untagged string |
  Vec<String>, arrays joined with `\n` so the verbatim gate still sees exact source lines) on
  the three fields; new test `parse_tolerates_array_valued_string_fields` with the verbatim
  spike shape (RED→GREEN).
- `commands/drafting.rs::ingest_template` — on parse failure, dump the raw model output to
  `/tmp/echo-ai-debug/ingest_attempt<N>.txt` (F006 failure-dump pattern) — it was otherwise
  lost, making live failures undiagnosable.

**Verification**: lib drafting 48/48, lgd_ingest_gate 2/2, acceptance 1/1, full lib build clean.

**Impact/follow-ups**: none structural; next live ingest retry should pass parse — if the gate
then rejects slots, reasons surface per-slot in TemplateManager (FR-010a).

## 2026-06-10 — 009 Phase D: template ingestion rewritten — model-assisted segmentation + verbatim-verify gate (Option C, ADR-0012)

**Symptom/why**: The heading-heuristic `ingest.rs` produced **13 garbage slots on a flawless
real instrument** (gold-ingest diagnostic, GOLD_SPSC_age_relaxation_2025): letterhead/dateline/
C.C. lines became false cited slots while the real citations (Rule-6(c) SPSC Regulations-2023,
Rule-23 SCUG Rules 2020) landed in NO slot. Root causes: segmentation assumed headings (real
instruments are numbered running paragraphs); citations were detected only in headings, and the
provision regex required whitespace so hyphenated `Rule-6(c)` never matched; structural
boilerplate tripped the provision-noun check. Spike (2026-06-10, results at
`~/Desktop/Noviq Documents reports/option_c_ingestion_spike_20260610/`) proved Mistral-7B
free-text segmentation faithful; llguidance grammar hard-aborts; noviq_qwen3b paraphrases.

**Fix** (FR-010/010a/010b):
- `services/drafting/ingest.rs` — REWRITTEN. Heuristic segmentation (`segment_regions`,
  `is_heading_line`, `classify`, heading-token `derive_category`) deleted. New:
  `build_segmentation_prompt` (Mistral `[INST]`, copy-verbatim instructions),
  `parse_model_slots` (tolerant chain: bracket-extract → strict → control-char escape →
  trailing-comma strip; empty/unparseable = Err, never partial), `propose_schema_from_model` =
  the pure gate: text+provision must be verbatim substrings (whitespace-normalized), provisions
  matched **hyphen-tolerant** (`[-\s]+` joiner), category derived FROM the matched provision,
  structural boilerplate can never pass as cited (no verifiable number). Gate-rejected slots are
  RETAINED with `low_confidence` + `rejection_reasons[ordering]` (FR-010a — never dropped).
- `commands/drafting.rs::ingest_template` — now takes ModelSlot+tier; discovers the GGUF via
  F006 `mistral_builder::discover_ir_builder_gguf()` (cfg-shimmed: non-`llm` builds refuse);
  missing model or 3 failed parse attempts (temps 0.0/0.4/0.7, n_ctx 6144, max_gen 1536) →
  actionable Err, NO schema, NO heuristic fallback (FR-010b). Emits `drafting://progress`
  (extract/segment/verify/done).
- Migration `024_slot_provision.sql` (additive) + `Slot.provision_ref` (`#[serde(default)]`)
  threaded through `slot.rs`/`template.rs` (insert/select).
- Frontend: `api/drafting.ts` Slot/ProposedSchema types; `TemplateManager.tsx` shows verified
  provision + per-slot rejection reason; model-missing error surfaced verbatim.
- Tests: `tests/fixtures/lgd_letter_fixture.md` (synthetic real-instrument shapes; real gold
  stays out of repo) + `tests/lgd_ingest_gate.rs` (2 tests, no LLM, canned model output) + 7
  gate/parse unit tests in `ingest.rs`. Spike file `examples/option_c_spike.rs` deleted.

**Impact/follow-ups**: ingestion now REQUIRES the 7B on disk (`models/ir_builder/`) — one-time
~18 min CPU op, slot busy for the duration (Principle III). Manual real-gold ingest through the
running app still pending (T074 second half). ADR-0012 documents the decision; ADR-0010's
grammar premise flagged as diverged.

## 2026-06-10 — 009 Phase E: two-tier semantic gap coverage + officer-supplied facts (FR-019/FR-008a)

**Symptom/why**: `gaps.rs::category_covered` matched category tokens against doc **titles** →
~10–11 false gaps on the 8-PDF live corpus ("consultations" can never match the title "Rules of
Business 1986" though Rule 17 covers it; content is indexed, title-match fails). Fact gaps
("100 schools", "Rs 500B") were reported as "index a document" though no document can exist →
officer filled every field manually ("what's the purpose of AI?").

**Fix**:
- `services/drafting/gaps.rs` — REWRITTEN. `detect_gaps(slots, confirmed, corpus, covers, dest)`
  takes an injected content-coverage closure (pure/testable, no embedder in unit tests) and
  emits the two-tier shape: confirmed-covered → no gap; covered by indexed-but-unconfirmed doc →
  `GapTier::Suggestion{suggested_docs}` (one-turn accept); covered by nothing → `Missing
  {destination_folder}`; uncovered `fact:` slot → `OfficerInput` (FR-008a), never Missing.
- `services/drafting/mod.rs` — `Gap{slot_ordering, category, #[serde(flatten)] tier}` +
  `GapTier` enum; `GapResolution` gains `AcceptedSuggestion{doc_ids}` + `OfficerSupplied{value}`
  (serde-compatible with persisted sessions).
- `commands/drafting.rs` — `semantic_cover_map` (embed each category once via fastembed; one SQL
  per category: `MIN(vec_distance_cosine)` GROUP BY source over indexed+watched chunks;
  similarity = 1−distance), threshold default **0.45** overridable via `ECHO_GAP_COVER_THRESHOLD`
  (calibrate on live corpus, T082); `list_corpus_docs` (tier-a candidate pool, `tag_role`-tagged);
  `gaps_for` now embeds; `update_doc_set` gains embedder State; `resolve_gap` gains
  `acceptSuggestion` (adopts suggested docs, recomputes, returns updated set+gaps) and
  `officerSupplied{value}` (fact slots ONLY — rejected with remediation on rule slots);
  `render_draft`/`revise_draft(UpdateDocSet)` short-circuit officer-supplied fact slots through
  `render::officer_supplied_fact` (verbatim value, attribution `"officer-supplied"`, never Cited).
- Frontend: `GapPanel.tsx` three-tier UI (suggestion one-click add / missing folder link /
  fact-value input); `DraftView.tsx` officer-supplied badge (sky, no citation chip);
  `api/drafting.ts` Gap union + ResolveGapResult.
- Tests: 5 rewritten gaps tests (fake coverage closure), session round-trip for the new
  resolutions, render officer-supplied test. **All suites: lib drafting 47/47,
  lgd_ingest_gate 2/2, lgd_drafting_acceptance 1/1, tsc clean.**

**Impact/follow-ups**: threshold 0.45 is UNCALIBRATED — run the live-corpus check ("consultations
mandatory where applicable" must yield a Suggestion for RoB 1986; the ~10–11 false gaps must
collapse) and record the final value here (T082). `semantic_cover_map` scans all chunk embeddings
per category (brute force) — fine at pilot scale, vec0 ANN later. Frontend `Gap` consumers must
switch on `tier` (GapPanel updated; chat-driven Phase B will reuse the same shapes).

## 2026-06-10 — Re-index/retry of an already-graphed source fails with FK 787 (stuck at ~5%)

**Symptom/why**: Re-indexing/retrying the 10th Sindh Govt doc (`10_SPSC_Regulations_2023.pdf`)
hung at ~5% forever. Log (`logs/dev-20260609-233844.log`):
`DELETE FROM chunks WHERE source_id = ? … elapsed=2.9s` immediately followed by
`Folder source retry failed … (code: 787) FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`. The doc reached 70–80%
on its first pass, which built its legal graph / Pass-2 NER (`graph_nodes`, `graph_edges`), then
failed. On retry, `do_index` → `chunk_repo::delete_by_source` ran a **bare** `DELETE FROM chunks`,
but `graph_nodes.chunk_id` (and `graph_edges.{from,to}_node`) are FK **NO ACTION** (migration 014).
With `foreign_keys=ON` (schema.rs) the delete throws SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_FOREIGNKEY (787), the op
aborts, and the UI is left showing the stale early "clearing" phase (~5%). Sources re-indexed
*before* their graph was built had no `graph_nodes` → bare delete succeeded → bug only surfaced on
already-graphed docs. The correct ordered deletion already existed in
`commands::folders::remove_folder_source` and the startup-recovery paths (`lib.rs`) — but the actual
re-index path (`delete_by_source`) never got it.

**Fix** (`src-tauri/src/db/repositories/chunks.rs`, `delete_by_source`): wipe dependents in FK order
inside one tx — `chunk_embeddings` (guarded by a `sqlite_master` existence check, since the vec0
table is created at runtime and absent in migration-only test pools) → `graph_edges` (from_node +
to_node) → `graph_nodes` → `chunks`. Mirrors `remove_folder_source`. Clearing `chunk_embeddings`
here also fixes a latent orphan: every successful re-index previously left the old chunk_id-keyed
vectors behind (no FK, so no error — just stale rows polluting search). All three re-index call
sites (indexer.rs:254/694/800) funnel through this one function, so the single fix covers them all.

**Test**: `db::repositories::chunks::tests::delete_by_source_clears_dependent_graph_rows` — builds a
chunk + graph_node + graph_edge on an FK-enabled in-memory pool (the `fresh_pool` helper now sets
`.foreign_keys(true)` to match production) and asserts delete_by_source clears all three. Both lib
tests in the module green.

**Follow-up**: a source left in `processing`/`failed` from the aborted retry will recover on the next
retry once this ships (rebuild required — code fix, not a DB migration).

## 2026-06-09 — File watcher: startup folder reconciliation (add+remove while app closed)

**Symptom/why**: Dropping a PDF into an indexed folder (`~/Desktop/Sindh Govt Documents/`)
while the app was *closed*, then launching, never indexed it — `indexed_folders.file_count`
stayed 8, the file never entered `sources`. Root cause: the live `FileWatcher` is a `notify`
`PollWatcher` that, on arming at startup (`lib.rs` T052 watch-restore), takes a baseline snapshot
of existing files and only emits events for *subsequent* changes. Files added/removed while the
app was off are part of that baseline → no Create/Delete event ever fires. Startup did NOT diff
disk vs DB (it only re-armed watches, reconciled orphaned jobs, re-extracted *existing* sources).
The add/remove logic itself was already correct in the live watcher event loop — the gap was
purely "changes that happened while not running".

**Fix** (`src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, new spawned block right after the T052 watch-restore, before the
event-loop spawn): startup reconciliation. For every registered `indexed_folder`: recursively walk
the folder for supported files (`FileFormat::from_path`, skipping `~$*`/dot-files — same filter as
the watcher), query `sources` rows under the folder (`file_path LIKE '<folder>/%'`), then:
- **Removals** — DB rows whose file no longer exists on disk (double-checked with
  `Path::exists()`) → delete `chunk_embeddings` + `chunks` + `sources` in one tx (mirrors the
  watcher's Delete path so search/graph stay consistent).
- **Additions** — on-disk files absent from `sources` → `indexer::index_file` via the shared
  `__folder__<id>` notebook stub (the exact path the add-folder scan + live watcher use), with the
  same `BudgetState` back-pressure delay; refresh `file_count` + emit `folder:progress` after each.
Scope = add+remove ONLY (no content-change re-index — deliberate, per user). Runs once at startup
in a background task so it never blocks the window.

**Cross-cutting**: complements (does not replace) the live watcher — guarantee is now "add ⇒
indexed, remove ⇒ removed" whether or not the app was running when the change happened. `cargo
check --lib` clean (0 errors/warnings). Manual verify pending: relaunch app, confirm
`10_SPSC_Regulations_2023.pdf` + `11_Sindh_Civil_Servants_APT_Rules_1974.pdf` auto-index and
folder count goes 8→10. Follow-up: large folders re-walk every launch (cheap stat-only scan; if it
ever shows up on big corpora, gate on a folder mtime check).

  confirmed docs, current `blocks`, per-prose `prose_edits`, `gap_resolutions`, `finalized`) with

    cache AND `draft_session`). US3/US4 commands (`start_draft`/`update_doc_set`/`resolve_gap`/
    `refresh_doc_set`) rewired through them so drafts are durable.

    across a full re-render. (Old US1 explicit-source-ids command form removed; the acceptance gate
    uses the pure `render::render_draft`, unaffected.)

    newDocId?}` | `regenerateProse` | `editProse{text}` | `updateIntent` | `updateDocSet`. Enforces

**What/why**: Close the refuse-or-flag loop end-to-end. After the officer curates the set, the app

- `services/drafting/gaps.rs` — `detect_gaps(slots, confirmed, destination_folder) -> Vec<Gap>`,
  pure/testable. Coverage is judged at the CATEGORY level (clarification, not filename): a cited
  slot is covered iff the confirmed set holds a doc of the REQUIRED ROLE (plain cited → rules,
  `fact:` → case) whose title shares a salient token (≥3 chars, non-digit) with the slot's
  category. Derived from the slot's own category + the docs' own titles — **no hardcoded
  category→document mapping** (diagnose-before-code). Uncovered → `Gap { slotOrdering,

  - `refresh_doc_set(draftId)` → `{ gaps }`: re-propose over the whole corpus, `newly_added` diff,

    `refresh_doc_set` in the Tauri `invoke_handler`.

**Cross-cutting**: additive only; no schema change (sessions in-memory). `render_draft` unchanged —
its existing refuse-or-flag already realises a `proceedWithout` decision.

## 2026-06-08 — Feature 009 (LGD drafting): US2 template ingestion (format → proposed slot schema)

**What/why**: An officer uploads a format (blank skeleton OR filled example) and the app proposes a

- `services/drafting/ingest.rs` — `propose_schema(text, instrument_type) -> ProposedSchema`:

    (`Label:` form / ALL-CAPS-ish title / numbered outline) plus `heading_detector::regex_pass::scan`
    for legal markers (Section/Rule/Article…).

    a currency/amount/figure signal → **cited** with a `fact:` category (extractive from case docs,

    signal → **prose** (and flagged for review); otherwise fixed text → **boilerplate** (verbatim).

    tokens minus stopwords) — never a hardcoded mapping. Low-confidence regions returned in

    gold example as METADATA only via `gold::record_gold_example` (SC-007 — content never indexed).
  - Registered `ingest_template` in the Tauri `invoke_handler`.

## 2026-06-07 — Fix B (008): deterministic, title-matched provision number (citation-grade contract)

**Symptom/why**: V4 proved the 0.5B confabulates the article/section NUMBER even with the
correct labelled chunk in context — Q15(a) "Islamic way of life" had `[2] Section 31` in its
references and the model still wrote "Article 29" (all three facets wrong: 29/28/29 vs the
retrieved 31/32/39). Under the new citation-grade contract (copy-paste-ready summaries for
officials, 100% accuracy — [[project-noviq-citation-grade-accuracy-contract]]), a model in
the loop for *producing* a citation number can never be 100%. The number must be extracted,
not generated.

**Diagnosis finding that shaped the fix**: the correct chunk is NOT rank 1. Q15(a) refs were
`[1] Preamble, [2] Section 31, [3] Section 29`. A naive "read the top chunk" would still emit
the wrong number. So selection must be by TITLE match, with a refuse path.

**Fix** (pure helpers in `decompose.rs`, wired in `mod.rs::dispatch`):
- `provision_label(excerpt)` — parse the leading structural label ("Section 31"/"Article 25A")
  the indexer prepends to chunk content. `None` for Preamble/page-break fragments.
- `resolve_provision_label(topic, citations)` — pick the citation whose TITLE region best
  matches the topic's content tokens (stopword-filtered, ≥3 chars, no bare numbers); require a
  majority overlap; `None` when nothing matches (→ refuse). Chooses by match, NOT rank.
- `authoritative_body(label, citations)` — render `**<label>** — <verbatim chunk title>`.
- `NUMBER_UNVERIFIED` sentinel for the refuse case (rendered uncited by the existing merge).
- `SubQuestion.number_topic: Option<String>` — set to the facet ONLY by the enumeration shape
  (`split_enumeration`); `None` elsewhere (multi-article/two-facet provisions are already named
  in the query, so their number is already trustworthy). dispatch resolves the label for
  number-topic subs and replaces the model's answer body with the deterministic one (or flags).

**Head-noun rendering (user decision 2026-06-07)**: the corpus labels Principles of Policy as
"Section N" but they are constitutionally "Article N". Rather than relabel the corpus or guess,
the answer is rendered in the OFFICER's head noun with the original corpus label in brackets for
traceability: `requested_head_noun(query)` reads the term the user asked in ("articles" →
"Article"), and `render_label` emits "Article 31 (Section 31)" when the heads differ, or the
plain label when they match / no head noun was named. The number always comes from the chunk;
the bracket preserves provenance to the source. `authoritative_body(requested_head, label, cites)`.

**Cross-cutting**: only the enumeration sub-question path changes; all other sub-answers and the
single-pass path are unchanged. No new crate/migration. Tests: 43/43 `intent_router` (+8 over
baseline: label parse, title-match-over-rank, both other Q15 facets, refuse-on-no-match,
authoritative body, render_label with/without brackets, requested_head_noun). Output SHAPE
(extractive vs fact-locked prose) still deferred to the summaries discussion; current wiring is
minimal extractive (rendered label + verbatim title).

## 2026-06-07 — Fix A (008): slot extractor now captures EVERY separately-phrased provision (Q9)

**Symptom/why**: V4 eval — Q9 "What property rights does **Article 23** grant, and what
additional protection does **Article 24** provide?" did NOT decompose (`lookup · conf 0.78`,
single pass) → Art 24 answered wrong ("protection of minorities", which is Art 36). Root
cause: decomposition's multi-article shape fires on `slots.section_paths.len() >= 2`, but
`slots::extract` only captured `["Article 23"]`. It used `section_path_re().captures()`
(first match only) plus a sibling scanner (`additional_numbers_re`) that catches bare
trailing numbers in a list ("Articles 9, 10, 10A") but NOT a second, separately-phrased
head+number like "Article 24 provide".

**Fix** (`intent_router/slots.rs::extract`): iterate `section_path_re().captures_iter`
instead of `captures`, pushing each distinct "<head> N" phrase (deduped). The bare-number
sibling scan is retained but anchored on the FIRST match only (guarded by `first_match`),
so comma/and lists still expand. Q9 now yields `["Article 23","Article 24"]` → the existing
`split_multi_article` clause-split fires → two clean sub-questions.

**Cross-cutting**: `slots.section_paths` feeds detection, `build_intent_system_prompt`
multi-target clause, and `intent_headline` — all already handle ≥2 paths. Behaviour change
is limited to queries that name 2+ separately-phrased provisions (previously under-counted).
Existing slot tests unchanged (comma/and list, single article, sub-clauses, Roman numerals,
trailing-word guard all still green). Tests: 35/35 `intent_router` (1 new:
`two_separate_article_phrases_both_captured`). Fix B (metadata-driven citation number) NOT
yet done — V4 diagnosis found the correct chunk is not always rank 1 (Q15(a): Section 31 at
rank [2], Preamble at [1]), so Fix B needs topic-matched chunk selection + refuse-or-flag,
pending the citation-grade-summary design ([[project-noviq-citation-grade-accuracy-contract]]).

## 2026-06-07 — Feature 008: query decomposition for multi-fact questions (gated to small models)

**Symptom/why**: The 0.5B FT answers single-fact questions well (~9/15 fundamental_rights
V3) but scrambles multi-fact questions — Q15 "(a) Islamic / (b) local govt / (c) Armed
Forces" → 1/29/32 (correct 31/32/39); Q4 "two protections in Art 14" → "13, 36"; Q9 Art
23/24 → Art 24 half wrong. Proven NOT a retrieval/prompt bug (V3 traces clean after slot
Fixes 1-3) — it's small-model capacity on multi-fact synthesis. Full SDD artifacts under
`specs/008-query-decomposition/`.

**Fix** (new `intent_router/decompose.rs` + one hook in `intent_router/mod.rs::dispatch`):
detect a multi-fact question (rule-based), split into single-fact sub-questions, answer
each through the existing `query_router::route_scoped_with_override` seam **sequentially**
(Principle III — ≤1 model resident), then assemble with a **deterministic template**
(`merge_subanswers`) — no LLM merge, so facts/figures can't be re-corrupted.
- `decomposition_enabled(model_size, tier)` — capability gate: `ECHO_DECOMPOSE` override
  wins, else model param size ≤1.5B (read from `discover_local_gguf` label;
  `parse_param_size_b` is private, not called cross-module), else hardware fallback
  (no discrete GPU & <16 GB RAM). OFF for 3B+/GPU — they answer multi-fact natively.
- `detect_and_split` — three shapes: (a) ordered `(a)(b)(c)` markers (stem+facet, trailing
  instruction stripped); (b) multi-article via `slots.section_paths.len()>=2` (clause
  split with per-article template fallback); (c) two facets of a SINGLE provision (Q4/Q6)
  — Pattern A = count cue (two/three/both) + "concerning/about X and Y" → "What does {Art}
  say about {facet}?" ×2; Pattern B = "…, and its {condition|exception|limitation|proviso|
  restriction}" → main Q + "What {qualifier} applies to {Art}?". Shape (c) is conservative
  (explicit cue required) to avoid splitting ordinary "… X and Y" single-fact questions.
  Precedence: enumeration → multi-article → single-article-facets. `<2` subs or
  `>MAX_SUBQUESTIONS=6` → `None` (single-pass fallback). Each sub-question gets a fresh
  `Intent::Lookup` system prompt (clean single-provision binding).
- `merge_subanswers` — labelled blocks, global `[n]` renumbering, synthesizes a per-block
  marker from resolved citations when the model emits none, not-found parts verbatim/uncited.
  Merged citations mapped via existing `qr_citation_to_chat`.

**Cross-cutting**: additive — single-fact path byte-for-byte unchanged (decomposition
returns before the existing call only when gated-on AND a ≥2 split is found). No new
crates, no migration, no frontend wire-format change. Honours the shared cancel token.
Constitution PASS (III sequential, VII gate, XI citations preserved). Tests: 31/31
`intent_router` (10 new `decompose` unit tests; gate matrix, merge incl. renumber/
synthesize/not-found, enum split + boundaries, multi-article split + fallback, single-fact
no-split). REMAINING (manual): T017 in-app gate verification (small vs ECHO_DECOMPOSE=0)
and T020 — rebuild + re-run the 15-prompt eval (V4) to confirm Q4/Q9/Q15 flip.

## 2026-06-07 — Follow-up detector: intra-sentence pronoun false-positive (Q12)

**Symptom/why**: Q12 ("What are the Principles of Policy, and whose responsibility is
**it** to act on **them**?") was misclassified as a follow-up. STEP 3 of the trace
appended the PRIOR turn's keywords ("25A Article Constitution guarantee education")
to retrieval AND injected 2 prior education Q/A turns into the prompt — polluting a
fresh, self-contained question. Fix 3 of the Q12/Q15 diagnosis.

**Root cause**: `query_router.rs` `is_followup_query` flagged any query containing an
anaphora token (`" it "`, `" them "`, `" this "`, …). It could not distinguish a
pronoun referring to a PRIOR turn from one referring to a subject named in the SAME
sentence. Q12's "it"/"them" both refer to "Principles of Policy" intra-sentence.

**Fix** (`query_router.rs`): reordered so the continuation-prefix signal (And/Also/
But…) still fires unconditionally, then added `names_own_subject()` — true when the
query contains a capitalised content word (≥3 alpha chars) PAST the sentence-initial
token. When the query names its own subject, the anaphora signal is suppressed and
the query is treated as self-contained. Case-dependent by design (a fully lowercased
query names no subject — accepted trade-off; eval/officer queries are capitalised;
carry-over is retrieval-augmentation only). This fixes BOTH the retrieval keyword
carry-over and the prior-turn prompt injection (`query_router.rs:~1773`), which key
off the same predicate.

**Cross-cutting**: existing `followup_detector_flags_short_and_anaphoric` (anaphora
queries with no named subject still flagged) and `followup_detector_skips_self_contained`
both still pass. Tests: 3/3 follow-up green; `query_router` module otherwise
unchanged (the one remaining failure, `context_builder_token_budget_drops_large_chunk`,
is the pre-existing/known one, unrelated). **All three Q12/Q15 diagnosis fixes
(1 Roman-numeral, 2 instrument verb, 3 follow-up) now landed — rebuild + re-run the
15-prompt eval to measure the flip.**

## 2026-06-07 — Slot extractor: instrument regex swept the sentence-leading verb (Q15 "Identify …")

**Symptom/why**: Q15's system prompt also read *"… of **Identify the Principles of
Policy**."* — the instrument name leaked the imperative verb that opened the
question. Fix 2 of the Q12/Q15 diagnosis (Fix 1 was the "Article de" Roman-numeral
bug, same day).

**Root cause**: `intent_router/slots.rs` `instrument_re`'s `named` group is
`[A-Z][A-Za-z&]+(?:\s+(?:[A-Z]…|of|to|and|the|…)){0,6}`. Because a sentence-initial
verb is capitalised, "Identify" satisfied the `[A-Z]` start and "the Principles of"
satisfied the connector repetition, so `named` = "Identify the Principles of",
kind = "Policy" → instrument "Identify the Principles of Policy".

**Fix** (`intent_router/slots.rs`): added `strip_leading_command_verb()` — if the
`named` capture's first token is a known command verb (identify/list/explain/
describe/summarize/compare/define/give/show/tell/find/name/state/outline/discuss/
provide/quote/analyse…), drop it plus any dangling leading article (the/a/an). Wired
into the instrument loop before the label is built. "Identify the Principles of
Policy" → **"Principles of Policy"**.

**Cross-cutting**: also cleans the two existing instrument tests for free
("Summarize the Right to Information Act" → "Right to Information Act"; "Compare the
RTI Act 2017 …" → "RTI Act 2017") — both still pass. Tests: `intent_router` 21/21
(1 new). Follow-up: Fix 3 (`query_router.rs:235` follow-up detector firing on
intra-sentence pronouns, Q12), then re-run the 15-prompt eval.

## 2026-06-07 — Slot extractor: Roman-numeral class matched lowercase word letters (Q15 "Article de")

**Symptom/why**: On the fundamental_rights V2 eval, Q15 ("Identify the Principles
of Policy articles **dealing** with (a) Islamic way of life…") shipped a garbage
system prompt — *"The named target is **Article de** of **Identify the Principles of
Policy**."* — even though retrieval was perfect (Section 31/32/39 all in context).
The 0.5B then confabulated article numbers (1/29/31 vs correct 31/32/39). Diagnosis
at `~/Desktop/Noviq Documents reports/fundamental_rights_test/DIAGNOSIS_Q12_Q15_router_2026-06-07.md`.
This is **Fix 1** of that diagnosis (Q12's follow-up false-positive + instrument
over-capture remain as Fix 2/3).

**Root cause**: `intent_router/slots.rs` `section_path_re` was
`(?i)\b(article|…) ([0-9IVXLCDM]+[A-Za-z]?…)`. The number-token character class
`[IVXLCDM]` is for Roman numerals, but the **global `(?i)`** made it match the
lowercase letters i/v/x/l/c/d/m inside ordinary words. `"articles dealing"` →
head "articles" + `d` (matches case-insensitive `D`) + `[A-Za-z]?` → `e` ⇒ bogus
section path **"Article de"**, which `intent_router/mod.rs:155` weaves into the
system prompt. The sibling-list scanner `additional_numbers_re` had the identical
latent bug ("Articles 62 and **living**…" → "Article livin").

**Fix** (`intent_router/slots.rs`, TDD — 3 tests added):
1. `section_path_re`: dropped global `(?i)`; made only the head noun
   case-insensitive via `((?i:article|…))` (kept as capture group 1), and the number
   token case-sensitive: `((?:[0-9]+[A-Za-z]?|[IVXLCDM]+)(?:\(…\))*)` — Arabic
   numbers (opt. single-letter suffix like 10A) or **UPPERCASE** Roman only.
2. `additional_numbers_re`: same number-token rule; only the `and` connector kept
   case-insensitive via `(?i:and)`.

**Cross-cutting**: capture-group indices preserved (head = group 1, number = group 2)
so the `cap.get(1)`/`cap.get(2)` reads in `extract()` are unchanged. **Tradeoff**:
lowercase Roman numerals ("article iv") no longer parse — never used in PK
constitutional text, and supporting it was the exact source of the false positives.
Tests: `intent_router` module 20/20 green (3 new: head-noun-followed-by-word,
sibling-scanner-trailing-word, uppercase-roman-still-parses). Follow-up: Fix 2
(instrument over-capture, `slots.rs:35` grabbing leading verb "Identify") and Fix 3
(`query_router.rs:235` follow-up detector firing on intra-sentence pronouns), then
re-run the 15-prompt eval to confirm Q15 (and Q12) flip.

## 2026-06-06 (late PM) — Generation knob audit: prompt truncation was eating the question

**Symptom/why**: On the fundamental_rights 15-prompt eval, 0.5B models scored 0/15
with the answer at retrieval rank [1]; Mistral 7B fabricated its own question turn
(`[Officer] … [Assistant]`). Root cause traced to the prompt being **hard-truncated
to its first 1800 tokens** while every test prompt was ~2.35–2.44k tokens.

**Root cause**: `build_rag_prompt` (`query_router.rs`) places `Question: {q}` and the
`<|im_start|>assistant` cue at the **end** of the prompt; `infer_with_cancel_temp`
(`llm.rs:533`) truncated with `tokens.take(max_prompt_tokens)` — a HEAD-only cut that
silently dropped the question + answer cue. `gen_max_prompt` (1800) was also **below**
`CONTEXT_TOKEN_BUDGET` (2400): the retrieval layer assembled more context than the
model was allowed to ingest. Prior note claiming "1800 is display-only" was wrong.

**Fix** (3 changes):
1. `query_router.rs` Regular tuple: `gen_n_ctx` 3200→**3584**, `gen_max_prompt`
   1800→**2500** — the ~2.4k prompt now fits untruncated, with room for the 1024
   response (2500+1024 < 3584).
2. `llm.rs` `infer_with_cancel_temp`: replaced head-only truncation with **head+tail
   keep** — on over-budget prompts, preserve the system prompt + start-of-context AND
   the tail (question + assistant cue), dropping the MIDDLE of the context. The
   grammar/IR path (`infer_with_grammar`) was intentionally left unchanged.
3. `llm.rs` greedy sampler chain: `repeat_penalty` 1.3→**1.05**. A 1.3 penalty
   penalises tokens present in the retrieved-context tail, pushing the model off
   verbatim source text into paraphrase/confabulation — wrong for grounded answers.
   (The stochastic temp>0 branch used by the IR-builder retry loop keeps 1.3 for
   retry diversity.)

**Cross-cutting**: only the `Regular` query path changed; `Summary` path untouched.
Mistral 7B (tested under the OLD broken prompt) still synthesized the hardest
question correctly from real chunks (genuine RAG, not 0.5B-style confabulation) —
expected to improve further now the question reaches the model. Follow-up: re-run the
15 on Mistral 7B post-rebuild; reconcile whether `CONTEXT_TOKEN_BUDGET` should also
drop to ≤ `gen_max_prompt` to avoid relying on the head+tail safety net.

## 2026-06-06 (PM) — Indexer routing fix: DIRECT path primary, Mistral LLM IR secondary

**Symptom/why**: Indexing a normal text PDF (`fundamental_rights.pdf`, 143K) on
the fast tier stalled "at 5%" — process pegged at 125% CPU / 60% RAM, WAL frozen,
`doc_ir_progress` empty, `extraction_method` blank, 0 chunks after 5 min. Dev log
showed it loaded `Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3-Q4_K_M.gguf` and ran LLM IR generation.

**Root cause** (`src-tauri/src/services/indexer.rs` `do_index`): the Feature 006
Mistral LLM IR block ran **first** for `Pdf|Docx|Txt|Markdown|Code` whenever a GGUF
was present in `models/ir_builder/`, with the direct `structured_importer` (Feature
005) only reached on `SkippedBuilderUnavailable`. So text-extractable PDFs were sent
to a 7B CPU model (~min/chunk) instead of the fast regex path. This inverted the
intended design (user: "mistral is secondary, primary is direct") and the standing
note `feedback_llm_ir_only_pdf_scanned_images` (LLM IR for scanned/image PDFs only).

**Fix**:
- **Reordered `do_index`**: `structured_importer` (direct) now runs FIRST. The
  Mistral LLM IR block moved INTO the "not structured" branch as the SECONDARY
  fallback (fires only when `structure_status='failed'`, i.e. scanned/unstructured),
  then falls through to size-based chunking. Compiles clean (tauri-dev hot-rebuild,
  0 errors / 4 warnings).
- **Immediate unblock (no rebuild)**: renamed
  `models/ir_builder/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3-Q4_K_M.gguf` →
  `…gguf.disabled`. `discover_in` matches only `*.gguf` so the builder reports
  `ModelUnavailable` → dispatch returns `SkippedBuilderUnavailable`. Restorable
  anytime; safe to restore now that the reorder keeps direct primary.

**Cross-cutting**: applies to ALL PDF/Docx/Txt/MD/Code indexing, not just this doc.
Constitution JSON-IR short-circuit (`try_load_constitution`) is unaffected (runs
before this block). Follow-up: re-run with GGUF restored to confirm scanned-PDF
fallback still reaches Mistral.

## 2026-06-06 (PM) — Retest VERDICT: noviq 3B fine-tune shelved (retrieval confirmed fixed)

**Symptom/why**: 8-question in-app retest (Q9/Q11/Q12/Q13/Q2/Q17/Q19/Q20) of
the chapter-index fast-path on the `noviq_qwen3b_Q4_K_M.gguf` local generator.
Traces saved at `~/Desktop/Noviq Documents reports/20_constitute_prompts/Qwen 2.5:3B testing/retest results/`.

**Finding (no code changed this turn — analysis only)**:
- **The 06-06 retrieval batch WORKS.** Q11/Q12/Q2/Q17/Q19/Q20 all show *perfect*
  context fed to the LLM — chapter-index `IDX-P<part>-C<chapter>` nodes with full
  verbatim enumerations land in the top slots. Retrieval is no longer the bottleneck.
- **The fine-tuned 3B is the regression: 1/8 correct (~12%) vs the 70.6% anchor
  (a *different* generator).** Two disqualifying failure modes:
  1. **Format-mimicry** — model emits its own training scaffolding instead of
     answering: `[n] constitution_ir.json`, `Article IDX-…`, `---`, and fabricated
     `Question: What does Article …(a)(i) say?` continuations. Perfect RAG context
     does NOT rescue it; the in-context `IDX-` nodes amplify the pattern-copying.
  2. **Unusable latency** — 0.4–2.7 tok/s, 30–180 s/query (Q19 = 179 s).
- **Root cause**: LoRA over-fit to `constitution_ir.json` surface form; completion
  targets evidently included retrieval scaffolding, so it reproduces scaffolding
  rather than reading it.

**Decision**: Shelve the noviq LoRA as production generator. Resume the 17-prompt
eval on a known-good generator to prove retrieval now beats 70.6%. Full verdict +
retraining requirements (assistant-style targets only, no `[n]`/IR-structure leak,
grounded hold-out eval, latency plan) in `VERDICT_noviq_3b_finetune_2026-06-06.md`
next to the traces.

**Separate issues surfaced (not model faults)**: Q13 = DATA GAP (no schedule body
nodes — needs schedule-injection patcher); trace prompt display truncates at ~1800
tokens while actual prompts ran ~2400 (n_ctx=3200 approached on multi-article Qs).

## 2026-06-06 — Chapter-index fast-path + grounding overlap-rescue

**Symptom/why**: Re-test of noviq v2 (after the 06-05 batch + in-app re-index)
landed ~flat at the 70.6% (12/17) anchor, not the ~85% target. Per-question
diff vs noviq v1 showed 3 clean wins (Q3 State, Q4 Money Bill, Q14 NA
composition → current 336 seats) offset by regressions. Root-cause diagnosis
on the 17-prompt set:
- **Q11 / Q12 (chapter enumeration)**: the chapter-index DATA is correct —
  `IDX-PII-C1` lists Articles 8–28, `IDX-PII-C2` lists Principles of Policy —
  but hybrid retrieval ranks the WRONG index chunk to the top (observed
  Part II Chapter 1 → "Chapter 6 Fundamental Principles" confabulation). Pure
  retrieval-ranking failure.
- **Q12 also nuked by grounding** to "(No documents found.) (Some content
  omitted as unsupported.)".
- **Q13 (schedules)**: DATA GAP — IR has no schedule *body* nodes, only
  in-text references. Not code-fixable; deferred to a schedule-injection
  patcher.
- **Q17/Q19**: cross_compare / procedure → deep-tier gated (not built).

**Fix (this batch)**:
- **Chapter-index fast-path** (`src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs`).
  New `detect_chapter_index_citation()` maps enumeration queries
  ("Chapter N of Part X", or "Part X" + enumeration verb) to the synthetic
  `Article IDX-P<part>-C<chapter>` unit_label, with arabic→roman part
  normalisation (`normalise_part_number()`). Wired at the top of
  `citation_fast_path()`: exact `unit_label` lookup, returns the IDX chunk
  id(s) directly (self-contained, no descendant walk, no source-affinity
  disambiguation — single-source corpus). Gated to NOT hijack specific
  `Article N` lookups. Falls through to hybrid if the IDX chunk isn't indexed
  yet (re-index pending).
- **Grounding overlap-rescue** (`validate_grounding` +
  `content_overlap_ratio()`, same file). CHANGELOG followup #2: a short answer
  with a bad/missing `[n]` marker is no longer hard-demoted when its content
  tokens overlap the retrieved context ≥ 50%. Rescued answers are marked
  `uncited_only` (kept + quality notice) instead of replaced with
  `GROUNDING_FALLBACK`. Catches list-form small-model answers ("Urdu,
  English") that drop the citation marker but are verbatim from context.
  Hallucinations (no shared vocab) still fall back.

**Cross-cutting impact**:
- Chapter-index fast-path requires the IDX chunks to be indexed → **in-app
  re-index still required** before Q11/Q12 improve (same prerequisite as
  06-05). App must also be **rebuilt** — these are Rust changes.
- Tests: 57 query_router lib tests pass (7 new: chapter_index ×4,
  part_number ×1, grounding overlap ×2); 1 pre-existing failure unchanged
  (`context_builder_token_budget_drops_large_chunk` — `build_context` not
  touched).

**Files touched**:
- `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` (new resolver + fast-path wiring +
  grounding overlap-rescue + 7 tests)

**Follow-ups** (not done this batch):
1. **Schedule-injection patcher** — add schedule body nodes to the IR so Q13
   has something to retrieve (mirror `patch_missing_articles.py`).
2. **Re-enable reranker** (`ECHO_RERANK=1`) — likely rescues Q2 (Majlis def).
3. Deep-tier (Mistral) for procedure/cross_compare → Q15/Q16/Q17/Q18/Q19.
4. Re-run the 17-prompt eval after rebuild + re-index; expected Q11+Q12 →
   ~14/17 (~82%).

## 2026-06-05 — Phase 3 deferred closeout + retrieval-quality batch

**Symptom/why**: 17-prompt eval (NOVIQ vs base Qwen2.5-3B over the
constitution) showed NOVIQ 12/17 fully-usable (70.6%) vs base 10/17 (58.8%).
4 of 17 questions failed identically on both models — pure retrieval rot.
3 of 20 prompts were intent-gated (procedure / cross_compare) and never
reached either model. Two diagnostic categories isolated: (A) base
genuinely can't extract the right sub-clause out of 20 near-identical
Article 260 chunks; (B) hybrid(rrf) retrieves wrong chunks on
non-numbered-citation queries (Majlis / Money Bill defs; Chapter-1 /
Chapter-2 enumerations).

**Fix (this batch)**:
- **Widened S2 definitional classifier regex**
  (`src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs:1949`). Added patterns for
  "definition of … for the purposes of", "Article N say about the term X",
  "List/Which languages mentioned in N". Fires the +30% pool boost on Q3
  (State), Q5 (citizen), Q9 (languages). Test
  `is_definitional_matches_canonical_question_shapes` extended + green.
- **Citation fast-path sub-clause re-rank**
  (`src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs:573`). When fast-path returns
  ≥10 chunks of the same Article AND the query carries content tokens
  beyond the citation, stable-sort chunks by content-token overlap with
  the citation-stripped query, promote best to slot [1]. Fixes the Q5/Q9
  failure mode where the right sub-clause sat mid-list (slot 9) on small
  models with K=20 budget. New trace step `Sub-clause re-rank` shows the
  promotion source.
- **Chapter-index injection script**
  (`tools/constitution_import/inject_chapter_index.py`). Generates synthetic
  `IDX-P<part>-C<chapter>` Articles enumerating each chapter's contents.
  Multi-path-aware, `--refresh` flag wipes & re-injects, idempotent
  re-runs. Required for Q11 (Chapter 1 Part II) and Q12 (Principles of
  Policy Chapter 2). Applied to all 4 IR copies.
- **15 missing articles patcher**
  (`tools/constitution_import/patch_missing_articles.py`). Extracts the 15
  articles flagged by the 2026-06-04 audit (71, 96, 96A, 134, 135, 152A,
  184, 186, 186A, 191A, 203I, 212A, 212B, 247, 270C) from cached
  pakistani.org HTML and inserts each into the correct Chapter at the right
  numeric position. Multi-path-aware. Flat-text body; `clauses[]` left
  empty as v2 work. Applied to all 4 IR copies.
- **Smoke-test harness (Ollama)** (`tools/smoke_test_llm.sh`). Extracts the
  `Full prompt sent to LLM` block from any trace `.log` and replays it
  through Ollama `/api/generate` (raw=true) on `noviq` + `qwen3b-base`.
  Pure bash + python3 (no jq dep). Run results:
  - Q5 citizen: noviq APP ✅ ↔ noviq CLI ❌ (prompt-truncation artefact —
    trace caps at ~1800 tokens; real prompt was 7466 chars). Base APP ❌ =
    base CLI ❌ → **Bucket A confirmed for base**.
  - Q9 languages: noviq APP ✅ ↔ noviq CLI ✅. Base APP ❌ (fallback)
    ↔ base CLI ✅ → **grounding validator over-strict** (empty `[n]`
    cites demote a valid list-form answer).
- **Settings → "Download last 30 traces" button**
  (`src-tauri/src/commands/system.rs::download_recent_query_traces_to`,
  registered in `lib.rs:147`, exposed in `src/api/index.ts:444`, wired in
  `src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx`). Mirrors `download_all_query_traces_to`
  capped at N=30; default filename `echoai-traces-last30-<stamp>.md`.
- **LLM temp 0.1 → 0 NO-OP verified**. Sampler chain is
  `penalties → temp(0.1) → greedy`. Greedy ignores temp scaling — argmax
  always wins. The pass1↔pass2 variance observed on NOVIQ is from
  multi-threaded GEMM reduction order in llama-cpp, not the temp value.

## 2026-06-02 — Constitution IR investor-demo retrieval batch on master branch (work-in-progress, uncommitted)

**Context**: ran 20-prompt investor demo against `constitution_ir.json` across 4 tiers
(local 0.5B, local 3B, Groq llama-3.3-70b, Cerebras). Headline result: Groq 70B at
`ECHO_CONTEXT_K=20` config delivers **80% OK / 1.61 s avg / zero hallucinations**.
K=25 widening regressed to 70% OK (model dilution on canonical queries) — pinned K=20
as the sweet spot. Trace files saved under `~/Desktop/20_constitute_prompts/`.

**Code changes (all in `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs`, uncommitted):**

1. **`CONTEXT_TOP_K`: 6 → 10** (`:27-34`). K=6 was starving jumbo articles split across
   many clause-grained chunks. Trace `38998dab` (Service of Pakistan) burned all 6
   context slots on Articles 240 & 275 fragments and never surfaced Art 260's definition.
   K=10 + per-query `ECHO_CONTEXT_K` env override gives the recommended demo configuration.

2. **`is_definitional()` regex broadened** (`:1865-1880`). Added phrasings
   `what does X define`, `how is X defined`, `quote the definition of`,
   `what is the definition of`, `definition of X`. Investor-demo phrasing
   ("What does the Constitution define as a 'Service of Pakistan'?") now triggers
   S2 pool-widening (2× pool) + 1.6× canonical-chunk boost. Test
   `is_definitional_matches_canonical_question_shapes` extended with 5 new positive
   assertions covering Q1, Q2, Q4 phrasings. 50/51 query_router tests pass; the 1
   failure (`context_builder_token_budget_drops_large_chunk:3381`) is pre-existing
   and unrelated.

3. **Citation fast-path keyword augmentation** (`:488-535` + new helper
   `strip_citation_refs()` at `:1953-1968`). Trace `deca5716` showed the fast-path
   pulling 6 chunks for "Article 260 ... citizen" but none was the citizen sub-clause.
   Article 260 is the master definitions article with 30+ sub-clauses sharing
   `unit_label = "Article 260"`. Fix: after the fast-path returns, strip the
   citation reference from the query (`detect_citation`-style regex) and if any
   substantive (≥4-char) tokens survive, run FTS5 scoped to the same source_id and
   union the hits with the fast-path chunks (deduped by id). Trace gains
   `Keyword augmentation: N chunks added (FTS5, scoped to cited source)` line under
   "Citation fast-path". Bypass label changed `vector search, FTS5, reranker` →
   `vector search, reranker` (FTS5 no longer bypassed for content-bearing citation
   queries). Existing `citation_fast_path` tests still pass.

4. **`ECHO_CONTEXT_BUDGET` env knob** (`:100-108` + `:715-721`). Previously
   `CONTEXT_TOKEN_BUDGET=2400` was a hardcoded constant; doubling `ECHO_CONTEXT_K`
   alone did not reach the model because the budget capped the context-builder first.
   `knob_context_budget()` reads the env override; `effective_ctx_budget` plumbing
   in the same shape as `effective_ctx_k`. Applied only to `QueryType::Regular`;
   Summary queries keep their existing 640-tok cap (per Idea-1 design).

**Demo command (validated on Groq 70B, 20-prompt set):**

```bash
ECHO_VEC_K=48 ECHO_FTS_K=48 ECHO_CONTEXT_K=20 ECHO_CONTEXT_BUDGET=4800 ./run-dev.sh
```


## 2026-05-31 PM (later) — Feature 006: three-fix batch for the n0008 stall

Lands all three fixes called out in the prior STALL entry. Compiles + tests
pending verification end-of-session (full lib rebuild was still running at
write time).

**Fix 1 — single-quote → double-quote pre-pass** (`mistral_builder.rs`):
- Added `convert_single_quoted_strings(&str) -> String` — 3-state walker
  (Outside / InDouble / InSingle) that converts Python/json5-style single-
  quoted JSON values to standard double-quoted form. Inside the body it
  escapes literal `"` as `\"`, drops the `\` of `\'` (literal apostrophe in
  the source), and preserves all other backslash escapes verbatim.
- Wired in front of `sanitize_json_string_newlines` so the existing newline /
  stray-quote heuristic operates on clean double-quoted JSON.
- Tests: 6 new — the verbatim n0008 dump must parse end-to-end, plus 5 unit
  cases (no-op on clean JSON, basic conversion, internal `"` escape,
  `\'` → `'` unescape, apostrophes inside double-quoted strings are not
  delimiters).

**Fix 2 — stochastic retries** (`llm.rs` + `mistral_builder.rs`):
- New `ModelSlot::infer_with_cancel_temp(...)` — same body, optional
  `temperature` + `seed`. When `temperature.is_some_and(|t| t > 0.0)`, swaps
  the sampler chain to `penalties → top_p(0.95) → temp(t) → dist(seed)`.
  Default (None) preserves existing greedy chain — no behavior change for
  query_router callers.
- Existing `infer_with_cancel` is now a thin wrapper calling the new method
  with `None, None` — zero diff at the 2 query_router call sites.
- `mistral_builder::temp_for_attempt(u32) -> Option<f32>`: attempt 0 = None
  (greedy default), 1 = 0.4, 2 = 0.7, 3 = 0.9. Seed is
  `chunk_seq * 1009 + attempt` so reruns of the same doc land on the same
  retry trajectory (debuggability) but each retry within a run is different.
- Chunk-gen call site uses the new method + per-attempt temperature.
  Classifier still uses the deterministic path (temperature only kicks in
  during retries).
- Test: `temp_for_attempt_schedule` covers monotone + cap at 0.9.

**Fix 3 — per-chunk progress persistence** (migration 019 + new module +
builder wiring):
- New `019_doc_ir_progress.sql` — additive: `doc_ir_progress` table keyed by
  `source_id`, columns `(source_sha256, doc_type, total_chunks,
  next_chunk_idx, id_counter, nodes_json, updated_at)`. Bumps
  `db_config.schema_version` 14 → 15. `TARGET_SCHEMA_VERSION` in
  `db/schema.rs` and the `schema_wipe_test` assertion bumped to match.
- New `services/doc_ir/progress_store.rs` — async `load` / `save` / `clear`
  on the new table. Stale/corrupt rows return Ok(None) (build proceeds from
  scratch instead of erroring). 5 unit tests (roundtrip, missing key,
  upsert collapses, clear deletes, corrupt-JSON tolerance).
- New constructor `MistralIrBuilder::new_with_pool(slot, tier,
  Option<SqlitePool>)`. `unconfigured()` keeps `pool = None` for tests. Old
  `new()` still works (no pool).
- `indexer::do_index` now constructs the builder via `new_with_pool(...,
  Some(pool.clone()))` so production runs persist progress.
- `build()` after chunking: `progress_store::load(source_id)` →
  if `total_chunks` matches the current chunker output and `next_chunk_idx
  ≤ chunks.len()`, restore `(start_idx, all_nodes, id_counter)` and skip
  ahead. Mismatch → warn + clear + start fresh. After every successful
  chunk: snapshot + save. On successful whole-doc validation: clear.

**Test status:** not yet verified (build was still running at edit-window
end). All three fix bodies are isolated — the n0008 dump test alone will
prove fix 1; `temp_for_attempt_schedule` proves fix 2's scheduling;

## 2026-05-31 PM — Feature 006 STALL: Mistral n0008 deterministic single-quote loop (4× retries exhausted)

- **Symptom**: Fresh app run at 17:30 PKT (log `dev-20260531-173011.log`) re-dispatched
  the Sindh PDF after morning battery death. Got chunks n0001–n0007 OK across pages 1,
  then chunk n0008 failed parse 4× in a row (attempts 0–3), all with **byte-identical
  raw output** (`raw len=286`). After 4 retries the build aborts the document and flips
  `sources.indexing_status='failed'` (current DB state confirmed).
- **Root cause** (read from `/tmp/echo-ai-debug/chunk-fail-20260531T13*.json`): Mistral
  emits Python-style single-quoted string with escaped inner double-quotes:
  `"text": '"Provincial Selection Board\" means a Board constituted under rule 6-A;',`
  plus a literal `\\n` and `\\"` inside the same line. Tolerant parser's json5 lenient
  path can't recover the mixed `'...\"...\\n...'` pattern. Temp=0 + identical reprompt
  → identical output → 4 wasted retries (~20 min each = 80 min lost on one chunk).
- **Why retry doesn't help**: validator-msg reprompt (Slice B T022) doesn't perturb the
  sampler enough at temp=0 to break the single-quote habit. The grammar-constrained
  sampler path is bypassed for chunks (only schema-light prompts in use this round).
- **Preserved artifacts** (before resume):
  - DB: `/home/riaz/.local/share/com.echoai.app/echo.db.preserved-n0008-fail-20260531-1858`
  - Log: `logs/dev-20260531-173011.preserved-n0008-fail.log`
  - Failure dumps: `/home/riaz/echo-ai-debug-preserved-20260531-1858/`
- **No code change this session** — battery critical, ran out of safe window.
- **Next session — fix order**:
  1. **Quick win**: in `mistral_builder.rs` tolerant parser chain, add a pre-pass that
     substitutes Python-style single-quoted strings → JSON double-quoted equivalents
     (regex `'([^']*)'` with inner `\"` → `"` after un-escape). Cheap, covers this case.
  2. **Real fix**: bump temp to 0.2–0.3 on retry attempts 1+ so the sampler actually
     explores a different surface form (currently temp=0 reprompt is a no-op).
  3. **Architectural**: persist per-chunk progress to a `doc_ir_progress` table so a
     stall on chunk N doesn't lose chunks 0..N-1 (currently in-memory only — same
     pain as overnight battery death).
- **State to resume from**: source row `230c1dc8-...` is `indexing_status='failed'`.
  Either flip to `pending` + rescan folder, or delete + re-add. Restart is from page 1.

## 2026-05-30 — Feature 006 Phase 3 LLM (Slice B): grammar-constrained Mistral inference + classifier + retry + indexer wiring

**What:** Filled in the real LLM runtime for the IR builder. Tasks completed this slice: T019, T020, T021 (real `build()`), T022. Plus a new `ModelSlot::infer_with_grammar` method and `indexer::do_index` wiring (T024 closure). `cargo build --features llm` GREEN; `--features llm` now implies `llguidance` on llama-cpp-2.

**Why:** Slice A only stubbed availability. Slice B is the workable end-to-end: drop a Sindh PDF in a watched folder, get a structured IR back via Mistral 7B + JSON-schema constrained sampling. Fits the spec's MVP (US1) gate.

**Cargo / feature wiring:**
- `Cargo.toml`: `llm = ["llama-cpp-2", "llama-cpp-2/llguidance", "dep:encoding_rs"]`. Pulls in `llguidance v1.7.5` + `toktrie v1.7.5` + `derivre`, transitively.

**New code (`src-tauri/`):**
- `services/llm.rs::infer_with_grammar` (~80 lines) — mirrors `infer_with_cancel` but takes a sampler-factory closure `F: FnOnce(&LlamaModel) -> Result<LlamaSampler>`. No ChatML stripping (Mistral instruct doesn't emit ChatML). Calls `sampler.accept(token)` so the grammar engine advances its parser state.
- `services/doc_ir/grammar.rs` — `build_ir_sampler(model)` (llguidance + `schema.json`) and `build_classifier_sampler(model)` (inline enum sub-schema).
- `services/doc_ir/mistral_builder.rs` (~560 lines, replaces slice A skeleton):
  - Holds `slot: Option<Arc<ModelSlot>>` + `tier: HardwareTier`; `new(slot, tier)` for production, `unconfigured()` for tests.
  - `available()` = slot present AND GGUF discoverable. No hardware-tier gate (per user direction earlier).
  - `classify_doc_type` — calls Mistral with `DOC_TYPE_CLASSIFIER_PROMPT` + classifier sampler; head of doc truncated to 2400 chars (~600 tokens). On JSON parse failure, falls back to rule-based `detect_profile`.
  - `build()` — classify → chunk via T017 → per-chunk grammar-constrained generation → assemble `DocIr` → final `validate_doc_ir` pass → emit progress events at each phase. Honors `CancellationToken` at every await boundary.
  - `generate_chunk_with_retry` (T022) — up to `MAX_CHUNK_RETRIES=3` re-prompts at temp 0 (grammar enforces temp via llguidance internals; we pass validator-error message in the user prompt). After exhaustion, emit one `LowConfidence` sentinel node carrying the chunk text + last error so the source is still represented in the index.
  - `rewrite_ids` — per-chunk LLM outputs use local ids (`n0001…`); we rewrite to a doc-global counter and remap intra-chunk `parent_id` refs. Cross-chunk refs (already-rewritten) are left as-is.
  - `sha256_file` helper for the indexer wiring.
- `services/indexer.rs::do_index` — between `try_load_constitution` and `structured_importer::import`, runs `dispatch::try_llm_ir_path` when (a) `llm` feature enabled, (b) Tauri app handle present, (c) format is PDF/DOCX/TXT/Markdown/Code. Computes file sha256, builds `MistralIrBuilder::new(slot, tier)`, registers a cancellation token via `commands::importer::register`, dispatches, unregisters. `DispatchOutcome::Indexed → return Ok`; `Unprocessable → return Ok`; `SkippedBuilderUnavailable → fall through` to structured_importer (FR-027).

**Inference parameters:**
- IR generation: `n_ctx=4096`, `max_prompt_tokens=3600`, `max_gen_tokens=2400`, IR-schema grammar.
- Classifier: `n_ctx=1024`, `max_prompt_tokens=700`, `max_gen_tokens=32`, enum sub-schema grammar.
- Chunk budget (existing chunker T017): 2400 tokens / chunk; leaves room for sys prompt (~700) + breadcrumb (~100) + few-shot in the 4096 window.

**Pragmatic simplifications (carry to follow-up):**
- Doc-level retry counter (`MAX_DOC_RETRIES=2`) is reserved but not wired — chunk-level retries already absorb cross-chunk breaks in observed Mistral outputs. Will revisit after the first real-PDF run shows whether doc-level retries help.
- Per-page index mapping uses chunker's `page_start`. Sub-page accuracy can wait for slice C.
- LLM model loaded via the shared `ModelSlot`: each IR run evicts the chat model and vice-versa. Acceptable because IR runs while chat is idle (background watcher trigger) and the queue (T029b) already serializes IR runs.

**Test status:** 80 GREEN this slice (37 doc_ir lib + 3 importer cmd lib + 40 integration across 8 files). New mistral_builder tests cover `discover_in`, `unconfigured`, `doctype_from_str` mapping, `rewrite_ids` self/parent/cross-chunk semantics, `build_user_message` formatting. Pre-existing lib failures unchanged (`doc_profiles::manual::tests::detection_matches_manual_corpus`, `query_router::tests::context_builder_token_budget_drops_large_chunk` — unrelated to Feature 006).
