## 2026-05-28 — Retrieval pipeline fixes from 22-prompt forensic audit (ANALYSIS_v3.md §8)

Four code changes driven by the V3 evaluation's forensic audit (`~/Desktop/test 22 prompts/V3/ANALYSIS_v3.md` §8). The audit cross-referenced every Q1–Q22 gold-text against live DB rows, the Groq trace's STEP-10 chunk dump, and per-source chunk distributions, and produced evidence per prompt instead of inference. The audit is the source of truth — read it before re-debugging any of these subsystems.

### Fix 1 — RoB 1986 rule-heading detection: add "bare-number + legal opener" pattern

**Symptom:** Q13 (RoB Rule 9), Q14 (RoB Rule 10A), Q15 (RoB Rule 11) deterministically fallback on every model tested (local-3B / 0.5B-FT / Groq Llama-3.3-70B). Audit query against `chunks` showed RoB 1986 had only **9 `Rule N` chunks** in `unit_label` of an expected ~47 (Rules 1–47); the other ~1,470 RoB chunks were tagged with sub-clause labels `(a)/(b)/(i)/(v)/(1)`. Q13's gold *is* in the DB — chunk content `"Rule 1\n9. The Chief Minister may in his discretion require any case to..."` — but mis-labelled as a `(b)` child of Rule 1, so `unit_label='Rule 9'` returns zero RoB rows.

**Root cause:** the OCR'd RoB rule headings are `9. The Chief Minister may...`, `11. Notwithstanding...`, `15. On Finanee Department's refusal...` — bare-number prefix, no literal "Rule" word, no `(M)` sub-clause paren, no trailing `----` dashes. None of the existing three patterns in `rules.rs` match this shape. (The single chunk that got `unit_label='Rule 33'` matched because `33. (1) Proocedings of the meetings...` happens to have a `(1)` immediately after — Pattern 2 fires.)

**Fix:** added a fourth `HeadingPattern` to `RULES.heading_patterns` matching `N. <opener> ...` where opener ∈ {The, Notwithstanding, On, If, Where, Subject, No, When, Every, Any, All, It}. The opener safe-list is the cheapest way to separate real rule headings from RoB footnote shapes (`3. Subs. Ibid.`, `4. Inserted ibid.`, `1. Sub rules (5) and (6) of rules 5 added vide ...`) without negative lookahead, which `regex_lite` doesn't support.

**Files:** `src-tauri/src/services/doc_profiles/rules.rs` — one new pattern between the dash-style pattern and the clause-paren pattern. Plus a guarding test `bare_number_rule_with_legal_opener_detects_rob_headings` exercising 4 RoB-shape positives and 4 negatives (E&D footnotes + the existing dash-pattern target, which must NOT cross-match).

**Caveat:** code-only fix; **requires re-indexing the RoB 1986 PDF** through Settings → Indexed Folders → RoB row → Reindex. Existing chunks have wrong `unit_label`s and `unit_path`s — code change alone does not retroactively re-label them. After re-index, expect ~40 `Rule N` chunks visible via `sqlite3 echo.db "SELECT unit_label, COUNT(*) FROM chunks c JOIN sources s ON c.source_id=s.id WHERE s.file_name LIKE '%rules of business 1986%' AND c.unit_label LIKE 'Rule %' GROUP BY unit_label"`.

### Fix 2 — Citation fast-path scope guard (zero-overlap multi-candidate ⇒ fall through)

**Symptom:** queries naming RoB ("Rule 9 of the Sindh Government Rules of Business 1986") retrieved E&D Rules instead — the fast-path bypassed vec+FTS5+reranker and locked onto E&D's Rule 9 (officers lent to other Government) because RoB's Rule 9 wasn't tagged.

**Root cause:** the existing source-affinity scoring (`source_affinity_tokens` + per-source head_text overlap) had no minimum threshold. When `unit_label='Rule 9'` returned only E&D candidates (RoB rows missing per Fix 1), `per_src` had a single entry, overlap was irrelevant, E&D won by default.

**Fix:** added a scope guard in `citation_fast_path` — when `per_src.len() > 1` AND the winning candidate's `best_overlap == 0` AND the query has at least one discriminator token (`!q_tokens.is_empty()`), return `Ok(None)` and fall through to hybrid retrieval. Single-candidate citations (typical Constitution corpus) keep the existing behaviour — no ambiguity to resolve.

**Why these three conjuncts together:** dropping any one regresses an existing test.
- Drop the `per_src.len() > 1` clause and the existing `citation_fast_path_resolves_cited_units` test fails because "what does Article 8 cover" has zero discriminator overlap against the single-source constitution corpus.
- Drop the `q_tokens.is_empty()` clause and pure citation queries ("explain Article 8(3)(b)") with no other tokens fail spuriously.
- Drop the `best_overlap == 0` clause and you've replaced the affinity tie-breaker entirely; queries that match weakly but consistently break.

**Files:** `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs::citation_fast_path` (~10 LOC added between the affinity-winner pick and the descendant fetch).

**Verification:** existing `citation_fast_path_resolves_cited_units` and `citation_fast_path_disambiguates_by_statute_preamble` both pass with `--offline`.

### Fix 3 — Cross-encoder reranker hardcoded OFF (default)

**What:** flipped `rerank_enabled` default from `true` to `false`. Reranker now runs ONLY when `ECHO_RERANK=1` is explicitly set in the environment. Bypass message in trace updated from "disabled via ECHO_RERANK=0" → "hardcoded off (ECHO_RERANK=1 to re-enable)".

**Why:** ANALYSIS_v3.md §8 shows the bge-reranker-base default is **net-negative on legal-text queries** at this corpus:
- **Q5 (APT BS-17):** reranker top-score was strong but the top chunk was a definitional stub, not the BS-17 rule; the LLM only recovered via the v5.3 prompt's logical-containment clause.
- **Q14 (RoB Rule 10A):** reranker top-score 3.448 picked the 2016-proviso chunk but DEMOTED the main "Cabinet shall be attended by Ministers" clause out of top-12.
- **Q21 (RoB Rule 14):** reranker promoted Article 175E (Constitution "dispute between Governments") over the actual RoB Rule 14 chunk via cross-document lexical overlap — top-score 1.340, weak.
- **Q17 (Authority overlap):** reranker top-score -0.230, NEGATIVE — yet Groq still produced a correct synthesis. The score signal is NOT calibrated as a gate.

The reranker also adds **~17–21 s of CPU latency** on the local pipeline (V3 evening reruns: Q22 took 157 s end-to-end, of which 60 s was a cold vec spike and ~21 s was the cross-encoder forward pass). With Fix 1 and 2 closing most of the retrieval failures pure-RRF can handle, the cost stops being worth paying.

**Re-enable path:** documented inline. Set `ECHO_RERANK=1` for an experiment after a domain fine-tune AND a top-score sweep against the 22-prompt eval. Do NOT re-enable as default without evidence the demote pattern is fixed.

**Files:** `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` — one-line change at the `rerank_enabled` declaration plus updated rationale comment block; trace-message string updated; the rerank confidence gate (`knob_min_rerank_score`) is now dead code in the default path but kept for the `ECHO_RERANK=1` experimental path.

### Fix 4 — Candidate-ID logging at vec / FTS5 / reranker steps

**What:** every retrieval stage now emits the chunk-ID list (first 8 chars of UUID) + source filename in the per-step trace. Reranker also emits per-candidate scores (`id=score`, sorted desc).

**Why:** the V3 forensic audit's §8.6 "What still cannot be determined" called out `VEC_MISS` vs `RRF_DROP` as indistinguishable because the trace only logged counts (24 vec + 24 FTS, 43 unique post-merge), not IDs. After this change, every future eval can answer four questions per prompt without re-running:
- Did gold reach the vec top-K? (compare gold chunk_id to `STEP "Vector search" • Candidates` list)
- Did gold reach FTS top-K? (compare to `STEP "Keyword search (FTS5)" • Candidates`)
- Did gold survive RRF merge? (it's in `STEP "Build context window"` if yes)
- If reranker is enabled (it isn't by default after Fix 3), did it demote gold? (look at `STEP "Reranker" • Per-candidate` ranking)

**Files:** `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` — three small additions to the trace `step()` calls for Vector search, Keyword search (FTS5), and Reranker (cross-encoder). Format: `{id8}:{filename}` for retrieval, `{id8}={score:.2}` for reranker. The candidate count is capped at the existing step limit (24 / 24 / rerank_pool_k = 12 by default), so trace size is bounded.

### Fix 5 — Context K hardcoded to 6 (was 12)

**What:** `CONTEXT_TOP_K` constant in `query_router.rs` reduced from 12 → 6. Vec and FTS recall pools decoupled from `CONTEXT_TOP_K` and pinned at 24 each (previously they were `CONTEXT_TOP_K * 2 = 24`; with the K reduction they would have shrunk to 12, which we did NOT want).

**Why:** Forensic chunk-inspection (`~/Desktop/db_inspection_22_prompts/v2/08_granularity.md`) shows 91–99% of corpus chunks per source are <80 tokens — far below the BGE embedding sweet-spot of 80–200 tok. Packing 12 such fragments into the LLM context loads it with mostly clause-isolation noise and inflates adjacent-chunk contamination (which `07_contamination.md` flagged: parent-title propagation + chapeau leakage). Six longer-effective chunks fits the 2400-tok `CONTEXT_TOKEN_BUDGET` cleanly and reduces the precision-killing effect of fragmented siblings flooding context. Also: the reranker is off post-Fix-3, so there's no second-stage pruning to clean up a wide top-12; a tighter K is the right post-rerank-off default.

**Decoupling rationale:** `knob_vec_k` and `knob_fts_k` previously derived from `CONTEXT_TOP_K * 2`. Halving the LLM K to 6 should not halve recall — RRF needs material to merge. Both pools now pinned at 24 (the old effective value) and the comment explicitly notes the decoupling so future K tweaks don't accidentally shrink retrieval again.

**Files:** `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` — `CONTEXT_TOP_K` constant (12→6) with rationale comment block; `knob_vec_k` and `knob_fts_k` defaults pinned to 24 (no longer derived). Env knobs `ECHO_CONTEXT_K`, `ECHO_VEC_K`, `ECHO_FTS_K` all still override.

**Verification:** `cargo check --offline` clean. Behavioural: expect V5 traces to show `STEP "Build context window" • Selected: 6 chunks (cap K=6)` and total content ≈ 1200–1800 chars (down from 3000–3500 in V4).

## 2026-05-26 (evening) — UI plumbing: X-button FK-787, constitution stuck-failed loop, OCR env defaults

Three coupled bugs surfaced while preparing the RoB 1986 re-OCR with PSM=4.

### Fix 1 — `remove_folder_source` silently rolling back (X button "does nothing")

**Symptom:** Clicking the X icon in Settings → Indexed Folders → expanded folder card on any source with graph data did nothing visually. The log showed `DELETE FROM chunk_embeddings rows_affected=1674` (success, ~106s for vec0) then `DELETE FROM chunks rows_affected=0 elapsed=1.5s`, no `"Unindexed folder source ..."` info line. DB state unchanged.

**Root cause:** `graph_nodes.chunk_id → chunks.id` is `ON DELETE NO ACTION`. The chunks DELETE failed with `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_FOREIGNKEY (code 787)`, whole transaction rolled back, frontend caught the error and logged `console.error("Remove failed:", e)` — invisible without devtools open. Devtools confirmed the 787 code.

**Fix** — `src-tauri/src/commands/folders.rs::remove_folder_source` (~30 LOC added). Three new ordered deletes in the same transaction, BEFORE the chunks DELETE:
1. `DELETE FROM graph_edges WHERE from_node IN (SELECT id FROM graph_nodes WHERE chunk_id IN (SELECT id FROM chunks WHERE source_id = ?))`
2. Same for `to_node`.
3. `DELETE FROM graph_nodes WHERE chunk_id IN (SELECT id FROM chunks WHERE source_id = ?)`

`chunks.parent_chunk_id` is also FK NO ACTION (self-ref) but SQLite enforces FKs at end-of-statement, so deleting all of a source's chunks in one DELETE is safe (every parent_chunk_id either points to another row in the same delete-set, or to NULL).

`chunk_embeddings` was already deleted first (no FK, vec0 virtual table). The 106s is normal sqlite-vec speed for 1674 rows, not a bug — the UI should show a spinner during the call (frontend gap, separate fix).

### Fix 2 — Constitution_ir.json stuck at `'failed'` every restart

**Symptom:** After every app launch, `constitution_ir.json` showed a red "failed Retry" pill in Settings. Self-heal from 2026-05-25 (failed→indexed if chunks exist) had been added but never resolved it.

**Root cause:** The startup recovery chain has three steps that interact badly:
1. `db/schema.rs::init_db` — `processing → pending` (line 144), then self-heal `failed → indexed if chunks exist` (line 163).
2. `services/indexer.rs::enqueue_structure_reextract` (called from `lib.rs::setup_models_and_watchers:224`) — selects sources where `indexing_status='indexed' AND structure_importer_version < CURRENT`, flips them to `'pending'`. **Spawns no worker.**
3. `db/repositories/sources.rs::reset_stuck_pending` (called from `lib.rs:304`) — flips any `'pending'` source to `'failed'` with error "Indexing interrupted".

`constitution_ir.json` was indexed via the Feature-003 constitution-specific path before Feature 005 shipped, so `structure_importer_version=0`. The current binary's `STRUCTURED_IMPORTER_VERSION=1`. Every restart, step 2 flipped it `indexed → pending`, step 3 flipped it `pending → failed`. Self-heal (which runs in step 1, BEFORE the enqueuer) doesn't catch it.

**Fix A — format filter (primary)**: `src-tauri/src/services/indexer.rs::enqueue_structure_reextract`. Added `AND format = 'pdf'` to the SELECT. constitution_ir.json has `format='code'` (it's a derived JSON IR, not a re-parseable source — the generic Feature-005 importer can't process it).

**Fix B — self-heal widened (belt-and-braces)**: `src-tauri/src/db/schema.rs`. WHERE clause widened from `indexing_status = 'failed'` to `indexing_status IN ('failed', 'pending')`. Catches the corner where ordering bugs leave a chunks-having source at `pending`. Log message string unchanged.

**One-shot DB heal** for the existing row (no rebuild needed — single UPDATE while app was running):
```sql
UPDATE sources
   SET indexing_status='indexed', error_reason=NULL,
       structure_importer_version=1,
       indexed_at=COALESCE(indexed_at, strftime('%s','now'))
 WHERE id='e4668221-8524-445b-ba7f-9b07e021f187';
```

**Architectural follow-up** (NOT in this commit): the `enqueue_*_reextract` functions flip rows to `'pending'` but spawn no worker. The file-watcher only reacts to inotify events, so nothing consumes those pending rows; `reset_stuck_pending` flips them to `failed` after the next restart. When any future PDF version-bump triggers the same pattern, the same bug recurs for PDFs. Either spawn workers in the enqueuer, or reorder + add a startup pending-poller.

### Fix 3 — OCR PSM/DPI defaults in run-dev.sh

`run-dev.sh` now exports defaults that the user can A/B-test for the RoB 1986 multi-column scan:
```bash
export ECHO_OCR_PSM="${ECHO_OCR_PSM:-4}"   # was hardcoded 1
export ECHO_OCR_DPI="${ECHO_OCR_DPI:-400}" # was hardcoded 300
```
PSM=4 = single column of variable text (avoids the column-interleaving from PSM=1 layout analysis that produced empty `(c)`/`(i)` shells). Override per-launch: `ECHO_OCR_PSM=6 ./run-dev.sh`.

### Files

- `src-tauri/src/commands/folders.rs` — `remove_folder_source`: +3 ordered deletes
- `src-tauri/src/services/indexer.rs` — `enqueue_structure_reextract`: `+ AND format = 'pdf'`
- `src-tauri/src/db/schema.rs` — self-heal: `WHERE indexing_status IN ('failed', 'pending')`
- `run-dev.sh` — `ECHO_OCR_PSM=4`, `ECHO_OCR_DPI=400` defaults
- DB: one-shot UPDATE on `e4668221-8524-445b-ba7f-9b07e021f187`

### Verification

- Live test: user clicked X on RoB 1986 after rebuild → transaction completed (~2 min), source flipped to `unindexed`, then user clicked Index → re-OCR running with PSM=4/DPI=400 (in flight at session end).
- Constitution row in DB: `indexing_status='indexed', structure_importer_version=1` after the one-shot UPDATE.
- Code-level: `cargo check` clean (verified during incremental rebuild — 4m51s full, will be quick incremental next launch).

### Caveats

- No automated test added for `remove_folder_source` graph-clear (would need test fixture with graph_nodes/edges for a source). Manual verification via UI click.
- `enqueue_structure_reextract` architectural issue (no worker spawn) is documented above but not fixed in this commit — out of scope; will recur for PDFs if `STRUCTURED_IMPORTER_VERSION` ever bumps.

## 2026-05-26 — LLM output quality fixes (query_router + llm + system prompt)

### Fix A — Citation-only response (`[1]` bare answer)
- **What**: Jaccard `Retry` arm was a dead stub — logged "legacy retry path handles it" then returned the original answer unchanged. When the model output only `[1]` (no text body), the grounding validator scored it 1.00/1.00 (0 uncited sentences), Jaccard detected it as a failed sentence → Retry → no-op → `[1]` reached the user.
- **Why**: `ECHO_REVIEWER=1` (the actual retry loop) is disabled by default; the stub was left as a placeholder but never wired.
- **Fix**: Retry arm now strips all `[N]` markers + whitespace from the answer body; if nothing remains, replaces with `GROUNDING_FALLBACK`.
- **Files**: `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` — `GroundingAction::Retry` arm

### Fix B — Bare `[N]` bullet lines in list answers
- **What**: Model emitted lines like `- [6]` with no text when a chunk contained only a section-header shard it couldn't paraphrase.
- **Fix**: Pre-grounding regex pass strips lines whose entire content is citation markers (`(?m)^[\s\-*•]*\[\d+\][\s,]*$`), then collapses blank-line runs.
- **Files**: `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` — new strip block before grounding validation

### Fix C — "Not explicitly mentioned" false refusal despite answer in context
- **What**: System prompt v5.2 banned all inference including trivial arithmetic. "Grade 16 and above" in context, BS-17 in question → model refused because it couldn't "infer" 17 > 16.
- **Fix**: Bumped to system prompt v5.3.0 — replaced "Do not infer" with "direct implications such as numerical ranges are permitted; do not invent or extrapolate."
- **Files**: `src-tauri/src/services/llm.rs` — `GROUNDING_SYSTEM_PROMPT`

### Fix D — Prompt leakage (model reproduces RULES section in output)
- **What**: `repeat_penalty=1.3` penalises `<|im_end|>` because it appears throughout prior-turn history in the 256-token lookback window → model overshoots turn boundary → reproduces training-memorised prompt text.
- **Fix**: String-based stop sequence check added to both decode loops. Uses existing 32-char `tail` buffer to detect `<|im_end|>` / `<|im_start|>`, then truncates output and breaks.
- **Files**: `src-tauri/src/services/llm.rs` — `infer()` and `infer_with_cancel()` decode loops

### Not fixed this session
- RoB 1986 wrong-source retrieval (Q13/Q15): OCR quality issue → re-index with `ECHO_OCR_PSM=4 ECHO_OCR_DPI=400` pending.
- Comparative/synthesis questions (Q16/Q17): needs query-decomposition layer, out of scope.
- Mistral 7B download stalled at 2.3/4.37 GB — resume with `wget -c`.

## 2026-05-26 — Source-affinity in citation fast-path (Fix #3 v2)

22-prompt eval on Qwen-1.5B revealed that the citation fast-path was picking
the wrong source when two statutes shared a unit_label. Q10 ("Rule 5 of E&D
1973") returned APT Rule 5 definitions; Q13/Q15 ("Rule 9/11 of Rules of
Business 1986") returned APT Rules 9/11; Q16 ("Rule 4 of E&D 1973") returned
APT Rule 4 committee row. 1.5B grading: 9/22 strict (41%). 5 of the 9 wrong
answers traced to this single retrieval bug.

**Root cause** — `source_affinity_tokens` tokenized only `s.file_name`. The
filenames `efficiency and disciplane rules.pdf` and `appointment promotion
and transfer rules.pdf` both reduce to one token after stopword filtering
(`{rules}`), so every query about either E&D or APT scored zero on filename
overlap and the first-encountered row won blindly.

**Fix** — `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs::citation_fast_path` now
batches a second SQL query that pulls each candidate source's filename **plus
the first 10 chunks (preamble + early body, 400 chars each)**. The statute
title, year, and key defined terms ("Cabinet", "Ordinance", "1973", "1986")
live in that head text — exactly the tokens the query carries. Overlap is
scored against the union vocab. Per-source root selection switched from
"longest content" to **shallowest unit_path** (depth-first, content-length
tie-break) — the longest-content tie-breaker was wrong for hierarchical
labels (e.g. Preamble's paragraph children share their parent's unit_label
under Idea 1, and a child's longer content would collapse the result to a
single paragraph instead of parent + every paragraph).

`source_affinity_tokens` also adds `"rules"` to the stopword list — singular
"rule" was already filtered but plural was leaking through and adding noise
to every legal query.

No hardcoded statute aliases. Generic, works for any future doc — discriminating
signal comes from each source's own preamble, not a curated list.

**Files**
- `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` — `citation_fast_path` (~80 LOC),
  `source_affinity_tokens` (1 stopword)
- New test: `citation_fast_path_disambiguates_by_statute_preamble` — two-statute
  fixture (E&D 1973 + APT 1974, both with "Rule 5"), asserts correct source
  resolves from either query direction.

**Tests**
- `cargo test citation_fast_path` → 2/2 green
- Full `query_router` suite: 50/51 (1 pre-existing failure
  `context_builder_token_budget_drops_large_chunk`, broken by Fix #2's
  anchor-only filter — unrelated to source-affinity)
- `constitution_v1_acceptance::a1_structural_counts_and_linkage` — pre-existing
  failure from Fix #1's chunk-shape change (expected 808, now 927) — unrelated

**Caveats / follow-up**
- Test failures above need triage with the rest of the uncommitted Fix #1/#2
  batch before merging branch 005-structured-importer.
- For docs with truly empty preambles (no chunks at chunk_index < 10), the
  affinity vocab degrades to filename-only — same as old behaviour. Not
  exercised in current corpus.

## 2026-05-25 (night) — Internal-node splitter fix + 500-char threshold + NER Pass 2 hardcoded OFF

Fresh-DB audit after the late-PM fix batch (run via UI on 5/6 PDFs) showed
three chunks still well over the intended cap:
- APT `Part_III/Rule_12/(3)` = **14 126 chars** — internal node carrying
  ~13.5 k chars of annexure / circular-letter text bled into the clause
- E&D `Rule_14` = **7 859 chars** — clause holding the Overriding-Provision
  preamble plus 25 detected sub-clauses
- Removal Act `Section_3` = **3 696 chars** — section preamble plus 2 sub-clauses

All three were **internal nodes** (have detected sub-clause children) AND
had huge `node.text` of their own. The existing `split_oversized_leaves`
at `structure_parser.rs:259` only operated on true leaves:
```rust
if !node.children.is_empty() || node.text.chars().count() <= threshold {
    return node;
}
```
→ any node with even one child was skipped regardless of own-text size.

### What

**1. Splitter fix** — `src-tauri/src/services/structure_parser.rs`
   `split_oversized_leaves` now splits ANY node (leaf or internal) whose
   own `node.text` exceeds the threshold. Paragraph children are appended
   **after** any existing structural children so chunk_index order stays
   detected-clauses-first, paragraph-fallback-after. Parent body is
   emptied; `unit_label` / `citation` / `unit_path` prefix preserved →
   citation fast-path and `LIKE 'X/%'` sub-tree lookup still work.

**2. Threshold lowered 1000 → 500** — `long_chunk_threshold()` default in
   the same file. Sized for local Qwen 0.5B/1.5B context (n_ctx≈3200)
   with TOP_K=12 retrieval.

**3. NER Pass 2 hardcoded OFF** — `src-tauri/src/services/indexer.rs`
   Two spawn sites disabled (commented + wrapped `if false`):
   - constitution path ~line 335 (incremental `run_ner_loop_for_source`)
   - generic index path ~line 855 (per-source LLM batch)
   Pass 1 (rule-based, in-process) still runs. Source's `ner_status` is
   immediately marked `'done'` so the Sources panel doesn't show "pending"
   forever. User decision: free CPU for indexing; re-enable when KG
   quality matters more than indexing speed.

### Why

The internal-node leakage made the 500-char target unachievable on its
own — lowering threshold alone would have left the same chunks intact.
NER Pass 2 was contending with OCR + structure parsing for CPU during
fresh re-indexes, doubling perceived indexing time.

### Files

- `src-tauri/src/services/structure_parser.rs` — splitter logic at 259,
  threshold default at 161, test rename/replace at 968
- `src-tauri/src/services/indexer.rs` — Pass-2 spawn sites at 335 + 855
- `run-dev.sh` — added `ECHO_LONG_CHUNK_THRESHOLD` (default 500)

### Env/flags

- `ECHO_LONG_CHUNK_THRESHOLD` (default `500`) — A/B tuning, no recompile
- NER Pass 2: no env flag (intentionally hardcoded off; to re-enable,
  flip `if false` back to `if let Some(ref app_handle) = app_for_entities`
  in indexer.rs and uncomment the constitution-path spawn)

### Tests

- `structure_parser::persist_tests::split_oversized_leaves_splits_internal_node_own_text`
  (NEW — replaces the inverted `..._does_not_split_internal_nodes` which
  encoded the bug as a feature)
- 11/11 structure_parser tests pass
- 50/51 doc_profiles + parsers tests pass (the 1 fail in
  `doc_profiles::manual::detection_matches_manual_corpus` for
  `"1. RECEIPT AND DESPATCH"` exists on master too — pre-existing)

### Caveats

- All 6 PDFs need re-indexing for the splitter to apply (existing chunks
  were persisted with the old shape).
- Re-enabling Pass 2 requires deleting the `if false { ... }` wrapper in
  two places — there is no runtime flag.

### Hallucination finding (separate from code change)

Audit of `~/Desktop/test 22 prompts/Qwen 2.5 0.5B fine tunned on sindh corpus/echoai-traces-*.md`
confirmed 0.5B-FT model fabricated **Article 397** (trace 162070) and
**Article 376** (trace 167438) in raw output. Constitution max is
Article 280. Grounding validator scored both `0.00 / 1.00` with 0
citations but the `Action: Ship` policy still let them through. Follow-up:
change ship policy to block when `grounding_score < 0.5`. Not in this commit.

## 2026-05-25 (late PM) — Retrieval-quality fixes batch (7 fixes shipped on 005-structured-importer)

User ran the 9 db-inspection scripts from `~/Desktop/db_inspection_22_prompts/`
on the post-Feature-005 index; the diagnostic outputs (`out/01–09*.txt`)
revealed the root causes behind the 22-prompt eval failures. This entry
covers the batch of fixes shipped against those findings.

### Diagnosis summary

- 4 667 chunks / 6 sources. 614 (13 %) low-signal; 741 (16 %) <50 chars;
  617 (13 %) >2500 chars.
- **APT rules**: 834 chunks but **1 573 648** total tokens — avg
  1 887 tok/chunk. 396 chunks share `unit_label='(a)'`; top 15 largest all
  carry the same 28 k-char "Rule 11 (4) If a vacancy ..." preview. Math:
  the full clause body was being replicated into every sub-clause child.
- **Sindh RoB 1986** (OCR'd): 1 597 chunks; **504** labeled `(c)`,
  **605** labeled `(i)`; many with 0 chars. OCR shed the bodies and left
  only the structural skeleton.
- **constitution_ir.json**: 1 488 chunks, all Articles 10A/19A present —
  but source flagged `indexing_status='failed'` from a previous
  mid-finalize kill. Query routing was silently sandbagging every
  constitution prompt.
- **Eval anchor audit** (new `10_eval_anchor_audit.sh`): 13/22 anchors OK,
  2/22 FILENAME_MISMATCH (constitution.pdf vs .json), **5/22
  COLLISION_ONLY** — E&D Rules 3/4/5, RoB Rules 9/11 absent from their
  expected source. The expected source has the doc; the parser missed
  the headings.
- **E&D detection deep dive**: parser detected only `Rule 10` and a
  false-positive `Rule 1976` (the *year* in "Sindh E&D Rules, 1976. (1)").
  All other rules collapsed into one 85-chunk "Preamble" because their
  real heading shape — `3.   Grounds for penalty. --- ...` — was not
  matched by any rules-profile pattern.

### Fixes shipped

1. **Constitution status self-heal** —
   `src-tauri/src/db/schema.rs:155-176`. Sibling to the existing
   `processing → pending` startup recovery: any source with
   `indexing_status='failed'` AND chunks present is flipped to `'indexed'`
   on next launch. No re-index required for the constitution.

2. **Parent-body no longer copied into every sub-clause** —
   `src-tauri/src/services/structure_parser.rs:641-666` (`node_content`).
   The `Clause/SubClause` branch was returning `(own, own)` so children
   inherited the full clause body. Now returns
   `(own, inherited + chapeau)` where chapeau = first non-empty line —
   matches the `Article` branch and the design comment on `DocNode.text`
   ("chapeau for an Article/Clause, full text for a sub-clause leaf").

3. **Whitespace normalization expanded** —
   `src-tauri/src/services/text_normalizer.rs`. Four passes added to
   `normalize()`: strip leading tabs per line, trim trailing horizontal
   ws per line, collapse 3+ blank lines to one paragraph break, collapse
   3+ inline spaces to one. 2-space boundaries are preserved so the
   act.rs marginal-label pattern (`label\s{2,}N\.\s+\(N\)`) still
   anchors. 4 new tests.

4. **Source-affinity in citation fast-path** —
   `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs::citation_fast_path` +
   new `source_affinity_tokens` helper. Replaced
   `SELECT ... WHERE unit_label = ? LIMIT 1` with a fetch-all-then-score
   pass: every chunk that matches the cited `unit_label` is gathered
   across sources, each candidate scored by token-overlap between the
   user query and the source's `file_name`, and the highest-scoring
   source's chunk + its sub-tree (filtered by `source_id` to prevent
   cross-bleed) is returned. Fixes Section 3 → Removal Ordinance vs
   Manual collision and the 5/22 collision-affected prompts.

5. **Anchor-only chunks suppressed in build_context** —
   `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs::build_context` split into
   two-pass `build_context_pass`. Pass 1 skips chunks with
   `content.trim().len() < 50` (heading shells like
   `content="Section 12"`); pass 2 admits them only if pass 1 returned
   nothing. The shells stay in DB as routing handles but never reach
   the LLM as evidence.

6. **Rules profile detects bare-number rule headings (E&D shape)** —
   `src-tauri/src/services/doc_profiles/rules.rs`. Added a new
   `HeadingPattern` for the form `N.   Title. ----` with `-{2,}` trailing
   dashes as the strong differentiator from footnote-style false
   positives (`3. Subs. Ibid.`). All existing `^Part`, `^Rule`,
   `^(N)`, `^(a)` patterns relaxed from `^` to `^\s*` to tolerate
   leading whitespace surviving from the source. New regression test
   covers Rules 3/4/5/7 positives + 3 footnote negatives.

7. **Eval anchor audit script** —
   `~/Desktop/db_inspection_22_prompts/10_eval_anchor_audit.sh`.
   Reports per prompt: ANCHOR_OK / FILENAME_MISMATCH / COLLISION_ONLY
   / GHOST_ANCHOR. Run once before drawing further conclusions from
   the 22-prompt grades.

### Fix #5 — OCR PSM/DPI made env-configurable (re-OCR lever for RoB)

`src-tauri/src/services/parsers/ocr.rs` + `parsers/pdf.rs`. The Sindh RoB
1986 PDF is a multi-column scan with marginal title labels — under
tesseract `--psm 1` (the previous hardcoded default) columns interleave,
producing the empty-shell chunks observed in the eval. Wired two env
vars and an `OcrConfig` field so the user can A/B different segmentation
modes on a single document without changing global defaults:

- `ECHO_OCR_PSM` (1–13; default `1`). Try `4` (single column of
  variable text) or `6` (single uniform block) on the RoB doc.
- `ECHO_OCR_DPI` (72–600; default `300`).

**Re-OCR recipe for RoB:**
```
# Set env before launching the app
export ECHO_OCR_PSM=4
# In the app: Sources → delete RoB → re-add (forces re-extraction)
# Then check chunk-shape with 02_chunk_size_distribution.sh
```

If PSM 4 / 6 don't recover the doc (likely — the marginal-label
interleaving is a layout problem OCR alone cannot solve), the only
remaining options are (a) swap to a different OCR engine such as
PaddleOCR / EasyOCR — out of scope for v1 — or (b) quarantine the doc
by deleting it through the UI. The other 5 indexed sources retain full
coverage either way.

### Verification path

- Existing unit tests: all passing (cargo check + targeted test runs).
- Empirical test: user re-indexes the 6 Sindh PDFs through the UI and
  re-runs `02_chunk_size_distribution.sh` and `10_eval_anchor_audit.sh`.
  Expected: APT avg chunk drops from 13 801 chars to ≤ ~1500;
  total APT tokens drops from 1.57 M to ≈150 k; no more 28 k-char `(a)`
  chunks; E&D detects Rules 1–9, 11+ (drops the 85-chunk Preamble);
  constitution source shows `indexing_status='indexed'`.

### Caveats

- `text_normalizer::normalize()` runs ONCE on the full doc before heading
  detection, so heading offsets remain consistent with the normalized
  text used for slicing. Re-running normalize on already-clean text is
  idempotent.
- Files touched: `db/schema.rs`, `services/structure_parser.rs`,
  `services/text_normalizer.rs`, `services/query_router.rs`,
  `services/doc_profiles/rules.rs`. No migration.

## 2026-05-25 (PM) — 22-prompt cross-model eval: quality bottlenecked by retrieval

Ran the 22 Sindh-corpus prompts on the post-Feature-005 index against four
local GGUFs. Results, per-prompt grades and 10-row root-cause table saved
to `~/Desktop/test 22 prompts/analysis_v1_repost.xlsx`.

**Per-model wall-clock totals** (22 prompts each):
- Qwen2.5-3B-instruct q4_k_m       — 66 min, 180 s avg, 8/22 OK+Partial
- Qwen2.5-1.5B-instruct q4_k_m     — 25 min,  67 s avg, 5/22 OK+Partial
- Qwen2.5-0.5B-instruct base       — 17 min,  48 s avg, 5/22 OK+Partial
- Qwen2.5-0.5B FT (sindh corpus)   — 14 min,  39 s avg, 5/22 OK+Partial

**Headline finding:** quality is dominated by RETRIEVAL errors, not model
size. The same prompts fail on every model because the citation fast-path
maps `unit_label = "Section 4" / "Rule 9"` to the first matching parent;
APT, E&D, RoB and the Manual all carry the same unit_label values.

**Top P0 fixes (ranked by impact / effort ratio):**
1. llama.cpp: add `repeat_penalty=1.15`, `no_repeat_ngram_size=4`, stop
   sequences `[<|im_end|>, "\nUser:", "\nSYSTEM:"]`. Kills the Q5/Q12/Q15
   repetition loops AND the Q20 system-prompt leak (XS effort).
2. `query_router.rs::resolve_unit_label_to_chunks`: filter matched
   `unit_label` hits by source-title keyword overlap with the query
   ("E&D", "Removal Ord", "APT", "RoB", "Manual") so cross-doc
   collisions resolve to the right parent (S effort, fixes ~5 prompts).
3. `structure_parser::persist_tree`: skip DocNodes whose own body is
   < 40 chars AND that have children — currently those heading-only
   chunks dominate top-K because unit_label is an exact match.
4. `build_context`: pre-truncate each chunk to 350 tokens before
   packing, allow K=4 chunks (current STEP-8 logs show "Selected: 1
   chunks (cap K=8)" because the first chunk is already 1912 chars).

**Other notable findings:**
- 1.5B over-refuses (9/22 "documents do not contain enough info" even
  when the chunks plainly contain the answer). Drop from tier2 auto.
- 0.5B fine-tuned on Sindh has LOST abstention — invents a fake
  "Rule 47 Section VIII" for "Karachi population 2025". Add ~15 %
  negative samples in next SFT batch.
- Whitespace pollution inside chunks: user reports LLM verbatim-pastes
  chunks including large blank-line runs. Text normalizer (Feature 005
  pipeline) is not collapsing repeated `\n`s on the indexing path for
  these PDFs. Diagnostic script `03_whitespace_pollution.sh` will
  quantify the extent.

**Diagnostic shell scripts written:** `~/Desktop/db_inspection_22_prompts/`
holds 9 read-only sqlite scripts (sources overview, chunk size dist,
whitespace pollution, empty heading-only chunks, unit_label collisions,
prompt-specific chunk dump, FTS hits per prompt, constitution failure
investigation, master runner). User runs them in their own shell per
`feedback-user-runs-db-inspection`.

**No code changed in this entry.** Branch `005-structured-importer`
state unchanged; act.rs patch + query_router.rs citation extension
remain uncommitted pending decision after the diagnostic outputs.

## 2026-05-25 — Feature 005 closed: generic structured importer (Act profile pattern fix)

**Symptom / why:** Feature 005 acceptance gate had 2/3 passing on
branch `005-structured-importer`. The Removal Act fixture
(`REMOVAL_FROM_SERVICE_SPECIAL_POWERS_SINDH_pdf.txt`, 20 628 bytes)
detected as `doc_type=act` correctly but produced
`structured=false`. Initial hypothesis (per pause-time memory note)
was a too-strict coverage threshold (`MIN_HEADING_COVERAGE=0.10`);
diagnosis showed the real cause was **zero heading regex matches**
in the fixture, not low coverage — the existing Act
`heading_patterns` did not fit the fixture's actual layout shapes.

**Diagnosed shapes the patterns missed:**
1. Marginal-label section: `Short title     1. (1) This Ordinance ...`
   — text label precedes the section number on the same line, so
   `^\s*N\.\s+\(N\)` cannot anchor.
2. Bare-number section with title or bracket marker:
   `3.       [Dismissal ...]`, `4.    Suspension. --- A person ...`,
   `15. Power to make rules. ---` — 13 such lines in the fixture; no
   existing pattern matched them.
3. Indented clauses: `        (2) It extended ...`,
   `      (3) The Inquiry Officer ...` — 7 such lines; existing
   `^\(N\)\s+[A-Z]` required column-0 `(`.

**Fix:** purely-additive change to `act` profile in
`src-tauri/src/services/doc_profiles/act.rs`:
- Added bare-number-section pattern
  `^\s*N\.\s+[\[A-Z][^\n]{0,120}` (leading `\s*` also tolerates the
  form-feed page-break that prefixes some sections in the OCR text).
- Added marginal-label section pattern
  `^[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+(?:\s+[a-z][a-zA-Z]*){0,4}\s{2,}N\.\s+\(N\)`,
  requiring 2+ spaces between Cap-leading label and the section
  number to avoid false positives on inline mentions like
  "section 5(2)".
- Relaxed existing Chapter/Section/Clause/SubClause patterns from
  `^…` to `^\s*…` so indent / form-feed prefixes don't defeat them.
- Existing patterns kept intact (dedup-by-offset in
  `regex_pass::scan_with_profile` collapses overlaps and keeps the
  deepest level).

**Post-fix numbers (same fixture):** 27 headings, coverage 0.91,
`structured=true`. Sections 1, 3, 4, 6, 12–16 detected at Article
level; sub-clauses `(a)`–`(c)` and clauses `(2)`–`(5)` slot under
their parents. Coverage threshold unchanged at 0.10.

**Acceptance gate
(`cargo test --test structured_importer_acceptance`):** 3/3 pass.

| Test | Status |
|---|---|
| every_sindh_fixture_gets_non_generic_doc_type | ✓ (Removal Act now `structured=true`) |
| generic_doc_produces_a_tree_with_at_least_one_chapter | ✓ |
| rules_fixture_persists_chunks_and_graph_nodes | ✓ |

Wall-clock: 1.33 s.

**Cross-cutting impact:** none — change is scoped to the `act`
profile constant. The `rules` profile reuses no shared regex with
`act`; the dedup-by-offset path in `heading_detector::regex_pass`
already handled multiple overlapping patterns.

**Caveats:**
- One pre-existing `manual` test was already failing on
  branch-tip before this change:
  `services::doc_profiles::manual::tests::detection_matches_manual_corpus`
  asserts that `manual` *detection_patterns* match
  `"1. RECEIPT AND DESPATCH"` / `"1.2 Indexing of files"`, but the
  detection patterns only carry word-class markers (`Manual`,
  `Instruction`, `Secretariat`, `^CHAPTER\s+[IVX]+`). This appears
  to be a test that confused detection-patterns with
  heading-patterns. Untouched here — flagged for a separate small
  fix.
- Acceptance run is offline-only (no LLM dependency); a manual UI
  re-index of the live Sindh corpus is still pending to confirm
  end-to-end persistence (graph_nodes jump from 1488 → >2000).

**Files:**
- `src-tauri/src/services/doc_profiles/act.rs` — added 2 heading
  patterns, prefixed `\s*` on 4 existing patterns.

**Env/flags:** `ECHO_STRUCTURED_IMPORTER=0` still disables the
pipeline. `STRUCTURED_IMPORTER_VERSION` unchanged (1).

## 2026-05-24 — Feature 004 closed: OCR integration for the PDF indexer

**Symptom / why:** Font-corrupted PDFs (Gutenberg-mirror Hamlet was the
canonical case; one of the six Sindh legal PDFs is image-only) extracted
via `lopdf`/`pdftotext` produced glyph-mangled text — curly braces
mid-word, replacement chars, broken word boundaries. This poisoned FTS5
tokenisation and dense embeddings, making downstream eval / retrieval
quality unmeasurable. The previous chars/page gate only caught image-only
PDFs and missed the font-corruption failure mode entirely.

**Fix:** three-tier extraction in
`src-tauri/src/services/parsers/pdf.rs::extract`:
1. `lopdf` (fast, no system deps)
2. `pdftotext` (poppler-utils — handles CID fonts / ToUnicode maps)
3. Tesseract OCR (`pdftoppm` rasterise → `tesseract` per page →
   form-feed stitched)

Tier promotion is gated by a new
`services::parsers::text_quality::score` combining four signals:
chars/page, non-ASCII-punct ratio, dict-hit ratio (bundled SCOWL
wordlist, 350 k words via `OnceLock<HashSet>`), mean token length. First
tier whose verdict is `Good` wins; otherwise the best-scoring candidate
is returned and marked `ocr_skipped` so it can be re-tried later.

OCR sub-flow lives in new `services::parsers::ocr` — subprocess
orchestration only, RAII temp dir under the data partition (never
`/tmp`; root-disk constraint). `OcrWork::Drop` deletes the dir + all
PNGs even on early-return.

**Schema:** migration `016_extraction_quality.sql` adds
`extraction_method TEXT` + `quality_score REAL` to `sources`. NULL for
legacy rows. Indexer persists both on every successful parse. Startup
hook `enqueue_quality_reextract(pool)` flips rows where
`quality_score IS NULL OR (quality_score < 0.6 AND
extraction_method != 'ocr')` back to `indexing_status='pending'`, so
they get re-extracted on next indexer pass. Idempotent; wired into
`setup_models_and_watchers` in `src-tauri/src/lib.rs`.

**Acceptance gate
(`cargo test --test ocr_integration_acceptance` with
`OCR_FIXTURE_DIR="/home/riaz/Desktop/Sindh Govt Documents"`):**

| File | Tier | Score | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| efficiency and disciplane rules.pdf | pdftotext | 1.000 | Good |
| Govt. of Sindh Manual of Secretariat instruction 2010.pdf | lopdf | 1.000 | Good |
| REMOVAL FROM SERVICE SPECIAL POWERS SINDH.pdf | pdftotext | 1.000 | Good |
| appointment promotion and transfer rules.pdf | pdftotext | 1.000 | Good |
| constitution.pdf | pdftotext | 1.000 | Good |
| sindh government rules of business 1986.pdf | **ocr** | 1.000 | Good |

6/6 PDFs end with `Verdict::Good`. The Sindh rules-of-business is
image-only and went through Tesseract; the others stayed on tier 1/2.
Wall-clock: 405 s total (OCR dominates). Born-digital control
(`constitution.pdf` did not need OCR) passes.

**Cross-cutting impact:** `ParsedDocument` gained two fields
(`extraction_method: &'static str`, `quality_score: f32`). All
non-PDF parsers (`text`, `document`, `image`, `audio_video`) updated to
emit `extraction_method = "native", quality_score = 1.0`. OCR module
emits `"ocr"`. Three-tier path in `pdf.rs` emits `"lopdf" |
"pdftotext" | "ocr" | "ocr_skipped"`.

**Drive-by fix:** `tests/integration/test_query_router.rs` had a
pre-existing compile error from feature 003's S3 reranker integration
— `route()` gained a `&RerankerSlot` argument that wasn't propagated
to the test. Two call sites updated to pass a lazy `RerankerSlot::new`
with `/dev/null` paths (loads only on `score_pairs`).

## 2026-05-23 — NER: Idea 2 — incremental full-coverage Pass-2 (10% batches × 30s rest until 100%)

**Why:** Diagnosis confirmed S3a NER ran on only **10 / 1467 chunks** (`ECHO_PASS2_CHUNK_LIMIT` default), so S3b entity-boost had nothing to match against — `entity_mentions` for the Preamble was zero, every NP boost reported `no-op`. The fixed-cap design treated Pass-2 as a one-shot sampling pass, never converging to full coverage no matter how many times the source was re-indexed. User-proposed fix: iterate. Cover the next 10% per batch, sleep, repeat, until 100% of chunks have entity rows.

**What:**
- **Migration** `015_ner_pass2_progress.sql` — new `chunks.ner_pass2_done INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (… IN (0,1))` column + partial index `idx_chunks_ner_pass2_pending` on `(source_id, ner_pass2_done) WHERE ner_pass2_done = 0` so the next-batch query is cheap.
- **Knobs:**
  - `ECHO_PASS2_BATCH_PCT` (default 10.0, range 1–100) — batch size as a percentage of *pending* chunks.
  - `ECHO_PASS2_SLEEP_SECS` (default 30, range 1–3600) — sleep between batches; yields to chat.
  - `ECHO_PASS2_CHUNK_LIMIT` — kept as a **deprecated absolute-count override** for one release. When set, logs a deprecation warning and uses the absolute count.
- **Helpers** (`services/indexer.rs`):
  - `pass2_batch_size(pending_total)` — returns batch size, honouring legacy override.
  - `pass2_sleep_secs()` — reads the sleep knob with range clamping.
  - `select_next_pass2_batch(pool, source_id)` — picks even-sampled indices across **pending** chunks, then **unions** with chunks whose `unit_label ∈ doc_profiles::is_salient_unit` (Preamble, Abstract, Foreword, …). Doc-agnostic — the salient list comes from registered DocProfiles, no constitution-specific code.
  - `run_ner_loop_for_source(pool, app, source_id, file_name)` — Pass-1 regex on all chunks once, then iterative Pass-2: register with `WorkloadKind::Pass2Ner` scheduler → `should_pause().await` → select batch → process each chunk (set `ner_pass2_done = 1` on success) → emit `kg://progress` with `pass`/`batch_size`/`batch_ms` → sleep → repeat. Exits when no pending chunks remain → marks `sources.ner_status='done'` (final). Cancellable mid-batch via the existing scheduler.
  - `resume_pending_pass2_ner(pool, app)` — startup recovery; scans for sources with any `ner_pass2_done = 0` chunks and spawns the loop for each. Idempotent.
- **Wired into:**
  - `index_constitution()` — replaces the S3a single-shot `run_ner_for_source` spawn with `run_ner_loop_for_source`.
  - `lib.rs::setup_models_and_watchers` — startup hook calls `resume_pending_pass2_ner` after the existing NER recovery block, so any source that didn't finish in the previous session continues from where it left off.

**Why this design — explicit non-goals:**
- Pass-1 still runs on all chunks at index time (fast, no need to batch).
- The cross-encoder reranker, salience boost, definitional classifier, entity boost — all unchanged. This is *NER coverage only*.
- `do_index` (non-constitution sources) still has its own inline Pass-2 spawn for now — not switched to the loop in this round to keep the diff focused on the constitution path that the F5-imperative diagnosis targeted. Queued as a follow-up: unify both code paths around `run_ner_loop_for_source`.

**Serialisation — matches existing inline Pass-2 path.** Loop uses
`entity_sem()` (the same single-permit semaphore the legacy
`run_ner_for_source` and `do_index`'s inline Pass-2 use) to ensure only
one Pass-2 LLM call runs at a time. **Foreground scheduler is NOT used
this round** — `WorkloadKind::Pass2Ner` would be cancelled by the
default-foreground `WorkloadKind::Chat`, and no production code
currently calls `set_foreground(Chat)` from query.rs to re-claim it.
Wiring proper scheduler coordination for Pass-2 (so the loop pauses
mid-batch when chat starts) is queued as a separate task — it touches
`query.rs::stream_query_notebook` to add the missing
`set_foreground(Chat)` call and could affect chat startup latency, so
not appropriate to bundle. Chat and Pass-2 chunks compete for the LLM
via `ModelSlot`'s mutex; worst-case latency for chat is one Pass-2
chunk (~5–10 s) waiting for the in-flight `extract_pass2` to release.
The `tokio::time::sleep(30s)` between batches is the breathing-room
that prevents continuous LLM hogging across batches.

**Operational behaviour after this ships:**
- A 1480-chunk constitution at 10% batches → **~10 passes**.
- Per-chunk Pass-2 ~5–10 s on local 0.5–3B → batch takes **~12–25 min**.
- 30 s sleep between batches → wall-clock convergence **~2–4 hours** of idle time after first index.
- Salient chunks (Preamble) processed in the **very first batch** — entity rows for `Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah`, `Pakistan`, `Founder of Pakistan`, etc. exist within minutes of indexing, even before full coverage is reached. S3b entity-boost starts paying off immediately.
- Chat any time → loop pauses mid-chunk, resumes when foreground returns to non-Chat.
- Quit / restart the app → next launch's `resume_pending_pass2_ner` picks up unfinished sources.

**Tests (7 new, all passing):**
- `pass2_coverage_tests::batch_size_pct_default_is_ten_percent` — defaults 10% of 100 = 10; 10% of 33 = 4 (ceil).
- `pass2_coverage_tests::batch_size_floors_at_one` — tiny corpora (5 chunks) still get batch size 1.
- `pass2_coverage_tests::legacy_absolute_count_overrides_pct` — `ECHO_PASS2_CHUNK_LIMIT=5` returns 5 with deprecation warning logged.
- `pass2_coverage_tests::sleep_secs_respects_range` — invalid values fall back to default.
- `pass2_coverage_tests::first_batch_includes_salient_even_when_offset` — Preamble at chunk_index=1 is included even though even-sample positions are 0, 10, 20, … → 11 chunks total (10 even-sample + 1 Preamble).
- `pass2_coverage_tests::second_batch_excludes_first_batch_chunks` — after marking first batch `ner_pass2_done=1`, the second batch is disjoint and covers 10% of the remaining 90 = 9 chunks.
- `pass2_coverage_tests::empty_batch_when_all_done` — terminator for the loop.

Full services suite: **125 / 125 pass** (118 pre-Idea-2 + 7 new).

**Operational steps (you):**
1. Rebuild — `./run-dev.sh`. Migration `015_…sql` applies on first launch.
2. Existing chunks (from before the migration) start with `ner_pass2_done = 0`. The startup hook will spawn the loop on each affected source.
3. Re-import the constitution if you want a fully fresh state, OR just let the loop catch up on the existing data over the next few sessions.
4. Watch `kg://progress` events. Each emits `pass: N · batch_size: K · batch_ms: T · processed: D · total: T` so you can see the loop's progress.
5. Smoke-test: ask a question, see the loop pause (no kg://progress events while chatting); after answer completes, see the loop resume.
6. After ~10 batches per source: `sources.ner_status='done'` final; entity coverage 100% per source.

**Cross-cutting / follow-ups:**
- Unify `do_index`'s inline Pass-2 spawn with `run_ner_loop_for_source` — same incremental coverage for non-constitution docs. Queued as separate task.
- Add a "Resume NER now" button in Settings (skip the next sleep, fire the loop immediately). Nice-to-have, not required.
- If batches feel too long, drop `ECHO_PASS2_BATCH_PCT` to 5 (20 passes) or raise sleep to 300s for a calmer trickle.

**Files:**
- `src-tauri/src/db/migrations/015_ner_pass2_progress.sql` — NEW.
- `src-tauri/src/services/indexer.rs` — `pass2_batch_size`, `pass2_sleep_secs`, `select_next_pass2_batch`, `run_ner_loop_for_source`, `resume_pending_pass2_ner` (~210 lines added), `index_constitution` spawn updated, 7 new tests (~145 lines).
- `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` — startup hook calls `resume_pending_pass2_ner`.

## 2026-05-23 — Retrieval: Idea 1 — paragraph-level splitting of long structural chunks (F5-imperative root-cause fix)

**Why:** A formal six-section diagnosis (`~/Desktop/test 5 prompts/diagnosis-F5-imperative.md`) measured why every F5-imperative attempt fixed nothing despite four sequential boosts (S1/S2/S3a/S3b). All boosts report `no-op` in the trace because the Preamble doesn't enter the post-RRF pool — and the boosts can only re-rank what retrieval found. Root cause has two compounding parts:

1. **BM25 length penalty (FTS5):** Preamble is 2775 chars — the **single longest chunk in the corpus of 1467**, at the 100th percentile, 11× the mean (253 chars). BM25 length-normalises it severely against short Articles (166–200 chars) that also contain "Pakistan" + "Constitution".
2. **Single-vector dilution (vec0):** the Preamble's 768-d embedding represents the *average* meaning of all 428 tokens (sovereignty, Allah, principles of democracy, Islam, federation, freedoms, judiciary, prosperity, declarations). The "Founder of Pakistan, Quaid-i-Azam" sentence is one signal in 14 paragraphs; cosine similarity to a focused query is low.

User proposed (and I confirmed) the indexing-time fix: split long chunks into paragraph-level pieces with the same `unit_label` so each piece has a focused embedding AND a small BM25 footprint. This is **the architecturally correct fix** rather than another post-retrieval boost.

**What:**
- New `structure_parser::split_long_text(text, threshold)` helper. Splits on paragraph boundaries (`\n\n`) first; falls back to sentence boundaries (`.` `?` `!` followed by whitespace); last resort character-cut at `threshold` chars. Drops empty pieces. Returns input unchanged when ≤ threshold. Generic — applies wherever long-text dilution hurts retrieval.
- New knob `ECHO_LONG_CHUNK_THRESHOLD` (default **1000 chars**, floor 100). At default, only the long tail (3/1467 chunks in the current corpus, of which the Preamble is the only canonical one) splits — no collateral damage to working retrieval.
- `structure_parser::build_preamble` rewritten:
  - Short preamble (≤ threshold) → same shape as pre-Idea-1 (single leaf node).
  - Long preamble → article-level **parent** with body `"Preamble"` (a citation marker) plus N **clause-level children**, each carrying one paragraph as content. Children share the parent's `unit_label = 'Preamble'` (so the salience boost still applies to every paragraph) and use `unit_path = 'Preamble/p1', 'Preamble/p2', …` (kept under the parent prefix so the citation fast-path's `unit_path LIKE 'Preamble/%'` returns the full sub-tree).
- Citation fast-path needs **zero code change** — the existing `unit_path = ? OR unit_path LIKE 'p/%'` query naturally returns the parent + all paragraph children.

**Why this design:**
- Parent stays at article level so `unit_label = 'Preamble'` resolves to exactly one canonical row (citation fast-path semantics unchanged for callers that want "the preamble").
- Children at clause level matches the structural metaphor (sub-units of an article) and respects the existing `chunks.unit_type` CHECK constraint.
- Same `unit_label` across parent and children → S1 salience boost lifts every Preamble chunk together; ranking decision is made by content relevance among them.
- Different `unit_path` per child → vec0 and FTS5 see them as distinct documents; the "Founder" paragraph wins on its own merits.

**Math on the actual Preamble:**
- 2775 chars → 14 natural paragraphs (separated by `\n\n` in the IR).
- Default threshold 1000 → triggers paragraph split.
- "Founder of Pakistan, Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah" paragraph: ~250 chars (in the mean band) → no BM25 penalty.
- Its single-purpose embedding has tight cosine alignment to "Who is the founder of Pakistan" — expected top-3 on vec0 alone, no boost needed.

**Tests:**
- `structure_parser::persist_tests::persist_tree_writes_every_node_with_resolving_parents` — updated: still asserts 313 article chunks (parent unchanged); adds positive assertions that ≥2 Preamble paragraph children exist, exactly one contains "Quaid-i-Azam", and every child links to the parent.
- 5 NEW `split_long_text` unit tests — input under threshold, paragraph split, sentence-fallback, char-cut for unbroken text, empty-piece drop.
- 1 NEW `build_preamble_splits_real_constitution_preamble_correctly` — loads the real IR, asserts ≥5 paragraph children, "Quaid-i-Azam" in exactly one.
- `query_router::tests::citation_fast_path_resolves_cited_units` — updated: previous assertion "Preamble resolves to 1 chunk" replaced with "Preamble resolves to ≥2 chunks (parent + paragraph children)".

**Operational steps (you):**
1. DB triplet asided to `echo.db.bak-pre-idea1-*` (live triplet is gone).
2. Rebuild (`./run-dev.sh`).
3. Re-import the constitution — fresh DB, fresh chunking. Expect 1467 → ~1480 chunks (Preamble splits into ~14 paragraphs; other chunks unchanged).
4. Smoke-test BEFORE running the full F5 set:
   - Inspect the DB: `SELECT unit_label, unit_path, length(content) FROM chunks WHERE unit_label='Preamble' ORDER BY unit_path;` — expect parent + N paragraph rows.
   - Ask **"what does the preamble say"** in the app — trace should show citation fast-path returns multiple chunks (parent + paragraphs). LLM should answer with the full Preamble.
   - Ask **"Who is called the founder of Pakistan in the Constitution?"** — trace STEP 8 should show top match is a Preamble paragraph (not Article 276). Salience boost may report no-op now since the paragraph wins on raw RRF; that's fine.
5. If smoke passes → run F5 × 3 registers × 3 local models, save as `preamble_v2_idea1.odt` per folder for comparison against `preamble_v1.*`.

**Cross-cutting / follow-ups:**
- Splitter is generic — when we add Acts / Policies, any long opening (Preamble · Abstract · Statement of Objects and Reasons) gets the same paragraph-level treatment automatically.
- If F5-imperative still fails empirically (cross-encoder buries the focused paragraph anyway), fall back to Option α canonical fallback as a query-time safety net. Idea 1 is the empirical test of whether indexing-time fix alone is enough.
- Idea 2 (NER percentage coverage + always-include salient chunks) is queued as the next change — gives S3b real data to work with for definitional queries whose answers depend on named entities outside structural openings. Chat-priority pause already implemented via `WorkloadKind::Pass2Ner` in `services/scheduler.rs`; no new work needed there.

**Files:**

- `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` — citation_fast_path test assertion updated (parent + children, not 1 chunk).

## 2026-05-23 — Retrieval: S3b entity-aware re-rank (post-RRF NP-match boost)

**Why:** S3a populated the entity tables for constitution chunks but the
data wasn't used by retrieval scoring. S3b wires it in: chunks whose
extracted entities match capitalised noun phrases in the query get a
multiplicative score boost. Closes the loop for queries that name a
specific person/place/concept that isn't a structural unit label —
e.g. "Who is Mohammad Ali Jinnah?" goes straight to the chunk whose
NER tagged "Mohammad Ali Jinnah" as a person entity, no matter where
that chunk sits in the hybrid pool.

**Why approach (b) post-RRF NP-match boost (over approach (a) FTS5-index
entity surface forms):**
- Matches the S1/S2 composition pattern (post-RRF reordering) — same
  shape, same trace step, same kind of test.
- No schema change required. `entities` and `entity_mentions` tables
  already exist (since 001_initial_schema.sql).
- Configurable via `ECHO_ENTITY_BOOST` (default 1.4). Disable with 1.0.
- Composes naturally with S1/S2 — each pass rebuilds base score from
  position, so an entity-matched chunk at salience-rank 3 (base 1/63 =
  0.0159, × 1.4 = 0.0222) can leapfrog a salience-rank 1 non-matching
  chunk (0.0164). Multi-signal lift without explicit coupling.

**Design:**
- New `extract_query_entities(query) -> Vec<String>` — regex picks
  capitalised runs (hyphens/apostrophes allowed inside, supports
  multi-word phrases like "Mohammad Ali Jinnah", "Quaid-i-Azam",
  "Federal Capital Territory"). Sentence-initial lone caps dropped
  as grammar. Case-insensitive dedup. Pure English grammar — works
  on any document type.
- New `apply_entity_boost(pool, ranked, query, boost)` — JOINs
  `entities` + `entity_mentions` to find chunks whose canonical entity
  values match any extracted NP (LOWER comparison). Boosts matched
  chunks' position-derived scores. Safe on DB errors — returns input
  unchanged. No-op when boost ≤ 1.0, no NPs in query, or no entity
  matches in DB.
- Wired in both production paths (main retrieval + retry path).
- Trace STEP "Merge & rank candidates" now reports
  `Entity boost: N NPs detected · applied (top changed) / no-op`
  so the in-app trace shows whether S3b fired and what its NPs were.

**Limitations (deliberate, documented):**
- Lowercase concept entities ("high treason", "fundamental rights")
  not matched by current NP extractor. Fix when needed via a
  lowercase substring scan against `entities.canonical_value`. Adding
  it now would risk false positives without evidence of need.
- Quality of S3b depends entirely on NER quality (S3a). MEMORY flags
  `bug_kg_poor_entity_extraction.md`; if NER tags garbage, S3b boosts
  the wrong chunks. Mitigation: `ECHO_ENTITY_BOOST=1.0` disables S3b
  entirely without removing S3a's data collection.

**Tests:**
- `services::query_router::tests::extract_query_entities_pulls_capitalised_phrases`
  — NEW. 6 cases: single proper noun, multi-word, hyphenated, lone
  sentence-initial dropped, no-caps empty, dedup.
- `services::query_router::tests::entity_boost_lifts_chunk_with_matching_entity`
  — NEW. Real entity + entity_mentions fixture; Preamble (rank 3)
  with "Mohammad Ali Jinnah" entity must lift to rank 1 for the query
  "Who is Mohammad Ali Jinnah?".
- `services::query_router::tests::entity_boost_noop_when_no_match`
  — NEW. Two scenarios: query has NPs but no matching entities; query
  has no capitalised NPs at all. Order preserved in both cases.

**Operational steps (you):**
1. Rebuild (`./run-dev.sh`).
2. Re-import the constitution so S3a NER runs and populates `entities`
   + `entity_mentions` for constitution chunks. Wait for `kg://progress`
   to reach 100%.
3. Re-ask "Who is Mohammad Ali Jinnah?" (and similar queries naming a
   specific entity from constitution). Trace STEP "Merge & rank" should
   show `Entity boost: ≥1 NPs detected · applied`.
4. Re-ask "What does Article 10 say" — entity boost should report
   `0 NPs detected · no-op` (Article + numbers don't qualify as NPs).

**Cross-cutting / follow-ups:**
- Both boost passes (S1/S2 salience + S3b entity) reset the score from
  rank position. If we later want strictly multiplicative composition,
  merge into one pass. Current behaviour is acceptable.
- The lowercase-concept matching gap is the next obvious extension if
  NER quality on legal text turns out good enough to justify it.

**Files:**
- `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` — `knob_entity_boost()`,
  `extract_query_entities()`, `apply_entity_boost()`, two production
  call sites (main + retry), trace step extended, three new unit tests.

## 2026-05-23 — Constitution NER: S3a enables Pass-1/Pass-2 extraction for constitution chunks

**Why:** The v1 design rationale ("constitution's structure graph IS its
knowledge graph, no NER needed") was correct for citation-style queries
that go through the Article-fast-path, but it left definitional queries
without entity-level matching. After S1+S2 close the canonical-section
gap, the next class of failures will be queries that need a specific
entity (person, place, concept) that is not a structural unit label.
NER tags Preamble with `Quaid-i-Azam`, `Mohammad Ali Jinnah`, `Founder
of Pakistan`, `Islam`, etc.; tags Article 41 with `President`; etc.

S3a only **populates** the entity tables — it does not change retrieval
scoring. S3b (queued) will wire the data into query ranking.

**Why S3a alone is shippable now:**
1. Removes a constitution-specific bypass in the indexer → symmetry with
   every other doc type → cleaner ground for the queued
   `index_constitution → index_structured_doc` generalisation.
2. Lets us inspect actual NER quality on real constitution chunks
   (MEMORY.md flags `bug_kg_poor_entity_extraction.md` — we need
   evidence on legal text to decide whether to invest in S3b or first
   fix NER quality).
3. No retrieval behaviour change — zero regression risk for the
   F1–F5 test set or any production query.

**What:**
- `services/indexer.rs::index_constitution` — the comment block
  `// v1 scope: ... not run here` plus the bare `Ok(())` is replaced
  with a `tokio::spawn(run_ner_for_source(...))` that mirrors the
  do_index pattern: fires after `set_indexed_at` so the UI flips to
  "indexed" immediately, runs Pass 1 (regex) then Pass 2 (LLM, capped
  by `ECHO_PASS2_CHUNK_LIMIT`) in the background.
- Only fires when `app: Some(AppHandle)` — Pass 2 reads `model_slot`
  from Tauri State. Integration tests with `app: None` keep the
  pre-S3a behaviour (no NER), which is fine for retrieval tests.

**Operational steps (you):**
1. Rebuild (`./run-dev.sh`).
2. Re-import the constitution (or wait for a re-index trigger).
3. Watch the `kg://progress` events flow as Pass 2 chews through up to
   `ECHO_PASS2_CHUNK_LIMIT` chunks. Default cap is 10; can raise via
   the env var if you want full coverage (slower).
4. After NER completes, inspect the `entities` / `graph_nodes` tables
   to see what NER extracted from constitution chunks. Quality
   evidence drives the S3b approach choice.

**Cross-cutting / follow-ups:**
- S3b (queued, task #6) will wire entity matches into retrieval. Two
  candidate approaches surfaced: (a) FTS5-index entity surface forms,
  (b) post-RRF NP-match boost. Pick after S3a NER quality assessment.
- The `index_constitution → index_structured_doc` rename (queued,
  task #4) becomes more important once NER also runs on this path —
  the two doc-type handlers now do the same thing and should share code.
- NER quality bug `bug_kg_poor_entity_extraction.md` is the gate for
  S3b's value. If NER extracts garbage from legal text, S3b will boost
  the wrong chunks.

**Files:**

## 2026-05-23 — Retrieval: S2 definitional-question classifier + widened candidate pool

**Why:** S1 alone fixes the F5-imperative class only when the canonical
chunk is already inside the post-RRF candidate window (default 24).
For harder pools where the canonical chunk lives at rank 25+, even a
1.3× boost can't lift it. S2 detects English question-grammar that
signals a definitional query and (a) doubles the FTS5 + vector pool
widths just for that query, (b) escalates the salience boost from
1.3× to 1.6×. Both knobs configurable.

**Design — language-grammar, no doc-specific tokens:**
- New `is_definitional(query)` regex matches universal English
  question stems: `who is/was/founded/created/established/wrote/coined/
  invented/discovered`, `whom does/did/is`, `what is the meaning of`,
  `what does X mean`, `define X`, `meaning of X`. Negative on
  instance / event / yes-no queries (`what does Article 10 say`,
  `when was X adopted`, `does X permit Y`).
- `apply_salience_boost(pool, ranked, boost)` now takes the boost
  multiplier as a parameter so S2 can pass `ECHO_DEFINITIONAL_BOOST`
  (default 1.6) on hits and `ECHO_SALIENT_BOOST` (default 1.3)
  otherwise. Mechanism stays in one function.
- `fts5_retrieve(..., limit_override)` accepts an optional per-call
  cap so the pool can be widened only when needed — no permanent
  cost on non-definitional queries.
- New knobs: `ECHO_DEFINITIONAL_BOOST` (default 1.6),
  `ECHO_DEFINITIONAL_POOL_MULT` (default 2.0). Set to 1.0 to disable
  the corresponding lever.

**Trace visibility:** new STEP "Definitional classifier (S2)" reports
`Matched: true/false`, `Pool multiplier: 2.00×`, `Salience boost: 1.60×`
so the in-app trace shows whether S2 fired.

**Tests:**
- `services::query_router::tests::is_definitional_matches_canonical_question_shapes`
  — NEW. 10 positive cases (who is, whom does, what is the meaning of,
  define X, who founded, etc.); 6 negative cases (instance, event,
  yes-no, empty).
- `services::query_router::tests::definitional_boost_lifts_salient_chunk_buried_deeper`
  — NEW. 8-chunk pool with Preamble at rank 8; 1.6× boost must still
  lift it to rank 1. Locks the stronger boost path in place.

**Operational steps (you):**
1. Rebuild (`./run-dev.sh`).
2. Re-ask "Who is the founder of Pakistan?" — trace STEP "Definitional
   classifier" should report `Matched: true · Pool multiplier: 2.00× ·
   Salience boost: 1.60×`. STEP "Merge & rank" should show salience
   boost applied. Top match should be Preamble.
3. Re-ask "Who founded the Federation?" / "Define high treason" —
   same trace pattern.
4. Ask "What does Article 10 say" — trace should report
   `Matched: false`, pool stays at 1.00×, boost stays at 1.30×.

**Cross-cutting / follow-ups:**
- The retry path (`retry_raw`) inherits the same definitional
  widening + boost so retries can also benefit.
- S2's regex is English-only. Urdu/Roman-Urdu definitional patterns
  (e.g. "کون", "kon hai", "kis ne") not yet covered; queue alongside
  the multilingual question-prediction work.

**Files:**
- `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` — `is_definitional()`,
  `knob_definitional_boost()`, `knob_definitional_pool_mult()`,
  `fts5_retrieve()` gains `limit_override`, `apply_salience_boost()`
  gains `boost` parameter, both production paths (main + retry) wired,
  new STEP in trace, two new unit tests.

## 2026-05-23 — Retrieval: S1 salience-aware re-ranking via DocProfile (F5-imperative fix)

**Why:** F5-imperative ("Who is called the founder of Pakistan?") failed on
all three local models post-Preamble-fix because the query contained no
citation keyword — fast-path skipped, hybrid retrieval picked Article 41
("President of Pakistan", surface-matches "founder of Pakistan" well) over
the Preamble (canonical chunk with the real answer "Founder of Pakistan,
Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah"). Even 3B can't answer correctly when
the wrong chunk is in the context.

User rejected the obvious-but-wrong "hardcode keywords like founder/
quaid/jinnah in detect_citation" patch — it doesn't generalise to Acts /
Policies / Rules / Notifications. Discussed four general solutions
(S1=salience boost, S2=definitional classifier + widened pool,
S3=re-enable NER for constitution, S4=HyDE expansion); user picked
S1 + S2 + S3, deferred S4 to a future "input-layer enhancements" feature
(combines with prompt prediction + runtime spelling autocorrect).

This entry covers **S1 only**; S2 and S3 land separately.

**Design — doc-agnostic mechanism, per-doc-type config:**
- `DocProfile` gains a `salient_units: &'static [&'static str]` field.
  Each profile lists the unit labels that are "canonical / declarative"
  for its document type. Constitution: `["Preamble"]`. A future Acts
  profile could list `["Preamble", "Statement of Objects and Reasons"]`,
  a research-paper profile `["Abstract", "Conclusion"]`, etc.
- New `doc_profiles::is_salient_unit(label)` walks all registered
  profiles and returns true if any lists the label. v1 has one profile;
  v2 will switch to per-source lookup via the queued `sources.doc_type`
  column when two profiles ever disagree on the same label.
- New `query_router::apply_salience_boost(pool, ranked) -> ranked`
  fetches `unit_label` for every chunk in the post-RRF candidate list,
  multiplies position-derived scores by `ECHO_SALIENT_BOOST` (default
  1.3) when the label is salient, and re-sorts. Safe on DB errors —
  returns input unchanged.
- Wired into both production paths in `route_scoped`:
  (a) main retrieval immediately after the RRF/FTS-only/vec-only
  selection and before the "Merge & rank candidates" trace, and
  (b) the reviewer-retry path (`retry_raw`) for consistency.

**Why a 1.3× multiplier is the right magnitude (math):**
- RRF position scores: rank 1 ≈ 0.0164 (1/61), rank 4 ≈ 0.0156 (1/64).
- 1.3× on rank-4 Preamble: 0.0156 × 1.3 = 0.0203 → leapfrogs rank-1 Article 41.
- 1.3× on rank-1 vs rank-2: 0.0164 × 1.3 = 0.0213 vs 0.0162 → still wins
  (but the chunk was already #1, so the swap is a no-op).
- A clearly dominant non-salient match (rank 1 by huge margin in both FTS and vec)
  still wins because RRF accumulates: 0.0164 + 0.0164 = 0.0328 > 0.0203.
- Result: boost lifts canonical chunks above leaf chunks **at comparable scores**
  without overriding a clearly better hybrid match. Anti-monopoly purpose of
  hybrid ranking is preserved.

**Trace visibility:** STEP 6 ("Merge & rank candidates") now emits a
`Salience boost: applied (top changed)` or `no-op` line so users can tell
whether the boost fired on any given query.

**Tests:**
- `services::doc_profiles::is_salient_unit` — covered indirectly via
  query_router test below.
- `services::query_router::tests::salient_unit_registry_recognises_preamble`
  — NEW. Sanity check for the registry helper.
- `services::query_router::tests::salience_boost_lifts_preamble_above_article_41`
  — NEW. Replays the F5-imperative scenario verbatim: 4-chunk pool with
  Article 41 at rank 1 and Preamble at rank 4, post-boost Preamble must be
  rank 1.
- `services::query_router::tests::salience_boost_noop_when_no_salient_chunk`
  — NEW. Negative case — order preserved exactly when no chunk is salient
  (non-canonical queries unaffected).

**Operational steps (you):**
1. Rebuild (`./run-dev.sh`).
2. Re-ask "Who is called the founder of Pakistan?" in the app.
3. Trace STEP 6 should show `Salience boost: applied (top changed)`,
   top match should now be the Preamble chunk, answer should quote
   "Founder of Pakistan, Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah".
4. Re-ask "Who founded Pakistan?" and "Pakistan's first leader was?"
   — both should also work for the same reason (no citation keyword,
   salience boost lifts Preamble).
5. Existing queries that don't touch Preamble must remain unchanged —
   trace will read `Salience boost: no-op` for those.

**Cross-cutting / follow-ups:**
- S2 (definitional-question classifier + widened pool) will stack on
  top — when the query is definitional AND a chunk is salient, the
  boost can be stronger (e.g. 1.6×) and the candidate pool wider.
- S3 (re-enable NER for constitution chunks) will reach noun-phrase
  matches that the salience boost alone can't (e.g. queries naming an
  entity that's mentioned in only one non-canonical chunk).
- `index_constitution() → index_structured_doc()` rename is queued and
  non-blocking; S1 works under the current name.
- The `sources.doc_type` column is the right long-term home for the
  per-source profile lookup. Adding it is a 1-line ALTER TABLE +
  1-line write in the importer; not done in this entry to keep the
  diff small.

**Files:**
- `src-tauri/src/services/doc_profiles/mod.rs` — `salient_units` field
  on DocProfile; new `is_salient_unit(label)` helper with documented
  v1 limitation.
- `src-tauri/src/services/doc_profiles/constitution.rs` —
  `salient_units: &["Preamble"]` on CONSTITUTION; doc comment.
- `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` — `knob_salient_boost()`
  (default 1.3, ECHO_SALIENT_BOOST), `apply_salience_boost()` post-RRF
  re-ranker (~50 lines), two call sites (main + retry), trace entry,
  three new unit tests.

## 2026-05-23 — Retrieval: single-chunk citation dropped by per-chunk cap (Preamble regression)

**Symptom:** `what does the preamble say?` returned `"No relevant information
found in provided documents"` despite the Preamble row being present in the
DB (`unit_label = "Preamble"`, 2775 chars) and the citation fast-path
correctly resolving it. Trace `~/Desktop/test 5 prompts/Qwen 3B/latest_test.log`
(2026-05-23 12:52, 88 ms total): STEP 5 fast-path returned 1 chunk; STEP 6
merge & rank passed it through (1 unique chunk, strategy `citation`); STEP 7
build context: **`Selected: 0 chunks (cap K=12)`** — the chunk was silently
filtered out by `build_context()`.

**Root cause (`query_router.rs::build_context`):**
- Preamble content: 2775 chars → estimated tokens `2775/4 + 20 = 713`.
- Per-chunk cap: `token_budget × ECHO_PER_CHUNK_CAP_FRAC = 2400 × 0.25 = 600`.
- `713 > 600` → `continue` (line 2267, pre-fix) — chunk dropped, unconditional.
- Pool size was 1 (citation fast-path), so the loop ended with `selected = []`.

The per-chunk cap exists to prevent a single oversized chunk from monopolising
the context window when there are competing chunks (e.g. a 4000-tok TOC chunk
crowding out 11 useful Articles). That is the right rule for hybrid retrieval.
On the citation fast-path, however, the pool can be a single chunk by design
(Preamble; an Article with no clauses; a sub-clause leaf) — there is nothing
to "protect from monopolisation", and the cap fires anyway.

The same `build_context()` already has an `!selected.is_empty() &&` guard on
the *budget-overflow* check one branch below ("Always admit the very first
chunk regardless of size"). The per-chunk cap was added later (Tier 3 Task 11)
and was missing the same guard — an oversight, not a deliberate divergence.

**Fix (smallest viable diff — Option A, one extra condition):**

```rust
// query_router.rs:2265-2275 (post-fix)
let per_chunk_cap = ((token_budget as f32) * frac) as usize;
if !selected.is_empty() && estimated > per_chunk_cap {  // ← guard added
    continue;
}
```

Mirrors the existing budget-overflow override exactly. First chunk always
admitted past both checks; subsequent oversized chunks still filtered.
Anti-monopoly purpose preserved for hybrid pools.

**Tests:**
- `services::query_router::tests::context_builder_admits_single_oversized_citation_chunk`
  — NEW. Reproduces the Preamble scenario verbatim: 1 chunk of 2775 chars,
  budget 2400 tokens, cap 0.25. Pre-fix: returns 0 chunks. Post-fix: returns 1.
- `services::query_router::tests::context_builder_always_includes_first_chunk`
  — existing. Asserts `result.len() == 1` for a 10 000-char single chunk at
  budget 100; this was failing under the pre-fix code path (the per-chunk cap
  would drop it before the first-chunk override could save it). Now passes
  for the right reason.

**Operational steps (you):**
1. Rebuild the app binary (`./run-dev.sh` or however you launch).
2. Re-ask "what does the preamble say?" — trace STEP 7 should show
   `Selected: 1 chunks (cap K=12)`, `Total content: ~2780 chars (~700 tokens)`,
   answer should quote the Preamble (Founder of Pakistan, Quaid-i-Azam, etc).

**Why:** Groq's free-tier quota is hitting during the F1–F5 cloud comparison
run (user reported during the three-model local test). All major OpenAI-

streaming, so adding multi-provider support is a config-only change — no
new code paths, no new dependencies.

  `groq` · `cerebras` · `openrouter` · `together` · `deepseek` · `openai` ·
  `fireworks` · `custom`.

  non-empty `endpoint_url` always wins (lets users point at internal
  proxies). Unknown provider strings fall back to Groq for backwards
  compatibility with pre-multi-provider `cloud_settings.json` files.

  `groq_complete` now derive their POST URL via `endpoint()`. Function
  names kept (`groq_*`) so call sites in `batch_processor`, `analysis_engine`,
  `entity_extractor`, and `query_router` don't churn — they're just names
  now, the actual provider is determined by `settings`.

  active; they say "{provider} HTTP …" instead.

**Frontend:**
- `src/api/index.ts::CloudSettings` adds optional `endpoint_url`.
- `src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx` Cloud Inference section rewritten:
  - Provider `<select>` with all 8 options (suggested model and
    key-console URL change with the selection).
  - Conditional Endpoint URL field shown only when `provider === "custom"`.
  - Model is now a free-text `<input>` (was a hard-coded 3-option dropdown
    that only matched Groq) — paste any provider's model id. A placeholder
    plus help line below shows the suggested model for the chosen provider.
  - Selecting a new provider pre-fills the model field only if the current
    value is empty or matches a known suggestion — never clobbers a user's
    custom model id.

**Operational steps (you):**
1. Open Settings → Cloud Inference.
2. Switch Provider to e.g. **Cerebras** (very fast free tier, generous quota).
3. Paste the matching API key (the help line shows where to get one).

5. Toggle "Enable cloud inference" on and Save.
6. Existing `cloud_settings.json` keeps working — the missing `endpoint_url`
   field defaults to `""` (use provider default) and the existing
   `provider: "groq"` stays valid.
