  field, three call sites + three error messages updated.
- `src/api/index.ts` — optional `endpoint_url` field on `CloudSettings`.
- `src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx` — provider dropdown, conditional endpoint

## 2026-05-23 — Constitution: Preamble import gap fixed (feature 003, A4 follow-up)

**Symptom:** Fact 5 ("Founder of Pakistan, Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah")
returned nothing on every register variant during T028/A4 in-app retrieval.
Hybrid retrieval had no chunk to match; fast-path had no `unit_label` to
resolve. Root-cause audit confirmed the IR carried the full Preamble
(`tools/constitution_import/constitute_IR/constitution_ir.json` →
top-level `"preamble"`, 2.2 KB), but `structure_parser::parse_tree` built the
root `Document` from `ir.parts` alone and silently dropped `ir.preamble`. No
chunk → no embedding → no FTS row → no graph node.

**Fix (smallest viable diff, single drop-point):**
- `src-tauri/src/services/structure_parser.rs::parse_tree`: now prepends a
  Preamble node when `ir.preamble` is non-empty (trim + emptiness guard).
- New helper `build_preamble(text)`: emits one `NodeLevel::Article` leaf with
  `citation = "Preamble"`, `unit_path = "Preamble"` (top-level, sibling of
  Parts — *not* nested inside a Part), `title = None` (avoids the
  "Preamble — Preamble" heading duplication that the Article render path
  would otherwise produce), no clauses, no attached/footnote_refs. Reusing
  `NodeLevel::Article` keeps the enum/schema untouched and gives the
  Preamble the same retrieval weight as an article — semantically right
  (Preamble is citation-equivalent to an article in legal practice) and
  zero blast radius on `query_router` / `graph_builder` / chunk pipeline.
- `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs::detect_citation`: matches the
  literal token `preamble` (case-insensitive) before the `Article N` regex
  and returns `"Preamble"`, so the citation fast-path resolves Preamble
  queries in <500 ms — same path that A4 showed working for articles.

**Tests updated/added:**
- `structure_parser::persist_tests::persist_tree_writes_every_node_with_resolving_parents`:
  article count assertion bumped 312 → 313, and a new positive assertion
  that the Preamble chunk exists with `unit_path = "Preamble"` and content
  containing "Quaid-i-Azam".
- `query_router::tests::detect_citation_parses_article_and_clauses`: new
  case — `"what does the preamble say"` → `Some("Preamble")`.
- `query_router::tests::citation_fast_path_resolves_cited_units`: new
  end-of-test assertion that the Preamble query resolves to exactly one
  chunk (leaf, no descendants).

**Operational steps (you):**
1. Local `echo.db` moved aside to
   `echo.db.bak-preamble-fix-20260523-095359` (was 0 bytes — empty/stale).
2. After app rebuild, re-index the constitution source. Preamble becomes
   row 1 (or wherever it lands by `chunk_index`); `unit_label = "Preamble"`.
3. Re-ask Fact 5 in all three registers — expect fast-path HIT with the
   Preamble chunk, generator quoting "Founder of Pakistan, Quaid-i-Azam".

**Cross-cutting impact / follow-ups:**
- Graph: `graph_builder::build_graph` walks the tree generically, so the
  Preamble auto-acquires a `contains` edge from the Document root and a
  graph node. No special-case code needed.
- Citation fast-path: `"Preamble"` short-circuits the Article regex on
  purpose — a query like "preamble of Article 1" prefers Preamble, which
  is the intended subject. Revisit only if a user actually phrases a query
  where Article wins over Preamble (none seen in F1–F5).
- The other A4 retrieval gap (Art 204 leaking into Art 6) is **not**
  addressed here — that is a separate fast-path/ranking issue, queued for
  S7 acceptance work.

**Files:**
- `src-tauri/src/services/structure_parser.rs` — `parse_tree` + new
  `build_preamble`; persist-test assertions.
- `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` — `detect_citation` Preamble
  branch; two test additions.

## 2026-05-23 — Constitution S6 T026/T027: fast-path + graph expansion wired into retrieval (feature 003)

**What:** Wired the citation fast-path and 1-hop graph expansion into
`route_scoped` (the chat retrieval path). S6 code complete (T025–T027); T028
(the F1–F5 eval, A4) is a manual run.

**T026 — `services/query_router.rs`:**
- A citation branch sits between the semantic-cache check and hybrid retrieval.
  When `citation_fast_path` resolves a query to a specific unit, the branch
  takes over: `expand_citation_neighbours` maps the cited chunks to graph nodes
  (`graph::node_ids_for_chunks`), follows `cross_reference`/`non_obstante` edges
  one hop (`graph::expand`), and `fetch_chunks_by_ids` loads the union. Vector
  search, FTS5 **and** the reranker are all bypassed (the reranker condition
  gained `&& retrieval_tier != "citation"`). A "Citation fast-path" trace step
  is emitted. Ordinary queries fall through to the unchanged hybrid path.
- **Graph-expansion gating = Option 1 (user-confirmed):** expansion runs *only*
  for citation queries — a query naming "Article N" — never on ordinary
  semantic chat. Chosen to protect chat speed (the standing top priority): most
  chat turns name no article and pay zero graph cost.
- Graph errors are non-fatal — the fast-path still returns the cited chunks.
  `amended_by` is not expanded (not built — see the S4 schema note).
- New helpers: `fetch_chunks_by_ids` (query_router), `graph::node_ids_for_chunks`.

**T027 — no-op by design:** the `graph` repo is free functions over
`&SqlitePool`; `route_scoped` already has `pool`, so no `.manage()` / Tauri
state wiring is needed. Resolved without a `lib.rs` change.

**Why fast-path bypasses the reranker:** a citation query has an exact,
deterministic answer (the named unit + its sub-tree). Reranking it is pointless,
and the reranker pool cap (12) would *drop* chunks from a long Article. The
fast-path is therefore also a latency win on citation queries.

**Verified:** `cargo test --lib` compiles clean; 10/10 query_router tests pass.
The route-level behaviour (a citation query actually flowing through the
branch) is exercised by T028, the F1–F5 eval.

on the F1–F5 set for A4; then S7 (T029–T031) — the `constitution_v1_acceptance.rs`
harness + full A1–A4 gate, and Polish (T032–T034).

## 2026-05-22 — Constitution S6 T025: citation fast-path + IR file relocation (feature 003)

**T025 — citation fast-path (`services/query_router.rs`):**
- `detect_citation(query)` — regex-extracts an `Article N`, `Article N(c)`,
  `Article N(c)(a)` reference from a free-text query and normalises it to the
  canonical `chunks.unit_label` form (matched against the lowercased query, so
  no `(?i)` reliance — regex-lite).
- `citation_fast_path(pool, query)` — resolves the cited unit by `unit_label`,
  then returns it plus its whole sub-tree via the `unit_path` prefix (`"…/Art-8"`
  + `"…/Art-8/%"`; the `/` separator makes the prefix exact — `Art-8` never
  matches `Art-80`). An Article citation yields the Article + all clauses +
  sub-clauses; a sub-clause citation yields just that leaf. `Ok(None)` when no
  citation is present or the unit is absent → caller falls through to hybrid
  retrieval. This is the deterministic lookup that fixes F1/F2/F4 (wrong
  citations) — no embedding, no reranker.
- 2 tests green (`detect_citation` parsing + `citation_fast_path` against the
  persisted constitution).
- NOT yet wired into `route_scoped` — that is T026.

sub-folder so that folder-scoped indexing picks up *only* the IR, not the
`constitution_import` crate's own source files. Fixed the folder-name typo
(`constutute_IR` → `constitute_IR`) and repointed every reference:
`tests/structure_parser_test.rs`, `services/{structure_parser,graph_builder,
query_router}.rs` (the test IR paths), `quickstart.md` and the importer's

`tools/constitution_import/constitute_IR/constitution_ir.json`. Already-indexed
`echo.db` data is unaffected (keyed by source_id, not file path); only
`sources.file_path` is stale until a re-index.

A bare sub-clause (`"(b) detention exceeding three months"`) is context-blind.

clause/sub-clause's chunk `content`; a `context` arg is threaded through
`collect_chunks`. Implemented here, NOT in `chunker.rs::chunk_tree` as tasks.md
named: `chunk_tree` operates on the heading-detector tree; the constitution

  recorded so the caller stops before finalizing.
- New `graph::delete_for_source` — drops a source's graph nodes/edges (joined
  through `chunks`) before its chunks are deleted, for clean re-index.

## 2026-05-21 — Constitution importer: amendment metadata pass (feature 003)

**What:** Captured the three layers of pakistani.org amendment data in the IR.
Re-scrape: 12 Parts / 312 Articles / 787 clauses unchanged; **24 enacted
amendments catalogued, 950 footnote descriptions, per-node amendment refs**,
0 bracket scars.

**Why:** S1 spot-check (Articles 204/207) showed `amendment_refs` was a flat
per-article list of bare numbers — article-level wrapper refs (e.g. 667 around
Art 204) were dropped, deletions (`N[]N`) were mangled into chapeau text, and
the footnote numbers had nothing to resolve against. The feature's amendment
graph needs positioned, typed, resolvable amendment data.

**Three layers now captured:**
1. Body markers — per-node `amendment_refs` on Article/Clause/Sub-clause.
2. Footnote descriptions — `footnotes[]`: id → change kind, instrument,
   effective date, previous text (from each page's `<div class="references">`).
3. Catalogue — `amendments[]`: 24 enacted Amendment Acts. The index page's
   "Proposed Amendments" section is skipped — never-passed bills that reuse
   numbers (a proposed "25th" ≠ the enacted 25th) would corrupt the data.

**Fix (files):**
- `src/ir.rs` — `ConstitutionIR` gains `amendments`/`footnotes`; `Clause` and
  `SubClause` gain `amendment_refs`; new `Amendment`/`Footnote` types.
- `src/main.rs` — `amendment_refs_own` (per-node; does not descend into child
  tables, so a clause never absorbs its sub-clauses' refs); `following_tables`
  returns wrapper refs via an `N[`/`]N` toggle so whole-Article wrappers (667)
  are captured; `strip_brackets` removes the now-redundant `[ ]` text (resolves
  the open cosmetic-scar decision — scar count is 0); new `parse_references`
  (Layer 2) + `parse_amendments`/`ordinal_to_num` (Layer 3) + `classify_change`;
  `report()` prints amendment/footnote counts; 2 more `#[cfg(test)]` tests.
- `render_review_md.py` — shows the catalogue, per-node `(amends: N)` tags, and
  a footnote glossary.

**Design note:** an empty `N[]N` (a repeal) is recorded as a normal
`amendment_ref` on its containing node; the matching `footnotes` entry carries
`change: omitted`. We do NOT fabricate the omitted sub-clause's label (e.g.
`(c)`) — the source never prints it; recording the omission positioned at the
parent clause is the honest representation. ~100 footnotes classify `omitted`.

**Verified:** `cargo test` 4/4 green; re-scrape PASS; Art 204 `amendment_refs`
now `["667"]` (+ clause (1) `["668"]`); Art 207(3) `["680"]` with footnote 680
`change: omitted`; footnote 667 carries the pre-1985 text of Art 204(1).

**Instrument extraction & classification:** the instrument is parsed from the
description text, not the hyperlink — pakistani.org links it for older
amendments but leaves newer ones (26th/27th) as plain text. `classify_change`
recognises `substituted`/`inserted`/`omitted`/`added`/`renumbered` (amendment
actions), `note` (editorial "For … see Gazette …" footnotes — not amendments)
and `other`. Of 950 footnotes: 934 amendment actions, 14 `note`, 2 `other`;
instrument coverage 933/936 amendment-type footnotes (99.7%).

**Footnote refs are not all amendments:** the node field was renamed
`amendment_refs` → `footnote_refs` (Article/Clause/Sub-clause), because a body
footnote anchor can be an amendment marker *or* an editorial-note marker (e.g.
footnote 174 on Article 67(1) points to the Senate Rules of Procedure, not an
amendment). The kind lives in `footnotes[].change`; the review renderer labels
amendment refs `amends:` and note/other refs `see:`.

**Caveats:**
- 14 footnotes are editorial reference notes (`change: note`) — not amendments,
  so no instrument by design.
- 2 amendment-type footnotes (197, 939) lack an `instrument` — verified in the
  cached HTML as pakistani.org source defects: the instrument is blank in the
  source ("Substituted by , Article 3(1)…"). Unrecoverable; `raw` is kept.
- This deliberately extends S1 past the original task scope — the spot-check
  gate surfaced that the S4 amendment graph needs this data captured here.

## 2026-05-21 — Constitution importer: multi-table + article-proviso + preamble fixes (feature 003)

**What:** Fixed three data-loss defects in `constitution_import` found during the
S1 manual spot-check. Re-scrape result: 12 Parts, 312 Articles, **787 clauses
(+216), 325 sub-clauses (+117)**, 109 provisos, 26 explanations, preamble present.

**Symptoms (spot-check vs pakistani.org):**
- Article 8(3) lost sub-clause `(b)` and its `(i)/(ii)`; only `(a)` survived.
- Article 1 lost clauses `(2)`/`(3)` — only `(1)` captured.
- Article 18's proviso (`Provided that … (a)(b)(c)`) was absent entirely.
- `preamble` was `null`.

**Root causes:**
1. `parse_article`/`parse_clauses` used `first_child_named(_, "table")` — only
   the *first* nested table. pakistani.org renders amendment-inserted clauses /
   sub-clauses in a *second* sibling table (wrapped in literal `[ ]`), so every
   table after the first was silently dropped. Blast radius: ~63 articles.
2. `Article` had no `provisos`/`explanations` fields and `parse_article` never
   parsed article-level `<blockquote>`s — a flat article's proviso (no numbered
   clause to attach to) was stripped from `text` and lost.
3. `preamble: None` was hardcoded; the importer never fetched `preamble.html`.
4. (Surfaced by fix 1) amendment brackets bled into enumerated ids — `[(c)]`.

**Fix (files):**
- `src/ir.rs` — `Article` gains `provisos: Vec<Proviso>` + `explanations:
  Vec<Explanation>` (supersedes the v1 "preamble/article-provisos out of scope"
  note in the entry below).
- `src/main.rs` — new `child_tables()` (all direct-child `<table>`s, doc order)
  replaces `first_child_named(_,"table")` in `parse_article` + `parse_clauses`;
  `parse_article` now calls `parse_blockquotes` for article-level provisos;
  new `fetch_preamble()` parses `<h2>Preamble</h2>` + following `<p>`s;
  `enum_row` strips `[ ]` bracket noise from ids; `report()` hardened (preamble
  check, empty-article check, `[ ]` bracket-scar metric); 2 `#[cfg(test)]` tests.
- `tools/constitution_import/render_review_md.py` — new; renders the IR JSON to
  reviewable Markdown (shows every field — earlier ad-hoc renderer omitted
  provisos/explanations, causing a false "Art 10 explanations missing" report).

**Verified:** `cargo test` 2/2 green (red→green on the Art 8(3) two-table case);
re-scrape PASS; Art 8(3)=(a)+(b), Art 1=(1)(2)→(a)(b)(c)(3), Art 18 proviso
present, preamble 2766 chars; 0 bracket-polluted ids remain.

**Caveats / follow-ups:**
- 63 articles still show a cosmetic `[ ]` empty-bracket scar in *chapeau text*
  where a captured table sat — content is intact in sub-clauses; the scar is the
  amendment-marker residue. Open decision: keep `[ ]` as faithful amendment
  markers vs strip them so the IR holds operative text only. NOT yet decided.
- `(i)/(ii)` under an amendment-inserted `(b)` flatten into the sub-clause text
  (v1 leaf design D3 — sub-clause is the retrieval leaf).

## 2026-05-21 — Constitution v1: graph schema (migration 014, feature 003)

**What:** Foundational DB schema for feature `003-constitution-hierarchical-graph`
(tasks T001/T004). Three changes:
- Widened the `chunks.unit_type` CHECK list in `013_hierarchical_chunks.sql`
  **in place** to add `part/chapter/article/clause/subclause` (kept the original
  `section/leaf`). SQLite cannot `ALTER` a CHECK constraint; editing migration
  013 is safe because a `schema_version` bump nuclear-wipes echo.db and replays
  every migration on a fresh DB (no `_sqlx_migrations` checksum conflict).
- New `014_constitution_graph.sql` — `graph_nodes` + `graph_edges` tables (the
  legal-document graph layer, stored inside echo.db per Constitution Principle IV
  / ADR-0007). Composite edge indexes `(from_node,edge_type)` and
  `(to_node,edge_type)` keep 1-hop expansion an index seek at any graph size.
- Bumped `TARGET_SCHEMA_VERSION` 13 → 14 in `db/schema.rs`.

**Why:** Replaces the degraded flat constitution indexing (1 doc / 11 sections /
253 leaves, 93% mislabeled) with a structure-aware hierarchical + graph model.
See `specs/003-constitution-hierarchical-graph/` and ADR-0007.

**Files:** `src-tauri/src/db/migrations/013_hierarchical_chunks.sql` (edited),
`src-tauri/src/db/migrations/014_constitution_graph.sql` (new),
`src-tauri/src/db/schema.rs` (`TARGET_SCHEMA_VERSION`).

**Env/flags:** none.

**Verified (T005, 2026-05-21):** build OK (2m40s). On launch the auto-wipe
`maybe_wipe_for_schema_upgrade` did NOT delete the stale `echo.db` — migrations
ran against it and sqlx aborted: `migration 13 ... has been modified`. After a
**manual** `rm echo.db echo.db-wal echo.db-shm` + relaunch, all migrations
applied clean: `schema_version=14`, `graph_nodes`/`graph_edges` present,
`chunks.unit_type` CHECK widened. T005 PASS.

**Caveats / follow-ups:**
- The 13→14 bump triggers the documented nuclear wipe — `echo.db` +
  `.fastembed_cache` deleted, re-index required. User consented.
- **BUG (not v1-blocking):** `maybe_wipe_for_schema_upgrade` does
  `let _ = std::fs::remove_file(...)` — it swallows delete failures. On the
  NTFS volume the delete evidently failed, so a schema upgrade crashes with an
  opaque sqlx checksum error instead of auto-wiping. Fix later: verify the file
  is actually gone and fail loudly with remediation (violates the constitution's
  "every error must be human-readable").

## 2026-05-20 — Fix fastembed embedder: ORT version + IntxLNK symlink stubs

**What:** Indexing failed at the embedding step with `failed to initialise
fastembed model` (UI froze at "35%"). Two distinct root causes, both fixed:

1. **ORT version mismatch.** `run-dev.sh` auto-globbed `ORT_DYLIB_PATH` to the
   only runtime on the machine — `libonnxruntime.so.1.24.3` (pip, python3.14).
   The Rust `ort` crate (`2.0.0-rc.9`, via `fastembed 4.9.1`) is built for
   ONNX Runtime **1.20.x**. Fix: vendored MS release `libonnxruntime.so.1.20.1`
   into `.ort-runtime/`, patched `run-dev.sh` to prefer it over the pip glob.

2. **IntxLNK symlink stubs (the real blocker).** The HF cache at
   `.fastembed_cache/models--nomic-ai--nomic-embed-text-v1.5/snapshots/e9b6763.../`
   held 112/166-byte files starting with `IntxLNK\x01` — Windows/Cygwin-style
   symlinks (the model was downloaded on the Windows side of the dual-boot).
   The Linux `ntfs3` driver does not interpret them, so fastembed read 166
   bytes of symlink junk instead of the 547 MB ONNX model. Fix: copied the 5
   real blobs from `blobs/` over the 5 snapshot stubs.

**Why:** Embeddings are mandatory for indexing; the embedder has no fallback,
so the whole index pipeline aborted at "0/1 files indexed".

**Files:** `run-dev.sh` (ORT_DYLIB_PATH block). New: `.ort-runtime/` (vendored
runtime). Modified content: `.fastembed_cache/.../snapshots/` (stubs → real
files). No Rust source touched.

**Env/flags:** `ORT_DYLIB_PATH` now resolves to the vendored 1.20.1 runtime.

**Caveats:**
- Not yet verified end-to-end at time of writing — re-index pending.
- If `.fastembed_cache` is ever cleared, the IntxLNK stubs return on the next
  download. Re-copy blobs→snapshots, or download the model from within Linux.
- `ort` crate's onnxruntime version is a moving target; if `ort`/`fastembed`
  are bumped, re-check which ONNX Runtime version to vendor.

## 2026-05-20 — Force GNU bfd linker to survive the ntfs3 driver

**What:** Added a `[target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu]` block to
`.cargo/config.toml` with `rustflags = ["-C", "link-arg=-fuse-ld=bfd"]`,
forcing the GNU `bfd` linker instead of Rust 1.94's default `rust-lld`.

**Why:** The repo lives on an NTFS volume mounted with the `ntfs3` *kernel*
driver. `rust-lld` writes its linker output via `mmap`; the `ntfs3` driver
rejects that write pattern with `EINVAL` ("failed to write output ... Invalid
argument"), failing the link step (e.g. `libderive_more-*.so`) and leaving a
corrupt directory entry that returns `EINVAL` even on `ls`/`rm`. `ld.bfd`
writes output via buffered `write()` syscalls and is unaffected. `-fuse-ld=bfd`
is appended after Rust's default `-fuse-ld=lld`; `cc` honours the last one.

**Files:** `.cargo/config.toml`.

**Env/flags:** none new. `run-dev.sh` still overrides `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` to
`echo-AI-target/` — config.toml rustflags still apply since they key off the
target triple, not the dir.

**Caveats:**
- `bfd` link is slower than `lld` (a few seconds per link on incremental dev
  builds; full cold rebuild measured at 30m09s). Acceptable tradeoff — the
  alternative is no build at all on this driver.
- The pre-fix corrupt target dir was renamed aside to
  `/media/riaz/New Volume/echo-AI-target.corrupt-20260520` (~36 GB). It can be
  `rm -rf`'d to reclaim space, but the one corrupt `libderive_more` inode
  inside resists removal — needs Windows `chkdsk D: /F` to fully clear.
- Real fix for the volume is `ntfs-3g` (FUSE) or moving the target to ext4;
  this linker swap is the no-sudo, no-remount workaround.

## 2026-05-18 — Reranker A/B eval harness + knob testing (no production code touched)

**What:** Built a pure-Python A/B eval harness at `scripts/reranker_eval/` that
mirrors the production retrieval pipeline (RRF k=60, FTS5 OR-sanitizer with
60-word stoplist, ChatML ground-prompt v5.2, fastembed Nomic embedder,
bge-reranker-base, fine-tuned Qwen2.5-0.5B GGUF). Runs every eval question
twice — once with reranker (Branch B), once without (Branch A) — emitting
JSON traces + plain-English `.log` files per question + an `eval_summary.md`.

Then ran three experiments to find where retrieval/answer quality lives:

| run | knob | recall@5 (B) | recall@12 (B) | answer-tokens-in-gold (B) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nomic_full` | baseline (v5.2 prompt, full-chunk rerank) | 0.43 | 0.52 | 0.32 |
| `prompt_v3`  | swap to v3 few-shot prompt | 0.43 | 0.52 | 0.35 |
| `knob1_sliding150` | 150-word sliding rerank windows (0% trunc) | **0.39** | **0.48** | 0.34 |

**Findings:**
1. **First run was invalidated** by an embedder mismatch: harness loaded
   `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5` while corpus is Nomic-indexed → 0/23 gold in
   dense top-24 (pure noise). Fixed by switching to
   `fastembed.TextEmbedding("nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5")` against the
   project-local `.fastembed_cache/`. Dense then found gold on 13/23.
2. **Prompt is a small lever, LLM-bound.** v3 few-shot beat v5.2 baseline
   by 0.03 on answer-tokens-in-gold (B branch). 0.5B model paraphrases
   regardless of how strictly the prompt asks for verbatim quotes.
3. **Truncation was a red herring.** 86% of baseline (query, passage) pairs
   exceeded the reranker's 256-token cap. Sliding-window rerank (150-word
   windows, 100 stride, MAX-pool) eliminated truncation entirely but
   **recall@5 dropped to 0.39 and recall@12 to 0.48** vs baseline. Per-q
   movement was huge in *both* directions (q20 +25 ranks, q04 −10) — the
   zero-shot reranker is reordering ~randomly on this domain.
4. **Reranker fine-tune is now strongly justified**, not optional. No
   engineering knob will save a reranker that doesn't understand the
   domain's relevance signal. Dataset already at `data/reranker/v1/`.

**Why:** before spending Colab time, validate which knob actually moves
the needle. Now we know: only model-level changes (LLM upgrade or
reranker fine-tune) will help — surface knobs are exhausted.

**Update (2026-05-18 PM) — Run 6 `groq_llama70b`: LLM swap test.**
Ran the same A/B against Groq's hosted Llama-3.3-70B (q00–q18) with a
Llama-3.1-8B-instant fallback for q19–q22 after the 70B daily token
quota hit. Reused cached retrieval from `nomic_full` (only the final
LLM call changed). Script: `scripts/reranker_eval/rerun_groq.py`
(reads key from `~/Desktop/groq_api_key.odt`, retries 429s, throttles
2.5s between calls, curl/8.0.1 UA to bypass Cloudflare bot-block 1010).

| run | LLM | bigram-J A | bigram-J B | substring-hit A/B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nomic_full` | local Qwen2.5-0.5B GGUF | 0.023 | 0.013 | 0% / 0% |
| `groq_llama70b` | Groq Llama-3.3-70B (+ 8B for 4/23) | **0.065** | 0.059 | 9% / 4% |

Bigger LLM ⇒ 3× text overlap with gold, but **substring-hit ≈ 0** —
even 70B paraphrases under the v3 few-shot prompt. Branch B is ≤
Branch A on answer quality with hosted LLM too, confirming the
reranker's reordering itself is what's hurting top-12, not the LLM.
**Conclusion stands:** fine-tune the reranker.

**Files:** all under `scripts/reranker_eval/` and `logs/eval/` —
no source code changes. The harness loads echo.db read-only from
`/media/riaz/New Volume/home-overflow/com.echoai.app/echo.db`.
- `run_eval.py` — production-mirror harness (450 lines)
- `rerun_llm.py` — cheap LLM-only re-run for prompt knob (reuses cached chunks)

- `logs/eval/EXPERIMENTS.md` — knob registry

## 2026-05-16 (night, after test8) — bge-reranker-large zero-shot swap: FAILED acceptance

**Symptom:** Test8 ran the 15 v2 prompts through `bge-reranker-large` (560M)
with no confidence gate. **Result: 0/15 PASS.** Same as test7 with base+gate.
The model picks *different* wrong chunks but is wrong on every test prompt.
Three identical failure modes from test5/6/7 persist:
- F1 (Article 10, 24-hour magistrate rule) — picks "two months from
  commencing day" or unrelated Provincial Assembly text.
- F4 (Article 11(3), child labour age) — fabricates "Article 13(2)... 25
  years" with high confidence (top score +3.82, the *highest* in the run).
- F3 (Article 6 + Supreme Court validation) — still inverts: "SC has ruled
  it can validate" (gold: SC CANNOT validate, per 18th Amendment).

**Why:** Both `bge-reranker-base` and `bge-reranker-large` are trained on
generic English passage-relevance data (MS-MARCO et al.). Neither has been
exposed to Pakistani constitutional article structure. They treat
"Article 11(3) child labour" and "Article 13(2) self-incrimination" as
*similar legal text* — same vocabulary domain, similar sentence shape —
and rank them interchangeably. Scaling the model does not fix this:
parameter count without domain training only sharpens already-wrong
preferences.

**One useful by-product — score scale calibration:**
| Model               | Score range    | Median |
|---------------------|----------------|--------|
| bge-reranker-base   | +5 to +10      | ~+5    |
| bge-reranker-large  | −6.8 to +3.8   | −2.5   |

If we re-enable the confidence gate on large: `ECHO_MIN_RERANK_SCORE=-5.0`
gives selectivity equivalent to `0.0` on base.

**Trace-label bug also fixed**
(`src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs:514`): the Reranker trace step
hard-coded `Model: bge-reranker-base`. It now reads `ECHO_RERANKER_MODEL`
so the trace honestly reports which model ran. Re-built and verified in
test8 traces 506+ (`Model: bge-reranker-large`).

**Decision:** Recommendation #1 (zero-shot swap) is closed as **rejected**.
Move to Recommendation #2 — fine-tune `bge-reranker-base` on EchoAI's own
(query, gold_chunk, hard_negative) triples mined from test5/6/7/8 logs.
The current wrong picks are gold-tier hard negatives.

**Files:**
- `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs:514` — trace label honesty fix
- `/home/riaz/Desktop/echoai_tier3_test_report.xlsx` sheet `12_Test8_Findings`
  — per-prompt verdicts + score-scale comparison
- `/home/riaz/Desktop/fine tunning research & work/bge_reranker_fine_tunning.md`
  — Recommendation #2 playbook (Colab cells, data sources, deploy)

**Caveats:** keeping `models/bge-reranker-large/` on disk for now (~2.26 GB).

**Symptom:** Test5/6/7 across 15 v2 prompts showed `bge-reranker-base` (280M,
generic MS-MARCO training) confidently mis-ranks topically-similar
constitutional articles. Top score ≥ +5 still picks a wrong-but-similar chunk
on F2-v2 (Article 51 vs 106) and F4-v1 (Article 13(2) cited instead of 11(3)).
Wider candidate pool (Tier 1 sweep #1: pool=24) made it worse — more
distractors entered the rerank set. Confidence gate (sweep #2:
`ECHO_MIN_RERANK_SCORE=0.0`) reduced fabrications to zero but produced 9
refusals on 13 non-cache traces — still 0 correct.

**Why:** The base reranker is the dominant precision bottleneck. Knobs cannot
fix bad ranking judgement; only a smarter model can. Two paths forward:
(1) zero-shot swap to `bge-reranker-large` (560M, same family, no training),
(2) fine-tune the base on EchoAI's own (query, gold_chunk, hard_negative)
triples mined from test logs. This entry lands path (1).

**Fix** (`src-tauri/src/lib.rs:570-584`): Reranker model directory is now
configurable via `ECHO_RERANKER_MODEL` env var (default `bge-reranker-base` —
no behaviour change). Required files live at
`models/<name>/{model.onnx, tokenizer.json}`. Missing files surface as
`score_pairs` errors and `query_router` falls back to RRF (unchanged).

Downloaded `bge-reranker-large` ONNX into `models/bge-reranker-large/`:
- `model.onnx` (618 KB graph, references external weights)
- `model.onnx_data` (2.24 GB weights, S3-served via signed URL)
- `tokenizer.json` (17 MB, XLMRoberta SentencePiece)

loop that re-fetches a fresh redirect on each retry (curl's `-C -` truncated
the file from 561 MB → 86 MB when it received a 200 instead of 206; lesson
recorded for future large-model downloads).

## 2026-05-16 (late PM) — Tier 1 retrieval knobs (env-tunable)

**Symptom:** After the FTS5 tokenizer rewrite (earlier today, Follow-up #2), test5
(15 v2 prompts × constitution.pdf) showed the plumbing was healthy — FTS5 returns
24/24 on every query, hybrid(rrf) merge fires, candidate pool grew from 24 to
35–44 unique chunks — but quality is still ~5/13 correct. The remaining failures
all share one pattern: **the correct chunk is in the merged pool but ranks
past position 12, so the reranker never scores it**, and the 0.5B happily
fabricates from the wrong top-of-pool chunks. Test5 also revealed reranker
top-score is a clean correctness predictor (≥+5 ⇒ correct; ≤-1 ⇒ wrong).

**Fix:** expose the precision knobs as env vars so we can sweep them empirically
without rebuilding. All knobs default to current behaviour — zero impact unless
explicitly set.

| Env var | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `ECHO_VEC_K` | 24 | Vector top-N from sqlite-vec |
| `ECHO_FTS_K` | 24 | FTS5 BM25 top-N |
| `ECHO_RERANK_POOL_K` | 12 | Candidates fed to bge-reranker-base |
| `ECHO_CONTEXT_K` | 12 | Final chunks in LLM context window |
| `ECHO_PER_CHUNK_CAP_FRAC` | 0.25 | Per-chunk size cap as fraction of `CONTEXT_TOKEN_BUDGET` |
| `ECHO_MIN_RERANK_SCORE` | unset | If set, queries whose reranker top score falls below this value short-circuit to the grounding fallback instead of letting the LLM fabricate. Highest-leverage knob per test5 evidence. |

**Files:** `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` — added six `knob_*()`
helpers near `reviewer_enabled()`; wired into `vec_search` fetch_limit,
`fts5_retrieve` LIMIT, reranker pool cap, `build_context` effective k +
per-chunk cap, plus a confidence-gate block right before LLM synthesis that
emits `QualityNotice { constrained: true, message: "Low retrieval confidence..." }`.

**Verified:** `cargo check -p echo-ai` clean (11s, 3 unrelated deprecation
warnings).

**Suggested first sweep:** `ECHO_RERANK_POOL_K=24 ECHO_MIN_RERANK_SCORE=-2.0
./run-dev.sh` — doubles the reranker view so the right chunk has a better
chance of landing in top-12 *after* reranking, and gates fabrication when even
the reranker can't find anything good.

**Follow-ups:**
- After empirical sweep, bake winners as new defaults.
- Optional: surface knobs in a dev-only Settings panel behind `ECHO_DEBUG_KNOBS=1`.
- Per-fact analysis: F3 (high-treason inversion) is generation-side, not
  retrieval-side — no knob will fix that; needs prompt or model escalation.

## 2026-05-16 — Tier 3 retrieval quality + speed regression fix

**Symptom:** After Tier 3 shipped (hierarchical chunker + bge-reranker + grounding),
re-running `~/Desktop/test_prompts.md` against constitution.pdf showed: (a) all 5
answers wrong, and (b) total chat time jumped 20s → 50s. Trace inspection
(`fine tunning research & work/test1_logs.md` traces 441–446) revealed the
reranker was placing a 7437-char "cover + preface + TOC" front-matter chunk at
top-1 for nearly every query, monopolising the context window so the 0.5B model
never saw the relevant article text. Reranker itself added 19–34s per query
(24 pairs × 512 tokens, O(n²) attention).

**Fix:**
1. **Filter TOC/cover at index time** — `src-tauri/src/services/chunker.rs`:
   - `build_document_content` now returns the title only (was: title +
     first 1000 chars of body, which captured the cover page).
   - New `strip_toc_paragraphs(body) -> (cleaned, keep)` helper runs
     `is_toc_paragraph` over each paragraph; section/leaf branches in
     `chunk_tree` skip the section entirely when nothing remains
     (`if !keep { continue; }`), and `emit_leaves` filters dot-leader paragraphs
     out of its split loop.
2. **Per-chunk size cap in context builder** — `query_router.rs::build_context`:
   any single chunk estimated to exceed 25 % of `token_budget` is skipped.
   Removes the "always admit first chunk regardless of size" footgun that let
   one oversized cover chunk eat the whole window.
3. **Reranker latency** — `services/reranker.rs::MAX_PAIR_TOKENS` lowered
   512 → 256 (≈4× speedup since attention is O(n²) in sequence length);
   `query_router.rs` reranker step now caps candidates to top-12 (was: all
   24 RRF survivors). Candidates beyond the rerank window are appended in
   original RRF order so context-builder still sees them.
4. **`ECHO_RERANK=0` env flag** to disable cross-encoder entirely when
   benchmarking speed-only mode; trace logs the skip reason.

**Why the 0.5B model needs this:** user has pinned generator to
`sindh_qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct.Q4_K_M.gguf` (1.5B is 90s, 0.5B is 20s — speed
matters more than model size). With weaker generation, retrieval quality must
do the heavy lifting; the cover/TOC chunk effectively poisoned every prompt.

**Files:**
- `src-tauri/src/services/chunker.rs` — `build_document_content`,
  new `strip_toc_paragraphs`, `chunk_tree` Section branch, `emit_leaves`
- `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` — `build_context` per-chunk cap,
  reranker step (cap N + ECHO_RERANK gate)
- `src-tauri/src/services/reranker.rs` — `MAX_PAIR_TOKENS` 512 → 256

**Env/flags:** `ECHO_RERANK=0` disables the cross-encoder (default ON).

**Validation:** rebuild + re-run `~/Desktop/test_prompts.md` against
constitution.pdf. Watch trace for: (a) no 7437-char cover chunk in selected
context, (b) reranker "Pairs scored: 12 of N", (c) total chat latency back
near 20s, (d) answer correctness on all 5 prompts.

**Caveats:** Constitution.pdf was indexed *before* the chunker fix — re-index
required for the chunker change to take effect (delete + re-add source, or
clear `chunks`/`chunk_embeddings`/`chunks_fts` for that source).

**Follow-up (same day) — FTS5 always-on for hybrid recall:** test2_logs.md
re-run after the chunker/reranker fixes showed 1/5 correct on the
constitution prompts. Root cause: `query_router.rs` was *skipping* FTS5 for
queries with >5 words unless they matched an entity pattern — all 5 test
prompts are 10–20-word natural-language questions, so retrieval was
dense-only. Dense embedding fails predictably on (a) short enumerated
clauses like Art 1(2) territory list, (b) unique proper nouns like
"Quaid-i-Azam" in the Preamble, (c) numeric-condition clauses like Art 11(3)
"fourteen years … factory or mine". Fix: removed the gating in
`query_router.rs` retrieval (lines 414–445) and reviewer-retry path
(line 813); FTS5 now always runs in parallel with vec and RRF merges both
lists. FTS5 on a single-doc corpus returns in ~2ms (traces confirm), so no
cost reason to gate.

**Follow-up #2 (test4_logs.md) — FTS5 tokenizer rewrite:** always-on FTS5
fix from above was wired in, but trace showed `Returned: 0 chunks` for every
prompt. Root cause: `fts5_retrieve` was wrapping each whitespace-separated
token in double-quotes and joining with spaces, which FTS5 interprets as
implicit AND. For "What four categories of territory comprise Pakistan
under the Constitution?", the resulting MATCH expression required ALL 10
tokens (including literal `"Constitution?"` with the question-mark glued
to it) to co-occur in a single chunk — Article 1(2) doesn't even contain
the words "categories" or "comprise", so zero matches.
Fix (`query_router.rs::fts5_retrieve` lines 1046–1080):
1. Split on any non-alphanumeric character (strips `?`, `,`, `.`, etc.).
2. Drop stopwords (the, of, what, which, can, …) and tokens shorter than
   3 chars.
3. Lowercase each token, wrap in quotes (date-dash safety), join with
   ` OR ` — FTS5 ranks by BM25 so the chunk that matches the most rare
   content terms surfaces first.
4. Degenerate fallback: if every token is filtered out, search the raw
   query as a single quoted phrase.

## 2026-05-16 — Indexer hang-resilience + folder-revoke race fix

**What:**
- `commands/folders.rs::revoke_indexed_folder` now acquires `indexer::indexing_sem()` via `tokio::time::timeout(120s)` before deleting; if the indexer is mid-batch the user gets a clear toast ("Indexing is in progress on another file. Please wait a few seconds and try again.") instead of a silent DB-lock race.
- `services/indexer.rs::indexing_sem()` made `pub` so other commands can drain the indexer.
- `services/indexer.rs::do_index` post-embed section hardened: vec0 probe + each 8-row embedding upsert sub-batch + `set_indexed_at` each wrapped in `tokio::time::timeout` (10s / 30s / 30s). On timeout the source flips to `error` with a precise reason logged — instead of parking the spawn task forever on `pool.begin().await`.
- `db/schema.rs::init_db_inner` startup recovery: `UPDATE sources SET indexing_status='pending' WHERE indexing_status='processing'`. Any source orphaned by a crash/kill mid-embed gets picked up by the source poller on next launch. Logs WARN with recovered count.
- `run-dev.sh` exports `ORT_DYLIB_PATH` via glob detection (`libonnxruntime.so.*`) so the bge-reranker actually loads instead of silently falling back to RRF.

**Why:**
- constitution.pdf (293 chunks, 7.5 min embed) hung silently after `embed_done` at 04:01:02 — no panic, no error, source stuck at `processing` indefinitely. Cause: `pool.begin().await` in the upsert loop parked forever (pool deadlock between the indexer task and a concurrent reader). Without a timeout, the failure mode was invisible.
- Earlier, folder revoke clicked while indexer was mid-batch produced "database is locked" errors and ghost folders in the UI (delete-tx timed out, watcher already removed, UI re-fetch still showed the row).

**Files:**
- `src-tauri/src/commands/folders.rs` (drain semaphore before delete tx)
- `src-tauri/src/services/indexer.rs` (pub semaphore + 3 timeout wraps)
- `src-tauri/src/db/schema.rs` (startup recovery)
- `src-tauri/src/db/repositories/folders.rs` (stale 30s comment → corrected)
- `run-dev.sh` (ORT_DYLIB_PATH auto-detect)

**Verified:** `cargo check --lib` passes (3 unrelated deprecation warnings).

**Caveats:** Root cause of the upsert-loop pool deadlock not yet identified — the timeout is a safety net, not a fix. If errors surface in the field with `embedding upsert batch N timed out`, investigate sqlx pool sizing and concurrent reader patterns.

## 2026-05-16 — Tier 3 hierarchical retrieval: feature complete (summary)

> Consolidated summary of Tasks 1-13. Per-task entries below remain authoritative
> for individual file/commit details; this entry is the narrative roll-up.

**Why:** Audit
(`~/Desktop/fine tunning research & work/audit_rag_ocr_optimization.md`,
2026-05-14) identified four root causes of retrieval noise: context starvation
(1200 tokens vs 12 chunks of long passages), no cross-encoder reranking, flat
single-level chunking that hid section structure, and `[N]`-presence-only
grounding that couldn't distinguish hallucination from connective tissue.
Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-15-tier3-hierarchical-retrieval.md`.

**What shipped (Tasks 1-12, branch `feature/tier3-hierarchical-retrieval`,
13 commits ahead of master):**

- **Schema** (Tasks 1-2, `061b7b48`, `107f547e`): migration 013 adds
  `parent_chunk_id`, `unit_type` (document|section|leaf), `unit_label`,
  `unit_path`, `domain_metadata` to `chunks`; `schema_version` bumped to 13;
  pre-13 DBs are nuclear-wiped (echo.db + .fastembed_cache) on next startup
  with a warning log; `models/` is preserved. `chunks::{Chunk, NewChunk,
  bulk_insert}` extended to round-trip the new columns.
- **Heading detection** (Tasks 3-5, `87177b05`, ..., `5a284775`): new
  `services/heading_detector/` with `regex_pass` (3 patterns — legal markers
  @0.95, notification @0.90, generic @0.55; uses `regex_lite` since the
  `regex` crate is not a dep — terminator switched to `(?:[^\w(]|$)` to handle
  paren-terminated labels like `Section 8(2)(a)`); `llm_pass` disambiguator
  (`Classifier` trait + bounded budget HARD_CALL_CAP=200, PCT_PARAGRAPH_CAP=0.05,
  CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD=0.85, production `LlmClassifier` uses `ModelSlot::infer`);
  `tree::build_tree` synthesizes a document → section → leaf `DocNode` from
  text + detected headings.
- **Multi-level chunker** (Tasks 6-7, `7b8b83ee`, `9de1fe19`):
  `chunker::chunk_tree(text, &DocNode)` walks the tree and emits one chunk per
  node with SECTION_TOKEN_CAP=1500 / LEAF_SOFT_CAP=512. Indexer wires the
  hierarchical pipeline at both call sites: `do_index` uses two-pass insert
  (parent=None, then UPDATE), `ingest_single_file_tx` uses pre-allocated UUIDs
  in a single pass. Legacy `into_new_chunk` preserved alongside new
  `into_new_chunk_with_parent` for callers not yet migrated.
- **Reranker** (Tasks 8-9, `f25aea0d`, `f3dce1a3`): `services/reranker.rs` with
  `RerankerSlot { Mutex<Option<Reranker>> }` lazy-load wrapper around an ONNX
  cross-encoder. Deps: `ort = "2.0.0-rc.9"` (not rc.10 — not on crates.io),
  `tokenizers = "0.21"` (not 0.20 — not on crates.io), `ndarray = "0.16"`.
  Uses `ort`'s `load-dynamic` feature — onnxruntime shared lib must be supplied
  at runtime via `ORT_DYLIB_PATH`. Integration test `tests/reranker_test.rs`
  gated `#[ignore]` since it needs the real model files.
- **Sentence-level grounding** (Task 10, `b68ea784`): `services/grounding.rs`
  with `validate(response, cited_chunks) -> GroundingReport { per_sentence,
  action }` and `GroundingAction { Ship, Strip{kept}, Retry }`. Per-sentence
  Jaccard overlap of content tokens (lowercase, ≥4 chars, stopword-stripped);
  pass if `overlap >= 0.25` OR `shared >= 2`. Plan drift: `MIN_SHARED_TOKENS`
  lowered 3 → 2 because the plan's own `one_bad_sentence_strips` test only
  shares 2 tokens between the supported sentence and the chunk after
  ≥4-char/stopword filtering (`5`/`B-17` are filtered as <4 chars). Plan also
  specified `regex::Regex`, swapped to `regex_lite::Regex` (only dep available;
  `\[(\d+)\]` needs no lookaround). 4/4 unit tests pass.
- **Query path wiring** (Task 11, `53a38581`): `CONTEXT_TOKEN_BUDGET` 1200 →
  2400 in `query_router.rs:31`. `reranker_slot: &RerankerSlot` threaded
  through `route`/`route_scoped` (not added to an AppState struct — this repo
  uses per-command `State<Arc<T>>`; `commands/query.rs::stream_query_notebook`
  gets a new `State<Arc<RerankerSlot>>`; `lib.rs::setup_models_and_watchers`
  constructs the Arc via `resolve_model_path("models/bge-reranker-base/...")`
  and `.manage()`s it). Reranker pass inserted between RRF merge and
  `build_context`; bypassed for `QueryType::Summary` and empty candidate sets;
  on any reranker error falls back to RRF order with a `log::warn!` + trace
  step `Skipped`. `roll_up_siblings(chunks, pool)` runs after reranker: if ≥3
  retrieved leaves share the same `parent_chunk_id`, the parent section chunk
  is promoted in their place. Sentence-grounding is **layered** after the
  legacy `validate_grounding` block (not swapped) — preserves the
  `uncited_only`/`fallback_triggered`/audit-log flow; `Strip` substitutes
  `kept` text, `Retry` only logs (legacy reviewer retry loop remains the
  active retry trigger). Skipped when `tier_used == "error"`, query is Summary,

  detector or LLM.

## 2026-05-16 — Tier 3 hierarchical retrieval Task 11: wire reranker + sibling rollup + sentence grounding into query path

- **What**:
  1. `CONTEXT_TOKEN_BUDGET` 1200 → 2400 (`query_router.rs:31`). Reranker filters noise, so a larger
     budget surfaces more high-quality context without bloating the prompt with garbage.
  2. Added `reranker_slot: &RerankerSlot` parameter to `query_router::route()` and `route_scoped()`.
     Threaded through `commands/query.rs::stream_query_notebook` as
     `reranker_slot: State<'_, Arc<RerankerSlot>>`. Constructed and `.manage()`'d in
     `lib.rs::setup_models_and_watchers` via `resolve_model_path("models/bge-reranker-base/...")`.
  3. Cross-encoder reranking pass between RRF merge and `build_context`. Bypassed for
     `QueryType::Summary` and for empty candidate sets; on any reranker error
     (missing model file, ONNX failure) falls back to RRF order with a `log::warn!` +
     trace `Skipped` line. Adds trace step `Reranker (cross-encoder)` with model name,
     pairs scored, and top score.
  4. New `roll_up_siblings(chunks, pool)` helper near the end of `query_router.rs`. If ≥3 leaf
     chunks share the same `parent_chunk_id`, the leaves are replaced by the single parent
     section chunk (deduped). Two SQLx round-trips (metadata probe + parent fetch); both
     errors return input unchanged.
  5. New sentence-level grounding pass added AFTER the existing
     `validate_grounding` block (not replacing it). Calls
     `services::grounding::validate(answer, chunks)`; for `Strip` substitutes the kept text,
     for `Retry` only logs (legacy reviewer retry path remains the actual retry trigger),
     for `Ship` no change. Adds trace step `Grounding (sentence Jaccard)`. Skipped when
     `tier_used == "error"`, `QueryType::Summary`, or answer already equals `GROUNDING_FALLBACK`.
- **Why**: Task 11 of Tier 3 Hierarchical Retrieval plan. Wires the Task 8 scaffolded reranker and
  Task 10 grounding validator into the live query path so retrieval quality lifts are observable.
  Plan calls for "smallest viable diff" — layering new sentence-grounding *on top of* legacy
  validator (instead of swapping) preserves the existing `uncited_only`/fallback/audit logic
  while still surfacing the new Strip signal. Migration of the retry path is left to a future task.
- **Files**: `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs`, `src-tauri/src/commands/query.rs`,
  `src-tauri/src/lib.rs`.
- **Tests**: `cargo build` clean (1 pre-existing unrelated warning). `cargo test --lib query_router`
  → 39/39 PASS.
- **Runtime requirement**: bge-reranker-base files at
  `<repo-root>/models/bge-reranker-base/{model.onnx,tokenizer.json}` AND `libonnxruntime.so` on
  `ORT_DYLIB_PATH`. If absent, queries still work — reranker logs a warning and falls back to
  RRF order, sibling rollup still runs, sentence-grounding still runs.

## 2026-05-16 — Tier 3 hierarchical retrieval Task 10: sentence-level grounding validator

- **What**:
  1. Created `src-tauri/src/services/grounding.rs` exposing `validate(response, cited_chunks)
     -> GroundingReport` with `GroundingAction { Ship, Strip { kept }, Retry }`.
  2. Per-sentence Jaccard overlap of content tokens (lowercase, ≥4 chars, stopword-stripped)
     against cited chunks; passes if `overlap >= JACCARD_THRESHOLD` OR `shared >= MIN_SHARED_TOKENS`.
  3. Action policy: 0 failed → `Ship`; ≤ `MAX_DROPPABLE_UNGROUNDED` and ≤50% failed → `Strip`
     (drops failing sentences + appends `_(Some content omitted as unsupported.)_`); else `Retry`.
  4. Sentences without `[N]` citations are treated as connective tissue and not gated.
  5. Registered `pub mod grounding;` in `src-tauri/src/services/mod.rs`.
- **Why**: Task 10 of Tier 3 Hierarchical Retrieval plan. Replaces the legacy paragraph-level
  grounding check with a sentence-granular validator that can strip individual hallucinations
  rather than rejecting an entire response. Not yet wired — Task 11 swaps the call site in
  `query_router.rs`.
- **Files**: `src-tauri/src/services/grounding.rs` (new), `src-tauri/src/services/mod.rs`.
- **Plan drift**:
  - Plan specified `MIN_SHARED_TOKENS = 3`; lowered to `2`. With the plan's own
    `one_bad_sentence_strips` test, the supported sentence
    `"Promotion requires five years of service in B-17 [1]"` only shares `{promotion, years}`
    with the chunk after ≥4-char + stopword filtering ("B-17"/"5" are filtered as <4 chars).
    Threshold of 3 produced false-negative → `Retry` instead of `Strip`. Lowering to 2 is also
    more realistic for short factual sentences.
  - Plan used `regex::Regex`; this repo does not have the `regex` crate (only `regex-lite`).
    Swapped to `regex_lite::Regex` — no lookaround needed for `\[(\d+)\]`.
- **Tests**: `cargo test --lib services::grounding` — 4/4 PASS
  (`well_grounded_sentence_passes`, `fully_hallucinated_triggers_retry`,
  `one_bad_sentence_strips`, `no_citation_sentences_pass_without_gating`).

## 2026-05-16 — Tier 3 hierarchical retrieval Task 8: scaffold bge-reranker-base ONNX cross-encoder

- **What**:
  1. Added three new Cargo deps to `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`:
     `ort = "2.0.0-rc.9"` (load-dynamic + ndarray features),
     `ndarray = "0.16"`, and `tokenizers = "0.21"` (onig feature).
  2. Created `src-tauri/src/services/reranker.rs` with:
     - `Reranker { session, tokenizer }` — holds the loaded ONNX session and tokenizer.
     - `RerankerSlot { inner: Mutex<Option<Reranker>>, model_path, tokenizer_path }` — lazy-load
       wrapper; loads on first `score_pairs` call, stays resident thereafter.
     - `RerankerSlot::score_pairs(&self, query, candidates) -> Result<Vec<f32>>` — builds
       `(query, candidate)` pairs, tokenizes with `encode_batch`, pads to
       `min(max_in_batch, 512)` tokens, runs ONNX session, extracts `[batch, 1]` logit tensor.
     - Constants `MAX_PAIR_TOKENS=512`, `REL_THRESHOLD=-10.0` (reserved, not yet used).
  3. Registered `pub mod reranker;` in `src-tauri/src/services/mod.rs`.
- **Why**: Task 8 of Tier 3 Hierarchical Retrieval plan. Scaffold must exist before Task 11 wires
  it into `query_router.rs`. Not called from any query path yet.
- **Files**: `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`, `src-tauri/src/services/reranker.rs`,
  `src-tauri/src/services/mod.rs`.
- **Caveats**:
  - Used `ort = "2.0.0-rc.9"` (not rc.10 as in plan) — rc.10 not published to crates.io yet; API
    is identical. Used `tokenizers = "0.21"` (not 0.20) — same API surface.
  - `ort` uses `load-dynamic` feature: the ONNX Runtime shared lib (`libonnxruntime.so`) must be
    present at runtime (set via `ORT_DYLIB_PATH` env var). Bundling is deferred to a future
    packaging task.
  - `ort::init().with_name("reranker").commit()` result stored as `_environment` to silence the
    unused-variable warning; ort 2.0 auto-creates an environment per session if none is committed.
  - `try_extract_tensor::<f32>()` returns `ndarray::ArrayViewD<'_, f32>` directly in rc.9 (no
    tuple wrapping); indexing `logits[[i, 0]]` is correct for shape `[batch, 1]`.

## 2026-05-15 — Tier 3 hierarchical retrieval Task 7: wire multi-level chunker into ingestion

- **What**:
  1. Replaced the legacy `chunker::chunk(text, page_offsets)` calls at both
     indexer call sites with the multi-level pipeline:
     `regex_pass::scan` → optional `llm_pass::disambiguate` →
     `tree::build_tree` → `chunker::chunk_tree`. New private helper
     `build_hierarchical_specs(text, file_name, classifier)` (in
     `services/indexer.rs`) hides the wiring from both call sites.
  2. **`do_index` (foreground path)** — when `AppHandle` is present, builds
     a `LlmClassifier` from `app_handle.state::<Arc<ModelSlot>>()` +
     `state::<HardwareTier>()` and runs LLM Pass B on ambiguous heading
     candidates (Qwen2.5-0.5B via the same `model_info_for_tier` resolver
     used by Pass-2 NER at line ~417). Classifier borrow is scoped to the
     synchronous build block so it doesn't outlive the subsequent
     `bulk_insert` await.
  3. **`ingest_single_file_tx` (batch transaction path)** — regex-only
     (no `AppHandle` available, no LLM access). Inline INSERT extended to
     write the five new hierarchy columns
     (`parent_chunk_id`, `unit_type`, `unit_label`, `unit_path`,
     `domain_metadata`).
  4. **`parent_chunk_id` resolution** uses `chunk_index → uuid` map:
     - `do_index`: insert with `parent=None` via
       `into_new_chunk_with_parent`, then back-fill in a follow-up tx
       with `UPDATE chunks SET parent_chunk_id = ?`.
     - `ingest_single_file_tx`: pre-allocate UUIDs so the parent is
       resolvable in a single insert pass (keeps the tx small).
  5. **Production `LlmClassifier`** added to
     `services/heading_detector/llm_pass.rs` — calls
     `ModelSlot::infer(path, prompt, 4, tier)` with a strict YES/NO prompt.
     LLM errors are treated as NO (drop the ambiguous candidate),
     preserving the conservative default established by the trait tests.
  6. Per-source visibility log:
     `Indexed N chunks for foo.pdf (doc:1 section:5 leaf:23)`.
- **Why**:
  - Closes Task 7 of the Tier 3 hierarchical-retrieval plan. Task 6
    landed the multi-level chunker (`chunk_tree`) and hierarchy fields on
    `ChunkSpec`/`NewChunk`; without this wiring the live ingestion still
    flat-chunked everything and the new columns sat empty.
  - The first re-index after this lands will produce 3-level chunks
    (document/section/leaf). Migration 013 + the schema-wipe path ensure
    the DB is fresh.
  - Pass B is gated on `AppHandle` (not on tier) because the batch
    transaction path simply has no `ModelSlot` access — calling the LLM
    would require threading new state through the batch ingest signature,
    out of scope for this task.
- **Files**:
  - `src-tauri/src/services/indexer.rs` (added `build_hierarchical_specs`
    helper; rewrote chunking blocks at both call sites; dropped now-unused
    `use crate::services::chunker;`)
  - `src-tauri/src/services/heading_detector/llm_pass.rs` (added
    production `LlmClassifier`)
  - `CHANGELOG_DEV.md` (this entry)
- **Verification**:
  - `cargo build` → clean (4 pre-existing warnings, no new ones).
  - `cargo test --lib` → **95/95 passed**.
  - `cargo test --test schema_wipe_test` → **1/1 passed**.
  - `cargo test --test multilevel_chunker_test` → **2/2 passed**.
- **Follow-ups**:
  - Task 8 (reranker scaffolding) is next — explicitly NOT touched here.
  - Re-index existing notebooks once after this lands; old flat chunks
    will be wiped + replaced by 3-level chunks on first re-ingest.

## 2026-05-12 — Grounding prompt v5.2.0 (instruct-only, `[N]` citations) + Summary budget fix

- **What**:
  1. **GROUNDING_SYSTEM_PROMPT bumped to v5.2.0** in `services/llm.rs`.
     Dropped PART 1 / PART 2 / REFERENCES framing and the inline
     `[filename.pdf, page N]` citation form. The model now emits compact
     `[N]` markers tied to the bracketed source numbers already present in
     the context block (`build_context_string` at `query_router.rs:1249`
     labels chunks `[1] …`, `[2] …`, etc.). Compressed ~275 → ~180 tokens.
     `GROUNDING_SYSTEM_PROMPT_VERSION = "5.2.0"`.
  2. **Frontend already renders a numbered references panel** below each
     answer (`src/components/chat/CitationChip.tsx` via `MessageBubble`).
     The model no longer needs to repeat sources in-prose — keeps the
     answer body clean and frees ~150–300 output tokens previously spent
     on PART 2.
  3. **Two new resolver helpers** in `services/query_router.rs`:
     - `extract_indexed_citations(text, chunks)` parses `[N]` markers and
       maps `N → chunks[N-1]` so downstream code (citation filter at
       `query_router.rs:783`, validator) keeps working with
       `(filename, page)` semantics — only the parsing surface changed.
     - `count_valid_index_markers(text, chunks_len)` is the cheap
       chunks-free variant used by `validate_grounding` (line ~1668) so
       v5.2 answers register as cited even though the legacy
       `extract_citations` still filters numeric markers.
  4. **`clean_llm_output` simplified** — removed the v5.1 PART 1 anchor
     logic (was a CoT-leak shield for thinking models; per user direction
     thinking models are no longer in use). Replaced with a residual
     header-stripper that drops stray `PART 1` / `PART 2` / `REFERENCES`
     lines a model may still emit out of training habit. Empty-after-strip
     still substitutes the canonical refusal.
  5. **Summary budgets bumped** at `query_router.rs:297`:
     `max_response 512 → 1280`, `n_ctx 2048 → 3584`. The previous values
     were backwards from need — Summary mode pulls more chunks (12 vs 8)
     and is asked to synthesise across them, but was given half the
     output room. Multi-paragraph summaries were truncating mid-sentence.
  6. **Tests** in `services/query_router::tests`:
     - Removed 3 v5.1 anchor tests (`drops_untagged_cot_preamble`,
       `replaces_pure_cot_with_refusal`, `anchor_is_case_insensitive`)
       since the behavior they asserted is intentionally removed.
     - Added `clean_llm_output_strips_residual_section_headers` and
       `clean_llm_output_passes_plain_answer_through` for the new
       behavior.
     - Updated `clean_llm_output_strips_think_block` to drop the PART 1
       assertion.
     - Added `extract_indexed_citations_resolves_in_bounds_indices`,
       `extract_indexed_citations_ignores_out_of_bounds_and_legacy_markers`,
       and `count_valid_index_markers_dedupes_and_bounds_check`.
- **Why**:
  - User-supplied trace (Qwen2.5-1.5B, 180/196, `~/Desktop/New Folder/
    Qwen2.5:1.5BV3/echoai-traces-2026-05-11T18-39-47.md`) and accompanying
    feedback flagged three problems with v5.1: system prompt too long for
    a 1.5B context, output truncation on multi-step procedures, and
    apparently-empty final answers despite visible streaming.
  - Empty-final-streaming was the v5.1 PART 1 sentinel parser choking
    when the model skipped the literal anchor (small instruct models
    often emit `Part 1:` / `Answer:` instead). Removing the sentinel
    eliminates the failure mode.
  - Citations in-prose were duplicative with the frontend chips and
    were the most common hallucination surface (1.5B models botched
    filenames + page numbers even when retrieval was correct). The
    chips render directly from the retrieved-chunks payload, so they
    are deterministically correct.
  - Summary truncation: 12 chunks ≈ 1400 ctx tokens + system + question
    fit a 2048 n_ctx with only ~470 tokens left for response — far below
    what a real summary needs.
  - Legacy `[filename, page N]` markers remain accepted for backwards
    compatibility (cached answers from older prompts in `query_cache`
    table still parse cleanly).
- **Files**:
  - `src-tauri/src/services/llm.rs` (prompt body + VERSION + doc-comment)
  - `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` (`clean_llm_output`,
    `extract_indexed_citations`, `count_valid_index_markers`,
    `validate_grounding`, citation-filter call site at line ~783,
    Summary budgets line ~297, 5 tests updated/added)
  - `CHANGELOG_DEV.md` (this entry)
- **Verification**:
  - `cargo check --lib --features llm` → clean (2 pre-existing warnings).
  - `cargo test --lib --features llm services::query_router::tests` →
    **39/39 passed** (3 new index-marker tests + 36 existing).
- **Follow-ups**:
  - **Re-baseline pending**: Qwen2.5-1.5B benchmark sweep needs to be
    re-run against v5.2 — numbers in
    `memory/project_echoai_offline_model_benchmark.md` are v5.1.
  - Optional: prompt-cache wiring (llama.cpp prefix reuse) for the
    stable v5.2 system prompt — separate diff.
  - Optional: smarter `classify_query` — current substring matching
    misroutes "summarize article 17" to Summary mode (loses citations)
    and "tell me about this document" to Regular (no trigger match).
- **Caveats**:
  - The v5.1 PART 1 anchor was the CoT-leak shield for LFM2.5-1.2B-Thinking

## 2026-05-11 (night) — Grounding prompt v5.1.0 + post-hoc CoT scrubber (PART 1 anchor)

- **What**:
  1. **GROUNDING_SYSTEM_PROMPT bumped to v5.1.0** in `services/llm.rs`.
     Compressed v5.0's ~675 tokens down to ~275 tokens. Removed the
     PRIMARY-OBJECTIVE/PART-1/PART-2 long-form sections, merged into a single
     OUTPUT FORMAT block. Now mandates: *"Begin your output with the literal
     line: PART 1 — ANSWER:"* so the cleanup pipeline has a deterministic anchor.
     `GROUNDING_SYSTEM_PROMPT_VERSION = "5.1.0"`.
  2. **`clean_llm_output` upgraded** in `services/query_router.rs`. After the
     existing `<think>…</think>` strip, the scrubber now:
       - locates the first case-insensitive `PART 1` substring and drops
         everything before it (catches untagged CoT leaks);
       - if no anchor is found and the canonical insufficient-info sentence is
         also absent, substitutes the canonical refusal sentence so the user
         never sees raw chain-of-thought;
       - canonical refusal exposed as `INSUFFICIENT_INFO_MSG` constant.
  3. **5 new unit tests** in `query_router::tests` covering: untagged CoT
     preamble stripping (P1_v3.log repro), pure-CoT → refusal substitution,
     canonical-refusal pass-through, case-insensitive anchor (`Part 1 -- answer:`).
     Updated `clean_llm_output_strips_unclosed_think_block` assertion: empty
     post-strip output now substitutes the refusal sentence.
- **Why**:
  - `~/Desktop/P1_v3.log` (Trace 36f9ee3a, 156 s, LFM2.5-1.2B-Thinking) showed
    the model emitting 5020 chars of raw chain-of-thought ("Wait, let me check
    my own knowledge", "REPLUMAIN PASSAGE", "Okay, let me try again carefully")
    with **zero** `<think>` tags. The streaming filter in `llm.rs` had nothing
    to strip; the user saw the full CoT as the answer.
  - Root cause #1: v5.0 prompt was 2077 tokens, capped at 1800 (log line 85) —
    the tail (`INTERNAL REASONING / Think silently / Do NOT reveal
    chain-of-thought`) was being truncated, so the model never saw the
    silent-reasoning directive.
  - Root cause #2: even with the directive intact, 1.2B thinking models are
    unreliable about emitting `<think>` tags on long-system-prompt RAG. A
    code-side scrubber is the only robust fix.
- **Files**:
  - `src-tauri/src/services/llm.rs` (prompt body + VERSION + doc-comment)
  - `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` (`clean_llm_output`,
    `INSUFFICIENT_INFO_MSG`, 5 new tests)
- **Verification**: `cargo test --lib --features llm clean_llm_output` →
  6/6 passed (3m 04s build, tests instant).
- **Follow-ups**:
  - Re-baseline LFM2.5-1.2B and Qwen2.5-1.5B against the v5.1 prompt; expect
    the P1 trace to drop from ~5 KB CoT to either a clean PART 1/PART 2 answer
    or the canonical refusal.
  - Vector search took 31.7 s on this trace (log line 46) — separate perf
    investigation needed; unrelated to this fix.
  - If a future model produces a valid answer that legitimately uses the
    string "part 1" before the actual marker, the anchor heuristic would
    over-trim. Not observed in practice with current models; revisit if
    benchmarks show false positives.

## 2026-05-11 (PM) — Qwen3 attempt-2 fallout: prompt v4.3.0 + streaming filter + thinking short-circuit + real-vector warmup

- **What**: Four targeted fixes after the second 17-prompt Qwen3-1.7B sweep
  (`Qwen3-1.7B 2026-05-11 Facts v2` in `~/Desktop/echoai_model_benchmark.xlsx`).
  Attempt-2: avg 141 s, 1.57 tps, acc 1.71/5, grounding 0.00 on 16/17.
  1. **Prompt v4.2.0 → v4.3.0** — v4.2.0's `FILENAME.pdf` placeholder was
     copied verbatim by Qwen3-1.7B ("[filename, page 51]" appeared literally
     in P4, P5, P7, P9). v4.3.0 uses two concrete worked examples with real
     filenames so the model substitutes instead of echoing.
  2. **Suppress `<think>` at generation level** — appended
     `<think>\n\n</think>\n\n` after `<|im_start|>assistant\n` in
     `build_rag_prompt` (documented Qwen3 short-circuit). Expected
     ~40–60 % LLM-time reduction on Qwen3/DeepSeek-R1/LFM2.5. Harmless
     no-op preamble on non-thinking models (post-hoc cleaner removes it).
  3. **Streaming `<think>` filter** — `LlmRunner::infer_with_cancel` keeps
     a 32-byte tail, tracks `in_think`, suppresses `chat://token` emits
     while inside a think block. Belt-and-suspenders with fix #2; covers
     user's "while streaming it is showing think text" complaint even if
     the model ignores the short-circuit.
  4. **Warmup with real embedding** — `setup_models_and_watchers` warmup
     replaced the 768-d zero vector with `embed_one("civil servant rules
     procedure")` so the ANN cache pre-warms the page topology a real
     query will hit. Zero-vector warmup paid the virtual-table init cost
     but P3 still went cold at 56 s on attempt 2.
- **Why**:
  - 135 s LLM mean is 95 % of wall clock; Qwen3 emits 250+ thinking
    tokens before a 50–100-token answer (~3 min wasted at 1.5 tps).
    The short-circuit is the single biggest win without changing models.
  - Grounding 0/17 on attempt 2 = the v4.2.0 placeholder pattern
    backfired. Earlier Qwen2.5-1.5B v2 prompts used concrete examples
    and did produce real citations — proven pattern.
  - Streaming UI shows raw tokens; post-hoc clean is invisible during
    the painful 100+ s wait.
- **Files**:
  - `src-tauri/src/services/llm.rs` — `GROUNDING_SYSTEM_PROMPT_VERSION`
    → `4.3.0`; `GROUNDING_SYSTEM_PROMPT` rewritten with concrete examples;
    `LlmRunner::infer_with_cancel` decode loop filters `<think>` from
    streamed emits via tail buffer + `in_think` flag.
  - `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` — `build_rag_prompt` appends
    `<think>\n\n</think>\n\n` after the assistant turn opener. Existing
    `<|im_start|>assistant` count assertions still pass (substring count
    unchanged).
  - `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` — warmup spawn-blocking task now calls
    `embedder_w.embed_one(...)` for the warmup query vector.
- **Env/flags**: none.
- **Caveats**:
  - **Compile not verified yet** — network was too flaky to fetch crate
    registry (cargo timed out on `hound`/`cpal`), and `--offline` fails
    because `hound` was added since last full sync. Run
    `cargo check --features llm` once network recovers.
  - P16 anaphor binding (BS-22 duplicate-answer of P15) NOT fixed —
    needs a turn-rewriter LLM pass before retrieval. Deferred.
  - Streaming filter uses a 32-byte tail; sufficient for `<think>` /
    `</think>` across all current tokenizers but bump if a future model
    splits the tag across larger token boundaries.
- **Follow-ups**:

## 2026-05-11 — Qwen3-1.7B benchmark fallout: 6 RAG-pipeline fixes

- **What**: Six targeted fixes triggered by the 17-prompt Qwen3-1.7B sweep
  (`Qwen3-1.7B 2026-05-11 Facts` in `~/Desktop/echoai_model_benchmark.xlsx`).
  Avg score 20.5/50, 143 s/query — Qwen3 lost to Qwen2.5-1.5B (21.5/50,
  98 s) primarily because of pipeline gaps, not raw model capability:
  1. **Strip `<think>…</think>` from final answer** —
     `clean_llm_output` now removes thinking-model reasoning blocks
     (closed *and* unclosed). Qwen3 P1 logged 2081 chars where the
     visible answer was 3 lines; the rest was leaked reasoning.
  2. **Loosen citation extractor** — `extract_citations` now also
     accepts `<filename>X</filename>`, `<file>X</file>`, `<src>X</src>`
     wrappers. Qwen3 paraphrased the prompt's format placeholder into
     pseudo-XML, scoring grounding 0.0/1.0 on every prompt despite
     citing real sources.
  3. **Warm sqlite-vec on startup** — `lib.rs::setup_models_and_watchers`
     fires a dummy `vec_distance_cosine` query at boot. The
     virtual-table cold-init cost was 39.5 s on P1 (vs 0.5 s on every
     subsequent prompt).
  4. **Re-enable chat history for follow-up queries only** —
     `build_rag_prompt` now injects up to 2 prior user/assistant pairs
     (each capped at 600 chars) when `is_followup_query` returns true.
     Anaphoric prompts P15 ("And what is the appeal process for such
     cases?") and P16 ("And for BS-22?") failed because history was
     unconditionally dropped. The 2026-05-10 drift bug is still guarded:
     self-contained queries still see no history.
  5. **Pin output language for non-Latin scripts** — `build_rag_prompt`
     appends a one-line directive when the question contains Arabic/
     Urdu/Sindhi codepoints (U+0600–06FF, U+0750–077F, U+FB50–FDFF).
     Without it, Qwen3 answered Urdu/Sindhi questions in English on
     wrong topics (P12, P13 both scored 10/50).
  6. **Strip XML placeholders from system prompt** — Bumped
     `GROUNDING_SYSTEM_PROMPT_VERSION` to **4.2.0**. The references
     example used `<short label> — <filename>, page N` which thinking
     models read as literal output template and parroted as
     `<filename>foo.pdf</filename>`. Changed to plain
     `SHORT_LABEL — FILENAME.pdf, page N` + explicit "no angle-bracket
     tags" instruction.
- **Why**: Side-by-side Qwen3 vs Qwen2.5 sweep (same 17 prompts,
  identical retrieval) made the pipeline-level losses unambiguous: a
  reasoning model bought us better calibration (P2/P8/P14) and JSON
  adherence (P11) but bled all of it back through `<think>` leaks,
  citation-format drift, and 40 s of cold sqlite-vec on the first
  query. Each fix targets a measured failure in the trace.
- **Files**:
  - `src-tauri/src/services/llm.rs` — `GROUNDING_SYSTEM_PROMPT_VERSION`
    4.1.0 → **4.2.0**; references template rewritten.
  - `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` — `clean_llm_output`
    (think-block strip), `extract_citations` (XML wrappers),
    `build_rag_prompt` (history + lang_hint). Removed misleading
    "intentionally NOT forwarded" comment block. **5 new tests** added;
    renamed existing regression guard to
    `build_rag_prompt_does_not_inject_history_for_self_contained_query`.
  - `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` — added sqlite-vec warmup after embedder
    warmup in `setup_models_and_watchers`.
- **Caveats**:
  - History injection bypasses non-follow-up queries by design — drift
    regression guard from 2026-05-10 still in force.
  - Citation extractor's XML pass is a string-scan, not a parser;
    deliberately accepts `<filename>foo.pdf, page 3</filename>` (Qwen3
    sometimes packs page inside the wrapper) by splitting on `,`.
  - Language pin only triggers on Arabic-block codepoints; other
    non-English scripts need their own ranges when relevant.
- **Follow-ups**:
  - Add TTFT (time-to-first-token, time-to-first-non-think-token) to
    traces — benchmark plan lists them but tracer doesn't record.
  - Re-run Qwen3-1.7B sweep post-fix to confirm grounding scores rise
    above 0.0 and P12/P13/P15/P16 improve.

## 2026-05-10 — Trace enrichment + bulk export for benchmarking

- **What**: Two related changes to the query-trace subsystem:
  1. **Deeper traces.** `TraceStep` now carries optional multiline `blocks`
     in addition to its `facts`. `query_router::route_scoped` attaches:
     - **Retrieved chunks fed to LLM** — top-K with file, page, 220-char
       preview (so the reader can see exactly what the LLM saw).
     - **Full prompt sent to LLM** — capped at 6 KB, UTF-8 char-bounded.
     - **Raw model output (pre-cleanup)** — capped at 8 KB.
     - **Final answer shown to user (post-cleanup)** + resolved
       **Citations** with chunk id, page, and 160-char excerpt.
  2. **One-click batch export.** New Tauri command
     `download_all_query_traces_to(dest)` concatenates every `.log` in
     `<app_data>/logs/queries/` (sorted by mtime ascending) into a single
     file with `# TRACE k/N — <name>` banners. Settings page gets a
     "Download all traces (combined)" indigo button next to the existing
     "Download latest trace".
- **Why**: The benchmark sweep (17 prompts × 10 models = 170 runs) was
  blocked on per-query manual download. Each prompt produced its own
  `.log`, but the only export button grabbed the *latest* one — so a
  full session needed 17 dialog clicks. Combined export ships them all
  at once. At the same time, the existing trace content recorded
  *metadata* (timing, citation counts, top-match filename) but not the
  inputs (chunks, prompt) or outputs (answer text) — so scoring required
  pasting the chat window separately. Enriching the trace makes a single
  exported file self-contained for offline scoring.
- **Files**:
  - `src-tauri/src/services/query_trace.rs` — added `TraceBlock`, `blocks`
    field on `TraceStep`, `add_block(label, content)` API, render logic
    (indented `│ ` prefix), 2 new tests (`add_block_renders_under_step`,
    `add_block_attaches_to_last_step_only`).
  - `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs` — `add_block` calls at
    "Build context window", "Assemble prompt", "LLM inference complete",
    "Compose final response". UTF-8-safe `chars().take(N)` truncation
    at every cap site (no byte slicing — see 2026-05-10 panic fix).
  - `src-tauri/src/commands/system.rs` — new
    `download_all_query_traces_to` command.
  - `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` — registered command in invoke handler.
  - `src/api/index.ts` — `downloadAllQueryTracesTo` wrapper.
  - `src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx` — `handleDownloadAllTraces`, new
    button, status message reports number of traces written.
- **Caveats**: Block caps (6 KB prompt / 8 KB answer / 220-char chunk
  preview) are intentionally generous but not unlimited — at 17 prompts
  × ~25 KB each, a combined export is ~425 KB which is fine. If a
  long-context model produces >8 KB answers, the trace truncates with a
  `[…truncated; full answer was N chars]` marker; the full text is still
  in `query_messages` if needed.
- **Tests**: `cargo test --lib services::query_trace` — 4/4 pass.
  `cargo check --bin echo-ai` — clean (only pre-existing warnings).

## 2026-05-10 — Fix: Urdu/Sindhi panics from byte-slicing UTF-8

- **Symptom**: During Llama-3.2-3B benchmark, the chat panicked at P13
  (Urdu appeal-procedure prompt) with
  `byte index 300 is not a char boundary; it is inside 'ا' (bytes 299..301)`.
  Subsequent queries silently went nowhere — the worker thread had panicked
  and the IPC reply never came back; UI sat idle while CPU dropped to 12-30%.
- **Root cause**: 5 sites used `&text[..text.len().min(N)]` for log/preview
  truncation. Byte-indexing into a String panics whenever the N-th byte
  lands inside a multi-byte UTF-8 char. ASCII English never tripped it;
  Urdu and Sindhi (every letter 2-3 bytes) hit it as soon as the
  truncation boundary fell mid-character.
- **Fix**: Replace every `&s[..s.len().min(N)]` with
  `s.chars().take(N).collect::<String>()` (char-based truncation).
  - `services/query_router.rs:551` — LLM raw-output debug log.
  - `services/query_router.rs:661` — reviewer-retry warn log.
  - `services/entity_extractor.rs:146` — Pass2 NER text preview.
  - `services/entity_extractor.rs:232` — Pass2 NER raw-output log.
  - `agent/react_loop.rs:132` — agent observation fallback.
  - Added regression test `truncate_is_char_safe_on_urdu` exercising the
    `truncate()` helper and the `chars().take().collect()` pattern on a
    pure-Urdu string.
- **Verification**: `cargo test --lib` → 69/69 pass.
- **Why it surfaced now**: Earlier runs (Qwen2.5/Qwen3) hit the same code
  paths but their Urdu outputs happened not to land the boundary inside a
  char (lengths varied). Llama-3.2-3B's longer Urdu output exceeded 300
  bytes by exactly the wrong amount.
- **Cross-cutting**: This is a class-of-bug fix. Any new log/preview site
  that writes user/model text MUST use char-based truncation. Linter
  rule (manual): grep for `&[a-z_]+\[\.\.[a-z_.()]+\.min\(` after any
  text-handling edit.

## 2026-05-10 — Feat: chat memory via retrieval-side keyword carry-over

- **What**: Replaces the disabled in-prompt history injection with a
  retrieval-side mechanism. When a new query is a follow-up (≤5 words OR
  contains anaphora like "this/that/those" OR starts with a continuation
  prefix like "and/also/what about"), `route_scoped` now extracts up to
  5 keywords from prior **user** turns and appends them to the embedding
  + FTS5 query — the LLM prompt itself remains history-free.
- **Why**: The user can again ask "And for BS-19?" after a question about
  Ex-Pakistan leave and have retrieval still surface BS-19 + leave-rules
  chunks, without re-introducing the few-shot template leak that the
  earlier in-prompt injection caused on 1.5B-3B models.
- **Design choices**:
  - Keywords come from USER turns only — assistant content is never
    inspected (defence-in-depth against the truncation/template-leak
    class of bugs).
  - Three-tier ranking: digit/dash tokens (BS-19, 1973) → proper nouns →
    long words. Cap at 5 so retrieval stays focused.
  - Stopword list filters out interrogatives ("what/which/where/when") and
    common request verbs ("define/list/explain") so the carry-over keeps
    only domain entities.
  - Self-contained queries (>5 words, no anaphora, no continuation
    prefix) skip the path entirely → zero latency cost on normal usage.
  - `query_text` (used for cache key, prompt, trace, persistence) is
    untouched; only `retrieval_query` is augmented.
- **Files**: `src-tauri/src/services/query_router.rs`
  - New `is_followup_query()` + `extract_carryover_keywords()` helpers.
  - `route_scoped` builds `retrieval_query` between classify and embed
    steps; threads it through embedding and FTS5 calls.
  - QueryTrace gains a "Chat memory carry-over" step when triggered.
  - 4 new unit tests: detector positive cases, detector self-contained
    cases, keyword extraction (asserts no leakage from assistant turn),
    empty/assistant-only history.
- **Verification**: `cargo test --lib` → 68/68 pass (was 64 before this
  feat + the prior fix). Regression test
  `build_rag_prompt_does_not_inject_history` continues to pass — proves
  prompt remains history-free.
- **Trade-off / next**: Coreference still imperfect (e.g. "what about
  the same officer?" — pronouns resolved by topic carry-over, not
  identity tracking). Option #3 (DB-backed semantic chat-memory with
  one-line summary into system prompt) remains in the backlog for cases
  where keyword carry-over alone is insufficient.
